# SOUL.md — catalerum

This document is the constitution and the living design plan of **catalerum**. It is
written for the humans and AI agents who build it. When a design decision is unclear, this
file is the tiebreaker — code that contradicts it is wrong, even if it works. The build loop
drives against §29/§31: survey the repo vs this document, implement one self-contained gap,
update the progress table.

## 1. Identity

catalerum is a self-hostable, automated, fully-integrated LLM assistant. It ingests your
calendars and storage buckets, keeps your notes, tasks, memories, and profile, maintains a
living catalogue of the things in your life — events, files, people, topics, projects — and
reasons and acts over them through LLM-driven automations.

The name is the intent: a **catalogue of things**. Not a chat window with
plugins, but a continuously-maintained model of your world that an LLM can query fast and act
on safely — from the web, your messenger, or another agent.

## 2. Why it exists

Your life is scattered across calendars, buckets, inboxes, and chat apps, each with its own
dialect and none aware of the others. Assistants that bolt an LLM onto one of them stay blind
to the rest and forget everything between turns. catalerum keeps a durable, queryable,
*personalized* model of all of it, lets the LLM gather across it in one hop, and turns
intentions into automations that run without you — safely, within scopes you grant.

## 3. Core principles

Decision rules, not aspirations. Apply them literally.

1. **Postgres is truth; Neo4j, Qdrant, and Valkey are derived.** Every fact lands in Postgres
   first. The Neo4j graph and the Qdrant vector index are fully rebuildable from Postgres;
   Valkey holds only ephemeral coordination/cache/stream data. Lose Neo4j or Qdrant → reproject
   / re-embed; lose Valkey → reconcile from Postgres; no durable data is ever lost.
2. **The core knows no concrete provider.** Calendars, buckets, LLM, executors, and channels
   are reached only through traits. If core code names Google, S3, OpenRouter, Docker, or
   Telegram outside its provider crate, it's a bug.
3. **The LLM acts only through typed, scoped tools.** It never touches a provider, the
   database, or a shell directly. Every side effect goes through the tool layer, authorized
   against the agent's capability grant and audited.
4. **Ingestion is idempotent and incremental.** Sync by ETag / sync-token / sequence;
   re-running never duplicates and never loses unsynced edits.
5. **Automations are durable and observable.** Definitions, queue, and run history live in
   Postgres. Every run records its trigger, steps, tool calls, and outcome. A crash mid-run
   resumes; it never silently drops or double-fires.
6. **Right store for the query.** Transactional + structured → Postgres. Multi-hop
   relationships → Neo4j. Semantic similarity → Qdrant. Blobs stay in buckets.
7. **Read is cheap, write is funneled.** Reads may fan across graph + vectors + relational
   freely. Writes go through one validated, logged, authorized path.
8. **Local-first, self-hostable.** Every integration has a local option. catalerum must run
   with no cloud account at all.
9. **Transparent by default.** No silent mutation of user data. Every automated action — and
   every denied attempt — is logged with its prompt, tool calls, and rationale.
10. **Config is the base; runtime state is a layer.** The system is fully defined by its config
    file; mutable state (workspaces, agents, grants, automations, notes, tasks, …) layers on
    via the API.
11. **Pods are stateless; coordination goes through Valkey.** Every pod is horizontally
    scalable and holds no durable local state; cross-pod coordination flows through Valkey, all
    truth through Postgres. HA is "add pods behind a load balancer".
12. **Dev is one command; tests are agent-runnable.** The whole stack comes up with a single
    `just` recipe; every build/test/e2e action is a recipe, so a human or an agent runs the
    identical path. E2E drives the real UI with Playwright against a deterministic echo-LLM.
13. **Authority is capability-scoped, attenuating, and sandboxed by default.** Every tool/API
    call needs an explicit capability; grants are deny-by-default and an agent never holds more
    authority than its creator. Destructive / production / host / egress scope is never
    implicit. Code execution defaults to a disposable sandbox; host-local is opt-in.
14. **Workspaces are the tenancy boundary; organisations group them; identity is pluggable.**
    Every object and capability belongs to one workspace; cross-workspace access is impossible
    by construction. Every workspace belongs to one **organisation** — an administrative
    grouping (members, workspace creation, org policy) that confers **no** implicit data access
    (§18). Auth is pluggable (SSO/OIDC/SAML) with a zero-config dev default (seeded admin +
    magic-link token).
15. **catalerum is itself a tool.** Its capabilities are exposed over an external MCP server so
    other agents (Claude Code, Codex, opencode) are first-class clients — under the same
    workspace + capability scoping as the built-in LLM. No privileged backdoor.
16. **The assistant learns, transparently.** It curates durable memories and a user profile to
    personalize responses and automations; every memory is stored, inspectable, and editable by
    the user — never a hidden black box.

## 4. Workspace layout

Cargo workspace under `crates/`, small single-purpose crates.

```
crates/
  catalerum-core/        # domain model, IDs, error types, shared traits
  catalerum-store/       # Postgres via sqlx: migrations, repositories (source of truth)
  catalerum-graph/       # Neo4j (neo4rs/bolt): projection writers + Cypher queries
  catalerum-vector/      # Qdrant: collections, embeddings upsert, filtered ANN search
  catalerum-bus/         # Valkey: pub/sub token relay, Streams work bus, locks, HA coord
  catalerum-llm/         # llmleaf / OpenRouter client: streaming, tool-calls, agent loop
  catalerum-iam/         # workspaces, users, SSO + dev-login, sessions, capabilities, grants
  catalerum-calendar/    # CalendarProvider trait + local(ics) / CalDAV-webcal / Google
  catalerum-storage/     # StorageBackend trait + local / S3 / WebDAV
  catalerum-email/       # EmailProvider trait + local Maildir / IMAP / JMAP (read-only ingest)
  catalerum-exec/        # Executor trait + local / docker-podman / k8s-operator / bao backends
  catalerum-skills/      # skill registry (markdown-defined): instructions + tools + optional code
  catalerum-channels/    # Matrix / Telegram / Discord: deliver + receive
  catalerum-fetch/       # WebFetcher trait impls + HTML->Markdown (HTTP / browser-CDP / Firecrawl)
  catalerum-ingest/      # sync orchestration: pull -> normalize -> store -> enqueue
  catalerum-automation/  # trigger/condition/action engine, durable queue, agent runner
  catalerum-api/         # Axum HTTP + WebSocket + SSE (the scoped agent tool surface)
  catalerum-mcp/         # external MCP server: scoped tools/resources/prompts for other agents
  catalerum-web/         # Leptos workbench
  catalerum/             # binary: load config, wire services, run API + workers
```

Dependency direction: `core` depends on nothing; everything depends on `core`; `api`/binary
wire the rest. `store`, `graph`, `vector` never depend on each other — `ingest`/`automation`
coordinate them.

## 5. Domain model (`catalerum-core`)

Canonical, provider-agnostic types. Every tenant object carries a `workspace_id`. Sketch
(refined as built):

```rust
struct Organisation { id, name, slug }
struct OrgMembership { organisation_id, user_id, role: OrgRole }  // Owner | Admin | Member
struct Workspace { id, organisation_id, name, slug }
struct User { id, email, display_name, sso_subject: Option<Subject> }
struct Membership { workspace_id, user_id, role: Role }   // Owner | Admin | Member | Viewer
enum  Author { User(UserId), Agent(AgentId) }

struct Connection { id, workspace_id, kind: ConnectionKind, name, credential_ref, cursor }
struct Calendar { id, workspace_id, connection_id, external_id, name, read_only }
struct Event { id, workspace_id, calendar_id, uid, start, end, rrule, summary, location,
               attendees: Vec<EntityRef>, body, etag, sequence }
struct Bucket { id, workspace_id, connection_id, name, prefix }
struct StoredObject { id, workspace_id, bucket_id, key, size, content_type, etag,
                      last_modified, sha256, extracted_text_id }
struct Mailbox { id, workspace_id, connection_id, external_id, name, read_only }
struct Email { id, workspace_id, mailbox_id, uid, message_id, from: EntityRef,
               to: Vec<EntityRef>, cc: Vec<EntityRef>, subject, received_at,
               body_text, body_html, has_attachments, flags, cursor_tok }

struct Entity { id, workspace_id, kind: EntityKind, display_name, aliases }
struct Document { id, workspace_id, source: SourceRef, text, summary }
struct Chunk { id, workspace_id, document_id, ordinal, text, qdrant_point_id }

struct Note { id, workspace_id, author: Author, title, markdown, tags, updated_at }
struct Profile { workspace_id, user_id, fields: Map }            // tz, hours, prefs, relations
struct Memory { id, workspace_id, scope: MemoryScope, text, source, point_id, created_at }
struct Skill { id, workspace_id, name, description, instructions_md, tools, code: Option<Code> }

struct Board { id, workspace_id, name, columns: Vec<Column> }
struct Column { id, name, order }
struct Task { id, workspace_id, board_id, column_id, title, body_md, assignee: Option<Author>,
              order, status }

struct Channel { id, workspace_id, kind: ChannelKind, config_ref }
enum  ChannelKind { Matrix, Telegram, Discord }

struct Conversation { id, workspace_id, title, origin: Origin }  // Origin = Web | Channel | Mcp
struct Message { id, conversation_id, role, content, tool_calls, created_at }

struct Grant { id, workspace_id, capabilities: Vec<Capability>, constraints }
struct Agent { id, workspace_id, name, system_prompt, tools, skills, grant_id, executor }
struct AgentProfile { id, workspace_id, name, model: Option<String>,    // §19 durable scoped agent
                      system_prompt: Option<String>, tools: Vec<String>, skills: Vec<String>,
                      subagents: Vec<String>, channels: Vec<String>, grant_id: Option<GrantId> }
struct Automation { id, workspace_id, name, enabled, triggers, condition, actions, spec }
```

`EntityRef`/`SourceRef` are stable typed pointers so Postgres rows, Neo4j nodes, and Qdrant
points share identity.

## 6. Data layer

### 6.1 Postgres — source of truth (`catalerum-store`, sqlx + migrations)
Tables: `organisations`, `org_memberships`, `workspaces`, `users`, `memberships`, `sessions`,
`connections`, `calendars`, `events`,
`buckets`, `objects`, `entities`, `documents`, `chunks`, `notes`, `profiles`, `memories`,
`skills`, `boards`, `columns`, `tasks`, `channels`, `conversations`, `messages`, `agents`,
`grants`, `automations`, `triggers`, `automation_runs`, `automation_steps`, `mcp_tokens`,
`job_queue`, `audit_log`. Every tenant row carries `workspace_id` and all queries are
workspace-filtered. Repositories expose typed CRUD; migrations are checked in, run via `migrate`.

### 6.2 Work dispatch — durable in Postgres, hot in Valkey
All async work (sync, projection, embedding, automation runs) is **enqueued durably** in
Postgres (`job_queue`) and **dispatched hot** via Valkey Streams + consumer groups, balanced
across worker pods. Enqueue = write the Postgres row + `XADD`. Workers claim from Valkey
(blocking, leased), then update Postgres run state. A reconciler re-drives any job left unacked
past its visibility timeout — a Valkey flush loses throughput, never work. Single-pod dev works
via the Postgres `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` path with Valkey disabled.

### 6.3 Neo4j — derived graph (`catalerum-graph`)
Rebuildable per-workspace projection optimized for multi-hop "data gathering".
- **Nodes:** Person, Org, Topic, Project, Place, Event, File, Note, Task, Conversation,
  Calendar, Bucket, Mailbox, Email, Memory, Document, Message.
- **Edges:** `ATTENDS`, `ABOUT`, `MENTIONS`, `STORED_IN`, `SCHEDULED_IN`, `FOLLOWS`,
  `RELATES_TO`, `DERIVED_FROM`, `REFERENCES` (Note/Task→Entity), `SENT_BY` (Email→Person),
  `ADDRESSED_TO` (Email→Person); an Email→Mailbox edge reuses `STORED_IN` (as File→Bucket).
  `RELATES_TO` is the **user/agent-authored link** between any two objects — a first-class
  `links` row in Postgres (`from`/`to` are `SourceRef`s, an optional free-text `label`/`note`),
  projected keyed on `(workspace_id, link_id)` so two links between the same pair coexist.
- Projection workers consume `job_queue` and upsert with idempotent `MERGE` on stable external
  ids (writers are parameterized Cypher behind typed helpers). The **query surface** is a safe,
  in-process **Datalog** language (`catalerum-logic`), not raw Cypher: a query loads only the
  caller's workspace facts (`node`/`edge`/`prop`) and is evaluated over them in-process, so scope
  is structural — the language cannot name a workspace, write, or reach another tenant (§18).

### 6.4 Qdrant — derived vector index (`catalerum-vector`)
Text chunks (from documents, notes, memories) are embedded and upserted into **Qdrant** (one
collection per workspace, or shared with a `workspace_id` payload filter). Payloads carry source
ref, kind, entity/topic ids, timestamps so semantic search is **filtered**. Qdrant is a derived
index, rebuildable from Postgres `chunks`/`memories`. **Embeddings go through llmleaf** (`POST
/v1/embeddings`) — it is multi-modal, not chat-only — via `catalerum-llm`'s `Embedder`; no separate
embeddings provider is needed (the embedding model is just another `[llm]` config field, §7/§13).

### 6.5 Intelligent retrieval = hybrid
The LLM gathers via composable tools (§7): `search_semantic` (Qdrant filtered ANN), `query_graph`
(Neo4j), `query_structured` (Postgres). Recall of memories + profile is injected automatically
(§22). All retrieval is workspace-scoped.

### 6.6 Valkey — ephemeral coordination & streaming (`catalerum-bus`)
Three roles, none a source of truth: **HA coordination** (locks, leader-election, cache
invalidation, grant-revocation fan-out), **token-stream relay** (§7), **workflow dispatch**
(§6.2). Everything in Valkey is rebuildable or transient; a cold Valkey costs latency, never data.

## 7. LLM layer (`catalerum-llm`)

- **Client** → llmleaf (`base_url = http://llmleaf:8080/v1`, bearer). Request shape is
  **OpenRouter** (OpenAI-superset): `model`, `messages`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `stream`, plus
  `provider { order, allow_fallbacks, require_parameters }`, `models`, `route`, `transforms`.
  llmleaf is configured `kind = "openrouter"` and routes to OpenRouter (and any provider) with
  fallbacks.
- **Modalities:** llmleaf is **multi-modal** over one base URL + bearer, so the single
  `catalerum-llm` client (`LlmleafClient`) implements all four core traits — `LlmClient` (chat,
  `/chat/completions`), `Embedder` (`/embeddings`, feeds Qdrant §6.4), `SpeechSynthesizer`
  (text-to-speech, `/audio/speech`), and `Transcriber` (speech-to-text, `/audio/transcriptions`).
  Routes are modality-agnostic: a logical model resolves the same fallback chain whatever the
  modality, and a target lacking a modality returns Unsupported and is skipped with no health
  penalty. Per-modality models are `[llm]` config fields (§13).
- **Streaming:** SSE → `StreamEvent` parser; assemble `tool_calls` deltas; every turn ends with
  a guaranteed `message_done`.
- **Cross-pod token relay (Valkey):** the generating pod publishes token deltas to a per-turn
  Valkey channel/Stream; the pod holding the client WS relays them, with replay-from-offset for
  reconnects. Chat streaming is correct under multi-pod HA.
- **Agent loop:** request → stream → execute typed tools → append results → loop until done.
  Shared by web chat, channel chat, MCP clients, and `LlmAgent` automation actions.
- **Tools** — the single registry: `search_semantic`, `query_graph`, `query_structured`,
  `get_events`, `get_objects`, `get_emails`, `search_emails` (§28), `create_event`,
  `update_event`, `move_object`, `create_note`,
  `edit_note`, `remember`, `recall`, `update_profile`, `use_skill`, `kanban_create_task`, `kanban_move_task`,
  `kanban_complete_task`, `kanban_next_task`, `notify`, `run_command` (§20), `fetch_url` (§27). Each tool is a
  thin client of a scoped API endpoint, authorized against the agent's grant (§19) and audited.

## 8. Calendar providers (`catalerum-calendar`)

```rust
trait CalendarProvider {
    async fn list_calendars(&self) -> Result<Vec<Calendar>>;
    async fn sync(&self, cal: &Calendar, cursor: Cursor) -> Result<SyncBatch<Event>>;
    async fn create_event(&self, cal: &Calendar, e: NewEvent) -> Result<Event>;
    async fn update_event(&self, e: &Event) -> Result<Event>;
    async fn delete_event(&self, e: &Event) -> Result<()>;
}
```
- **Local** — parse `.ics` (icalendar), watch a directory. Read-only by default.
- **CalDAV / webcal** — RFC 4791 `sync-collection` REPORT + ETags; `webcal://` read-only.
  CalDAV **write-back**: `PUT <uid>.ics` (`If-None-Match: *` / `If-Match: <etag>`) + `DELETE`.
- **Google Calendar** — OAuth2, `events.list` with `syncToken`; optional push webhook.
  **Write-back** via `events.insert`/`patch`/`delete` (the connect flow requests the
  `calendar.events` read/write scope; pre-write-back read-only connections keep syncing and
  fail writes with a re-connect hint).
- **Outlook / Microsoft 365** — OAuth2 (Microsoft identity platform v2, the
  `/auth/microsoft/*` flow, `[microsoft]` config), Microsoft Graph `GET /me/…/events`
  **snapshot** sync (Graph delta only covers bounded calendarViews, so
  `is_incremental = false` + a `(id, changeKey)` hash cursor; deletions ride the snapshot
  reconcile) and write-back via `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`; recurrence maps a common
  RRULE ⇄ `patternedRecurrence` subset (outside it: reads sync recurrence-less, writes
  fail loudly).

Event **write-back**: the REST event routes and the `create/update/delete_event` tools
accept any **non-read-only** calendar — a provider-backed one writes the provider FIRST
(the API's `calendar_writeback` seam), then mirrors the provider's canonical event
(uid/ETag) locally by `(calendar_id, uid)`, so the next sync converges. `WriteEvent`
(collect) stays provider→local only — it never loops back out.

Calendar collection, like email (§28), is **automation-driven, no dedicated settings**: a
`CollectCalendar { connection }` **trigger** (§11) — filled with a calendar connection — heads an
automation that pulls new external events and fires one run each; an explicit `WriteEvent` action
persists them. Until such an automation exists the connection is **dormant** (nothing collected). The
distinct `CalendarEvent { lead }` trigger is a *reminder* that fires before an **already-written**
event — so it only sees what a `WriteEvent` action stored.

## 9. Storage backends (`catalerum-storage`)

One `StorageBackend` trait per backend (FS / S3-Swift / WebDAV), optional `MultiBackend`.

```rust
trait StorageBackend {
    async fn list(&self, prefix: &str) -> Result<BoxStream<ObjectMeta>>;
    async fn stat(&self, key: &str) -> Result<ObjectMeta>;
    async fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Result<ByteStream>;
    async fn put(&self, key: &str, data: ByteStream, meta: PutMeta) -> Result<()>;
    async fn delete(&self, key: &str) -> Result<()>;
}
```
- **Local FS**, **S3** (`object_store`/`aws-sdk-s3`), **WebDAV** (`reqwest_dav`).

**Previews (`catalerum-preview`).** A stored object → a raster image preview (an
image thumbnail, or the first page of a PDF/office/spreadsheet/presentation)
behind a `Previewer` trait. Rendering runs in a **standalone preview service**
(`catalerum-preview-service`) — its own slim container image carrying the
LibreOffice + poppler toolchain plus one Rust binary, exposing `POST /render` —
because the API image is distroless and ships none of that toolchain. The API
reaches it over HTTP via a thin `HttpPreviewer` client (`[preview].service_url`);
inside the service, image formats decode with the pure-Rust `image` crate and
documents render via `soffice`→PDF then poppler `pdftoppm`. Served to the
workbench by `GET/POST /storage/preview`.

## 10. Ingestion pipeline (`catalerum-ingest`)

Per connection, on schedule or webhook: `pull (cursor)` → `normalize` → `upsert Postgres` →
enqueue `project-to-graph` + (text/docs/notes/memories/**email** bodies) `chunk → embed → upsert-to-Qdrant`.
Ingestion is **not an always-on subsystem** — it is a library of pull/normalize/upsert primitives
invoked by automation nodes (§11): a `CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar` **trigger** (filled with a
connection) pulls new external items on its cadence and fires one run per item, and an explicit
`WriteEmail`/`WriteEvent` **action** upserts each and enqueues the `project-to-graph` + `chunk → embed`
steps above. Nothing runs — and nothing is stored or embedded — unless an automation does it (§28).
Entity extraction/dedup populates `entities` and graph edges (email `From`/`To`/`Cc` → Person
entities + `SENT_BY`/`ADDRESSED_TO`, §28). Every step idempotent and
resumable from `job_queue`.

Stored **image/PDF** objects are OCR'd at object-ingest when the `[ocr]` engine chain is
configured (`OcrEngine` trait: Mistral-dialect `/v1/ocr` API → vision chat model via llmleaf →
offline `tesseract` fallback) — the text enters the same `documents` → chunk → embed pipeline as
text-like files; unconfigured, a binary object catalogues no text.

## 11. Automations engine (`catalerum-automation`)

Durable trigger→condition→action engine; definitions in Postgres, execution via `job_queue` +
`automation_runs`/`automation_steps`, under a workspace and a grant (§19).

- **Triggers:** `CollectEmail { connection, mailbox?, filter? }` and `CollectCalendar { connection,
  calendar?, filter? }` — **source triggers you fill with a §28/§8 connection**: each polls its
  provider on a cadence and **fires once per new external email/event** (the raw item is the trigger
  event), so ingest *is* the head of a graph, not a background poller. Each carries a **`commit_on`**
  reference — set it to the id of a downstream write node and the connection cursor advances for an
  item **only once that write `Succeeded`** for the item's run (intended no-loss; at-least-once,
  conditional on the §29 prefix/skip rules) — leave it unset for fire-and-forget collect.
  `CollectSql { connection, tables, cursor_column?, commit_on?, every? }` — the **external-database
  twin** (§19 `db:read@<conn>`): polls an external Postgres connection and fires one run per
  **newly-inserted row** in every table matching the `tables` wildcard pattern (later-created
  matching tables join automatically; per-table monotonic cursor — a serial/identity id or
  `created_at`-style timestamp, auto-detected unless pinned — anchored at first sight so existing
  rows never replay). The row rides the trigger (`trigger.row.<column>`); the emerged-UI loop is
  "an App INSERTs via `sql_query`, an automation reacts per row".
  `CalendarEvent { lead, filter }`
  (reminder — fires `lead` before a **stored** event), `StorageObject { event, bucket, prefix }`,
  `Schedule { cron }`, `Webhook { path }`, `GraphQuery { query, every }` (periodic Datalog query,
  §6.3), `ChannelMessage {
  channel, filter }` (inbound from Matrix/Telegram/Discord, §25), `TaskMoved { board, to_column
  }` (Kanban, §24). (`CollectEmail` supersedes the old `MailReceived` reactor — with no background
  ingest, there is nothing for a reactor to fire on.)
- **Condition:** a predicate over store/graph/vectors.
- **Code / Condition graph nodes (Boa JS, §20):** inline `{ runtime, source }` nodes run **sandboxed JS** (no fs/net; bounded loop/recursion/stack + wall-clock). A code node may call registry tools via `catalerum.callTool(name, args)`, dispatched **under the automation's own authority** — the *same* deny-by-default capability gate an Action node runs through, so a code node can reach **no tool an action node couldn't** (no separate allow-list; delete/exec/egress stay unreachable unless the grant confers them; a `dry_run` grant simulates each call). With no tool host wired it is a pure data-transform — `catalerum` is undefined.
- **Actions (typed; also the LLM's tools):** `LlmAgent { system, model, tools, skills }`,
  `RunProfile { profile, input? }` (run a named §19 agent profile under its own grant, which the
  runner verifies is ⊆ this automation's — attenuation),
  `RunSkill { skill, input?, model?, output? }` (run a named §23 skill through the **same** §7 agent
  loop — the skill's `instructions_md` seeds the system prompt and its `tools` confine the loop,
  capability-gated `skill:use@<name>` like the `use_skill` tool; the first-class counterpart to
  hand-wiring an `LlmAgent`),
  `WriteEmail { … }` / `WriteEvent { … }` — **persist a collected item**: take the email/event from
  an upstream `CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar` trigger and **upsert it into Postgres** (idempotent by
  `(mailbox_id, uid)` / event uid), enqueuing the §10 `chunk → embed → project` pipeline. This is the
  **only** thing that lands external mail/events in the store (gated `email:write`/`calendar:write` —
  writing to *our* store, still read-only w.r.t. the provider, §14); classify the item with an
  `LlmAgent` node and record the verdict with a second write — `LabelEmail { labels }`, `CreateNote`,
  or `CreateTask`,
  `CreateEvent`/`UpdateEvent`, `MoveObject`/`WriteObject` (relocate / create-or-overwrite stored
  files via the `move_object`/`write_object` registry tools, gated `storage:write`; a write is
  catalogued + §10-ingested like an upload, a move is copy-then-delete-source so content is never
  destroyed), `RunCommand { exec, … }` (§20),
  `CreateNote`/`EditNote`, `CreateTask`/`MoveTask`, `Notify { channel }` (§25),
  `Summarize { input?, instructions?, max_words?, model? }` (a **one-shot** LLM completion — no
  tools, no loop — condensing the templated `input`, or unset the firing event, into a `summary`
  downstream nodes reference),
  `Webhook { url, payload?|body?, headers?, method? }` (outbound delivery via the `send_webhook`
  tool, gated **`web:write`** — the egress-write counterpart to `fetch_url`'s `web:read` — behind
  the same §27 SSRF guard; redirects are never followed and a non-2xx receiver status **fails the
  step**, so an unacknowledged delivery never advances a run or a collect cursor).
  `LlmAgent` runs the §7 loop with the automation's restricted tool/skill set + grant.
- **Profiles as durable jobs (§19/§25):** a `run_profile` job kind runs an agent profile out-of-band
  on the worker (via the §11 `ActionRunner`); the channel→profile bridge enqueues one per profile
  listening on an inbound channel, so "a messenger message wakes a scoped agent that replies in place"
  survives a pod loss (at-least-once, same caveat as `run_automation`).
- **Email/calendar ingestion is a user-authored graph (§8/§10/§28):** there are **no dedicated
  email/calendar settings and no background poller** — you build an automation whose head is a
  `CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar` trigger (filled with a connection) and wire what happens to each
  item, e.g. `CollectEmail(conn) → WriteEmail → [LlmAgent classify → LabelEmail]`, setting
  `CollectEmail`'s `commit_on` to the `WriteEmail` node. Adding a connection provisions **nothing**;
  until a Collect automation exists the source is **dormant**. Collection runs durably: the trigger
  pulls on its cadence via the §6.2 `job_queue` (heavy provider I/O off the clock) and **enqueues one
  run per new item** (at-least-once). **The cursor commit is a node reference, resolved post-run:** the
  trigger names a write via `commit_on`, and a finalization phase after each run reads that node's final
  status (already tracked per-node by the executor). The connection's `sync_token` advances for an item
  **only after the referenced write `Succeeded`** — a write **Skipped** behind a not-taken `Condition`
  counts as *intentionally not written* and does not block; a **Failed** or never-reached write leaves
  the item uncommitted, re-collected next poll and made idempotent by `WriteEmail`'s `(mailbox_id, uid)`
  upsert. Because runs finish **out of order**, the collector advances only over the **contiguous
  committed prefix** of an ordered per-item set (compacting once the cursor passes a uid), never jumping
  to the latest committed uid. The `commit_on` signal is **carried on the trigger node, not a DAG edge**
  — it never enters topological ordering, so graphs stay acyclic by construction (a literal
  write→trigger edge would fail acyclicity validation *and* be ignored at runtime, since a trigger is an
  entry node whose output is just the firing event). With `commit_on` unset the cursor advances on
  enqueue (fire-and-forget): the run is still recorded (`automation_runs`/steps audit) and any pre-write
  side effects (`LlmAgent` tokens, external calls) still fire — only durable storage of the item is
  skipped; a Collect trigger with no `commit_on` surfaces a validation warning so the drop is an
  explicit choice. The collect grant is scoped to pull that one connection (`email:collect@<connection>`),
  never to write back to the provider (§14). **Nothing is stored — and nothing is searchable (§6.4) —
  unless the graph writes it.**
- **Durability & HA:** durable run/step state + audit in Postgres; hot Valkey Streams dispatch;
  a Valkey lock guarantees single-fire per automation across pods; the §6.2 reconciler re-drives
  unacked work; crash/pod-loss resumes.

## 12. API + Web

- **`catalerum-api` (Axum):** REST CRUD (organisations, workspaces, connections, calendars/events,
  buckets/objects, notes, tasks/boards, skills, agents, grants, channels, automations,
  conversations); **WebSocket** for streaming chat + live updates; **SSE** event feed. Auth +
  workspace-scoping enforced on every request (§18). Anything the UI does, `curl`, the agent, or
  an MCP client does — the LLM's tools are thin clients of these same endpoints, every call
  carrying a capability token authorized against the grant (§19).
- **`catalerum-web` (Leptos workbench):** Chat panel (SSE→`StreamEvent`→WS→ChatPanel), Calendar
  view, File browser, **Notes editor**, **Kanban board**, **Skills** manager, Automation + Agent
  / grant builder, Channels config, Memories/Profile viewer, Graph/data explorer, and an
  **organisation + workspace switcher** with policy-gated create-workspace / create-organisation
  flows (§18). The **settings surface adapts to the deployment mode** (§18): `single_user`
  exposes the full per-user settings depth; `multi_user` shows members curated,
  admin-preconfigured defaults and hides the rest.
- **Emerged UIs (AI-authored Apps).** The assistant authors custom UIs — forms, dialogs,
  dashboards, multi-view mini-apps — as a typed, closed-vocabulary JSON tree (`UiSpec`,
  `catalerum-core::model_ui`), stored as versioned `ui_definitions` rows and rendered by one
  generic Leptos interpreter, inline in chat and in a standalone **Apps panel**. No runtime
  code-gen reaches the browser: interactivity is three handler kinds — `client` (local ops),
  `tool` (a capability-gated registry tool from the server-defined `[ui].handler_tools`
  allow-list), and `script` (server-side Boa whose only host bridge is `catalerum.callTool`,
  gated identically) — plus an `ai` relay that opens a chat turn. Every handler runs under the
  viewing user's authority, capped to their base role capabilities: an App can never do what
  its user couldn't.
- **Apps own durable data.** An emerged App is only fully featured if it can persist:
  automations (§11) build a data model up over time and the App presents and edits it. The
  sanctioned stores are the same capability-gated tools everything else uses — first-class
  catalerum objects (notes, tasks, events, labels, links), **files** in a storage backend (§9,
  `storage:read`/`storage:write`), and **external Postgres** connections via `sql_query`
  (per-connection scope) — reachable from `tool`/`script` handlers when the allow-list + the
  user's grant confer them. Transient view state (open dialog, active tab, unsubmitted inputs)
  stays client-only; *data* lives in real stores so it outlives the session, is
  workspace-scoped, and is visible to automations, chat, and the graph like any other fact.
  "Automation collects → data model grows → App presents" is the intended loop.

## 13. Config & secrets

TOML config is the immutable base (llmleaf endpoint + key + per-modality models
[chat/embedding/speech/transcription], Postgres/Neo4j/Valkey/Qdrant URLs,
default `Executor` backend + **bao** endpoint, web-fetch backend + egress policy (`[fetch]`, §27),
base capability policy,
deployment **`mode`** (`single_user` | `multi_user`) + organisation/workspace-creation
policies (§18),
auth/SSO config, dev-login toggle, MCP server enable, channel + an optional generic `[[connections]]`
seed array — **no dedicated `[email]`/calendar settings block**: email and calendar carry no special
config; their provider settings, credentials, and per-source cursor live in `connections` rows
(`config` JSONB + `credential_ref` + `sync_token`) and ingest is a user-built
`CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar` automation (§11), not a background poller);
runtime-mutable state (organisations, workspaces, agents, grants, notes, tasks, skills, channels,
automations) layers on via the API. Provider credentials (Google OAuth, S3 keys, channel tokens, IMAP/JMAP/Gmail email credentials) are stored
encrypted, referenced by `credential_ref` — never plaintext. (Storage mechanism is an open
question; see §29.)

## 14. In scope / Non-goals

**In scope:** multi-provider calendar + storage ingest with write-back; multi-provider email
**read-ingest** (IMAP / JMAP / local Maildir; Gmail in M7, §28); Postgres truth +
rebuildable Neo4j graph + Qdrant semantic search; OpenRouter-via-llmleaf chat & agentic tool-use
with cross-pod token streaming; durable automations; multi-pod HA via stateless pods + Valkey;
organisations grouping multi-workspace tenancy, single-/multi-user **deployment modes** (one
config knob; presentation + defaults, never schema), pluggable SSO + zero-config dev login;
capability-scoped agents from
chat; sandboxed terminal/code execution (local / container / Kubernetes / **bao**); markdown
**notes**; auto-curated **memories** + **profile**; **skills**; **Kanban** tasks; **channels**
(Matrix/Telegram/Discord); an **external MCP server**; **web fetching/browsing with HTML→Markdown**
(HTTP / browser-CDP / Firecrawl, §27); Leptos workbench; local-first self-hosting.

**Non-goals:** being an inference engine for any modality (llmleaf's job — chat, embeddings,
speech, transcription); a general workflow-orchestration
platform (no Temporal/Argo — automations stay Postgres-simple; the k8s/bao executors are
sandboxed code execution, not orchestration); being a mail client — no composing / sending /
replying (email is read-only ingest, §28); storing blobs in the DB; silent prompt/data
mutation; implicit authority; requiring any cloud account to run.

## 15. Decision filter

- New capability? Prefer a new **tool** / **skill** / **provider** behind an existing trait over
  new core surface.
- Where does the fact live? Postgres first; graph and vectors are derivations.
- Granting authority? Deny by default; delegate only what the creator holds, narrowed.
  Destructive / production / host / egress scope is never implicit and may require approval.
- External surface (MCP, channel)? Same auth + capability scoping as everything else — no
  backdoor, no privileged path.
- Personalization (memory/profile)? Stored, inspectable, editable data — never hidden.
- Scope every object and query by workspace; cross-workspace reach is a bug.
- Match provider semantics exactly (sync tokens, ETags, RRULEs), even when awkward.

## 17. Developer experience & test harness

Simplicity is a feature: clone to a running, testable, **logged-in** stack in one command, no
undocumented steps.

**`justfile` is the single entrypoint.** No hidden scripts; humans and agents run the same
recipes. Backing services (Postgres, Neo4j, Valkey, Qdrant) via a committed `docker-compose.yml`.

```
just up        # start Postgres + Neo4j + Valkey + Qdrant (docker-compose)
just migrate   # run sqlx migrations
just seed      # seed admin + default organisation/workspace + fixtures (calendar, bucket, notes, board)
just dev       # up + migrate + run API (watch) + web (trunk serve) + echo-llmleaf;
               #   single-user mode (§18); prints the dev magic-link login URL to the console
just test      # cargo test across the workspace (ephemeral services per crate)
just e2e       # boot stack w/ echo-LLM -> seed -> Playwright specs -> tear down
just e2e-docker# e2e, but Playwright runs in the pinned container (docker-compose.playwright.yml) — no local node/browsers
just mcp       # run the external MCP server against the dev stack (for agent integration tests)
just reset | just fmt | just lint | just check | just down
```

**Zero-config login.** `just dev` seeds an admin + a **default organisation** (slug `default`)
holding the default workspace, runs in **single-user mode** (§18), and prints a magic-link URL
with a generated token — open it, you're in. No IdP, no password on dev systems.

**Deterministic, key-free LLM.** A bundled `llmleaf.dev.toml` uses the `echo` provider, so chat,
tool-call shaping, and streaming run offline and reproducibly in CI — no credentials.

**Agent-runnable end-to-end.** `just e2e` is the contract an agent calls: ephemeral stack, seed +
admin session, headless **Playwright** (`@playwright/test`) against the Leptos workbench, non-zero
exit on failure. Specs cover login, chat → token stream → `message_done`, calendar, file browser,
notes editor, kanban, scoped-agent creation. `websocat` gives low-level WS/SSE smoke beneath the UI.

**Test layers.** Unit/integration `cargo test` per crate against ephemeral Postgres / Neo4j /
Valkey / Qdrant; Playwright e2e via `just e2e`; deterministic echo-LLM for stable chat assertions.
Every milestone lands with the `just` recipes and Playwright specs that prove it.

## 18. Workspaces, identity & SSO (`catalerum-iam`)

**Workspace = the tenancy boundary.** Every object belongs to exactly one workspace; queries are
workspace-filtered; Neo4j and Qdrant are partitioned per workspace. Cross-workspace access is
impossible by construction — which makes capability scoping (§19) airtight.

**Users & roles.** A user authenticates, then acts as a **member** of one or more workspaces with
a **role** (Owner / Admin / Member / Viewer). The role sets the base capability set; grants (§19)
attenuate within it.

**Organisations group workspaces.** Every workspace belongs to exactly one **organisation** —
the administrative grouping above the tenancy boundary. An organisation has its own membership
(`OrgMembership`, role Owner / Admin / Member) governing administration only: creating/archiving
workspaces in the org, managing org members, org-level policy. **Org roles confer no data
access** — reading a workspace still requires a workspace membership; an org Admin who is not a
member of a workspace administers its shell, never its contents. The workspace stays the data +
capability boundary (§19); organisations never appear in capability strings. `just dev` seeds a
**default organisation** (slug `default`) holding the default workspace (§17).

**Switching & creation.** Belonging to several organisations/workspaces is normal. The web
switcher (§12) picks organisation → workspace and re-scopes the session — sessions are
workspace-scoped, so switching mints a new token, it never widens an old one — and every panel
re-reads under the new scope. Creation is policy-gated, deny-by-default:
- **Workspace** — org policy `workspace_creation = admins | members | disabled` (instance
  default derives from the deployment mode below); the creator becomes the workspace's
  **Owner**. A new workspace starts empty — nothing is shared across workspaces at creation.
- **Organisation** — instance policy `organisation_creation` (same values); the creator becomes
  the organisation's **Owner**.

**Deployment mode: single-user vs multi-user.** One instance-level knob, `[server] mode =
single_user | multi_user` (§13). The invariant: **mode changes presentation, defaults, and
optimizations — never the model.** Schema, API, authorization, and org/workspace tenancy are
identical in both; a single-user instance is a multi-tenant instance with one human in it, and
flipping the mode later is a config edit, not a migration.
- **`single_user`** (what `just dev` runs, §17) optimizes for one person: the UI surfaces the
  full settings depth for that user (per-modality models, voice, theme, profile, executors),
  hides member/role/SSO management chrome, auto-selects the default organisation/workspace, and
  the runtime may cache aggressively around the sole user (session, profile, recall prewarm).
  Creation policies default to `members`.
- **`multi_user`** optimizes for a shared deployment: admins preconfigure (models, themes, tool
  allow-lists, channels) and members see **fewer settings** — curated defaults rather than every
  knob — while the member-management + SSO surfaces appear. Creation policies default to
  `admins`.

**Authentication is pluggable.**
- **SSO** — OIDC and SAML (Keycloak, Google, Azure AD, …); SSO subject → user; membership
  assigned (optionally JIT from claims/groups).
- **Dev default (zero config)** — first run seeds an **admin** + default workspace and prints a
  **login URL with a generated one-time token**; open it → logged in. Auto-off once real auth/SSO
  is configured.
- **Service tokens** — long-lived, workspace-bound scoped tokens for scripts/CI/MCP clients.

Sessions issue short-lived, workspace-scoped tokens; agent + MCP-client runs carry a capability
token (§19) bound to {workspace, grant}. The API enforces auth on every request.

## 19. Authorization — capabilities & scoped agents (`catalerum-iam`)

A user can, from chat, stand up an agent that does one narrow job and *cannot* do anything else —
not delete production data, not touch the host. The API is the single enforcement choke point;
every tool is a thin client of a scoped endpoint, authorized server-side against the caller's
grant. The model is never trusted to self-limit.

- **Capability** — `(action, resource-selector, constraints)`, read/write/delete split, always
  within a workspace. E.g. `calendar:read@work`, `email:read@work`, `storage:write@local/out/*`, `notes:write`,
  `tasks:write@board/ops`, `graph:query`, `vector:search`, `skill:use@summarize`,
  `exec:run@bao{lang=python, net=none, cpu=1}`, `web:read@*.wikipedia.org`,
  `mcp:expose@tools=[query_graph,kanban_create_task]`.
- **Grant** — a named capability bundle + global constraints: env allow-list (`prod` only if
  explicit), rate/cost/resource caps, time window, dry-run, per-action `requires_approval`.
- **Agent** — system prompt + allowed tools + skills + a Grant + Executor backend, created from
  chat or API. Web/channel/MCP chat runs under the *user's* grant.
- **Agent profile** — the **durable, named** form of an Agent (`agent_profiles` table): a reusable
  scoped-agent configuration bundling a **model**, a system prompt, an allowed **tool/skill** set,
  the **subagents** it may delegate to, the **channels** it listens on, and the **Grant** that is
  its authority — all within **one workspace** (the tenancy + data boundary). It makes *separate,
  securely-scoped data access* a first-class object: a "calendar bot" profile carries a grant of
  exactly `calendar:read@…` (+ `channel:write` to reply) and so **cannot** touch storage or email.
  Admin-only to manage (gated `agent_profile:read`/`write`, like grants); a profile's grant must be
  ⊆ its creator's authority. **Subagent delegation** is a tool (`delegate`), **on by default in every
  agent run** (profiles, chat-as-profile, and plain chat all carry it, with a standing nudge) — because
  a subagent burns its **own** context window on a subtask and returns only the result, keeping the
  caller lean and (with a cheaper per-call `model`) cheaper. Two modes, both **⊆ the caller** and one
  level deep (no nested delegation): a **named profile** (runs under its own grant, verified ⊆ the
  caller at delegation time — an empty `subagents` list means *any* workspace profile, a non-empty one
  is an allow-list) or a zero-config **ephemeral worker** under the caller's own authority. So no agent
  can widen access by delegating. **Channel binding**: an inbound message on a channel a profile lists routes to
  that profile's §7 loop, which replies in place — chat-from-messenger without an automation. A
  grant carrying a not-yet-enforceable constraint **fails closed** (the profile refuses to run).
  Name-keyed (tools/skills/subagents/channels are names within the workspace), like the rest of the
  system. The runtime lives in `catalerum-api` (`profile_agent` + the channel listener / inbound route).
  **Reach:** a profile can be invoked four ways — listening on a **channel** (durable `run_profile`
  job per inbound message, §11/§25), as an automation **`RunProfile` action** (§11), **delegated** to
  as a subagent (the `delegate` tool), or **chatted as** via the per-conversation **picker** (a
  `conversations.agent_profile_id` binding; the §7 chat loop then uses the profile's model/prompt/tools
  under the user's authority **intersected** with the profile's grant — it can scope a thread *down*,
  never **escalate** the user). Every path enforces ⊆ its caller's authority, so no path widens access.
- **Attenuation (safety invariant).** A grant is minted only from capabilities the creator holds,
  equal-or-narrower. A chat-built agent is provably ⊆ its creator; nothing escalates.
- **Deny-by-default + protected scopes.** Nothing runs without a matching capability. Protected
  scopes need explicit inclusion (and may require human approval): `env=prod`, the **Local**
  Executor (host), `*:delete`, `exec` without an image/lang/command allow-list, network egress,
  broad `mcp:expose`. "Destroy production" / "wipe the local computer" is unreachable unless that
  exact capability is handed over on purpose.
- **Audit & revocation.** Every authorized action and every denied attempt is logged; grants can
  be revoked instantly (Postgres truth + Valkey fan-out), killing authority mid-flight.

## 20. Terminal tool calls & code execution (`catalerum-exec`)

The LLM and automations run shell commands / code via `run_command` (and skill code, §23) — never
directly. Execution goes through a pluggable `Executor`, gated by `exec:*` capabilities (§19) and
audited.

```rust
trait Executor {
    async fn run(&self, cmd: CommandSpec) -> Result<CommandResult>; // argv/code, env, cwd, stdin, timeout, limits
    async fn open_session(&self) -> Result<Session>;
}
```

Backends, selected per config / agent grant:
- **Local** — `tokio::process` on the host. Highest blast radius; *protected*, opt-in only.
- **Container (docker / podman)** — ephemeral container per command/session: pinned image,
  explicit mounts, network policy, CPU/mem/time limits, dropped caps. **Default sandbox.**
- **Kubernetes operator** — short-lived Jobs / ephemeral Pods, namespaced isolation, quotas, same
  multi-pod HA story; scales execution out of the API/worker pods.
- **bao** — the **bao** agent runs workflow **code natively and securely** (the preferred backend
  for code steps in automations/skills): native-speed execution inside bao's secure sandbox,
  without a full container per call. Used for `exec:run@bao{lang=…}`. (Integration interface to
  confirm — §29.)

The same Executor powers terminal-capable automations and skill code. Default posture: sandboxed
(container / bao / Kubernetes), Local opt-in, commands/code deny-by-default and scoped to an
allow-list.

### Per-workspace sandbox (`[exec].per_workspace`)

The backends above spin a **fresh** container/Pod per command or session. Opting in to
`[exec].per_workspace` (for the container/kubernetes backends) instead keeps **one long-lived,
secure sandbox per workspace** (§18): every terminal session and `run_command` for a workspace
`exec`s *into* that single `catalerum-ws-<id>` sandbox, sharing a persistent `/work` volume. Two
backends sit behind a `WorkspaceSandbox` trait (`catalerum-exec`):
- **`PodmanSandbox`** — manages a long-lived container per workspace directly via podman/docker; an
  in-process idle reaper (`WorkspaceSandboxManager`, `catalerum-api`) destroys it after the idle
  timeout (the `/work` named volume persists).
- **`K8sSandbox`** — declares a `WorkspaceSandbox` **custom resource** (`catalerum.dev/v1alpha1`) and
  waits for the **`catalerum-operator`** (kube-rs, `crates/catalerum-operator`) to reconcile a
  per-workspace Namespace + hardened Deployment + `/work` PVC + ResourceQuota/LimitRange +
  NetworkPolicy + the API's exec RoleBinding, then `kubectl exec`s into the operator-managed Pod.
  The operator idle-suspends (`replicas:0`) and hard-deletes per the CR's TTLs; the API bumps
  `status.lastActivity` on each use. CRD types are shared via `crates/catalerum-k8s`; manifests live
  in `deploy/` (`kubectl apply -k deploy/`). Durable state: the `workspace_sandboxes` table.

## 21. Notes (markdown)

User- or LLM-authored **markdown notes** — shopping lists, goals, journals, meeting notes. Stored
in Postgres (`notes`), editable in the web editor and via tools (`create_note`, `edit_note`,
`read_note`, `list_notes`). Notes are ingested like documents: chunked, embedded into Qdrant, and
projected into the graph (`REFERENCES` edges to entities/topics) so they're searchable and
linkable. Authored by `Author::User` or `Author::Agent`, so an automation can draft a note and the
user can edit it.

## 22. Memories & profile (personalization)

catalerum learns about you, transparently (principle 16).
- **Profile** — a structured per-user record (timezone, working hours, preferences,
  relationships, defaults). Injected into the system prompt for every turn. Editable in the UI and
  via `update_profile`.
- **Memories** — durable free-text facts auto-curated during conversations and automations (the
  `remember` tool, plus a background extractor that proposes memories from chats). Scoped
  `User` or `Workspace`, embedded into Qdrant, and **recalled** automatically (semantic `recall`)
  into context when relevant. Every memory is a row the user can view, edit, or delete — no hidden
  state. Memories refine the profile over time.

## 23. Skills (`catalerum-skills`)

A **skill** is a reusable, named capability bundle: `name`, `description`, markdown
`instructions`, an optional restricted tool set, and optional **code** (run via the Executor §20,
preferably **bao**). Skills are authored by users or agents (markdown-first, like a runbook),
stored per workspace, and invoked by the LLM via `use_skill` or attached to an agent/automation.
Invoking a skill is itself capability-gated (`skill:use@<name>`); a skill can never exceed the
caller's grant. First-party skills (summarize, triage-inbox, weekly-review) ship as fixtures.

## 24. Tasks & Kanban board

A **board** has ordered **columns** (e.g. Backlog → To-do → Doing → Done) holding **tasks**
(markdown body, assignee = user or agent, order). Tasks are created by the user or by the LLM /
automations, and **worked one by one**: an agent pulls `kanban_next_task` from a column, does the work
within its grant, and `kanban_complete_task`s it (moving it along). `TaskMoved` is an automation trigger
(§11), so "when a task enters *Doing*, the assigned agent works it" is a first-class flow. Managed
in the web Kanban UI (drag with insert-above reordering, a card detail modal, inline column
management, a card filter) and via tools (`kanban_create_board`, `kanban_create_task`,
`kanban_move_task` — with an optional `position`, `kanban_complete_task`, `kanban_next_task`,
`kanban_edit_task`, …) that address boards and columns **by name or id**.
Tasks project into the graph for "what's blocked / who owns what" queries.

## 25. Channels (`catalerum-channels`)

Bidirectional messaging integrations — **Matrix**, **Telegram**, **Discord** — behind one trait:

```rust
trait Channel {
    async fn send(&self, target: ChannelTarget, msg: OutMessage) -> Result<()>;
    async fn subscribe(&self) -> Result<BoxStream<InMessage>>;   // inbound
}
```
- **Outbound** — the `Notify { channel }` action and automation outputs deliver to a chat.
- **Inbound** — messages arrive as a `ChannelMessage` automation trigger (§11) and can open a
  `Conversation { origin: Channel }`, so you **chat with catalerum from your messenger**, under
  the channel's mapped user + grant. Credentials (bot tokens, homeserver access) are encrypted
  `credential_ref`s configured per workspace.

## 26. External MCP server (`catalerum-mcp`)

catalerum exposes its capabilities as an **MCP server** so external agents — **Claude Code,
Codex, opencode** — are first-class clients (principle 15). It surfaces:
- **Tools** — the §7 registry (query_graph, search_semantic, get_events, create_note,
  kanban_create_task, run_command, use_skill, …), each authorized per call.
- **Resources** — read views (calendar, notes, tasks, files, graph slices).
- **Prompts** — packaged skills (§23) as MCP prompts.

An MCP client connects with a **workspace-bound service token** mapped to a **grant** (§19), so an
external agent gets exactly the scoped slice you granted — no more than the built-in LLM, deny-by-
default, fully audited. The MCP server is the same scoped API surface in MCP clothing; there is no
privileged backdoor.

## 27. Web fetching & browsing (`catalerum-fetch`)

The assistant must read the live web — a docs page, an article, a release note — without drowning
in HTML. Raw HTML is hostile to an LLM: mostly markup, scripts, and navigation chrome, it burns
context for almost no signal. catalerum fetches a page and hands the model **clean Markdown of the
main content** — a fraction of the tokens, all of the meaning.

One trait, pluggable backends (principle 2/8):

```rust
trait WebFetcher {
    async fn fetch(&self, request: FetchRequest) -> Result<FetchedPage>;
}
```

- **HTTP** — a plain `reqwest` GET. Local-first, no JavaScript, the cheapest path and the default;
  `FetchMode::Auto` falls back to it.
- **Browser / CDP** — drives an *external* JS-capable browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
  (headless Chrome `--remote-debugging-port`, a Playwright `launchServer` endpoint, or
  Browserless). catalerum stays the controller; the browser is just another provider. Renders
  JavaScript, optionally waits for a selector, then snapshots the DOM. (Build feature `browser`.)
- **Firecrawl** — the self-hostable-or-cloud scrape API (the one non-open-source option), which
  returns Markdown server-side. Credentials are an encrypted `credential_ref` (§13).

**HTML→Markdown is the core of the value.** Every backend funnels HTML through one converter:
strip the structural boilerplate (`script`/`style`/`svg`/forms/`head`), extract the main content
(`<main>`/largest `<article>`, else drop page chrome by ARIA role and class/id heuristics), then
emit GitHub-flavoured Markdown (headings, lists, links resolved against the base URL, code fences,
tables). `FetchFormat` selects `Markdown` (default), `Html` (raw), or `Text`. The page reports its
raw vs. converted byte sizes so a caller can see the context it saved.

**Exposed as the `fetch_url` tool** (§7): a thin client of the scoped `POST /fetch` endpoint,
authorized by the `web:read@<host-glob>` capability (§19) and audited like every side effect. The
LLM never fetches directly.

**Egress is a protected scope (§13/§19).** An SSRF guard runs before any socket opens: only
`http(s)`, and — unless explicitly allowed — never a private, loopback, or link-local address;
hostnames are resolved and re-checked (a public name pointing at `127.0.0.1` is refused) and every
redirect hop is re-validated. `allow_private_hosts` is opt-in, for trusted internal targets only.
Config lives under `[fetch]` (§13): default backend, timeout, byte cap, Firecrawl/browser settings.

A fetched page is not yet a catalogued source, but it carries a `SourceRef::External { uri }`, so a
later ingest step can chunk + embed + project it like any other document (§10) when we choose to.

## 28. Email providers (`catalerum-email`)

Reading email is a read-only ingest, the same shape as calendars (§8) and storage (§9): pull
messages on a cursor, normalize to the canonical `Email`, land them in Postgres, then chunk +
embed + project like any document (§10). catalerum **reads** your mail; it is **not** a mail
client — no composing, sending, or replying (§14). One trait, pluggable backends (principle 2/8):

```rust
trait EmailProvider {
    async fn list_mailboxes(&self) -> Result<Vec<Mailbox>>;
    async fn sync(&self, mailbox: &Mailbox, cursor: Cursor) -> Result<SyncBatch<Email>>;
}
```

- **IMAP** — RFC 3501 IMAP4rev1; incremental by `UIDVALIDITY` + `UID` (and `MODSEQ`/`CONDSTORE`
  when offered). The open-protocol workhorse: Dovecot, Fastmail, Migadu, any self-hosted server.
- **JMAP** — RFC 8621; `Email/query` + `Email/changes` from a `sinceState`. Modern, efficient
  delta sync (Fastmail, Stalwart).
- **Local Maildir / mbox** — read a local mail directory, watch it. Read-only; the local-first
  dev fixture (mirrors local `.ics`, principle 8).
- **Gmail API** — OAuth2, `messages.list` with `historyId` deltas; lands in **M7** alongside
  Google Calendar (§16).

Sync is idempotent and incremental (principle 4): messages upsert by `(mailbox_id, uid)`, the
per-mailbox cursor is the provider's native delta token (IMAP `UIDVALIDITY/UIDNEXT`, JMAP state,
Gmail `historyId`), and a re-run never duplicates. **Collection is a trigger you fill with a
connection, not a background poller** (§11): there is no `[email]` config block and no always-on
sweep — a `CollectEmail { connection }` trigger heads an automation that pulls new external mail and
**fires once per message**, and an explicit downstream `WriteEmail` action upserts it (idempotent by
`(mailbox_id, uid)`) and enqueues the §10 `chunk → embed → project`. Setting `CollectEmail`'s
`commit_on` to the `WriteEmail` node makes the **cursor advance only after the message is durably
written** (intended no-loss; otherwise it re-collects next poll — §29); leave it unset for fire-and-forget.
**Nothing is ingested or searchable until an automation writes it** — a connection with no Collect
automation is dormant.
Email is still a strictly **read-only ingest** (§14): `CollectEmail` only pulls and normalizes, never
composing or sending. `From`/`To`/`Cc` resolve to `EntityRef`s so
senders and recipients become **Person** nodes (§6.3) — the graph answers "who emailed me about
X". Bodies are chunked + embedded into Qdrant (§6.4), so mail is **semantically searchable**
alongside notes and events.

**Exposed as read tools** (§7): `get_emails` (recent / unread / by-sender) and `search_emails`
(semantic + structured), thin clients of scoped endpoints authorized by `email:read@<account>`
(§19) and audited — over **whatever a `WriteEmail` action has stored**. The `CollectEmail` trigger
(§11) heads these flows directly, so "collect my mail, and when one's from my bank run the
**triage-inbox** skill (§23)" is a single automation — `CollectEmail → WriteEmail → LlmAgent`.
Attachments carry a `SourceRef` for later object-style ingest (§9) — see §29.

## 29. Open questions

- **bao integration** — confirm the bao agent's exact interface (CLI / RPC / lib) and sandbox
  model so `catalerum-exec`'s bao backend maps cleanly to `exec:run@bao{…}`.
- **SSO first cut** — OIDC vs SAML to ship first in M7; JIT-provisioning policy. _Resolved 2026-07-02
  (see §31): **OIDC shipped** (Authorization Code + PKCE S256, confidential client, discovery + cached
  JWKS, hardened id_token validation), SAML deferred (XML-DSig weight; target IdPs all speak OIDC).
  JIT policy: `jit_provisioning` **disabled by default**; when enabled a new user gets organisation
  membership only (`jit_organisation`/`jit_org_role`) and NO workspace until invited — fail-closed.
  Open remainder: web login button (`/status.sso` is the seam), logout/RP-initiated logout, refresh
  tokens, fake-provider integration test._
- **Credential storage** — dedicated encrypted vault vs Postgres-encrypted columns vs OS keyring.
- **MCP transport** — stdio vs streamable-HTTP for external agents; token issuance UX.
  _FULLY RESOLVED 2026-07-02: stdio + authenticated HTTP `POST /mcp` (request/response), the
  SSE-streaming half (`GET /mcp` push + progress-streaming POST — see the §31 entry), and the
  token-issuance UX — **grant-scoped tokens** (`POST /tokens` + `catalerum token --grant`): a bearer
  bound to a §19 grant is a member-shaped principal holding the grant's capabilities (attenuation-gated
  at mint against the caller's current authority; deleted grant → 401 fail-closed via DB cascade;
  never passes admin checks), so an external MCP client holds exactly what it was granted._
- **Qdrant tenancy** — collection-per-workspace vs shared collection with payload filter.
  _Provisionally **collection-per-workspace** as of the `catalerum-vector` slice (§6.4/§18); every
  point also carries a `workspace_id` payload that searches always filter on, so switching to a
  shared collection later is a cheap migration, not a rewrite._
- **Entity/memory dedup** — *both halves resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31). Memories: a single
  `store_memory_deduped` seam (all three write paths) layering normalized-exact/superset heuristics with a
  0.95-cosine ANN check; skip+touch on duplicate, in-place refine on strict superset. Entities: the
  `entity_dedup` seam — kind-scoped normalization → deterministic `UUIDv5(ws, "<kind>:<key>")` ids so
  Neo4j `MERGE` folds duplicates onto the survivor, plus `project_entity_deduped` reporting
  created-vs-deduplicated for future extraction paths. Still open (recorded escalations): retroactive
  merge of existing entities, LLM-assisted judging of borderline pairs, entity embeddings (none exist yet).
- **Email attachments** (§28) — *resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31): **bucket + link.** Raw `.eml` +
  each attachment become objects in the workspace's default files store
  (`emails/<mailbox>/<uid>/…`, path-safe segments), referenced from the email row
  (`raw_ref` + new `attachments` JSONB refs, migration 0049) — riding the §10 object-ingest
  pipeline (extraction/embedding/`download_link`) for free, never inlined as chunks. Opt-in by
  having a default store; warn-not-fatal; redelivery-idempotent; deletion reconcile cleans the
  objects. Wired for Maildir/IMAP/Gmail; JMAP defers (no raw-blob download in its client yet).
- **Email folder / label topology** (§28) — *resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31): **per-folder/label
  mailboxes** — one `mailboxes` row per synced folder/label, the provider's sync-cursor scope
  (already how all four providers work; Gmail's synced label IS its mailbox); sync depth is the
  per-`CollectEmail`-trigger `mailbox` field, no hardcoded Spam/Trash skip-list. *Decision needed:*
  JMAP's default with `mailbox` unset syncs **ALL** folders incl. Spam/Trash — the one
  deny-by-default violation, deliberately left unchanged (changing it breaks whole-account JMAP
  setups and touches the CollectCalendar twin). *Also open:* Gmail's full label set as tags
  (collides with `labels` = classifier verdicts; needs a distinct provider-label surface).
- **Cross-folder dedup** (§28) — *resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31): **N rows stay** — each folder's
  `(mailbox_id, uid)` row is the sync-correct unit (per-folder cursors/ledgers/deletions), collapsed
  logically via `message_id` (column + `(workspace_id, message_id)` index existed since 0015 and all
  providers populate it; duplicates are REAL today — a filterless JMAP connection syncs every
  folder). New `EmailRepo::list_by_message_id` is the grouping surface. *Deferred:* indexing-layer
  dedup (skip re-embedding a known Message-ID) — a naive skip orphans search results when the
  embedded copy is deleted/moved; needs message_id-aware deletion reconcile + primary election;
  query-time collapse is the cleaner seam meanwhile.
- **Collect cursor commit** (§11/§28) — *resolved* by the `commit_on` node reference (§11): the trigger
  names a write, a post-run finalization reads its status, and the collector advances the `sync_token`
  over the **contiguous committed prefix** (out-of-order runs can't jump it forward); a write **Skipped**
  behind a not-taken `Condition` counts as intentionally-committed; multiple `commit_on` targets are
  **AND** (all must `Succeed`/`Skip`). *Still open:* the exact committed-set compaction + crash-window
  bookkeeping in the collector when it lands.
- **First-run backfill flood** (§11/§28) — *resolved in shape:* a Collect trigger carries a
  `backfill_window` (default: items newer than the automation's creation) and a first-poll cap (remainder
  drains incrementally), so a large existing mailbox doesn't enqueue one run per historical message at
  once. *Open:* the default window + cap values.
- **Idempotent redelivery** (§11) — *resolved 2026-07-02* (see the §31 entry): `WriteEmail` reports
  `newly_written: false` on a redelivered item (store probe before the upsert), the executor latches a
  per-run `redelivery` flag from any such signal (or `trigger.redelivery`), and non-idempotent actions
  (`ActionKind::is_idempotent()`) auto-`Skip` once latched — `commit_on` still advances (write `Succeeds`,
  skips count as committed). Per-node `rerun_on_redelivery: true` opts back in; `input.redelivery` is
  branchable in Condition/Code nodes. `WriteEvent` emits the signal too as of the same-day cadence entry
  (`EventRepo::get_by_uid` + probe mirroring `run_write_email`) — both collect paths are covered.
- **Dormant-connection warning** (§12/§28) — a connection with no Collect automation ingests nothing.
  Should the UI flag it as idle so "I added my email but see no mail" is obvious, given there is no
  settings page to signal status?
- **Collect cadence** (§11) — *resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31): per-trigger optional `every` (bare int =
  minutes, `{minutes}`/`{seconds}`, or `"30s"/"5m"/"1h30m"/"2d"` strings), clamped to `[60 s, 1 week]`,
  defaulting to the shared 60 s tick; scheduling stays stateless deterministic bucketing (pod-safe, no
  durable per-trigger state). "Collect now" is NOT a plain manual run (a collect's "run" is a poll):
  new `enqueue_collect_now` + `POST /automations/{name}/collect` enqueue one immediate poll, bypassing
  the cadence bucket. *Open remainder:* the web "Collect now" button.
- **Multi-user settings split** (§18) — *resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31): per-user preferences
  (theme, timezone, models/voices, personal search + files defaults) stay full-depth for everyone
  in every mode; operational/diagnostic views (LLM gateway, Status) and API-keys chrome collapse
  for a *positively-detected* non-admin member in `multi_user` (`settings_tabs_for(mode, role)`);
  admins and `single_user` always see everything. Server-side, the mode-independent fixes landed:
  external-DB connection and storage-store *lifecycle* writes now require workspace admin.
  *Still open:* admin re-exposure of individual knobs (no config surface for it yet).
- **Sole-user caches** (§18) — *resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31): only the **profile snapshot** is
  safely cacheable — recall embeds the *current message* (inherently per-message, never cached), and
  no static memory injection exists, so memory writes can't stale anything. Implemented as a
  mode-gated generation-counter cache (`PersonalizationCache`: bump on profile writes, 5-min TTL
  backstop, race-safe fills, `multi_user` never consults); the mode-flip invalidation story is that
  a flip is a restart and the fresh process never reads the process-local cache. Prewarm skipped
  (first read warms; no clean sole-user id at boot). *Remainder:* the chat hot path in reserved
  `routes/ws.rs` still reads the profile directly — a one-line `cached_profile` adoption when free.
- **Organisation backfill** (§18) — existing deployments hold workspaces with no organisation:
  migrate them all into the seeded default org, or offer a per-workspace choice at migration
  time? And does org membership auto-derive from workspace membership on backfill?
- **Per-App durable state** (§12) — *store half resolved 2026-07-02* (see §31): a dedicated store
  IS warranted — the "objects + files + external Postgres cover it" claim was aspirational (no
  generic file-write tool existed in the registry at the time — `write_object` has since landed
  with the §11 object actions; notes/tasks/memories are mis-shaped and
  pollute their indexes; external Postgres is admin-heavy and per-connection, not per-App). Built:
  `app_data (workspace_id, app, key) → JSONB` (migration 0051, 64 KiB/value + 1000 keys/app caps)
  + `app_data_get/set/list/delete` tools (`ui:read`/`ui:write`), on the default `handler_tools`
  list; from an App handler the namespace is **forced to the fired UI's id** (`ToolContext.ui_id`,
  spoof-proof), from chat/automation the caller names the app id — which also answers the binding
  sub-question *for app_data*: resolved per handler call from context, not pinned in the spec.
  *Still open:* bucket / external-DB binding declaration (pinned vs per-call) for Apps that
  outgrow the KV; per-user isolation within one App is key-convention only.

## 30. Backup & restore (`catalerum-backup`)

catalerum's **recoverable state is exactly two things**: the **Postgres** source
of truth (§6.1) and the **object blobs** in the storage backend (§9) — the bucket
bytes that deliberately never live in the DB (§14). Everything else is *derived*:
**Neo4j** (graph, §6.3) and **Qdrant** (vectors, §6.4) rebuild from Postgres, and
**Valkey** (§6.6) is ephemeral. So a backup captures Postgres + blobs and nothing
else; a restore reloads those two and **re-ingest rebuilds the derived stores**.

**Destination = a second `StorageBackend` (§9).** A backup is written through the
same trait the live storage layer uses, so the target is an **S3/MinIO bucket, a
WebDAV collection, or a local directory** — "back up to S3" is just pointing
`[backup.destination]` at a *different* backend than `[storage]`, so the backup
survives the loss of the primary. One abstraction, two uses: the
`build_storage_backend` builder is shared by the live store and the backup target.

**Artifact.** Each run writes `<prefix>/<backup-id>/` (the id is a UTC timestamp,
so listings sort chronologically):
```
manifest.json              # format + schema version, timestamp, per-table column-list/row-count/sha-256, object inventory
postgres/<table>.copy.gz   # one gzipped `COPY … TO STDOUT` (text format) per table
objects/<store>/<workspace-key>  # a verbatim copy of every live blob, per source store (when include_objects)
```

**The Postgres dump is pure-Rust — no `pg_dump`.** It streams `COPY <table> TO
STDOUT` for every `public` base table over the sqlx COPY protocol, so it needs no
external binary on the host and is testable against the same ephemeral Postgres the
repo tests use (§17). The manifest records each table's column list (used verbatim
on restore, so a column reorder can't misalign the load), row count, and the
sha-256 of its compressed dump.

**Restore is destructive and fail-safe.** It reloads on a single connection inside
one transaction with foreign-key triggers disabled
(`session_replication_role = replica`): truncate every table, then `COPY … FROM
STDIN` each from its **checksum-verified** dump. FK checks are off, so load order is
irrelevant; the schema must merely already exist (the binary migrates on boot,
§6.1). Restore **refuses a `schema_version` mismatch** unless forced — data never
loads into a schema it was not dumped from — and a checksum mismatch aborts the run.
A failure rolls the transaction back, so the live DB is never left half-loaded.

**Two ways to run it.** A scheduled `BackupWorker` (a §11-style clock loop) runs
`backup + prune` every `[backup].interval`, **single-firing each window across
pods** via the bus lock (§6.2) and retaining the newest `[backup].keep`. The
on-demand subcommands run the identical engine: `catalerum backup` takes one now;
`catalerum restore` lists backups (no id) or restores one
(`<id> --yes`, `--force` to override the schema guard).

**Config (`[backup]`, §13).** `enabled` (default off) gates only the scheduled
worker — the subcommands work whenever a destination is set. `interval_secs`
(default 24 h, floored to 60 s), `prefix` (default `backups`), `keep` (default 7;
0 = keep all), `include_objects` (default true; false → Postgres-only), and
`destination` — a full storage-backend block (local / `s3` / `webdav`) whose
secrets are injected via the environment
(`CATALERUM_BACKUP__DESTINATION__S3__SECRET_KEY=…`) like every other credential,
never the committed TOML.

**Non-goals / later.** Incremental or content-addressed blob dedup (today a full
copy each run); streaming compression (tables buffer in memory, mirroring the
storage backends' whole-object buffering, §9); point-in-time / WAL-continuous
recovery (this is logical, snapshot-granular); auto-rebuilding the derived stores
on restore (today: re-ingest); and artifact-level encryption beyond what the
destination provides (an SSE-enabled S3 bucket) until a backup envelope lands.

A live run forwarded `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, set `CATALERUM_LLM__DEFAULT_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, and exposed a topology bug: `PUT /llmleaf/routes/deepseek%2Fdeepseek-v4-pro` returned 404 because route names were constrained to one Axum path segment. new `mcp_endpoint_tokens` table, migration 0068 + SQLite mirror 0004) so they are individually revocable (`GET`/`DELETE /mcp-endpoints/{id}/tokens[/{token_id}]`) and die with their endpoint — the `/mcp/s/{token}` serve path now requires a live row in addition to a valid HMAC, 404ing identically either way. **(2) `POST /mcp/e/{name}` no longer lets a caller ride an endpoint's authority:** the endpoint's capability set is intersected with the caller's effective authority (`intersect_caps` — an endpoint cap survives only if some caller cap covers it); an empty intersection fails closed with 403, so a Viewer invoking a write-pinned endpoint is refused. **(3) Session tokens out of URLs:** the magic-link and SSO browser flows now redirect with a short-lived (5-minute, `HANDOFF_TOKEN_TTL`) one-time `?code=` handoff the SPA exchanges over `POST /auth/exchange` for the real bearer (new iam `consume_login_token` + `issue_login_token_with_ttl`; the request-tracing span redacts `token`/`access_token`/`code` query values so credentials never land in logs/traces. **(4) CORS** is a config-driven allow-list (`[server].web_url` + new `[server].cors_extra_origins`, env `CATALERUM_SERVER__CORS_EXTRA_ORIGINS`) with the methods/headers the SPA uses and no credentials, replacing `CorsLayer::very_permissive()`. **(6) Server-side logout:** `POST /auth/logout` revokes the very session the request authenticated with (the `Auth` extractor now carries the raw token). **(9) LLM-quota endpoints gated:** `POST /ocr` requires `storage:write`, `POST /audio/transcriptions` and `GET /ws/speech` require `conversation:write` — a Viewer or empty grant-scoped token can no longer spend provider quota. **Drive-by pre-existing fixes (all verified broken on the clean tree first):** the justfile `NEO4J_URL` default was `bolt://localhost:7687` while every graph consumer expects the HTTP endpoint — now `http://localhost:7474` (fixes 63 `just test` failures); _2026-07-19 — **Chat now follows live tool-heavy and emerged-UI turns without stealing the reader's scroll position** (SOUL §7/§12) — the transcript previously kept its old `scrollTop` while streamed prose, tool cards, and inline App-authoring artifacts extended the log, leaving the composer visible but the newest work below the fold (the recipe-App run was visibly stranded at “Now building…” although later `present_ui`/`edit_ui` rounds had landed). `ChatPanel` now tracks whether the log is within a small rounding/touch slop of its bottom, coalesces reactive line growth into one `requestAnimationFrame` scroll per paint, and follows only while that state remains true. Strict API all-target clippy reaches the change cleanly and remains blocked solely by the pre-existing unrelated `unnecessary_sort_by` warning in `tools.rs:734`._

_2026-07-15 — **Emerged-App authoring now self-corrects the exact failure chain from the Asian-recipe App transcript (SOUL §7/§12/§27; user ask).** The standing UI guidance now requires `explain_ui_schema` before focused lookup, forbids guessed component kinds and unchanged error retries, and tells the model to carry `present_ui.ui_id` (or the stable name) into every later authoring call. Staged Apps also gained the previously missing `set_initial_state {state,merge?}` patch, so recipe arrays and other seed data can be added before state-bound components without falling back to one giant definition. Web-research guidance and the `web_search`/`fetch_url` descriptions now steer agents toward one focused 3–5-result search, non-overlapping batches, and fetching only selected pages; `web_search` advertises and enforces a four-query context bound, while sourced App content is directed to link/attribute and summarize rather than reproduce whole pages. Finally, the shared LLM loop performs one bounded recovery turn when a provider cleanly stops with an empty answer, preventing the blank post-research response seen in the transcript. **Verified:** focused core/API/LLM/search/fetch regressions green (initial-state replace+merge JSON round-trip, component enum exclusions, target constraint/error/handoff coverage, standing guidance, bounded-search schema/runtime behavior, fetch guidance, and empty-finish recovery); workspace formatting and diff checks green. _2026-07-15 — **Purpose-built subagent tool calls can select a named agent profile instead of being locked to the workspace default model (SOUL §7/§19/§20; user ask).** `computer_subagent`, legacy-compatible `computer_agent_task`, and `terminal_subagent` now accept optional `profile` names. The constrained child keeps its machine-pinned or no-egress-terminal registry, while adopting the profile's model, system prompt, skill runbooks, explicit tool allow-list, programmable guard, dry-run posture, and cost ceiling.
