Terminal's mandatory PR/story Boa boundary and the profile guard are composed so both must allow every child call/output, and launcher infrastructure tools (`upstream`, plus terminal `finish_work`) remain available through an otherwise restricted profile. Calls without `profile` retain the previous default-model behavior, including background lifecycle handling. **Verified:** full API lib suite **518 green**, including schema regressions for all three launchers and a composed-gate regression; `cargo check -p catalerum-api`, targeted subagent/profile/gate suites, workspace formatting, and diff checks green. Strict API all-target clippy reaches the changed code cleanly and remains blocked only by the pre-existing unrelated `clippy::unnecessary_sort_by` finding in `tools.rs:734`._

_2026-07-15 — **Apps can now be created and edited component-by-component instead of passing gigantic JSON definitions through whole-App calls (SOUL §12; user asks).** `present_ui` accepts a title without `definition` and creates a valid minimal `main`/`root` shell. `create_ui_components` attaches ordered `{parent_id,index?,node}` subtrees by app id or name, so later entries may nest below earlier ones and agents can build one logical section per call. The symmetric `edit_ui_components` replaces ordered `{node_id,node}` subtrees after a scoped `read_ui {node_id}`; it is the whole-logical-component path, while `edit_ui` remains for tiny property/event changes and structural remove/move operations. Both component tools apply their closed `UiPatchOp` operations to a working clone, validate the complete resulting `UiSpec` under the handler-tool allow-list, and persist once with optimistic versioning — an invalid child, duplicate id, or missing edit target leaves no partial changes. Re-presenting an existing named shell without a definition is metadata-only and cannot wipe assembled components; full-definition creation remains compatible. The standing agent prompt and focused UI schema teach the staged workflow. Live artifact streaming, transcript replay, and tool-card suppression recognize all four authoring tools, so component creation and edits refresh the mounted App rather than rendering as generic JSON. **Verified:** API lib suite **515 green**, including the database-backed staged create/edit nesting, atomic rollback, and no-reset regression; web suite **375 green**, including explicit authoring-tool mount/card classification; API all-target check, web wasm clippy `-D warnings`, API all-target clippy with only the pre-existing `unnecessary_sort_by` finding at `tools.rs:729` allowed, workspace formatting, and diff checks green. The unmodified strict API clippy gate remains blocked solely by that already-documented unrelated warning._

_2026-07-15 — **Hands-free conversation speech now has an explicit one-block-ahead synthesis pipeline (SOUL §7/§12; user ask).** While block N is being read aloud, the browser synthesizes completed block N+1 over the held-open speech socket; it waits for N to finish before starting N+1 and before requesting N+2, so an already-buffered reply cannot fan out synthesis for every later block. The scheduling rule moved into `voice::pump_one_ahead`, while the existing generation/mute/pause/error checks remain at the browser-operation boundaries. **Verified:** full web suite **374 green**, including a deterministic pipeline test that stalls playback and proves the event order `prepare 1 → play 1 → prepare 2`, with no `prepare 3` until clip 1 ends and clip 2 starts; wasm clippy `-D warnings` and diff checks green. Audible provider behavior still requires a configured TTS model and browser audio output._

_2026-07-15 — **Automation execution now has an explicit ports-and-adapters microarchitecture (SOUL §3/§5/§11; user ask).** The backend is divided into control (Leptos/REST/authoring + Postgres definitions), dispatch (trigger matching + durable jobs), and execution planes. A storage-neutral `AutomationEngine` now owns graph/linear orchestration behind three narrow ports: `ExecutionState` (run journal + snapshotted-grant resolution), `ActionRunner` (typed capability-gated effects), and `CodeRunner` (sandboxed code). Direct repository calls were removed from the engine algorithm and isolated in the feature-gated `PostgresExecutionState`; `--no-default-features` removes the store dependency completely, while default compatibility entry points preserve existing worker/API callers and not-found semantics. The architecture contract is documented in `docs/automation-architecture.md`, and an in-memory state adapter proves a complete automation run needs neither Postgres nor frontend/API code. **Verified:** all 97 automation tests green (85 unit + 12 DB-gated integration cases; DB cases self-skip without a URL), native checks for automation/ingest/API/binary green, storage-free build green, targeted automation + ingest all-target clippy `-D warnings` green. The broader API clippy gate reaches the change cleanly but remains blocked by the pre-existing `clippy::unnecessary_sort_by` finding in untouched `tools.rs:721`._

_2026-07-14 — **`run_javascript` is advertised to models by default (SOUL §7/§11; user ask).** The shared deferred-advertising seed now includes the ungated Boa sandbox alongside `search_tools` and `list_tools`, so ordinary chat, unpinned profiles, LLM-agent actions, and skill-agent runs can use exact computation and JSON/string shaping immediately without spending a discovery round first. _2026-07-14 — **`delegate`, `computer_subagent`, and `terminal_subagent` can run in the background under parent lifecycle control (SOUL §7/§19/§20; user asks).** All three launch tools accept `background=true` and immediately return a UUID run handle instead of holding the parent tool call open; `delegate` supports this in both named-profile and ephemeral-worker modes without changing its authority attenuation or one-level recursion boundary. A shared pod-local manager bounds execution to eight concurrent workers and retains at most 256 run records, queues excess work without unbounded task execution, catches panics, and publishes race-safe `queued → running → completed|failed` / `stopping → stopped` snapshots through Tokio watch channels without holding the run-map lock across an await. Three parent tools operate on those handles: `monitor_subagent` inspects one result or lists owned runs (including `kind=delegate`), `wait_subagent` waits up to a caller-selected bounded 600 seconds and returns current state on timeout, and `stop_subagent` cooperatively cancels queued/running work. Handles are scoped to the exact workspace, user/agent, grant, conversation, and emerged-UI origin; a mismatched caller gets not-found rather than run disclosure. Cancellation is wired into every child LLM agent loop and checked by computer/terminal upstream bridges; terminal cancellation forces a not-met verdict, prevents finalization from starting, and makes the Boa finalizer host refuse any new parent calls after stop. Terminal children cannot request lifecycle controls through their own upstream allow-list. `delegate`'s standing prompt, deferred-discovery seed, and explicit profile tool allow-lists always include the three lifecycle controls; interactive turns reuse AppState's manager across later turns in the same conversation, while headless profile parents receive an isolated run-local manager and matching derived control tools. Foreground behavior remains the default. The manager is deliberately in-process/pod-local: records do not survive API restart and control calls must retain pod affinity. **Verified:** full API lib suite **508 green** (including four manager lifecycle/stop/race/ownership tests, delegate support-advertising coverage, and cancellation-aware delegate/computer/terminal regressions), API all-target clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace formatting, and diff checks green._

_2026-07-14 — **`open_terminal` → `terminal_subagent`: a no-egress coding worker whose PR/story access is parameter-inspected by the same Boa guard engine as profiles, with publish-after-goal finalization (SOUL §7/§11/§19/§20; user ask + clarification).** The intended orchestration is explicit: the parent acquires a work item from its central repository, gathers information, creates the PR, opens a terminal and stages/copies the repository/repositories, then calls the newly advertised `terminal_subagent` on that existing `session_id`. Admission requires an **OS-level no-egress boundary** — per-session Podman/Docker only when `podman.network=none`, or a shared workspace sandbox with `sandbox_network=none|isolated`; local/lightweight-sandbox, networked container, and per-session K8s terminals fail closed with a setup fix. This is the hard boundary that prevents an arbitrary PTY command from pushing before review. The child gets a fresh seven-tool registry: five terminal operations (`terminal_write/read`, `read_file`, `create_file`, `edit_file`) forcibly pinned to the prepared session (the `session_id` parameter is removed and any injected value overwritten), a single `upstream` proxy, and `finish_work`; no open/list/close/stage/store/persist, discovery, storage, MCP, generic delegation, or parent tool specs. `upstream_tools` is a parent-selected static name allow-list (framework/exec/computer/terminal escape tools are rejected), and the child requests one as `{tool, arguments}`. On top, the existing **`ProfileToolGate`** now optionally binds immutable `input.policy_context` into each review; `terminal_subagent.guard_script` is a profile-format Boa body (allow/deny/ask, fail-closed) run on **both call and output phases**, seeing `input.phase`, tool name/description/capability, the complete `input.args` (therefore the nested upstream tool + its exact PR/story ids/fields), `input.output`, principal ids, and the unforgeable parent scope (normally `{pull_request:{id,...},user_story:{id,...}}`). Its own lookup registry is empty so policy code cannot bypass `upstream` through `callTool`; `classifyWithLlm` remains available. An allowed upstream request re-dispatches through the parent's exact per-run registry/context, applying the parent's capabilities, guard, dry-run, and approval flow again. Completion is structured, not inferred from prose: `finish_work` accepts exactly one `{goal_met,analysis,evidence[],summary}` with non-empty evidence; no call means not-met. Only `goal_met=true` runs the bounded parent-authored `finalize_code` Boa handler, which receives the verdict/scope/session/final child content and may call parent tools to update the PR/story and publish; recursion is blocked, original parent authorization remains active, and the returned `pushed_upstream` is true only when the finalizer succeeds and explicitly returns `{pushed:true}`. No mutex is held across the awaited child/finalizer and no detached task outlives the tool call. `open_terminal` now explicitly advertises `terminal_subagent` after staging. **Verified:** full API lib suite **503 green**, including terminal tests **16** (exact child surface + pin override/schema, upstream name allow-list, explicit backend isolation tokens, one-shot evidence verdict, publish-result truth table, and the existing terminal/file/sandbox/cross-pod suite) and profile-gate tests **9** (new Boa regression compares nested attempted PR args with immutable policy context: correct PR allow, wrong PR deny); API all-target clippy `-D warnings`, formatting, and diff checks green. Live LLM/provider + real central-repository publication is not exercised here because provider tool names/contracts are deployment-defined; the orchestration/finalizer deliberately consumes those exact registered tools rather than hard-coding GitHub/GitLab/Jira._

_2026-07-14 — **`computer_subagent`: a machine-pinned child with a parent-mediated Boa `upstream` boundary (SOUL §7/§11/§19/§20; user ask).** The new `computer_subagent` tool resolves one enrolled machine, then runs a fresh LLM context against a newly built registry containing only eight direct computer controls plus one dynamically defined `upstream` tool — no workspace discovery, storage, memory, search, MCP, generic delegation, or other parent tools are advertised. Every computer wrapper forcibly overwrites `agent` with the parent-selected host and removes that parameter from its child-facing schema, so prompt drift cannot redirect the worker to another enrolled machine. The orchestration chat supplies `upstream_code` (a bounded Boa function body), an optional child-facing contract, and optional private JSON context; each child `upstream({request})` call evaluates the handler with `{request, context}`, and only its return value crosses back. The handler alone may use `catalerum.callTool` to re-dispatch through the parent's exact per-run registry and original context, preserving capability checks, programmable guards, dry-run simulation, conversation approvals, and dynamic/per-profile tool surfaces. The child never receives those specs or calls them directly. The bridge fails closed without a dispatching parent registry / from emerged-UI context, caps source at 64 KiB, uses the existing loop/recursion/stack limits plus a 60 s I/O backstop, and rejects `run_javascript`, `computer_subagent`, and legacy `computer_agent_task` nested calls to prevent Boa/subagent recursion tunnels. The existing `computer_agent_task` remains registered for compatibility. **Verified:** targeted API unit tests green (5 total: restricted exact registry + host pinning/schema, private-context Boa transform, authorized parent redispatch, recursive-tunnel refusal, existing timeout/policy parsing); `cargo check -p catalerum-api` and API all-target clippy `-D warnings` green; workspace formatting and diff checks clean apart from preserved pre-existing telemetry/SOUL worktree changes._

_2026-07-13 — **OpenTelemetry tracing + optional native Langfuse export landed (SOUL §7/§13; user ask).** The binary now upgrades the existing `tracing` subscriber into an OTLP/HTTP protobuf pipeline with configurable `service.name` and head-sampling ratio, W3C `traceparent` extraction on inbound Axum requests, resource/version attributes, batched export, and flush-on-graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown. A vendor-neutral `[telemetry.otlp]` destination and direct `[telemetry.langfuse]` destination can run alone or together; Langfuse uses its `/api/public/otel` base endpoint, Basic auth from redacted public/secret-key config, and ingestion version 4. Streaming llmleaf calls emit generation spans with OpenTelemetry GenAI plus Langfuse-native attributes (model/settings, finish reason, token/cache usage, cost, errors, and optional input/output/reasoning/tool payloads). Each destination has an independent privacy policy: `metadata-only` (safe default), `all-except-system-prompts` (removes every system-role message before serialization), or `everything`; a single SDK provider plus target-filtering exporters prevents the two policy-specific generation spans crossing destinations while retaining the same ordinary HTTP/application trace in both. Config-file examples, env overrides, and README operations/privacy guidance are included; invalid sampling, endpoint, or enabled-Langfuse credential config fails loudly at boot. **Verified:** targeted LLM redaction and telemetry config/routing/validation tests green; `cargo check -p catalerum`; and all-target clippy `-D warnings` for `catalerum-llm`, `catalerum-api`, and the binary green. Langfuse mapping follows its current native OTEL documentation (OTLP/HTTP only; `/v1/traces` appended by the exporter)._

_2026-07-13 — **`computer_search` is substantially faster on large directory trees (SOUL §19/§20; user ask: “fix the speed of the computer search, it is really, really slow”).** Root cause was entirely in the installed daemon's search hot path: one task serially walked every entry, read each eligible file into a fresh whole-file `String`, then allocated a second lowercased `String` for every filename and every line. The daemon now compiles one shared matcher (plain queries are escaped case-insensitive literals, regex queries remain verbatim), removes overlapping granted roots so a nested grant cannot make the same tree scan twice, splits roots into independent subtrees, and searches them with a bounded pool of up to eight scoped workers. Files are streamed through reusable 64 KiB buffered readers instead of whole-file allocations. A shared atomic deadline/result budget preserves the operation's global timeout and match cap across workers; hidden-directory pruning, name + content hits, line/snippet fields, file-size ceiling, and the wire response are unchanged. **Verified:** `cargo test -p catalerum-agent --bin catalerum-agent` 12 green, including a new multi-subtree regression proving the workers enforce one exact global result cap; agent all-target clippy `-D warnings` green; workspace-wide `cargo fmt` and `git diff --check` clean._

_2026-07-13 — **Tool-only chat rounds no longer render an empty prose segment above their tool cards (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: “fix some empty segments before tool calls”).** Chat rows now render the `.msg-text` bubble only when they contain actual prose, or while an otherwise-empty assistant row is still the initial waiting placeholder. As soon as a live tool card or emerged UI becomes the row's visible output, the placeholder disappears; persisted/replayed tool-only rounds follow the same rule. The assistant role label, tool cards, narration that genuinely precedes a call, and the pre-first-token streaming cursor are unchanged. **Verified:** `cargo test -p catalerum-web` 369 green (two new regression tests covering replay/live suppression and intentional waiting-placeholder retention); wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean; targeted `rustfmt --check` + `git diff --check` clean. The workspace-wide `cargo fmt --check` remains blocked by a pre-existing formatting diff in `crates/catalerum-api/src/tools/skills.rs`, unrelated and untouched._

_2026-07-13 — **Dictation + hands-free conversation can time-compress microphone input before STT, defaulting to 1.5×, with a per-user setting (SOUL §7/§12/§13; user ask: “in tts and conversation mode can we speed up input voice 1.5x to save on costs? also expose this as a setting”).** Both 🎙 composer dictation and 🎧 conversation already share one `MediaRecorder` handoff; that handoff now decodes the browser recording through Web Audio, linearly resamples it to `duration / voice_input_speed`, down-mixes to mono, writes a self-describing PCM16 WAV, and uploads those genuinely shorter bytes to `/audio/transcriptions` (a playback flag alone would not change provider-visible duration). Browser decode failure degrades to the untouched original take rather than losing speech. `llm_settings.voice_input_speed` is a migration-backed per-user `REAL` constrained to 1.0–2.0, defaults to 1.5 for new/legacy rows and request bodies, is validated at the API, and appears beside the transcription model in Settings with the duration-billing/accuracy trade-off disclosed. The chat loads it independently of capability probes; 1.0 disables processing. Assistant TTS output is deliberately unchanged: this setting controls microphone input shared by dictation and conversation. **Verified:** web 371 tests green (new duration/down-mix + WAV framing coverage); API settings 5 + store settings focused tests green; native core/store/API all-target clippy `-D warnings` green; wasm web clippy `-D warnings` green; production `trunk build` green; `git diff --check` clean. **Not machine-verified (disclosed):** microphone capture + provider transcription needs a real browser/mic/STT model; the dev echo gateway has none. **Cost caveat:** savings apply only when the chosen STT provider bills by submitted audio duration; byte-, request-, or fixed-price billing may not change.

_2026-07-13 — **Chat speech controls no longer pop into the composer late (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: “fix TTS/conversation buttons — they take too long to decide whether they should be visible”).** The dictation 🎙 and hands-free 🎧 controls now render in their final layout slots on first paint instead of treating an unresolved model-catalog request as “feature absent”; they are disabled with an `aria-busy`/checking tooltip until the relevant capability is known, and remain visibly disabled with a useful tooltip when STT or TTS is unavailable. STT and TTS catalog probes now run as two independent tasks (maximum of the two request times for 🎧, rather than their sum), and successful answers are cached for the page lifetime so navigating away from and back to Chat keeps already-known controls ready while revalidating in the background. The capability gate still protects every click: dictation needs STT, conversation needs both STT and TTS. **Verified:** `cargo test -p catalerum-web` 367 green (new tri-state capability regression test); full `just lint` green (native + wasm `-D warnings`); production `trunk build` green; `git diff --check` clean.

_2026-07-12 — **Chat + hands-free conversation transport hardened for spotty mobile networks (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: fix resiliency findings 1–8).** The browser now mints stable conversation and user-message UUIDs; conversation creation is idempotent in Postgres (`ConversationRepo::create_with_id`), every ordinary/queued/approval turn reuses its client message id, duplicate live turns attach to the existing Valkey buffer, and duplicate persisted turns acknowledge/replay without invoking the model or injecting queued text twice. A localStorage outbox retains unacknowledged turns across reloads, restores a client-minted conversation after a lost create response, removes entries only on the persisted-user ack, and serially replays leftovers on reconnect. The chat WebSocket now gets direct 10 s server heartbeats; the client treats 25 s silence as half-open, polls `navigator.onLine`, retries with longer capped backoff and an `online` wake-up, resends unacknowledged frames safely, re-sends Stop/queued commands after reconnect, and keeps the highest replay cursor outside each disposable socket (so a second drop before its first frame cannot regress to replay-from-zero). Transcript loads carry a generation fence (a slow A response cannot overwrite newly-opened B); lost/expired turn buffers send `message_done {reconcile:true}`, and both that terminal and exhausted/error recovery replace partial UI state from durable Postgres/outbox state. Approval decisions gained stable retry coordinates, so an ack-loss replays their original turn instead of double-resolving or hanging. Voice STT now keeps each raw recording + completed result in Valkey for 5 minutes under a client request id; retries first retrieve the result, otherwise regenerate transcription from cached audio, re-upload only after a cache miss, and a distributed lock prevents concurrent provider work. The browser retains the original bytes through eight connectivity-aware retries and gives each upload a 20 s request timeout. **Verified:** full web suite 366 green; API audio 4 + WS 22 focused tests green; live-Postgres idempotent conversation test green (including cross-workspace denial); native API/store and wasm web clippy `-D warnings` green; `git diff --check` clean. **Deferred:** Playwright cellular fault injection (WS black-hole/lost-ack/multi-drop) remains desirable; the server-side STT cache cannot help until at least one upload reaches the API, so the browser remains the pre-acceptance copy by design._

_2026-07-12 — **The chat system prompt advertises the workspace's skills (name + description), with a per-skill "visible to agent" opt-out that defaults to on (SOUL §23/§12; user ask: "add skill name + description in system prompt of chat. Add option in skills for this (visible to agent) which is true by default").** Before, the model only discovered skills via a `list_skills` round-trip (or a user's explicit `/<skill>`), so a saved runbook that matched the request usually went unused. Now every chat turn's ephemeral seed prefix carries a "Skills available in this workspace" block — one `- name: description` line per skill (bare name when the description is blank) pointing at `use_skill` — built by `skills_system_prompt` in `ws.rs`, inserted right behind the profile persona, injected nothing when nothing is advertised. The block is **double-filtered**: a new `skills.advertised` column (migration 0062, `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE` — additive-safe, existing skills stay visible) read via the lean `SkillRepo::list_advertised` (`(name, description)` only — no runbooks/code dragged through every turn), then the same per-skill `skill:use@<name>` capability check `use_skill` enforces, against the turn's effective authority (profile grant ∩ user role when bound, else the user's own) — so the prompt never dangles a skill the agent would then be denied. A store failure skips the block rather than failing the turn. The flag rides the whole stack: core `Skill.advertised` (serde `default_true` for old JSON), `NewSkill`, create/upsert (+ `advertised = EXCLUDED.advertised`), REST `CreateSkill`/`UpdateSkill` bodies (serde-default true), the `create_skill`/`edit_skill` LLM tools (create defaults true; edit keeps-when-omitted like its other fields; `skill_summary` + `list_skills` echo it), and the web Skills panel — a "Visible to agent" checkbox in the form's Basics group (new shared-pattern `.skills-check`), a muted "Hidden from the agent" note on the read view, wired through populate/clear/dirty-check/save; the onboarding skill-draft persist sends `advertised: true` explicitly. First-party fixtures advertise. **Verified:** full `just lint` green (native + wasm `-D warnings`); native workspace suite green against live Postgres incl. the DB-gated `skills_repo` test extended to cover the flag's upsert round-trip + `list_advertised` filtering, new REST-body serde tests (default-true / opt-out / omitted-on-update), and `skills_prompt_lists_names_with_optional_descriptions_or_nothing`. **Not machine-verified (disclosed):** `cargo test -p catalerum-web` (native) currently fails on **pre-existing uncommitted WIP** in `chat.rs`/`api.rs` (`StreamUpdate::Done.reconcile`, a moved `content`) unrelated to this change — wasm clippy covers the web edits. **Deferred:** headless/`run_agent` and channel-profile runs don't get the block (profiles already embed their named skills' full runbooks); a profile's embedded skills also appear in the ad list (harmless duplication); no web toggle surfaced in the skills *list* rows (detail view only)._

_2026-07-12 — **Chat sidebar "Debug" section: copy the whole conversation as JSON so a broken thread can be handed to an AI model or pasted into a bug report (SOUL §12; user ask: "in chat sidebar add debug section for e.g. copying chat as json so e.g. an ai model can look over that and fix issues").** The right panel's Settings tab gained a Debug field (shown only once the thread exists server-side — a brand-new chat has nothing to dump) with a "Copy chat as JSON" button: it fetches `GET /conversations/{id}/messages` and puts the body on the clipboard **verbatim** (pretty-printed via `serde_json::Value`, deliberately *not* decoded into the web `Message` type, so every persisted field — roles, tool calls + results, `tool_is_error`, durations, token usage, attachments, even fields this client doesn't model — survives the export). `rest.rs` factored the raw-body half out of `get_json` into `get_body` and added `conversation_debug_json` on top; chat.rs mirrors `widgets::copy_button`'s "Copied ✓" flash by hand (the shared widget reads its text synchronously at click time; this one fetches async first) with in-flight disable and an inline `chat-set-error` on fetch failure. Fetch-then-copy rides the click's transient user activation, same silent-failure contract as every other `copy_to_clipboard` caller. **Verified:** wasm clippy `-D warnings` green; driven live headless against `just dev` + trunk — existing thread: click → "Copied ✓" flash → reverts, clipboard received a pretty-printed 2-message JSON array with full fields (writeText intercepted in-page); API down: inline "network error…" rendered, cleared on the next successful copy; new chat: section absent. (Verification re-confirmed the repo-root-playwright-artifacts→cargo-watch-restart trap — twice.)_

_2026-07-12 — **`run_javascript` can now call other tools: `catalerum.callTool(name, args)` inside the Boa sandbox re-dispatches through the full §19 authorization chain (SOUL §7/§11/§19; user ask: "allow boa sandbox tool call to call other tool calls, but still with the whole authorization system like normal tools").** The LLM's `run_javascript` tool was a deliberately pure compute scratchpad (`eval_pure`, zero host functions); scripts can now chain/loop/aggregate registry tools with exact logic. **Mechanism — the dispatching registry rides the context:** `ToolContext` gained `registry: Option<ToolRegistry>`, injected by `ToolRegistry::dispatch` itself right before `tool.invoke` (never set by callers; `Debug` prints presence only). This means a nested call re-dispatches against the **caller's exact tool surface** — per-run derived registries included (a chat/profile run's `registry_with_delegate` clone, the computer subagent registry), not a boot-time snapshot — and under the **caller's own context**, so every nested call passes the identical deny-by-default capability check, programmable tool guard (a Defer hands the script the same `awaiting_approval` stand-in the model would see), and §19 `dry_run` simulation a directly-issued call would. The tool itself stays **ungated**: it confers no authority of its own; a script wields only what its caller already holds. `catalerum-script` gained the thin public `eval_with_host(source, input, host)` (eval_pure + the existing `UiScriptHost`/`UI_HOST`/`native_call_tool` bridge, code-node calling convention — no UI envelope); the per-invocation host (`JsToolHost` in `tools/run_code.rs`) is `Handle::current().block_on(registry.dispatch(…))` on the eval's `spawn_blocking` thread (the automation code-node pattern). **Fail-closed edges:** the host refuses `run_javascript` itself (no Boa-in-Boa recursion stacking blocking threads — a script defines a plain JS function instead); a context carrying `ui_id` gets **no** bridge at all (an emerged-UI handler's `[ui].handler_tools` allow-list is enforced at its own `callTool` entry (§12) and must not be tunnelled through this tool — noted on `UiConfig`; `run_javascript` isn't on the default list anyway); a direct `invoke` without a dispatching registry (unit tests, embedded contexts) stays the pure transform. Registration bumps the wall-clock backstop 5s→60s to leave room for nested tool I/O (runaway JS is still cut by the loop/recursion/stack limits); tool description + `code` param teach the model the bridge. MCP-endpoint scripts stay confined (their host allow-lists `search_semantic` only); guard-script `callTool` keeps its deliberate `gate: None` re-entrancy. **Verified:** `just lint` green (native + wasm `-D warnings`); full native suite vs live Postgres green (117 result groups, 0 fail) incl. new tests — core `dispatch_injects_its_registry_into_the_invoke_context`, script `eval_with_host_bridges_call_tool_with_code_node_convention`, api `run_javascript_call_tool_redispatches_under_caller_authority` (nested chain + capability denial catchable in-script) and `run_javascript_nested_bridge_fails_closed` (self-recursion refused · `ui_id` pure · no-registry pure); **live e2e** over `POST /mcp` `tools/call` against `just dev` — a script created a note via nested `create_note`, listed it back (`saw: true`), self-recursion refused with the exact message, and nested `run_command` matched the same bearer's direct-call authority exactly (the dev token holds `exec:run` — parity, not escalation). **Deferred (disclosed):** the seven exhaustive `ToolContext` literal sites gained `registry: None` (dispatch overwrites; a future constructor could centralize); a gate Defer inside a script returns the stand-in marker mid-run (the approved re-run later executes standalone — the script has moved on); nested calls of a *pinned* profile can reach capability-covered tools outside its advertised pin (same standing decision as automation code nodes: the capability cap is the gate, advertising is not authority)._

_2026-07-11 — **`collect_sql` trigger: automations fire on new INSERTs in external-DB tables matched by a wildcard, closing the "emerged App writes a row → automation reacts" loop (SOUL §11/§12/§19; user ask: "automations based on new inserts in the external dbs on wildcard matched tables; make it possible to insert entries there via emerged ui apps and automate stuff based on that").** The **write half already existed** — `sql_query` runs INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (`db:write@<conn>`, mode=write), is on the default `[ui].handler_tools` allow-list, declares no confirm-capability, and Member's base set holds domain-wide `db:read`/`db:write` — so an App's `tool`/`script` handler can INSERT today; `get_ui_schema` gained an `external_db` section documenting the $1/$2-placeholder pattern and the trigger pairing. The **new trigger** is the third Collect head: `Trigger::CollectSql { connection, tables, cursor_column?, commit_on?, every? }` rides every existing collect seam unchanged (`is_collect`/`collect_connection`/`collect_every`/`commit_on` arms → the scheduler's `scan_collect_triggers`, `enqueue_collect` (new job kind `collect_sql`), `enqueue_collect_now`, the worker's per-connection collect mutex, the exactly-one-trigger graph rule, and the flow editor's `commit` port). `ingest/collect_sql.rs` runs the poll: discovers matching base tables each poll via `information_schema` + a glob→LIKE translation (`*`→`%`, metacharacters escaped; unqualified patterns match the connection's configured schema, default public; later-created tables join automatically, discovery capped 200 with a logged overflow), resolves each table's **monotonic cursor column** (explicit `cursor_column`, else a sequence/identity integer preferring the PK, else a `created_at`-style timestamp; neither → skip + warn), and reuses the email/calendar `CollectLedger` (connection `sync_token`, source key = qualified table) with `run_item`/`committed_for` for per-row runs + `commit_on` gating. Two semantics differ from email: the **first sight of a table anchors** its cursor at the current MAX and fires nothing ("new inserts" = after wiring, never a history replay), and the steady pull is **`>=` + a `cursor␟row-uid` committed set** (so timestamp ties are never missed; uid = PK values, else a v5 uuid of the row JSON) with the set pruned to the boundary on advance — which required marking the anchor-boundary rows committed at anchor time (the live test caught the anchor row re-firing). The worker builds its own short-lived pool from the shared `PostgresConnectionConfig` (moved api→`catalerum-store::pool`, api re-exports) + the sealed credential (fails closed without a master key); the poll is grant-gated `db:read@<name-or-id>` (name = the `sql_query` selector convention), and authoring-time guards extend: `validate_collect_connections` (postgres kind + REST-not-tool fix-hint), `collect_capabilities` → `db:read@<conn>`. Rows ride the run as `{kind:"collect_sql", connection, table, cursor_column, row}` → downstream `trigger.row.<column>`. Surfaces: catalog.json `trigger.collect_sql` doc; web flow editor `collect_sql_config` (existing-source picker over new `GET /db/connections` rest fn, tables/cursor fields, shared cadence field, commit-port hint) + raw-builder fields + collect-now button coverage. **Verified:** `just lint` (native + wasm `-D warnings`) green; automation 12 + store + web 362 native green; **live integration test** (`collect_sql_live.rs`, DB-gated) drives the full loop against real Postgres — sealed credential, 2 wildcard tables anchored (pre-existing rows never fire), 4 inserts → 4 runs each carrying its row in order, re-poll fires 0, a later-created matching table anchors then fires — plus api lib 483 (one stale trigger-count assertion updated 10→11). **Deferred (disclosed):** updates/deletes invisible by design (insert trigger only); two automations watching the same table share the per-connection ledger (first-committer wins — same caveat as email collect); no backfill_window (anchor-only first poll); no MySQL (Postgres-only, like `sql_query`); web has still no dedicated DB-connections settings panel (admin REST / chat only)._

_2026-07-11 — **`computer_search` is now a broad search — file/directory names match alongside file contents — with an `include_hidden` gate for dotfiles (SOUL §19/§20; user ask: "make computer search broad search instead and add a boolean input to ignore/not ignore hidden files").** Previously the op only grepped file contents line-by-line (case-sensitively), so a query like "invoice" couldn't surface `Invoice_2026.pdf` at all (binary, unreadable as text) and walked every dotdir (`.git`, `.cache`) it was granted. Now `ops.rs::search` matches each walked entry's *name* (files **and** directories, not the walk root) as well as each text line, plain queries match case-insensitively on both (regex stays verbatim — `(?i)` opts in), and every match carries `kind: "name"|"content"` (`line`/`text` only on content hits) so the model can tell them apart. Hidden (dot-prefixed) entries are pruned from the walk via `filter_entry` unless the new `include_hidden` flag is set — but never the walk root itself, so a granted `~/.config` stays searchable. The flag rides `ComputerOp::Search` as a serde-`default` bool (wire-compatible both directions, no protocol bump) and is surfaced in the `computer_search` tool schema + description; the shared match cap now counts name+content hits together. **Verified:** clippy `-D warnings` clean across core/agent/api `--all-targets`; new agent test `search_is_broad_and_gates_hidden_files` (case-insensitive content + name hits, hidden pruned by default, included on request) — agent 8, core 88, api computer-registry/forwarding 6 all green. **Deferred:** no Windows hidden-attribute check (dotfile convention only); name matches report no snippet by design._

_2026-07-11 — **`computer_exec` default timeout raised 60s → 300s, shared by both ends (SOUL §19/§20; user ask: "increase timeout for computer tool call").** The bite was two-sided: the agent killed a no-`timeout_secs` command at its own hardcoded 60s default (`ops.rs`), while the API's wait fell back to the generic `DEFAULT_OP_TIMEOUT` (120s) — two unrelated constants that only worked because 60 < 120. Now `catalerum-core::computer` owns `DEFAULT_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECS = 300` and `MAX_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECS = 3600` next to the wire protocol both ends already share: the agent clamps its kill deadline to them, and the API's exec wait is always `effective timeout + 15s` margin (explicit or default — no more `DEFAULT_OP_TIMEOUT` fallback for exec), so the agent's structured `timed_out` result reaches the model as data instead of a dead-air dispatch timeout. `DEFAULT_OP_TIMEOUT` stays 120s for the quick ops (file/dir/desktop) with its doc updated; the tool schema now advertises the default/max. Cross-pod forwarding needed nothing — `timeout_ms` rides the sealed envelope end-to-end and the forward's HTTP deadline derives from it. **Verified:** clippy `-D warnings` clean across core/agent/api `--all-targets`; agent's 7 tests + api's 6 computer registry/forwarding tests green._

_2026-07-11 — **`catalerum-agent` exec unbroken under Landlock: the sandbox denied the child `/bin/sh` itself, so every `computer_exec` failed "spawn failed: Permission denied (os error 13)" (SOUL §19/§20; user ask: "fix catalerum-agent computer_exec always denied").** Root cause in `sandbox.rs::apply_landlock`: the ruleset handled **all** filesystem access (`AccessFs::from_all`) but added rules only for the granted directories — so the forked child, restricted in `pre_exec`, couldn't read/execute `/bin/sh`, `/usr`, `/lib`, … and `execve` returned EACCES before the command ever ran. File tools worked (they're path-scoped in-process, no sandbox), which is why only exec died. The existing exec test never caught it because it sets `sandbox: false` ("Landlock may be unavailable in CI"). Fix makes the Linux confinement **write-scoped, mirroring the macOS `sandbox-exec` profile** (allow default, deny writes outside rw grants): read+execute on the standard system prefixes (`/usr /bin /sbin /lib* /etc /opt /nix /proc /sys /run /var`, missing ones skipped like missing grants), full access on `/tmp` and `/dev` (`> /dev/null`, mkstemp; device nodes still DAC-guarded), and the grants as configured (rw ⇒ full, ro ⇒ read+exec). Two real Landlock tests in `sandbox.rs` (linux-gated): `sandboxed_exec_spawns_and_runs` — the regression test, fails EACCES under the old ruleset on any Landlock kernel — and `sandbox_denies_writes_outside_grants`, which probes kernel support (skips without it), grants only a temp dir, and asserts a write into a `target/`-scratch dir outside the grants exits non-zero and leaves no file (the outside target deliberately avoids `/tmp`, which the sandbox now allows). **Verified:** clippy `-D warnings` clean; all 7 agent tests green on a Landlock kernel, deny test confirmed exercising the real deny path (no skip message with `--nocapture`)._

_2026-07-11 — **`catalerum-agent` connects from a real machine: rustls crypto-provider panic fixed, internal-CA trust, wrong-URL UX, and a systemd user-service installer (SOUL §19/§20; user ask: "please fix catalerum-agent" + "automatically fill this option in the settings menu with the api url and document it better" + "add … install via subcommand to systemd user services (if compiled for linux)").** Three defects surfaced in sequence on first real-world `catalerum-agent run`: (1) **panic at first `wss://` dial** — tokio-tungstenite's `rustls-tls-webpki-roots` ships rustls 0.23 with no crypto backend, so it can't auto-pick a process-level `CryptoProvider` (same trap `catalerum-operator` hit with kube). Fix mirrors the operator: pin `rustls = { features = ["ring"] }` and `install_default()` at the top of `main()`. (2) **cert rejection against the internal cluster** — webpki (Mozilla baked-in) roots don't know a self-hoster's internal CA; added `rustls-tls-native-roots` so the OS trust store is consulted too (tungstenite composes both root sets). Also, the connect error only logged the outermost context; the reconnect loop now logs the anyhow chain (`{:#}`) so the TLS/DNS/HTTP root cause is visible. (3) **wrong `--server` URL is the natural mistake** — the web Settings enroll dialog printed `--server <YOUR_CATALERUM_URL>`, and pasting the web origin yields the SPA's `200 OK` on every path instead of the WS `101`. The dialog now prefills the real API origin via `api::api_base()` and says the daemon dials the API, not the web app; `EnrollArgs`/`Config::server_url` docs state the same; and the daemon turns a 2xx upgrade answer into a self-diagnosing error ("server_url likely points at the web UI; use the API origin"). Plus **`catalerum-agent install-service`** (Linux-only, cfg-gated): validates the config first (else the unit would crash-loop), writes `~/.config/systemd/user/catalerum-agent.service` (XDG-aware, absolute exe + `--config` path, `Restart=always`), then `daemon-reload` + `enable` + `restart` (restart, not `enable --now`, so re-installing picks up a new binary), printing status/logs/remove commands and the `loginctl enable-linger` hint. **Verified:** agent clippy `-D warnings` + unit tests green, web wasm-clippy green, `--help` shows the subcommand, `install-service` with a missing config fails early with the enroll hint; the user confirmed the panic and TLS fixes live against their cluster (the 200-OK diagnosis is what led to the URL prefill)._

_2026-07-10 — **Chat no longer widens past the phone screen: the min-content of wide chat content (code blocks, tables, mermaid diagrams, tool output) propagated up the flex chain and stretched the whole page (SOUL §12; user ask: "fix chat not being responsive design — it gets wider with some chat content on mobile").** Root cause: `.chat-layout` — a flex item of the `.wb-main` row — had no `min-width: 0`, so its automatic minimum (min-content) floor let any unbreakable-wide descendant (a code block's longest line under `white-space: pre`, a many-column table, a mermaid `<pre>`/SVG, a long unbroken tool-output token) become the layout's minimum width: the layout grew to ~1500px at a 390px viewport and the document itself scrolled sideways. The per-element guards already in the sheet (`.msg-markdown pre/table { overflow-x: auto }`, `.msg { max-width: 94% }` on mobile) couldn't help — a percentage max-width is ignored in intrinsic-size contributions, which is also why desktop (70ch cap, fits anyway) never showed it. Three CSS fixes in the embedded sheet (`catalerum-web/src/lib.rs`): (1) **`.chat-layout { min-width: 0 }`** breaks the propagation chain — content now scrolls inside its own block as designed; (2) **`.chat-log { overflow-x: hidden }`** as the backstop so the log itself can never pan sideways (its `overflow-y: auto` made the computed overflow-x `auto`, so residual overflow read as "the chat gets wider"); (3) the markdown engine's block-math and mermaid hooks — `figure.catalerum-mermaid` (margin reset + `overflow-x: auto`, inline SVG display-block) and `.catalerum-math-block` (`overflow-x: auto` + centering, the styling the engine's own doc comment expects) — were entirely unstyled in this sheet. **Verified:** wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean; headless-Chromium probe at 390×844 on the extracted sheet + faithful chat DOM covering 11 content cases (long user URL, code block, inline code, long token, table, math, mermaid figure + source fallback, streaming tail, tool card, approval args): before — 4 cases widened the document to 774–1507px; after — every case holds `docScrollWidth == 390`, the log never pans, and code/mermaid pres scroll internally (nothing clipped); desktop 1280px layout unchanged. **Not machine-verified (disclosed):** probed on a static repro of the extracted stylesheet + hand-mirrored chat DOM, not the live wasm app. **Deferred:** the same missing-`min-width: 0` audit for the other `.wb-main` panels (calendar/files/graph headers already have mobile wrap fixes, but their content panes weren't probed)._

_2026-07-10 — **Voice conversation keeps the device awake: the overlay holds a Screen Wake Lock while open (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: "during conversation can we prevent device from sleep (e.g. smartphone)?").** On a phone, the idle timeout locking the screen mid-conversation kills the mic and the playback — the hands-free loop died with the display. New `ScreenWakeLock` (web `components/voice.rs`): `acquire()` in the 🎧 click (next to the AudioContext), `release()` on overlay close and on panel unmount (added to the `cleanup_voice` teardown tuple); deliberately held across pauses. Calls `navigator.wakeLock.request("screen")` **dynamically via `js_sys::Reflect`** (the settings-panel Intl pattern) — the typed web-sys `WakeLock*` bindings are still `web_sys_unstable_apis`-gated, and threading that RUSTFLAGS cfg through trunk + the wasm clippy gate + CI isn't worth one call — so an unsupported browser or insecure context degrades silently: the conversation works, the screen just dims as usual (localhost dev is a secure context). The browser auto-releases the lock whenever the page hides (tab switch, power button), so `acquire` also installs a `visibilitychange` listener that re-requests it once the page is visible again; a `want` cell gates the async request against an overlay close racing it (a sentinel arriving after close is released immediately), and a fresh sentinel supersedes-and-releases any stale one. A rejected request (battery saver, permissions policy) is ignored — the loop must never notice. **Verified:** wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean (the shared `KeptClosure` alias — generalized from `EndedClosure` — absorbs the type-complexity lint); web suite 362 green; trunk build ok; **real-browser probe** (headless Chromium on the built dist, served statically): the exact dynamic sequence returns a `WakeLockSentinel` (`released:false` → held), `release()` flips it, and double-release is harmless (the supersede path relies on that). **Not machine-verified (disclosed):** actual sleep prevention needs a physical phone — same standing caveat as the other voice entries; note the OS may still refuse the lock on low battery (handled: silent). **Deferred:** plain chat streaming (no overlay) intentionally holds no lock; no UI hint when the lock is denied._

_2026-07-10 — **Voice mode speaks long paragraphs sooner: the streaming segmenter now cuts at sentence boundaries, in manageable batches (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: "break up very long paragraphs … into sentences and convert a manageable amount of sentences to speech; … if in 3+ sentences start generation for those so the generation feels better").** Before, `ParagraphSegmenter` (web `components/voice.rs`) emitted to the TTS pump only at a blank line — a model writing one long unbroken paragraph kept the overlay silent until the whole paragraph finished, and then synthesized it as one monolithic clip. Now `push` has a second cutter behind the paragraph one: once the still-open paragraph holds **`EARLY_SENTENCES` (3) completed sentences** and at least **`EARLY_MIN_CHARS` (160) bytes**, that head is emitted immediately (batches of ~3 sentences in steady state) while the model keeps writing; completed paragraphs and the `flush` tail run through the same `split_spoken_chunks`, so a very long finished paragraph also becomes several manageable synthesis requests instead of one (`flush` returns `Vec<String>` now — both chat.rs call sites loop). The boundary detector (`speech_cut`) is deliberately conservative, mirroring `paragraph_break`'s streaming discipline: a sentence ends at `.`/`!`/`?`/`…` plus closing quotes/emphasis **followed by whitespace** (buffer end never cuts — the stream may still extend the token, e.g. "3." → "3.14"), never inside a ``` / ~~~ fence (the "(code omitted)" elision still sees whole blocks) or an inline code span (backtick parity, reset per line so a stray backtick can't poison the stream), and not after list markers/bare numbers ("1."), single letters/initials, dotted abbreviations ("e.g.", "z.B."), or a small spoken-abbreviation set (`boundary_token_ok`). Short paragraphs — under 3 sentences or 160 bytes — pass through whole, so ordinary replies gain no extra seams. **Verified:** wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean; web suite **362 green** incl. 5 new tests (early cut at the 3rd streamed sentence with the tail flushing separately; abbreviations/list markers never cut; no cut inside a fence; a completed 7-sentence paragraph splits into ≤3-sentence batches that reassemble verbatim; a short "Ok. Sure. Done. Fine." paragraph stays whole). **Not machine-verified (disclosed):** the audible effect needs a real TTS model (dev echo gateway has none) — same standing caveat as all voice entries; the segmenter is pure and unit-covered. **Deferred:** no early cut for long sentence-less runs (e.g. bullet lists without periods — they still wait for their blank line, as before); tuning `EARLY_MIN_CHARS`/batch size against a real voice._

_2026-07-10 — **Voice conversation hardened against connection drops (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: "make voice conversation more resilient against connection drops").** Four gaps, each a way a network blip ended or degraded the hands-free loop. **(1) The big one, found + reproduced live during verification, and it affected ALL chat, not just voice:** `ChatSocket::next_update` mapped a transport-level read error (an abnormal close — code 1006, the thing an actual network drop produces) to `StreamUpdate::Error`, which `drive_turn` treats as a server stream error → terminal "[stream error: WebSocket Closed…]" bubble. The mid-turn reconnect+reattach machinery lived only in the `None` (clean close) arm — nearly dead code for real drops. Transport errors now map to `None` (the socket is equally dead; gloo yields `Err` only terminally), routing every drop into the reconnect path. **(2) The swallowed open:** a send into a zombie socket (dead connection the browser hasn't noticed) reports no error, so a voice utterance's turn-opening frame could vanish — no ack, no turn, transcript lost. The `None` arm now recovers an **un-acked** open: probe `GET /active_turn` — if the turn IS running (delivered, ack lost) attach to it; if nothing is running, `reconnect_and_resend` the original frame on a fresh socket (bounded backoff; `Outbound::Chat` only — an approval resume is never resent, avoiding a double resolve; residual duplicate window disclosed in the doc comment: the frame landing AND its whole turn finishing before the probe). The initial send also retries once on a fresh connection when the reused socket fails outright (`send_outbound` factored for both attempts). **(3) Speech synthesis (`/ws/speech`):** `fetch_speech_bytes` retried only a failed *send*, once; a mid-reply close lost the paragraph, and a half-open socket (dropped network keeps a browser WS "open" for minutes) hung the pump forever in Waiting/Speaking. Now: per-paragraph bounded retry (`SPEECH_FETCH_ATTEMPTS` = 3 fresh-socket attempts, 400·n ms backoff — synthesis is stateless, so re-speaking the same text is always safe) around a `collect_speech_reply` whose every event wait is capped by `SPEECH_EVENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (20 s) — timeout/close → retry; a server `error` frame → permanent (retrying fails identically), socket kept (protocol keeps it usable); supersession/overlay-close abandon quietly. A chat-stream reconnect also proactively drops the held speech socket (same blip almost certainly killed it too — cheaper than the next paragraph's 20 s timeout; the socket cell moved up beside the segmenter so `drive_turn` reaches it). **(4) STT:** a failed `POST /audio/transcriptions` discarded the recorded take (the utterance only exists client-side). `transcribe_with_retry` retries **transient** failures (transport / 5xx / 429; classified by `transient_rest_error`) twice with backoff before surfacing; definitive 4xx (no STT model, bad audio) surfaces at once. **Verified:** full `just lint` green; web suite **357 green** incl. new `transient_rest_errors_retry_definitive_ones_do_not` (and a pre-existing unrelated red fixed en route: `settings_tabs_collapse…` still asserted "3 admin-chrome tabs" from before the MCP-servers + Computer-agents tabs landed — now derives the count from `is_admin_chrome`). **Live E2E (real API + trunk + headless browser):** send a turn → **restart the API** (cargo-watch) → send another turn on the same page: before the fix it dead-ended in "[stream error: WebSocket Closed: code: 1006]"; after, the client detects the dead socket, probes `active_turn`, reconnects, re-sends — the turn opens and streams server-side (the dev gateway's provider error shows, same as turn one), and the conversation's persisted messages show **exactly one copy** (no duplicate from the resend). **Not machine-verified (disclosed):** the speech-socket retry/timeout and STT retry paths need a mic + real TTS/STT models (the dev echo gateway has neither) — same standing caveat as the voice feature's own entries; logic is compile- + unit-covered. **Deferred:** an overlay "reconnecting…" hint while retries run (silent today); sentence-level resegmentation after a mid-paragraph reattach gap (MAXLEN-eviction edge); server-side synthesis timeouts._

_2026-07-10 — **The second sidebar (every panel's master-detail list pane) is one shared component family instead of nine near-identical per-panel copies (SOUL §12; user ask: "unify the second sidebar ui more").** Chat sessions, Notes, Skills (+Profiles, which reuses its classes), Automations, Grants, History, Memory, MCP Endpoints, Apps, Calendars and Email each hand-rolled the same list-pane CSS under their own prefix (`.notes-list*`, `.skills-list*`, `.mcpe-*`, `.auto-*`, `.grant-*`, `.conv-*`, `.mem-*`, `.cal-sidebar*`, `.chat-sidebar*`, `.email-mailboxes`/`.email-list`, `.apps-sidebar`) — the container/header/title/body/status/error, the item rows (hover / `-active` ring / title / preview / meta), the search input, and the header button trio were byte-identical or trivially divergent (stray paddings, one `gap` value). New shared families in `lib.rs` next to the `.list-drawer*` block: **`.pane-split`** (the master-detail flex row — also carries the mobile stack + `> :not(.pane-list) { min-height: 0 }` rules, replacing the two ten-selector enumerations), **`.pane-list`** + `-header`/`-title`/`-body`/`-status`/`-error`, **`.pane-search`**, **`.pane-items`/`.pane-item`** + `-active`/`-title`/`-preview`/`-meta`, **`.pane-btn`** + `-primary`/`-danger`, and **`.pane-detail`** (the editor side; the per-panel `*-editor-empty` copies now reuse the existing `.panel-placeholder`). Panels keep their own class only for real deviations: widths (`.mcpe-list` 300, `.mem-list` 360, `.cal-sidebar` 240, `.apps-sidebar` 220, `.email-mailboxes` 230, `.email-list` 320), padded bodies (`.cal-sidebar-body`/`.chat-sidebar-body`), row extras (`.notes-item-tag*`, `.skills-tag`, `.auto-pill`, `.conv-item-origin`, mem cards), and the chat/email drawer mechanics (`.chat-sidebar`/`.email-mailboxes` keep their own off-canvas classes; their look now comes from `.pane-list`). Chat's sidebar width unified 260→280 and its `+ New` button became the shared `pane-btn pane-btn-primary`; the Apps rail gains the standard panel background/border. The two e2e specs selecting `button.auto-item` now select `button.pane-item`. **Verified:** full `just lint` gate green (native + wasm); drove the live app headless (magic-link login) across Chat/Notes/Calendar/Automations/Memory/Endpoints/History/Email/Skills/Apps at desktop width — unified headers/buttons/rows everywhere — and at 420px: the ☰ list-drawer opens over the scrim (Skills), Email stacks with its mailboxes toggle, the chat sessions drawer + inline row actions work; `button.pane-item` clicked a live automation row end-to-end (fixture created + deleted via REST). **Disclosed (not this change):** the two automation e2e specs fail in fixture setup on main too — the server now rejects placeholder collect connections (`connection` must be an existing calendar connection's uuid), so `POST /automations` 400s before any UI step; also the dev `cargo-watch` restarts on repo-root screenshot/test-result writes, which mimics API flakiness during browser drives (artifacts now land outside the repo). **Deferred:** Notes' tag-chip bar and the three search variants (`.pane-search` vs chat's padded-body variant vs History's clearable search row) are still per-panel; the Apps rail keeps its mini caps-label head instead of the standard `.pane-list-header`._

_2026-07-10 — **Chat streaming un-degraded: redis 1.x's default 500 ms client response timeout was killing every blocking Valkey stream read mid-block (SOUL §6.6/§7/§12; user ask: "fix voice conversation having web socket errors" → logs showed `turn buffer read failed error=redis: timed out` every ~1.5 s).** redis-rs 1.x defaults **every** async connection to a 500 ms response timeout (`client.rs DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT`), so `TurnBuffer::read`'s `XREAD BLOCK 20000` — and `WorkQueue::pull`'s `XREADGROUP BLOCK` — timed out client-side at 500 ms whenever no frame was already waiting; `forward_turn` then logged + backed off 1 s, degrading live token streaming (chat AND the voice overlay's paragraph pump riding it) to ~1.5 s polling with warn spam, and making the last-chance terminal read (2 s block) always fail. Fix in `catalerum-bus`: new `conn::blocking_read_connection(client, block_ms)` opens the dedicated per-read connection with `AsyncConnectionConfig::set_response_timeout(block_ms + 5 s margin)` — used by both `RedisTurnBuffer::read` and `RedisQueue::pull`; and `Bus::connect` now builds the shared `ConnectionManager` with an explicit **5 s** response timeout instead of the twitchy 500 ms default (one hiccup must not drop a load-bearing append — e.g. a turn's terminal frame, whose loss strands forwarders into the liveness fallback). Pub/sub paths (`get_async_pubsub`) are unaffected (message waits aren't responses). **Verified:** bus clippy `-D warnings` + 20 unit tests green; full `just lint` gate green; **live probe against the running Valkey**: empty `XREAD BLOCK 3000` returns `Ok([])` after 3.0 s (previously errored at 0.5 s), a blocked read wakes with the frame when an append lands 1.5 s in, empty `XREADGROUP BLOCK 2000` returns clean after 2.0 s._

_2026-07-09 — **`ask_user` Q&A made durable end-to-end: the structured answers now persist, and a replayed transcript re-renders the question form's Q&A instead of a raw JSON tool chip (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: "fix persistent storage of model question tool calls and answers").** The gap: the questions were durable (`pending_questions.questions`) and the tool call itself rode the assistant row's `tool_calls`, but the user's **structured** `Answer`s were flattened into the follow-up user message's prose by the web form and then discarded — nothing recorded which options were picked, and a reopened conversation showed the `ask_user` exchange as opaque JSON. **Storage:** migration `0061` adds `pending_questions.answers` JSONB; `PendingQuestion.answers: Option<Vec<Answer>>`; `PendingQuestionRepo::resolve_for_conversation` now takes `answers: Option<&[Answer]>` and stamps them onto the row(s) it closes — `None` (typed past the form / superseded by a fresh `ask_user`) leaves NULL, so "answered" vs "dismissed" stays distinguishable; new `list_for_conversation` returns the thread's full Q&A history oldest-first. **Wire:** `ClientFrame`/`ClientChatMessage` gain an additive `answers` field (serde-default; old clients unaffected) — the web form submit sends the structured answers alongside the formatted prose (`content` stays what the model reads), consumed-and-cleared per submit like the `/<skill>` handoff so a declined send can't leak them; `run_turn`'s resolve passes them through, and `inject_user_frame` resolves+stamps when a **mid-turn** frame carries answers (previously a form answered while another turn streamed left its row unresolved forever → the form re-materialized on every reload). **Read surface:** `GET /conversations/{id}/questions` (conversation-ownership-checked, `conversation:read`); on transcript replay the web fetches it once (only when the thread contains `ask_user` calls) and grafts each row's answers into its tool call's result JSON keyed by the `pending_question_id` the result already carries (the emerged-UI `ui_by_call` correlation pattern); `tool_render.rs` gains a bespoke `ask_user` card — summary = first question (+N more), body = per-question rows showing the given answer (picked options + typed text, "(no answer)" for skipped) or the offered options while unanswered. **Verified:** DB-gated repo test green against live PG (answers round-trip verbatim, supersede keeps NULL, idempotent re-resolve doesn't clobber stored answers, history ordering); api clippy clean + 483 unit tests green; web wasm-clippy clean + tool-render summary test green. **Deferred (disclosed):** the LIVE turn's card shows answers only after a reopen (the live prose bubble already carries them); channels (prose-degraded forms) record no structured answers — their replies are plain messages with no form correlation._

_2026-07-10 — **Preview service: a stored object → a raster image preview (an image thumbnail, or the first page of a PDF / office document / spreadsheet / presentation) rendered by a STANDALONE service with its own container image, reached over HTTP (SOUL §9/§10; user ask: "implement preview service that can create … an image preview of a document, tables, presentations, pdfs, a lot of image formats", then "what to do instead: separate container image for the previewer" → HTTP service / Rust binary / all previews).** **Why a separate service:** the API image is **distroless** and ships no render toolchain; rather than piggyback on the batteries exec sandbox (rejected first cut — couples preview to `[exec]`, drags in the huge image, lives under the 1 MiB `Executor` stdout cap), previews render in their own slim image. **Core (`catalerum-core/src/preview.rs`):** `PreviewRequest {document(skip-serde), content_type, max_dimension, format, page}` + `PreviewResponse {image(skip-serde), content_type, width, height, page_count, engine}` + `PreviewFormat {Webp|Png|Jpeg}` (WebP default) + a `Previewer` trait next to `OcrEngine`, plus the single-source type predicates `is_image_type`/`is_document_type`/`is_previewable` both the engines and the client key on. **Service (`catalerum-preview`, lib + `[[bin]] catalerum-preview-service`):** an axum server (`POST /render?size=&fmt=&page=` body=document + `Content-Type` header → `image/*` bytes + `X-Preview-Width/Height/Page-Count`; `GET /healthz`; optional `PREVIEW_TOKEN` bearer; SIGTERM graceful shutdown; env config) over a `PreviewChain` of (1) **`ImagePreviewer`** — pure-Rust `image`-crate decode → Lanczos3 resize-to-fit (**never upscales**) → re-encode (WebP/PNG/JPEG), on `spawn_blocking`; and (2) **`DocumentPreviewer`** — shells the local **poppler** (`pdfinfo` for page count, `pdftoppm -scale-to N -singlefile` for the page raster) and **LibreOffice** (`soffice --convert-to pdf`, unique per-call `UserInstallation` for concurrency) via `tokio::process`, re-encoding the page raster through the shared image path. No PyMuPDF/Python — all Rust + CLI. **API client (`catalerum-api/src/preview_client.rs`):** `HttpPreviewer` (reqwest) is the single `Previewer` behind `AppState.previewer`, built by `build_http_previewer` from `[preview]` config (`enabled`/`service_url`/`service_token`/`default_format`/`max_dimension`/`hard_max_dimension`/`timeout_secs`; `service_url` empty → previews off). The API dropped its `catalerum-preview` dep entirely — it carries no codec. Routes unchanged: `POST /storage/preview` + `GET /storage/preview/{key}` (`storage:read`; a wildcard `{*key}` must be the last segment, hence the own prefix), which POST to the service. **Image/deploy:** Dockerfile `build-preview` (cross-compiled) + `runtime-preview` (slim `debian:bookworm-slim` + `libreoffice-nogui` + `poppler-utils` + fonts, non-root, RO-rootfs-friendly `HOME=/tmp`, listens 8790); `docker-bake.hcl` `preview` target + `.gitlab-ci.yml` build/publish wiring (QEMU binfmt like `sandbox`, its apt layer is target-arch); `deploy/preview.yaml` (Deployment ×2 + Service :80→8790 + PDB) with `[preview].service_url="http://catalerum-preview"` in the API ConfigMap; `just preview-image` / `just preview`. **Verified:** clippy `-D warnings` clean (core/-preview/-api/binary, `--all-targets`) + full-native-workspace `cargo check`; unit tests green (core predicates + shapes; image engine downscale/never-upscale/per-format magic/undecodable→Invalid; document engine `office_ext`/`parse_pages`/supports + a REAL one-page-PDF render via poppler; chain routing). **Live E2E against the real service binary:** started `catalerum-preview-service` (`PREVIEW_TOKEN` set) → `/healthz` ok, engines `["image","document"]`; no-token→**401**, `text/plain`→**415**; a PNG→WebP 256×128 (aspect kept), a **3-page PDF page-2→WebP with `X-Preview-Page-Count: 3`** (poppler), a **CSV→PNG via LibreOffice** — all valid, in-bounds, correct headers. Only the API↔service network hop from inside a DB-backed `AppState` is unexercised (the request/response contract is identical to what the E2E drove). **Deferred (disclosed):** web file-browser thumbnails consuming `GET /storage/preview` (endpoint ready); a `preview_object` LLM tool; caching rendered previews as derived objects; ETag/`304`._

_2026-07-09 — **OCR for stored images & PDFs: image objects become searchable text at ingest via an `OcrEngine` trait + fallback chain (SOUL §7/§10 — the seam `object.rs` reserved; user ask: dedicated OCR APIs "like mistral ocr and others" primary, "offline ocr library as fallback").** **Core:** `catalerum-core/src/ocr.rs` (`OcrRequest {document(skip-serde), content_type, language, model}` / `OcrResponse {text, engine}`) + `OcrEngine` trait (`name`/`supports`/`ocr`) beside `Transcriber`. **Engines:** (1) **`MistralOcr`** (new provider crate `catalerum-ocr`) — Mistral-dialect `POST {base}/v1/ocr`, document in-band as a `data:` URI (`image_url` for images, `document_url` for **PDF** — the one engine that takes PDFs), pages' markdown joined; configurable `base_url` = any compatible endpoint; 401/415/422 → `Invalid` (permanent), 429/5xx → `Provider` (transient). (2) **`VisionOcr`** (`catalerum-llm/src/ocr.rs`) — any image-capable chat model on llmleaf: one multimodal turn (strict transcribe-only system prompt) collected via `client.chat()`. (3) **`TesseractOcr`** (`catalerum-ocr`) — the offline fallback: shells out `tesseract stdin stdout -l <langs>` (a RUNTIME binary, deliberately no build/link dep so the multi-arch CI bake is untouched); startup `probe()` runs `--list-langs` and verifies every configured pack, so binary-present-but-no-traineddata means "engine absent", never per-job errors. **`FallbackOcr`** chains them **mistral → vision → tesseract** (first supporting member that succeeds wins; failures warn + fall through). **Ingest seam:** `ObjectIngestContext.with_ocr(OcrContext {engine, caps})` — after the `is_text_like` miss, a supported image/PDF is read and OCR'd into the SAME document/chunk/Qdrant pipeline (`read_object`/`search_files`/`search_semantic` see it for free); size caps **skip, never truncate** (8 MiB image / 32 MiB PDF, read cap+1 to catch stale sizes); `Unsupported|Invalid` → warn + clean skip (purge path — a bad config must not burn the job's 5 retries per image per scan); other errors → job retry/backoff like embed; trimmed-empty text → no document; ingest is **config-level only** (jobs carry no acting user; workspace truth stays deterministic). **Config `[ocr]`** (default = all off = exactly the prior binary-skip path; dev/CI echo untouched): `vision_model` (deliberately NOT "echo"), caps, `[ocr.mistral] api_key/base_url/model` (enabled iff key), `[ocr.tesseract] enabled(true)/path/languages`; env `CATALERUM_OCR__…`; chain built once in the binary (`build_ocr_chain`, async probe) and shared by AppState + the ingest worker. **Surfaces:** per-user `llm_settings.ocr_model` (migration **0060**, nullable like `transcription_model`; validated `ModelKind::Chat` — a vision model IS a chat model advertising `image` input) routes user-invoked OCR through `VisionOcr` with that model; **`ocr_document` tool** (`tools/ocr.rs`, `storage:read`, args key/store/model/language, description cross-references `read_object`); **`POST /ocr`** (`routes/ocr.rs`, byte-in/JSON-out mirror of `/audio/transcriptions`, no cap gate); `GET /status` `LlmInfo.ocr_engines`; **web** Settings picker (chat catalog client-filtered to image `input_modalities`) + "OCR engines" line in the gateway card. **Tests:** `catalerum-ocr` unit (serde fixtures, chain fallback semantics, tesseract args) + a binary-gated tesseract round-trip on a committed `hello.png` (self-skips w/o the binary); DB-gated `catalerum-ingest/tests/object_ocr.rs` (FakeOcrEngine: extract+link, Unsupported→clean-skip+purge, Provider→Err, oversize→engine-never-called, text-free→no doc, context-removed→purge). Deferred: PDF rasterization for vision/tesseract, more OCR providers (Azure/Google — the trait is the plug point), configurable chain order, SVG stays text/XML._

_2026-07-09 — **Cross-pod computer-agent forwarding: a `computer_*` tool call on ANY pod now reaches the agent's live socket wherever it is held (SOUL §11/§16 M7/§19/§20; user ask: "implement Cross-pod forwarding of agent connections, cross pod running is required to work" — closing the deferral in the computer-agents entry below).** An agent's WebSocket is pod-local, so under N replicas a tool call can land on a pod that doesn't hold it. **Ownership discovery** rides a self-healing Valkey registry key `cat:computer-agent:{id}` → owning pod (the bus `Registry` role, exact-key — no scan): announced on `Hello`, refreshed on the 25s WS heartbeat (`OWNER_TTL` 90s), withdrawn on disconnect (a crashed owner's key lapses on its own — the SOUL §11 ephemeral-coordination fit, mirroring the §7 `cat:activeturn` pattern rather than a durable `terminal_sessions.pod_id` column). **`ComputerRegistry`** now carries `pod_id` + `bus` + `store` + a late-bound `Arc<PodComms>` (`set_pod_comms`, sync via `std::sync::RwLock` so the non-async `AppState::new` can bind it once a master key exists): `request(id, op)` tries the local map, else looks up the owner and **forwards over the same sealed `POST /internal/pod` AES-256-GCM transport the terminal path uses** — two new `PodOp::ComputerRequest {agent_id, computer_op, timeout_ms}` / `ComputerDisconnect {agent_id}` (nil `session_id`; the inner op is the field `computer_op` to dodge the outer `op` serde-tag), dispatched in `routes::internal::respond` via `execute_computer_op` **before** the terminal ownership check (a computer op carries no session). Owner-side dispatch = `request_local` against its live conn; a stale key → an `ok:false` `OpResponse` (surfaces as ordinary "not online", not a transport error); an unreachable owner (addr key lapsed) → `Offline`. **`online_in_workspace` is now cross-pod aware** (local live conns + a DB-list × ownership-key scan, remote caps from the persisted snapshot), so the REST list + the tools' `resolve_machine` see agents on any pod with **zero tool-layer changes**. **Cross-pod revoke**: `disconnect_everywhere` closes locally, withdraws the key, and forwards `ComputerDisconnect` to the owner for instant teardown; the WS heartbeat's revoked-check (`get` → `revoked_at`, ordered **before** the re-announce so a revoked agent is never re-advertised) is the safety net if the forward is missed. Degrades cleanly to today's single-pod behaviour when no bus/master key is configured. **Verified:** clippy-clean; an in-process **two-pod integration test** (`pod_forward::two_pod_tests::pod_b_drives_a_computer_agent_owned_by_pod_a`) drives the whole path through the REAL sealed HTTP transport + real ownership registry — pod B forwards a `Stat` op to the agent held on pod A, gets the agent's response back, a local-only request on B is `Offline`, and a revoke on B tears A's socket down (its close-handle fires). **Live two-process E2E (real API pod-a:8787 + pod-b:8788 sharing Postgres + Valkey + master key):** enroll + connect the daemon to pod A → the `cat:computer-agent:{id}` = `pod-a` key appears in Valkey → **pod B's `GET /computer-agents` shows the agent `online:true` with its capabilities** (cross-pod discovery) → **`DELETE` on pod B (the non-owner) → 204 → the ownership key is withdrawn, pod A shows `online:false` + `revoked_at`, and the daemon's socket is dropped on A** (its reconnect is 401-rejected, token revoked). **Env caveats hit + worked around (not code):** this dev box's host→container podman port-forward for Valkey was stuck (Postgres's was fine) — a container restart revived it; a concurrent OCR session's half-wired `build_ocr_chain` transiently broke the shared binary build, and a stale pre-wiring binary initially masked the ownership announce (a `bus=None` registry announces nothing yet still reads `online` locally) — a clean rebuild resolved it. **Still deferred:** the live op-*forward* between two real processes isn't exercised (driving a `computer_*` tool needs a tool-calling LLM; the dev echo model doesn't) — the in-process integration test covers it through the real transport; persistent runtime-grant/audit storage; desktop input control; Windows exec sandbox._

Fixed en route: `speech_text` glued text directly following a code block onto "(code omitted).". **Verified:** wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean, `trunk build` ✅, 9 voice unit tests green (segmenter incremental / fence / multi-paragraph cases + the new post-code-block spacing regression test). **Deferred:** as below (barge-in, voice picker, live browser E2E), plus sentence-level segmentation for even earlier first audio._
