REST `POST /connections` is untouched (proper JSON clients were never affected). Unit test covers all spellings; the DB tool test now also creates a webcal source from flat args and asserts the stored blob._

_2026-07-07 — **Calendar write-back lands for every writable provider (CalDAV `PUT`/`DELETE`, Google `events.insert/patch/delete`) and Outlook / Microsoft 365 joins the provider roster end-to-end (SOUL §8/§11/§12/§13; user ask: "implement writeback to external calendars and implement outlook google calendars also for calendar collection").** **(1) Provider write halves (the M7 deferral, closed):** `CalendarProvider::create/update/delete_event` were `Unsupported` in every backend. CalDAV now `PUT`s a serialized `VCALENDAR` (`ical::event_to_ics`, the parse module's new write half — UID/DTSTART/DTEND incl. `VALUE=DATE`, RRULE, CATEGORIES-per-label, ATTACH w/ params, SEQUENCE; round-trip-tested through the crate's own parser) to the conventional `<uid>.ics` resource (`If-None-Match: *` on create, `If-Match: <etag>` on update, `412` → `Error::Conflict` "re-sync and retry", idempotent `DELETE` on 404; webcal stays refused). Google implements `events.insert`/`patch`/`delete` — PATCH-only-mapped-fields so server-side attendees/reminders survive, explicit `null`s clear unset optionals, `date`/`dateTime` twin-nulling flips timed↔all-day, deletes idempotent on 404/410; the connect flow now requests the **`calendar.events` read/write scope** (new `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_EVENTS_SCOPE`; a pre-existing read-only-scoped connection keeps syncing and fails writes with a 403 carrying a re-connect hint), and `GoogleCalendarProvider::calendar()` flips `read_only → false`. Core `NewEvent` gains `all_day` (serde-default; nothing constructed it before). **(2) The `calendar_writeback` seam (API):** REST `POST/PUT/DELETE /events` and the `create/update/delete_event` tools now resolve an `EventWriteTarget` — Local keeps the store-only path byte-for-byte; a **writable provider calendar** builds the live provider (via new ingest re-export `provider_from_connection_with` + both OAuth seams) and writes **provider first, mirror second** (`upsert_by_uid` under the provider-issued uid/etag — provider failure leaves the store untouched; a mirror failure is disclosed in-error and healed by the next sync). `merge_event_update` (pure, tested) carries identity/etag and bumps SEQUENCE. The web's `Calendar::is_writable` drops its `is_local()` clause (any non-read-only calendar is editable; picker + ✎/✕ affordances follow), and the create/update/delete tool descriptions now say so. `WriteEvent` (collect) deliberately untouched — provider→local only, no loop. **(3) Outlook provider (`catalerum-calendar/src/outlook.rs`, google.rs's structural twin):** Microsoft identity platform v2 auth (tenant-parameterized endpoints, `offline_access + Calendars.ReadWrite`, refresh-token **rotation persisted every grant** through the sealed-blob seam), Graph `GET /me/events` / `/me/calendars/{id}/events` **snapshot** sync — Graph's event delta only exists over bounded calendarViews, so `is_incremental = false` with an `osnap:` `(id, changeKey)`-set hash cursor (unchanged ⇒ empty batch; deletions ride the existing snapshot reconcile), `Prefer: outlook.timezone="UTC"`, `$select`-scoped, `@odata.nextLink` paging, bounded reads; mapping: `changeKey` → etag (`W/"…"` If-Match wrapper), text body verbatim / html degrades to `bodyPreview`, `categories` → labels, `isAllDay`; **recurrence** maps a common RRULE ⇄ `patternedRecurrence` subset both ways (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly, INTERVAL, weekly BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY, ordinal BYDAY first…fourth/last, COUNT/UNTIL; pure + fixture-tested) — an out-of-subset server pattern syncs recurrence-less, an out-of-subset local RRULE **fails the write loudly** (never silently de-recurs). Wire-up: `CalendarSubKind::Outlook` (`microsoft` alias) + factory arm requiring the new `OutlookTokenStore` seam (`provider_from_connection_with` grew the fourth param; `SecretOutlookTokenStore`/`outlook_token_store_for` in ingest mirror the Google pair; sync + collect thread it, so **CollectCalendar collects Outlook connections** exactly like Google). **(4) `/auth/microsoft/*` flow:** new `[microsoft]` config (`client_id`/`client_secret`/`tenant` — blank = `common` —/`redirect_url`/`state_secret`, env overrides `CATALERUM_MICROSOFT__*`), a dedicated state-cookie signer instance (same HMAC machinery, independent key) on AppState, and `routes/microsoft_oauth.rs` mirroring the Google dance (CSRF state cookie → Entra consent → code exchange erroring without a refresh token → AES-GCM-sealed blob on a fresh-or-reauthorized `{"provider":"outlook"}` Calendar connection; 404 when unconfigured, hard-requires `[secrets].master_key`). `create_calendar_connection`'s description points agents at both OAuth flows (OAuth-born connections stay out of the REST/tool provider enums). **Verified:** native workspace clippy + wasm clippy clean (`-D warnings`); calendar **83** (incl. ICS round-trips, CalDAV url/etag/webcal-refusal, Google insert/patch body shapes, Outlook mapping/recurrence-both-ways/cursor/token-rotation/url tests), api lib **452** (vs live PG; incl. `merge_event_update`, microsoft authorization-url/cookie tests, google scope-switch tests), ingest 75, core 70, web **336** (writability flip) green; `trunk build` succeeds. **Deferred (disclosed):** CalDAV update rewrites the VEVENT from catalerum's model (unmapped server-side props — VALARMs, attendee lists — are not preserved; Google/Outlook PATCH semantics do preserve them); no Outlook push channel (Graph subscriptions) — the poll cadence collects; multi-calendar discovery still one-calendar-per-connection for Google + Outlook; Outlook attachments unmapped; attendee write-back only on create (the stored event holds resolved entity pointers, not addresses); web "Connect Google/Outlook" buttons don't exist (both flows are URL-driven, at parity); existing Google connections need a one-time re-connect to gain the write scope._

_2026-07-07 — **Agenda events are editable: an ✎ per row opens the event form in edit mode, saving `PUT /events/{id}` (SOUL §8/§12; user ask: "implement edit button for calendar events").** The server route + store patch existed since the calendar slice and `rest::update_event` was already client-side — nothing in the UI called it. Now the add-event form is **one form, two modes**: a new `editing: RwSignal<Option<EditingEvent>>` session (id + the stored stamps/`all_day`/`rrule` + the prefilled datetime inputs) flips it from POST to PUT. The agenda row gains an **✎ edit button** beside ✕ (same local-writable-calendar gate; shared CSS block, the pair's right-push `margin-left:auto` moved to the leading edit button). Clicking it prefills every field **from the raw UTC event in `events`** (not the agenda's local-shifted copy): timed events prefill in local wall clock (exactly what `local_input_to_rfc3339` inverts), all-day blocks prefill their date-pinned stamps unshifted (mirroring `to_local_event`), labels join back to the comma form, attachments stage as-is, and the form scrolls into view. **Preservation rules (the subtle part):** an *untouched* datetime input sends its **original stamp back verbatim** — so a title-only save never shifts an all-day event's midnight stamps through the local→UTC conversion (which would move it a day in any non-UTC zone) nor drops seconds the minute-grain input can't express; `all_day` and `rrule` aren't form fields, so the session sends the stored values back unchanged — which required adding **`rrule` to the web `UpdateEvent`** (it was missing: the server clears an absent rrule, so any UI edit of a recurring event would have silently killed its recurrence). The calendar picker locks while editing (the PUT has no `calendar_id` — events can't move calendars); submit reads "Save changes" + a Cancel button appears; closing the form (header toggle, cancel, or save) runs a shared `reset_event_form` so the next open is a fresh create, never a stale edit. **Verified:** wasm clippy (`-D warnings`) clean; web suite green (336); `trunk build` ok; **driven end-to-end headless** — seeded a recurring timed event (rrule `FREQ=WEEKLY`, label, location, body) + a flagged all-day event, clicked ✎, screenshot-confirmed the prefilled form (local times 11:00 for 09:00Z, locked picker, Save changes/Cancel), retitled + saved both via the real UI, then asserted over REST that the timed event's stamps came back **byte-identical** with rrule/labels/location/body intact and the all-day event kept `all_day:true` + both `T00:00:00Z` date-pinned stamps; seed calendar deleted after (cascade). **Deferred (disclosed):** editing is agenda-only (grids have no row affordance, same as delete); the form still has no all-day/rrule *controls* — this change preserves those fields, it doesn't edit them; attendees aren't editable (the server's `EventPatch` doesn't touch them either); mixed edits of an all-day event (changing one stamp but not the other) convert only the touched input, which can read oddly across zones — the flag still wins for display._

_2026-07-07 — **Emerged-UI client ops learn `{{path}}` values — the master-detail navigation fix (SOUL §12; user ask: "fix navigation between subapps not working", diagnosed against the prod `asian-recipes` App).** The prod recipe App's card button does `{op:set, path:selectedId, value:"{{recipe.id}}"} → {op:navigate, view:detail}`, but a client `set`/`append` value was a **literal** (only `{"$path":…}` copied) — so `selectedId` stored the braces string verbatim, the detail view's `equals`-filtered `for_each` matched nothing, and "View Recipe" landed on an empty page (navigation *looked* broken; the AI authors this pattern naturally because every other string in a spec interpolates). Fix: web `state.rs::resolve_set_value` now mirrors the server's tool-arg interpolation exactly — a string that is *one whole* `{{ref}}` yields the **raw typed** scope-resolved value (a number stays a number; loop vars like `recipe.id` resolve against the `for_each` row), a mixed string splices display text, arrays/objects resolve recursively, `$path` directives keep working (and now also nested). Docs updated where authors read them: core `ClientOp::{Set,Append}` doc comments + `get_ui_schema`'s `handlers.client` string (spelling out the set-selectedId→navigate master-detail pattern). **Verified:** web native tests green incl. new `set_value_interpolates_templates` (row-scoped whole-ref, raw-type keep, splice, recursive append, literal passthrough); wasm + core/api clippy `-D warnings` clean. **Prod hotfix (user-approved):** the App itself was patched live via `present_ui` (op value → `{"$path":"recipe.id"}`, which the *deployed* runtime already resolves) — now version 3, read back and confirmed; prod picks up the runtime fix itself with the next image roll._

_2026-07-07 — **Chat sidebar recency groups gain "Today" and "Yesterday" sections (SOUL §12; user ask: "in chats introduce today and yesterday section").** `Bucket` (web `chat.rs`) grows `Today`/`Yesterday` tiers above `Last7`; `classify` is rewritten fully **calendar-day based** (day-number diff: `<=0` Today — future-dated/clock-skew items read as Today —, `1` Yesterday, `2..=6` "Previous 7 days" (relabelled from "Last 7 days"), `7..=55` week buckets, else month) instead of the old rolling `7×24h` age windows. Day boundaries follow the **browser's local calendar**: new `local_tz_offset_ms()` (`-getTimezoneOffset()·60_000`) is threaded through `group_sessions`/`classify` as a `tz_offset_ms` param, so a 00:30-local chat lands in Today, not in yesterday's UTC day — this also makes the week/month labels local. Pure-function change; the keyed-`<For>`/`group_key` machinery and CSS (`chat-group-label`) are untouched. **Verified:** wasm clippy clean (`-D warnings`); web unit tests 336 green incl. the extended `classify_splits_today_yesterday_last7_week_month`, a new `classify_uses_local_day_boundaries` (same instant flips Yesterday→Today at UTC+2), and the regrouped `group_sessions_labels_and_orders` (5 groups newest-first); `trunk build` green._

_2026-07-07 — **Kanban board usability, both faces: name-addressed + positioned agent tools (with `kanban_create_board` and column CRUD) and a rebuilt web board (card detail modal, insert-above drag, inline column management, filter; SOUL §24/§12/§11; user ask: "improve the ui and usability of the kanban board (for the user and tool calls for the agent)").** **Store:** `TaskRepo::move_to_column` gains `position: Option<i32>` — the task's final 0-based index in the destination column (clamped; `None` = end, preserving old behaviour); a `place_at` tx renumbers the column densely under `FOR UPDATE`, so a same-column positioned move is a within-column reorder. `BoardRepo` gains `add_column` (next ordinal), `rename_column`, and `delete_column` — delete refuses (`Invalid`) while tasks sit in the column or when it is the board's last, so it can never orphan cards. **Tools (the agent face):** new shared resolvers `resolve_board_arg`/`resolve_column_arg` let every kanban tool take **`board`/`column` names (case-insensitive) or the ids** — an unknown name errors *with the known names* (self-correction in one step), a duplicate name errors asking for the id. New `kanban_create_board` (name + optional custom `columns`; also added to the emerged-UI `handler_tools` allow-list). `kanban_create_task` now needs only a `title` + a board name; `kanban_move_task` takes `column` by name + optional `position` (and reuses the pre-fetched board for the `TaskMoved` dispatch names); `kanban_next_task` accepts `board`+`column` names; `kanban_edit_task` is **partial** (title and/or body; omitted field keeps its value; explicit empty body clears). `query_structured`'s boards operation demoted to discovery/dup-escape-hatch in its description; the `create_task`/`move_task` automation catalog entries document the name params + `position`. **REST:** `POST /tasks/{id}/move` takes optional `position`; new `POST /boards/{id}/columns`, `PUT /columns/{id}`, `DELETE /columns/{id}` (400 with the repo's actionable message when non-empty/last). **Web (the user face, `tasks.rs` rebuilt):** cards **click open a detail modal** — rendered-markdown body (`notes-preview` styling), status + column selects (the accessible move fallback), Edit mode (title input + the shared `MarkdownField` source/preview editor), Delete with confirm; Escape backs out editor→modal via a window listener. Drag-and-drop now supports **insert-above**: dropping *onto a card* computes the position against the column's list minus the dragged card (exact for same-column drags) and calls the positioned move; a card-top indicator (`task-card-over`) and the column highlight show the target; a column-background drop appends (skipped when already last). Cards decluttered to title/badge/assignee/preview + a quick status select (edit/move/delete live in the modal); cards are keyboard-openable (`role=button`, Enter). **Columns are managed in place**: hover/focus tools on each header (✎ inline rename with Enter/Escape, ✕ delete with confirm) + a trailing dashed "+ Add column" stub. Header adds a client-side **filter** (title+body substring, per-column counts follow); add-task inputs submit on Enter/cancel on Escape (form stays open for rapid multi-add); board delete now confirms (it cascades). Status badges migrated from raw hexes to the semantic theme trios (`--ok-*`/`--err-*`/accent tokens — the §12 theme rule). **Verified:** native workspace + wasm clippy clean (`-D warnings`); store suite green incl. new `positioned_moves_and_column_management` (reorder/clamp/dense renumber, column CRUD + tenancy); api 447 green incl. the extended kanban tool test (whole flow by names, positioned move, self-correcting errors, partial edits, viewer gating); web 334 unit tests + trunk build green; **live e2e**: the running dev API drove create-board→add/rename column→positioned same-column & cross-column moves→non-empty delete refused (400 message)→empty delete OK, and a headless-chromium drive of `/app/tasks` exercised board pick, Enter-add, the modal (view/edit/markdown render), modal column move, Escape close, and the filter — screenshots checked. **Deferred (disclosed):** column *reordering* (columns keep creation order; needs an ordinal-shuffle repo op + UI gesture); assignee is still display-only (no set-assignee tool/route/UI); no agent tools for column CRUD (REST/UI only — create-board with the right columns covers the authoring path); drag reorder waits a server round-trip (no optimistic apply)._

_2026-07-06 — **Two recorded multi-pod/authz gaps closed: the latent `GET /mcp` grant-bypass gate and the workspace-sandbox ownership guard (SOUL §16 M7 / §19 / §20 / §26; user ask: "fix 1 mcp issue, also fix sandbox ops, remove stale block comment").** **(1) `GET /mcp` capability gate (the recorded §19 grant-bypass class instance, closed before the push hub gains its first producer):** the SSE push stream fans out **workspace-wide** and its messages carry no per-message capability tag, so any authenticated bearer — including a grant-scoped token minted `{notes:read}` for an external MCP client — would have received every push. New `require_workspace_read` gate in `routes/mcp.rs`: holding the stream requires `read` over **every standard domain** (`catalerum_iam::STANDARD_DOMAINS`, the previously-private role-base domain list now exported for exactly this "whole-workspace surface" case). Every role-derived token passes (a Viewer's base set is exactly these reads — behaviour unchanged for normal tokens); a grant-scoped token narrower than workspace-wide read gets `403` instead of pushes its grant doesn't cover. `POST /mcp` unchanged (per-call registry dispatch already grant-bounds it); module header updated to state the POST/GET asymmetry. **(2) Workspace-sandbox ownership guard (the recorded pod-forwarding gap "WorkspaceSandboxManager run/sessions have NO ownership guard"):** in an N-replica deployment, `ensure` on a pod that didn't own a workspace's **podman** sandbox silently minted a second container — a divergent `/work` twin (the row's `pod_id` ping-ponging between owners). `WorkspaceSandboxManager` now takes an optional bus seam (`set_peers`, attached in `state.rs` iff pod comms are configured, mirroring `TerminalManager::set_forwarder`): before ensuring, a `Ready` row stamped with a *different* pod (`foreign_owner`, pure + unit-tested) triggers a registry liveness lookup (`pod_forward::lookup_pod_addr`, now `pub(crate)`) — owner still announced → actionable `Error::invalid` ("sandbox ops do not forward across pods yet"); owner gone → logged takeover (its container died with it, mirroring the terminal "session died with it" semantics); registry error → fail closed (proceeding blind risks the duplication the guard exists to prevent). Kubernetes backend exempt by design (the CR/Pod is cluster-shared + deterministically named, every pod's `ensure` converges); single-pod dev (no seam) byte-identical to before. Also: the stale `CalendarSubKind::Google` **"M7 TODO"** doc label corrected (Google is implemented, read-only; write-back deferred). **Verified:** native workspace clippy clean (`-D warnings`); api lib suite **447** green (new: 3 gate tests — every role passes / narrow grant refused / viewer-shaped grant passes — and 2 `foreign_owner` shape tests); iam 50 + calendar 56 green. **Deferred (disclosed):** sandbox ops still do not *forward* (the guard fails actionably instead of duplicating — forwarding is the follow-up); per-message capability tagging on the push hub (would let narrower grants hold a filtered stream) waits for the first real producer._

_2026-07-06 — **Agenda tag chips: multi-select with per-tag event counts (SOUL §8/§12; user ask: "improve calendar tag ui").** The agenda's label bar was single-select (`label_filter: Option<String>` — picking #work dropped #personal) and the chips were bare text with no sense of weight. Now: **(1) multi-select** — `label_filter` is a `Vec<String>` of lowercased selections; each chip toggles independently and an event shows when it carries *any* selected label (OR), "All" clears; **(2) counts** — every chip (incl. "All") shows how many events carry that tag, and both the chip list and its counts derive from a new `bar_labels`/`bar_total` source that respects the sidebar's hidden-calendar set (previously the bar was built from *all* loaded events, so a hidden calendar's tags lingered), with `distinct_labels` generalized into `label_counts(impl IntoIterator<Item=&Event>)` (per-event dedup so "Work, work" counts once; sorted case-insensitively, first-seen casing kept); **(3) self-healing selection** — an `Effect` prunes selected labels that vanish from the visible set (reload, calendar hidden), so a disappeared chip can never keep filtering invisibly; **(4) polish + a11y** — chips gained a muted `#` prefix span, pill count badges, hover/active transitions, a `:focus-visible` ring, `aria-pressed`, and the bar is a `role="group"` ("Filter by label"); all colors ride existing theme tokens (`--accent`/`--fg` via `color-mix`), no raw hex. The "no events with label" empty state now lists every selected tag; the `For` keys on `label:count` so a count change re-renders its chip. **Verified:** wasm clippy (`-D warnings`) clean; native web suite green (**333**, incl. the reworked `label_counts_and_filter_membership` — case-insensitive merge, per-event dedup, counts); `trunk build` succeeds; **driven end-to-end headless** (playwright against `just dev` on :8080/:8787) — seeded 5 labeled events via REST, screenshot-confirmed the counted chip bar (All 5 / #friends 1 / #personal 2 / #subscriptions 1 / #team 1 / #work 2) and a two-chip #work+#personal selection showing exactly the 4-event union, then deleted the seed calendar (cascade) leaving the dev DB as found. **Deferred (disclosed):** the chip bar (like before) stays agenda-only — Month/Week/Day grids ignore the label filter by design; no AND-mode toggle (OR is the natural chip semantic); selections still don't persist in the URL/reload (same as before)._

_2026-07-06 — **All-day events render only in the all-day strip — the `all_day` flag now flows store → core → API → web (SOUL §8/§12; user ask: "a full day event may not be shown from top to bottom in the month/week/day but only on top (multiple full-day events stack vertically)").** The `events.all_day` column existed since the calendar slice and the REST/tool write paths set it — but the core `Event` never carried it, so the API projection **dropped the flag** and the web could only *infer* all-day from exact `00:00`–`00:00` stamps: a flagged event with any other times (e.g. a chat-created `all_day:true` 09:00–17:00) rendered as a full-height top-to-bottom block in Week/Day and a timed chip in Month. Fix: core `Event.all_day` (`#[serde(default)]`, so old payloads still deserialize), `EventRow→Event` maps it (the stale "store-only" accessor removed), `ParsedEvent::into_event` + Google `event_from_json` propagate the parsed flag (the Google end-endpoint's flag was previously discarded), and `sync::event_to_upsert` passes it through instead of hardcoding `false` — collected/synced all-day events finally keep the flag across a round-trip. Web: `Event.all_day` mirrored (serde-default), `is_all_day_block` = **flag OR the midnight-span fallback** (flag-less pre-existing rows behave exactly as before), agenda rows say "All day" for flagged events regardless of stamps, and Month cells now sort all-day chips **on top** (stacking vertically when several), matching the Week/Day all-day strip — which already stacked one row per event (cap 4 + "+N more") and now receives every flagged event instead of only midnight-spanned ones. **Verified:** native workspace clippy + wasm clippy clean (`-D warnings`); tests green across core/store/calendar/ingest/api/web (api **441** vs live PG; calendar incl. new Google timed/all-day flag asserts; web incl. a new flag-wins classification test); `trunk build` succeeds. **Deferred (disclosed):** the web create-event form still creates timed events only (no all-day checkbox — display was the ask); flagged all-day events skip UTC→local conversion by design (their stamps mark calendar *dates*); rows synced before this change carry `all_day=false` and rely on the midnight fallback until their next sync re-upserts them._

_2026-07-06 — **`/<skill>` now ATTACHES the runbook to the user message — the model gets it inline, the UI shows only the typed command (SOUL §12/§23; user ask: "the skill text should be attached … in the ui only the message is shown").** Replaces the previous client-side "call `use_skill`" rewrite (which cost a `search_tools` discovery round and put synthetic text in the transcript) with the **attachments pattern**: a new `SkillInvocation {name, instructions, tools}` core type + nullable `skill` JSONB on `messages` (migration `0056`, additive) holds a **point-in-time snapshot** of the invoked skill's runbook on the user row — frozen like a file attachment, so the transcript stays stable if the skill is later edited/deleted. The row's `content` stays the literal typed `/summarize notes` (what the UI renders, what a queued-send reclaim puts back in the composer — where a resend re-parses it); `to_chat_messages` (shared with `chat_compact`) renders the runbook block into the **ephemeral seed** on the live turn and every replay via a new `user_seed_content(content, skill, attachments)` helper (also used by the observer's mid-turn injection). Wire: web `ClientChatMessage.skill: Option<String>` (+`with_skill`; `submit` hands the parsed name to `send_turn` via an `invoke_skill` signal consumed-and-cleared on entry so a declined send can't leak it) → WS `ClientFrame.skill` → `run_turn` resolves + gates + snapshots **before the user row persists** (the seed reads it back from the row). **Gate:** the same per-skill capability `use_skill` enforces (`skill:use@<name>`), checked against the invoking **user's own** authority (`user_caps`, grant-aware per the §19 rule — hoisted above the persist; a bound profile confines the agent's tools, not what the user may hand it), so a user can never extract a runbook their grant doesn't permit; unknown skill → 400, denied → 403, regenerate ignores the field (the anchor's snapshot stands). Mid-turn queued `/skill` frames resolve **best-effort** (observer gained `ws_id` + `invoker_caps`): on unknown/denied the message injects without the runbook — the slash text still names the skill so the agent's own `use_skill` path takes over — rather than a queued frame killing the streaming turn. **Verified:** native workspace clippy + wasm clippy clean; api lib suite **441** green vs live PG incl. new `skill_snapshot_rides_the_seed_not_the_content` (runbook + tools render into the seed, stored content untouched, non-user rows untouched); new DB test `messages_skill_repo::user_message_round_trips_skill_snapshot` green (snapshot verbatim round-trip, plain rows None — migration 0056 applied); store/core/ingest suites green; web 333 green; `trunk build` succeeds. **Deferred (disclosed):** no UI badge marking a skill-invoking message (not asked — the visible `/command` already reads as one); the REST `messages` JSON now carries the snapshot (web ignores it) — a size concern only if runbooks grow huge; channels/automation surfaces don't set `skill` (chat-only)._

_2026-07-06 — **Slash-menu Tab completion: shell-style candidate cycling with no keyboard trap (SOUL §12; user ask: "add autocomplete … suggestions that can be tab through, if reached end => close, no keyboard trap").** Tab on an open slash menu no longer picks-and-commits; it now runs a **completion session**: the first Tab remembers the typed stem (`slash_stem: RwSignal<Option<String>>`) and previews the highlighted command in the draft (`/name`, no trailing space so the menu stays up); repeated Tab / Shift+Tab cycle forward/back through the candidates, each previewed in place. The matches memo filters by the **remembered stem** while a session runs — not the candidate on display — so completing to one name doesn't collapse the list mid-cycle. Stepping past either end (Tab on the last candidate, Shift+Tab on the first) **closes the menu, restores the typed stem into the draft, and lets the next Tab do its browser default** — as does Shift+Tab with no session, and any Tab with the menu closed — so the composer never traps the Tab key (the explicit a11y ask). Sessions end on any input (the new text is the stem now), on Esc (which also restores the stem), on blur (keeps what's shown), and on pick; Enter still commits the highlighted candidate as `/<name> `. Menu rows gained `role="option"` + `aria-selected` under the existing `role="listbox"`. **Verified:** wasm clippy clean; native web suite green (333); `trunk build` succeeds (one transient stage-dir write error on first run; clean on rerun)._

_2026-07-06 — **Composer slash commands: `/new` + `/<skill>` with an inline command menu (SOUL §12/§23; user ask: "add `/` commands for calling skills and starting new chats with /new").** Typing `/` as the draft's first character opens a command menu floating above the composer (`.chat-slash-menu`, absolutely positioned over `.chat-input` so attachment chips never shift it): the built-in **`/new` — "Start a new chat"** first, then one row per workspace skill (name + description, loaded once on mount via `rest::list_skills` — best-effort like the profile/model loaders, so a user without `skill:read` just gets `/new`). Filtering is name-prefix (case-insensitive) on what's typed after the `/`; the menu closes itself the moment the text stops spelling a command name (args, a newline, divergence), plus Esc/blur via a `slash_dismissed` latch that any input/refocus resets. Keys while the menu shows: ↑/↓ highlight (mouse hover follows), Enter/Tab pick, Esc dismisses — Enter reaches "send" only with no menu up. Picking `/new` acts immediately (the sidebar button's `new_chat()`); picking a skill inserts `/<name> ` for the user to append their request. On submit, module-level `parse_slash_command(draft, &skills)` resolves the command: **`/new [opener]`** starts a fresh chat and, with an opener, sends it as the first turn (so `/new plan my week` is one gesture); **`/<skill> [request]`** rewrites the outgoing content into an explicit instruction — *Use the "X" skill: call `use_skill` with name "X" and follow its runbook [for this request. + args]* — sent (and persisted) transparently as the user message, riding the existing `use_skill` tool + deferred-advertising discovery (§7; no server change). Matching handles skill names **with spaces** via longest-exact-prefix on the raw draft (byte-safe — no lowercased-index slicing), then a case-insensitive first-token fallback; the built-in `new` shadows a same-named skill in both menu and parse; anything unrecognized sends as typed (`/etc/hosts …` stays a message). **Verified:** wasm clippy (`-p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -D warnings`) clean; native web suite green (**333**, incl. 4 new `parse_slash_command` tests: `/new` ± opener + case, spaced-name args split, longest-name preference + built-in shadowing, non-command pass-through); `trunk build` succeeds. **Deferred (disclosed):** no server-side forcing of the skill (the rewrite is a strong nudge, not a pinned tool call — the agent may still need one `search_tools` round to load `use_skill`); no slash commands mid-draft (leading `/` only); the transcript shows the rewritten instruction, not the literal `/command` typed._

_2026-07-06 — **Chat authors the skill library: `create_skill` + `edit_skill` LLM tools (SOUL §23; user ask: "add a new create skill tool call" + "and another edit skill tool call").** The skill tool surface was read-only (`use_skill`/`list_skills`) — a model asked to capture a working recipe as a reusable skill had no write path short of telling the user to open the Skills panel. Two new thin `SkillRepo` clients in `catalerum-api/src/tools.rs`, registered beside their read twins, both dispatch-gated on whole-domain `skill:write` (exact REST parity — `routes::skills` gates `POST`/`PUT` the same way; no per-skill write selector exists anywhere, unlike `skill:use@<name>`). **`create_skill`** mirrors `POST /skills`: `name` required (trimmed, per-workspace unique — a taken name is a `Conflict`, never a silent replace), optional `description`/`instructions_md`/`tools`/`code {language, source, entrypoint?}`; the tool list is normalized through the route's own `clean_tools` (now `pub(crate)`, the `clean_tags` pattern) so tool- and user-authored skills get identical handling. **`edit_skill`** is deliberately **partial** where the REST `PUT` is full-replace (a chat edit usually touches one field): only supplied fields change, an omitted field keeps its stored value, an explicit `"code": null` clears the code (absent ≠ null, distinguished at the arg level), the name itself is immutable, and an unknown name is a hard `Invalid` pointing at `create_skill` (never an implicit create). Read-merge-upsert via the existing `upsert_by_name` (not a transaction — a concurrent delete turns it into a create, which still lands the caller's stated definition). Both return a compact summary (`id`/`name`/`description`/`tools`/`has_code`) instead of echoing the full runbook back into context. Neither joins the emerged-UI `handler_tools` allow-list (defining what tools a skill wields is above that bar). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets` clean; full api lib suite **441** green vs live PG incl. the new DB-gated `create_and_edit_skill_tools_write_the_library` (Member create w/ trim+dedup normalization, duplicate-name `Conflict`, Viewer denied both writes deny-by-default §19, partial edit keeps the omitted runbook/tools, `code` attach → `null`-clear, unknown-name `Invalid`). **Deferred (disclosed):** no `delete_skill` tool (not asked; REST + panel cover it); no rename (name is the public key `use_skill`/grants target — renaming under a `skill:use@<name>` grant would silently orphan it); `tools` entries aren't validated against the registry (REST/panel don't either; the checklist UI is the guided path); skills created by chat aren't embedded/indexed (skills have no ingest pipeline at all today)._

_2026-07-06 — **Chat moved off `/v1/chat/completions` onto the OpenAI Responses dialect (`/v1/responses`) — llmleaf-client 0.1.6 → 0.1.8 (SOUL §7; user ask: "use the new llmleaf version + the response endpoints").** The adapter seam held: only `catalerum-llm/src/client.rs` changed shape — the provider-agnostic `ChatRequest`/`StreamEvent` surface (agent loop, compaction, every caller) is untouched. `OpenRouterClient::stream` now encodes a `ResponsesRequest` (role-based history flattened to `input` items: system/user → message items, assistant → reasoning items + message + `function_call` items in the dialect's reasoning-first order, tool results → `function_call_output`; flat `tools`, `reasoning.effort` from `reasoning_effort`, `max_output_tokens`, provider/models defaults into the flattened top-level passthrough) and folds the SDK's typed SSE (`responses_stream`) back into core events: `output_text.delta` → `TextDelta`; `reasoning_text.delta` → visible `ReasoningDelta` (details-less); a reasoning item's bracketing `output_item.done` → one structured details event (`content[]`/`summary[]`/`encrypted_content` → `reasoning.text`/`.summary`/`.encrypted`, keyed by output index so the assembler folds per item — nothing double-counts); `output_item.added(function_call)` + `function_call_arguments.delta` → `ToolCallDelta`s; the terminal snapshot supplies usage + finish (a `"completed"` with `function_call` items ⇒ `ToolCalls`, `incomplete_details.reason` ⇒ `Length`/`ContentFilter`, `failed` ⇒ `Error`-then-`Done`). Signed open reasoning replays: the SDK's typed reasoning item has **no `signature` field (0.1.8)**, but the gateway accepts the OpenRouter item-level `signature` on input — a signed detail is spliced as a raw `ResponseItem::Other`, and a details-less `reasoning` string (old persisted history) replays as a plain reasoning item. Only the **batch** path still speaks chat shapes — that is the SDK's batch contract (`BatchRequestItem.body: ChatRequest`), so `to_chat_request` + `collected_from_response` survive for it alone. **Verified:** workspace clippy `-D warnings` clean; full workspace test suite green (catalerum-llm **60**, incl. new responses-stream folds: text/usage, tool-call assembly across added+deltas, reasoning delta+done-item fold, incomplete→Length, failed→Error, request/item encodings with signature splice + defaults injection); live smoke against the freshly published server image (quay `latest`, pulled today): new `responses_stream_round_trip` integration test + all 6 `llmleaf_modalities` tests green over real HTTP/SSE. **Deferred (disclosed):** the SDK's `ResponsesUsage` (0.1.8) models neither the gateway's `cost_usd` extension (the server *does* emit it on the responses surface) nor a cache-write count, and its typed reasoning item drops the item-level `signature` on **receive** — so per-turn cost lands `None` (§19 cost-cap accounting sees 0 for live chat; batch still carries cost) and newly-received signed reasoning loses its signature until llmleaf-client models those two fields (both trivial adds; bump + a ~5-line mapping change here picks them up). Dev-stack note: the compose llmleaf container was recreated for the new image; provider API keys (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` & co.) ride the creating shell's env, which this session doesn't hold — recreate from a key-bearing shell to restore live upstreams._

_2026-07-05 — **The thinking picker actually thinks now: three llmleaf gateway gaps closed + new chats default to low effort (SOUL §7/§12; user ask: "enable low thinking by default" + "changing the thinking settings does nothing").** The user's feeling was correct — catalerum's side of the plumbing (2026-07-04 entry below) was sound, but the effort token died inside the **llmleaf sibling repo** three separate ways, so the picker was a no-op in every environment: **(1) the OpenAI compat surface never mapped `reasoning_effort` onto the canonical `Thinking` knob** (it rode through `extra`, reaching only OpenAI-wire upstreams verbatim; budget-style providers — Anthropic/Gemini/Cohere — and the dev echo provider saw `thinking: None`, i.e. nothing); **(2) the same surface dropped every `Thinking`/`ThinkingSignature`/`RedactedThinking` chunk on output** ("no OpenAI representation" → `return false`), so even a really-thinking upstream's visible trace vanished at the gateway and catalerum's `delta.reasoning` parser (SDK 0.1.6, already shipped) never got a byte; **(3) the echo provider ignored `req.thinking`**, so the offline dev stack had nothing to show regardless. Fixes, all in `../llmleaf`: the compat parse maps ladder-expressible efforts (`minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`, plus serde names `med`/`highx`) to canonical `Thinking` and **consumes** the field (exotic vocab still rides `extra` untouched); the chunk encoder emits OpenRouter-extension frames — `delta.reasoning` for open text, `delta.reasoning_details` (`reasoning.text` w/ signature, `reasoning.encrypted` w/ data) for signed/redacted blocks — and the collected `chat.completion` gains `message.reasoning` (+`reasoning_details`), omitted when absent so non-reasoning responses stay byte-identical; `openai_wire` now parses **upstream** `delta.reasoning` (OpenRouter) / `delta.reasoning_content` (DeepSeek) and their collected-message twins into canonical Thinking chunks, ordered ahead of content; the echo provider emits a deterministic `echo thinking (<effort>): <last user msg>` chunk when effort is requested, so the whole path is exercisable offline. **Catalerum side (the default):** new-chat threads now request **low** thinking by default — `DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT = "low"` seeds the pre-send `pending_reasoning` pick (init, "+ New" reset, post-bind reset), which binds onto the fresh conversation at first send like any other pick; explicitly choosing "Off" before sending still wins (nothing binds → provider default), and existing threads are untouched. Server/DB unchanged — the default is a chat-UI seed, deliberately not a column default, so automations/profiles/API callers keep their explicit semantics. **Verified:** llmleaf full workspace tests + clippy `-D warnings` clean (new: effort-ladder parse incl. consumed-not-doubled + exotic passthrough, all three reasoning frame encodings, collected reasoning + byte-compat bare case, upstream reasoning/reasoning_content parses, echo thinking-chunk shape/absence); **live SSE proof** against a patched gateway on :8098 — `reasoning_effort:"low"` in → `delta.reasoning` frame ahead of content, no effort → historical byte-shape, collected carries `message.reasoning`; catalerum web trio green (wasm clippy, tests, `trunk build`). **Deferred (disclosed):** the dev stack's gateway is the **published `quay.io/codefionn/llmleaf:latest` container** — the fix reaches `just up` stacks on the next image publish (or stop the container and `just llmleaf` from the sibling checkout); `openai_wire` doesn't parse upstream `reasoning_details` (signed chains) yet — signature round-trips work through the Anthropic provider only; the LlmAgent automation node keeps its explicit per-node effort (no default-low there)._

_2026-07-05 — **`search_models` — agents search the gateway model catalog by name/id to pick the right model id for a delegation (§7; user ask: "implement a search_models skill").** The `delegate` nudge says "prefer a cheaper `model`", but the agent had no way to learn what model ids exist — a guessed id fails at call time. New ungated discovery tool `search_models` (`tools.rs`, beside `search_tools`/`list_tools`): takes `{query?, kind?, limit:1-25=10}`, fetches the kind-filtered catalog via the existing `OpenRouterClient::list_models`, and matches **locally** over model id AND display name (the gateway's `?search=` covers ids only) — exact-id hits rank first, then id substrings, then name-only matches, ties sorted by id; both deciders (`filter_model_catalog`, `parse_model_kind`) are pure and unit-tested without a gateway. Returns each match's `id` (the value to pass as `model`), `name`, and `context_length`/`prompt_price`/`completion_price` when known — enough to actually pick the *cheaper* model; over-limit matches add a "narrow the query" note (no silent cap). `kind` defaults to `chat` (the delegation class; `llm` accepted as alias) and an unknown kind is a hard `invalid` (unlike the REST route's silent fall-back to `All`) so the model corrects its call. Ungated like the other discovery tools — the catalog is global gateway metadata, the same list `/llm-models` shows any authed user. **Wiring:** registered in `AppState::new` with the discovery group, before the `search_tools` snapshot (so it's tool-searchable); `DELEGATE_NUDGE` now names it, so per the deferred-advertising rule (§7: prompt-promised tools ride the seed) it's pushed onto both unpinned seeds (web chat `ws.rs`, profile `prepare_run`) and force-appended to both confined allow-lists (chat profile in `ws.rs`, `build_request`) exactly like `delegate` itself; the `delegate.model` + `speech_to_text`/`text_to_speech` `model` param docs point at it. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets` clean; discovery tests 4/4 (+2: ranked id/name matching incl. blank-query browse + no-match-yields-empty, kind parsing defaults/aliases/rejection). Deferred (disclosed): `delegate` still doesn't validate a `model_override` against the catalog at call time (a bad id fails at the gateway with a clear error, and `model_validation.rs` stays the persistence-time guard); the ephemeral-worker system prompt doesn't mention the tool (workers rarely delegate further — and can still discover it via `search_tools`)._

_2026-07-05 — **Workdir file tools now work on sandboxed (container-backed) terminals (§20; user ask: "implement read and create file too" + "and edit file for these terminals too").** `read_file` / `create_file` / `edit_file` used to hard-error `no_host_dir()` on a per-workspace-sandbox session (files live in the container); they now ride the same copy channel `stage_object`/`store_object` already use. **(1) `read_file`:** `FileRoute::InSandbox` stages the file out (`copy_out`) to an ephemeral-root staging temp file, then runs the exact host logic — factored into a shared `read_file_windowed(file, path_label, offset, limit)` free fn (stat + is-dir check + 8 MiB bounded read + line window + 256 KiB cap) so local and sandbox paths can't drift. Whole-file staging is disk-bounded, not memory-bounded — the same trade `store_object` already accepts on this route. **(2) `write_file` (`create_file` tool):** content → temp file → `copy_in` (its script mkdir-ps in-container parents). The created-vs-overwrote flag comes from a prior existence probe run inside the sandbox (`sh -c 'test -e "$1"' sh <dest>`, positional, 10 s timeout, best-effort → `created` on probe failure). **(3) `edit_file`:** copy_out → shared `read_text_for_edit` (refuses over-ceiling / non-UTF-8, same messages) → shared `apply_edit` (uniqueness/replace_all contract) → write temp → `copy_in` back; the local arm now uses the same two helpers. Not atomic vs. a concurrent in-container writer (neither is the local path vs. a concurrent shell). **(4) Free rides:** cross-pod forwarding needed no change — the owner-side `PodOp::ReadFile/WriteFile/EditFile` handlers call these manager methods; `no_host_dir()` is now only `persist`'s (doc updated). Verified: clippy clean; new podman+Postgres-gated e2e `sandboxed_file_tools_ride_the_copy_channel` (TerminalManager over `WorkspaceSandboxManager`/`PodmanSandbox`, busybox: create→overwrite-flag→read→window→edit→re-read proves container write-back, ambiguity contract, missing/traversal errors, close+destroy) — api terminal tests 10/10, pod_forward 11/11. Remaining deferral: `persist_terminal` on a sandboxed session still errors (whole-dir flush needs a recursive copy channel, e.g. `tar` through exec, not the single-file scripts)._

_2026-07-05 — **Exec/terminal method audit + fixes (§20; user ask: "analyse exec terminal methods and fix them").** A systematic pass over the `Executor`/`WorkspaceSandbox` backends and `TerminalManager` found one bug cluster and several one-offs, all fixed. **(1) Shared CLI capture (`catalerum-exec/src/proc.rs`, new):** every CLI-driven backend (container / k8s / both sandboxes) collected output via `Command::output()`, which (a) buffers unbounded — a runaway command in a container OOMs the api worker, the exact failure `LocalExecutor` was already hardened against — and (b) has no `kill_on_drop`, so every `tokio::time::timeout` cancellation leaked a live `podman`/`kubectl` client. `capture_capped` is now the one collector: piped-stdin fed concurrently (no full-pipe deadlock), per-stream 1 MiB cap with remainder drained + truncation marker, `kill_on_drop(true)`; `read_capped`/`finish_capture` moved out of lib.rs and shared. **(2) Remote cleanup on timeout:** killing the CLI client doesn't stop the runtime's detached child, so `ContainerExecutor::run` now names its `--rm` container (`cat-run-<uuid>`) and `rm -f`s it on timeout, and `KubernetesExecutor::run` deletes its pod; the workspace-sandbox `exec` runs document why the in-container process is left (killing it would kill the shared sandbox). **(3) `cmd.stdin` was silently dropped** by all four non-local `run`s while the `run_command` tool advertises it — now piped through (`-i` added where the runtime needs it). **(4) `KubernetesExecutor::run` dropped `cmd.env` and `cmd.cwd`** — env rides `--env`, cwd rides the positional `sh -c 'cd "$1" …'` wrapper (never spliced). **(5) Shell arg-splitting:** a pinned `[exec].shell` carrying flags (`bash --noprofile`) was passed as ONE exec argv token by container/k8s/podman-sandbox session opens (runtime execs a program literally named "bash --noprofile"); `pty::split_command` is now `pub(crate)` and used by all of them. **(6) `K8sSandbox::exec_session` spliced cwd+shell into a `sh -c` format string** (quoting/injection surface, inconsistent with the positional pattern everywhere else) — rewritten to `sh -c 'mkdir -p -- "$1" && cd -- "$1" || exit 1; shift; exec "$@"' sh <cwd> <shell…>`. **(7) `pipe_file_in/out`** (sandbox copy channel) get `kill_on_drop` so an aborted HTTP request can't leak the copy client. **(8) `TerminalManager::open` leaked the live PTY + temp dir when the `terminal_sessions` row insert failed** (session never entered `live`, so even the reaper couldn't find it) — now torn down via the right driver before the error returns. Verified: clippy clean; `catalerum-exec` 28/28 (incl. the podman-gated container-session + workspace-sandbox e2e tests, which exercise the split-shell exec argv and shared capture against real podman) and the 9 `catalerum-api` terminal tests against live Postgres. New `proc::tests` cover exit/stream capture, concurrent stdin feed, closed-stdin default, the 1 MiB cap marker, and timeout-kills-client. Known deferrals: `SessionSpec.env` is still ignored by the sandbox `exec_session`s (the manager never sets it), and a timed-out workspace-sandbox `exec` leaves the in-container process running (documented in the timeout arms)._

_2026-07-05 — **Apps can be pinned: a quick menu flies out beside the Apps nav entry (SOUL §12; user ask: "apps can be pinned, showing up as a quick menu '>' beside apps on hover").** Client-only, no server state. **(1) Pin store (`emerged/pins.rs`):** a `localStorage` list of `{id, title, workspace}` records (the theme-cache pattern) shared through one `RwSignal` created in the Workbench; `toggle` edits signal + storage, and `reconcile_workspace` — run against every `GET /uis` list fetch (Apps panel mount, plus a Workbench-mount fetch that fires only when pins exist) — refreshes stale titles, drops pins whose app was deleted, projects out the current workspace's slice, and leaves other workspaces' pins untouched in storage (apps carry `workspace_id`; the signal only ever holds the active workspace's pins, so a multi-workspace browser doesn't leak pins across switches). **(2) Apps panel:** each sidebar row grows a ☆/★ toggle — hover-revealed (always visible when pinned or on touch viewports), `aria-pressed`, accent-colored when on; `UiDefinition::display_title` factored onto the model (was a local fn). **(3) Nav quick menu (`shell.rs::AppsNavItem`):** when any pins exist the Apps entry (in "More") shows a `▸` beside it; hovering the row (desktop) or clicking the chevron (touch/keyboard, `aria-expanded`, chevron rotates) opens a flyout of pinned apps — absolutely positioned beside the nav on desktop, inline-indented inside the mobile drawer (a right-side flyout would clip the drawer's `overflow-y`). Picking one hands the app id through a one-shot `app_target` signal (the History→Chat `resume_target` pattern) and lands on the Apps panel with that app open. **(4) Deep links:** the selected app now syncs to `/app/apps/<id>` via `replace_state` (the calendar-view pattern) and a reload/deep link preselects it (validated against the fetched list, falling back to most-recent). One real bug caught by live verification, not review: jumping via the quick menu **while already on the Apps panel** re-set `active` to the same panel, remounting it — and the remount raced away the one-shot target before the consumer effect ran (selection silently stayed put). Fix: only switch panels when not already there; the mounted panel's effect applies the target in place. **Verified (live stack, headless chromium):** full flow driven end-to-end — pin via row hover → ★ + chevron appear → hover flyout lists the app → select other app, quick-menu jump back (URL `/app/apps/<id>`, correct row active, stage renders) → reload keeps pin + deep-linked selection → cross-panel jump from Chat works → unpin removes chevron+flyout → garbage `localStorage` degrades to no pins, panel intact; mobile 400px probe (drawer → chevron toggle → inline flyout → pick closes drawer); wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean, web **331** native tests green (+3 `reconcile_in`: title-refresh/deleted-drop/other-workspace-keep, no-change no-write, empty-list can't-identify-workspace), `trunk build` green. **Deferred (disclosed):** pins are per-browser `localStorage` — they don't roam across devices/users (a server-side per-user preference is the follow-up if wanted); on a workspace with **zero** apps the reconciler can't identify the workspace so the flyout just shows nothing (stale cross-workspace pins aren't filtered there — harmless, hidden); the quick menu lives on the Apps entry inside the collapsed "More" section, so it's only visible while More is expanded; a chevron-opened flyout on desktop stays open until a pick or re-click (no outside-click dismiss)._

the two-way `bind` itself stays per-keystroke/local) — for live server-backed lookups; `change` remains the committed-value event. **(2) `app_ref` by name:** core relaxes the target to "ui id or 1–128-char name slug" (`parent_app` stays UUID-only — written once, precisely); new `GET /uis/by-name/{name}` (`ui:read`, workspace-scoped, repo `get_by_name`); `EmergedUi` picks id-vs-name fetch via a `is_uuid_like` heuristic and the **cycle/depth guard moved post-fetch onto the RESOLVED `def.id`** (a name can't be compared to the ancestor chain before the server says which App it is; `UiState.ui_id`/chain always carry the resolved id so `/event` posts stay id-addressed); the shared-namespace verification (`tools::shared_app_namespace`) now accepts the reciprocal `app_ref` matching the child's id **or its name** (child's `name` is on the very row already fetched — no extra read). **(3) Chat-replay load-once guard:** mount-time `load` fires route through `handlers::dispatch_load` — a `thread_local` cache keyed `(ui_id, version, node_id)` holding `Pending(waiting UiStates)` / `Done{at, actions}` (30 s TTL): the first mount performs the one `POST /uis/{id}/event`, concurrent replay mounts join its waiter list, later mounts within the TTL apply the cached actions — sound because every copy of the same `(ui, version)` posts the identical seeded `initial_state` at mount; **navigate-to loads (state has diverged per mount) intentionally bypass the cache** via plain `dispatch` (the mount-vs-navigate split uses the load `Effect`'s `prev.is_none()`); errors clear the slot (later mounts retry) and notice every waiter; actions apply outside the cache borrow (a signal write may run reactions). `get_ui_schema` updated (events cadence incl. debounced `input`, app_ref id-or-name, shell_apps name form, load replay-sharing note). **Verified:** both clippy gates `-D warnings` clean; `select`/`radio`/`checkbox` don't fire `input` (their `change` IS the keystroke-equivalent); the load cache is per-tab (`thread_local`), not cross-tab._

_2026-07-05 — **Emerged UIs, recipe-app-closing chunk: timers, live server-side computed, file/external-DB images, multi-field filters, sub-views, and shell/sub-app suites with a shared durable namespace (SOUL §12; user ask: "timer components / fix live derived values server-side / images from Files + our external DB / multi-field filters + subviews / shell app + subapps so the agent edits smaller files").** Six additive slices across core/api/web. **(1) Timers:** `NodeKind::{Timer,Stopwatch}` (leaf; `duration` seconds — number or `{{path}}` —, `label`, `auto_start`, `controls`), run-state client-only in `UiState.timers` keyed by node id (the tabs/dialogs pattern; never in form `data`), one 250 ms interval per mounted node bumping a local `tick` only while running; a countdown stops exactly at its duration and fires the new `EventName::Complete` **once** per run (guarded by `TimerState::finish`'s bool; validation restricts `complete` to `timer` nodes). Handler-addressable via `ClientOp`/`UiAction::{StartTimer,PauseTimer,ResetTimer}` (server fold = passthrough like `select_tab`), so a recipe step's button can start the 10-minute timer. Pure `TimerState` math (`now` injected; `now_ms()` is `js_sys::Date::now()` on wasm, constant natively) + `format_clock`. **(2) Live computed (the "servings scaler needs a button" fix, server-side per the user's steer):** every input's bind-write now calls `handlers::bind_changed` — a 350 ms generation-debounced `POST /uis/{id}/compute` with a fresh snapshot, stale responses dropped — so `{{computed.*}}` tracks typing/sliding with no authored handler; and the renderer finally fires declared **`change` handlers** on committed values (DOM change: text blur/Enter, select pick, slider release, radio/checkbox toggle) through the normal dispatch path. **(3) Images:** `image.src` accepts `files://<store>/<path>` / `files:<path>` → the authed storage download URL (token-in-query, the files-panel pattern); or a spec-held `db` prop `{connection, sql, params?, column?}` → new `GET /uis/{id}/image/{node_id}?p=[…]` which re-gates like any handler (`ui:read`, `[ui].handler_tools` allow-list via the shared `gate_dispatchable`, then dispatches the real `sql_query` tool under the caller's capped ctx forced to `mode=read, max_rows=1` — so `db:read@<conn>` is enforced on the VIEWER and the client can never run SQL the author didn't write; only bind VALUES ride the URL). The one cell decodes from Postgres `\x…` bytea hex / base64 / `data:` URL, is size-capped (10 MiB), and is served **only** if it magic-byte-sniffs as png/jpeg/gif/webp — never SVG/HTML — with `nosniff`. **(4) Multi-field filters:** `ForEach.filters: [ForEachFilter]` ANDed with the existing `filter` (text search + category dropdown over the same rows), paths validated, rows keep original indices. **(5) Sub-views:** `NodeKind::ViewRef` (`props.view`) renders another view of the same spec inline (shared fragments); unknown targets rejected, an authoring-time DFS rejects `view_ref` cycles, the interpreter's depth cap is the runtime backstop, embedded roots do NOT fire `load`. **(6) Shell suites:** `NodeKind::AppRef` (`props.app` = ui id, UUID-validated) mounts a whole other emerged UI inline (own `EmergedUi`, own state/authority, `ai_sink` threaded through; client cycle/depth guard via a `UiState.app_chain` capped at 4), and `UiSpec.parent_app` + a **mutual, server-verified opt-in** (`tools::shared_app_namespace`: child names parent AND parent's spec `app_ref`s the child, walked ≤4 hops, visited-set cycle guard, fail-closed to self) makes the whole suite share the SHELL's `app_data_*` namespace — so browse/editor sub-apps operate on the same durable rows while a one-sided claim stays isolated (the existing isolation test still passes). Sub-apps (`parent_app` set) are hidden from the Apps panel list. `get_ui_schema` documents all of it (timers/ops, live-computed + `change` cadence, both image sources, `filters`, `view_ref`, and the 3-step shell/sub-app authoring order incl. the namespace rule). **Verified:** non-web clippy gate + wasm clippy both `-D warnings` clean; core 70 (5 new: timer events/ops roundtrip, multi-filter paths, view_ref resolve+cycle, app_ref/parent_app UUID + `collect_app_refs`/`references_app`, image-db shape) · api 435 vs live PG (new: timer-fold passthrough, `image_cell`/hex-base64-dataURL decode/raster-sniff units, and `app_data_shell_suite_shares_namespace` — shell writes, sub reads same row, rogue one-sided claim isolated) · web 324 native (new: TimerState math incl. backwards-clock clamp, `format_clock`, `parse_files_src` forms, `db_image_params` typed-vs-spliced, mirror decodes) + `trunk build` green. _2026-07-05 — **App system rounded out for real data-backed mini-apps (recipe-app grade): `load` lifecycle event, declarative `for_each` filtering, and `list`/`table` collection kinds (SOUL §12).** The emerged-UI vocabulary could render and mutate, but a data-backed App still needed a human to press "Load" (no lifecycle hook), couldn't search/narrow a collection without a server round-trip per keystroke (no client expression language, by design), and had no compact way to present rows (charts or hand-rolled `for_each` cards only). Three additive slices close that: **(1) `EventName::Load`** — append-only in core + the web mirror; fired **client-side** when a view becomes active (mount + navigate-to), for that view's **root node only** (an `Effect` on `st.view` with a previous-value guard against same-id re-sets; `rest::event_token` gains `"load"`). Validation now checks events **per event name**: `load` is legal on containers (a root Stack), everything else still demands an interactive kind — so the old "events only on interactive kinds" rule is not widened for click/submit/…. Server-side it's just another event: `run_handler` resolves it off the node like any other (new api test proves a root-`load` → tool → `result_path` dispatch). The intended pattern — root `load` → `app_data_list` → `result_path` — makes "automation collects → App presents" open populated. **(2) `ForEach.filter`** (`{ query, path?, mode: contains|equals }`) — a declarative, **client-evaluated** row filter: a row passes when the value at `path` *within the item* (whole item when unset) matches the live state value at the `query` path; `contains` = case-insensitive substring (bind a `text_input` to the query path for keystroke-live search), `equals` = JSON equality with scalar↔string coercion (bind a `select` for category filters); a **falsy query passes every row** (an untouched search box shows the full list) and an unknown future mode degrades to unfiltered. Rows keep their **original array indices** (scope bindings, `remove_at`, keys all still address the unfiltered array); `check_path` covers `query`/`path` so the no-expression-language rule holds. **(3) `NodeKind::List` + `NodeKind::Table`** — read-only collection leaves in the chart mold (validator rejects children/bind/events for free): `list` renders `data` (literal / `$path` / `{{path}}`) as `<ul>`/`<ol>` with `item` picking the display path per element; `table` renders an array of objects with `columns` (`["path"]` or `[{header?,path}]`, omitted → derived from the first row's keys, scalar rows → one whole-row column), horizontal overflow scrolling inside the wrapper, both with an interpolatable `empty` text and `for_each`-budget row caps. Per-row *actions* deliberately stay `for_each`'s job. `get_ui_schema` documents all three plus a `durable_data` recipe (root `load` → `app_data_list` → `stored.entries`; write-then-refresh via a script handler calling `app_data_set` then `app_data_list`). New `.eu-list*/.eu-table*/.eu-empty` CSS uses theme tokens only. **Verified:** workspace clippy clean (native `--all-targets -D warnings` + wasm); core lib **65** green (+3: load-on-container-only, filter path grammar, list/table read-only leaves); api lib **427** green vs live PG (+1 `load_event_on_view_root_dispatches`); web trio green — **317** native tests (+4: decode of load/list/table/filter incl. unknown-mode degrade, `filter_passes` matrix, `list_items`, `table_columns`) + wasm clippy `-D warnings` + `trunk build`. **Deferred (disclosed):** `load` fires per mount — a chat transcript replaying N copies of the same App re-fetches N times (idempotent reads; a per-`(ui_id,view)` session guard is the follow-up if it ever hurts); no `sort` counterpart to `filter` yet (authors can pre-sort in the load script); `table` has no column formatters/row-click (use `for_each` for interactive rows); `filter` matches one field — multi-field OR-search needs a `script`-computed derived array._

_2026-07-04 — **Two multi-pod races closed: overlapping collects no longer duplicate automation runs, and chat Stop reaches the streaming pod from any socket (SOUL §11/§12/§16 M7).** **(1) Per-source collect mutex.** Observed in the live 3-pod cluster: one `collect_email` automation (`every: 5m`) produced **373 runs in 84 minutes** in bursts. Root cause: the scheduler's fire lock single-fires only the *enqueue*; under a backlog (pod restart + a 7-day backfill whose inline per-item LLM runs outlive the cadence) several queued collect jobs for the same source were claimed concurrently by different pods, each decoding the same not-yet-committed ledger and fanning out duplicate per-item runs — the collect.rs design note "only one pod runs it at a time" was asserted but never enforced at the *run* side. Fix: `SyncWorker` gains `.with_bus(...)` (wired in main.rs) and both collect arms now take a **per-source distributed mutex** (`collect-src:{connection}` — the connection, because the committed ledger lives on its `sync_token` and two automations sharing a connection share that ledger; automation-id fallback) with TTL 300s + a background refresher (an inline item can be a whole LLM run). Held → the overlapping job **skips as done** (loss-free: the cursor-based next occurrence re-collects); bus *error* → proceed with a warning (§6.6: hint, not oracle — and the enqueue-side lock already thins the herd). **(2) Cross-pod chat turn control.** A turn runs on the pod holding the client's socket; the Stop token, mid-turn queue and ask_user seam are process-local — a stop from a reconnected client (or second tab) behind the round-robin Service silently no-op'd, and two sockets could stream **concurrent turns into one conversation**. Now: `run_turn` acquires a TTL'd **per-conversation turn lock** (`conv-turn:{id}`, 120s, refreshed every 30s by the turn's control listener; waits up to 15 min checking the cancel token; bus error → uncoordinated, chat never blocks on a Valkey outage; `Drop` releases on every exit) — turns on one conversation are serialized across sockets *and* pods, and a queued turn's user message persists only after the streaming turn's rows (clean transcript order). The turn also subscribes the new `cat:conv:ctl:{conversation}` push channel: `StopFrame` gains an optional `conversation_id`, the web client sends it (`send_stop(Some(conv))`), and a **stray** stop (no turn on this socket) is workspace-checked then relayed over the channel — whichever pod streams that thread's turn cancels it. In-process bus gives the same fix to two-tabs-one-pod for free. **Verified:** workspace clippy clean (native + wasm); ingest **75** green (+2: `collect_gate_serializes_a_source_across_workers` — second worker skips while held, proceeds after release, cross-automation same-connection contention; resource-key derivation), api **426** green (+2: `control_channel_stop_cancels_a_streaming_turn`, `turn_coordination_serializes_a_conversation` — queued turn aborts on its user's stop, acquires after release). **Deferred (disclosed):** cross-pod **mid-turn message injection** — a peer-pod send now waits for the lock and runs as the next turn (correct order, not injected into the live exchange); cross-pod **ask_user answers / approvals** still resolve on the asking socket's pod (the durable pending rows already survive reloads); needs the same image rollout as the session-forwarding entry below._

_2026-07-04 — **Cross-pod terminal-session forwarding: Valkey service discovery + AES-256-GCM-sealed pod-to-pod transport (SOUL §16 M7/§20; retires the "route there / enable session affinity" errors as the only answer).** A request landing on a pod that doesn't own a terminal's PTY now **forwards the op to the owner** instead of erroring. **(1) Discovery over Valkey:** new fifth bus role `Registry` (`catalerum-bus/src/registry.rs`: `announce`/`lookup`/`withdraw`, `SET PX`/`GET`/`DEL` + an in-process TTL-map fallback; key `cat:pod:{pod_id}` via `pod_key`). Each pod announces `{"addr":"<ip>:<port>"}` — IP from the new `[server].pod_ip` (`CATALERUM_SERVER__POD_IP`, k8s downward-API `status.podIP`; empty auto-detects the primary local IP via a connected-UDP-socket probe), port from `listen` — initially at boot and re-announced on the existing 30s heartbeat clock (TTL 120s), so a dead pod's entry lapses on its own and a forward to it degrades to a precise "owning pod is no longer reachable" error. **(2) Encrypted transport (`catalerum-api/src/pod_forward.rs`):** one `POST /internal/pod` per unary op, body = `CPF1 ‖ nonce ‖ AES-256-GCM(json)` under a **subkey derived from the shared `[secrets].master_key`** (SHA-256 domain-separated — the raw master key is never a traffic key). The AEAD is the *entire* authn/authz story (only master-key holders can mint/read an envelope; the route takes no session `Auth` and `404`s without a key, exactly the signed-token-route pattern); a sealed timestamp bounds replay to ±30s; a response is sealed against the **request's nonce** (AAD) so it can't be swapped between calls; op errors ride *inside* the envelope with their kind (`invalid`/`provider`/`other`) and are rebuilt on the requesting pod, so a forwarded failure reads exactly like a local one. The `Output` op streams the owner's live PTY as length-prefixed sealed frames with a **per-frame counter in the AAD** (reorder/replay within a stream fails closed) — the web terminal pane works from any pod. **(3) Routing (`terminal.rs`):** `route()`/`file_route()` replace `live_session`/`session_host_dir`'s error-only fallbacks — live handle → local; still-`active` row stamped with a peer pod + forwarder configured → `Route::Remote(pod)`; else the old precise errors (unchanged without a master key, e.g. single-pod dev — the existing attach-guard test still passes verbatim). Forwarded ops: write / read / **read_wait (the owner runs the whole drain-until-quiet loop — one round trip, not one per poll)** / resize / close (owner tears down + marks the row; unreachable owner falls back to a local row-close so the session doesn't stay listed) / persist (owner uploads to the *shared* object store + catalogues/notifies) / read_file / write_file / edit_file, and the `stage_object`/`store_object` tools pre-route via `remote_owner` (the op carries `user_id` so the owner resolves the caller's per-user default store; shared `stage_object_via`/`store_object_via` keep tool and forwarded defaulting identical). Owner side re-checks row ownership before executing (`routes/internal.rs`), so forwarding is one hop by construction — no chains, no ping-pong. **Ops:** `deploy/catalerum.yaml` + the infrazeug chart gain the `CATALERUM_SERVER__POD_IP` downward-API env (+ the manifest's POD_ID, previously chart-only); manifest header + Service `sessionAffinity` note updated — affinity is now a latency optimisation, not a correctness requirement. **Verified:** workspace clippy clean; bus suite 14 green (registry announce/lookup/TTL/withdraw); api suite **424** green incl. 9 envelope unit tests (roundtrip, tamper, wrong-key, stale-replay, response-nonce binding, error-kind rebuild, frame order + chunk-boundary reassembly) and a **two-pod end-to-end integration test** (`pod_forward::two_pod_tests`): pod A owns a real `/bin/sh` PTY behind a live axum `/internal/pod`; pod B (no backends) discovers A over a shared bus registry and drives it — write → waited read sees the command output, the sealed output stream sees the same bytes, write_file/read_file/edit_file round-trip across pods, close via B tears down A's PTY + closes the row; plus a rejection test (garbage body and a wrong-key envelope both bare-`403`). **Deferred (disclosed):** per-workspace **sandbox** ops (`WorkspaceSandboxManager::run`/sessions) still have no pod-ownership guard or forwarding — sandboxed *terminal* sessions forward fine (they live in the terminal manager's live map), but a one-shot `run_command` against a sandbox ensures/creates a per-pod sandbox locally instead of routing to an existing peer's (k8s-backend sandboxes are operator-owned and HA-safe; podman ones can duplicate per pod). MCP SSE `SessionHub` unsolicited notifications remain process-local (unchanged). In-cluster rollout needs the next image build; the manifests are ready._

_2026-07-04 — **Deferred advertising remembers across chat turns: tools discovered on an earlier message stay advertised, so the model stops re-running `search_tools` every message (SOUL §7; "don't re-search tools already discovered").** Two-part fix in `catalerum-llm/src/agent.rs`. **(1) Re-widen from replayed history:** a discovery run's advertised set was re-seeded to the pinned subset on every new chat message even though the prior turns' `search_tools`/`list_tools` results (naming the loaded tools) sat right there in the replayed transcript — the model had to re-search for tools it had already found. `run_loop` now calls the new `rewiden_from_history` before the first turn: it collects the history's discovery-tool call ids (assistant `tool_calls` whose name ∈ `config.discovery_tools`), finds each answering `tool` message, and feeds its content through the existing `widen_advertised` — same `"tools": [{"name"}]` protocol, same allow-list/registry/dedup guards, so a replayed result can't advertise past the run's allow-list any more than a live one could. Replayed messages carry no error flag, but that's inert: error payloads never match the widening shape. **(2) The discovery note says so:** the standing catalog note now tells the model that tools loaded through an earlier discovery call in this conversation are still loaded — call them directly, do NOT re-run `search_tools`/`list_tools` for an already-discovered tool; search only for tools not yet loaded. The added text is static, so the note stays byte-stable for provider prompt caching. Benefits every discovery run whose seed history carries prior discovery results (web chat is the main one; `ws.rs` untouched). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-llm --all-targets` clean; agent suite **23** green (+1: `deferred_advertising_rewidens_from_replayed_history` — seed history with a prior `finder` call + result naming `echo`, assert round 1 of the new run already advertises `finder`+`echo` and the unknown name is still skipped)._

_2026-07-04 — **HTML mail now renders — sanitized server-side, contained in a fully sandboxed iframe (SOUL §28/§12; "fix emails not displaying HTML, securely").** The Email panel used to show an HTML-only body as escaped source (the safe-but-unreadable v1 fallback); now it renders, behind three independent layers. **(1) Server sanitizes:** `GET /emails/{id}` passes `body_html` through the new `sanitize_email_html` (`routes/email.rs`; new `ammonia` dep) — an allowlist pass dropping scripts/event handlers/forms/frames/comments, constraining URLs to `http(s)`/`mailto`/`tel`/`cid` plus `data:image/*` on `<img src>` **only** (an `attribute_filter` that parses with the same URL parser as ammonia's scheme gate, so a tab-smuggled `da\tta:` spelling can't pass one check and dodge the other), keeping inline `style` + the legacy table/font presentation attributes HTML mail is built from, and force-annotating links `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`. The stored body stays raw (sanitizer improvements apply retroactively); raw HTML never crosses the wire. **(2) Client contains:** `render_body` now **prefers HTML** (the message's intended rendering; plain text is the fallback) and renders it inside `<iframe sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" srcdoc=…>` — NO `allow-scripts`/`allow-same-origin`, so the message gets an opaque origin (no cookies/session token/parent DOM/workbench API) and never touches the page DOM (still no `inner_html` anywhere). **(3) The frame document self-restricts:** `email_frame_doc` wraps the body with a `<meta>` CSP (`default-src 'none'; img-src data:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`) + `<base target="_blank">` (links leave the sandbox into a new tab; nothing a message contains can navigate the workbench) + a minimal readable default style; **remote images / tracking pixels stay blocked until a per-message "Load remote images" click** swaps in a document whose CSP adds `img-src https: http:` (a live document's CSP can't be relaxed — the whole srcdoc swaps). The white canvas is intentional and unthemed (HTML mail is authored against light backgrounds). The escaped-source UI (`.email-body-html`/`-note`) is gone. **Verified:** api — clippy clean in the touched files + **421 lib tests pass (4 new:** script/handler stripping, scheme constraints incl. forced `rel`, data-URL gating incl. the smuggled spelling, presentation-markup fidelity + `cid:` survival**)**; web trio green — wasm clippy clean, **310 native tests (1 new:** frame-doc CSP off/on**)**, `trunk build` success. **Deferred (disclosed):** `cid:` inline-attachment images survive sanitization but don't resolve (would need an `/emails/{id}/parts` route mapping Content-IDs to archived attachment objects and rewriting `cid:` srcs to it); no plain-text/HTML view toggle; no per-sender "always load remote images" preference; the iframe has a fixed (user-resizable) height — no auto-sizing, since the sandboxed document can't postMessage its height without `allow-scripts`, which we will not grant._
