_2026-07-04 — **Chat agents author email/calendar ingest end-to-end: source-connection tools, an authoring-time connection-existence guard, scanner hardening, and the editor's reverse commit gesture (SOUL §7/§10/§11/§28; kills the "go to Settings → Connections" LLM-chat confusion).** Observed live: a chat asked to set up Fastmail ingest had no way to create a connection, so it invented a placeholder id (`fastmail`), saved an **enabled** Collect automation with it, told the user to finish in a settings page that doesn't exist, and the scheduler then enqueued a doomed `collect_email` job every tick — WARN spam retrying forever. Four-part fix plus one editor gesture. **(1) Three registry tools** (`tools.rs`): `list_connections` (kind = email|calendar; per-kind `email:read`/`calendar:read` enforced in-invoke — the `query_structured` pattern, §19; each row = `id` + name + the §29 `collecting` flag via `connection_status::is_collecting`; the config blob and its credentials are never returned), `create_email_connection` (`email:write`; imap/jmap/gmail/maildir through the **exact** REST blob — `routes::email::build_email_config` made `pub(crate)`), and `create_calendar_connection` (`calendar:write`; local/caldav/webcal through the new shared `routes::calendar::build_calendar_config`, factored from the route's validate+stamp logic so both surfaces build one shape). Create results carry a `next` hint (wire this id into a collect trigger, `commit_on` the write, enable) so the model finishes the job instead of stopping at the connection. **(2) Authoring guard** `connection_status::validate_collect_connections`, wired into BOTH the `create_automation`/`update_automation` tools and the REST create/upsert (on the *compiled* triggers, so graph and legacy shapes validate identically): every collect trigger's `connection` must parse as a uuid, exist in-workspace, and match the trigger's kind — else an actionable 400/invalid that names `list_connections`/`create_*_connection` and the visual editor's source picker. **(3) Scanner hardening** (`schedule.rs::first_collect_trigger`): a collect trigger whose `connection` doesn't parse as a `ConnectionId` is warned + skipped — pre-guard placeholder automations stop enqueuing doomed jobs, so the retry-spam loop dies at the source (the run-time `parse_connection` check stays as the worker's backstop). **(4) Catalog** (`catalog.json`, collect_email/collect_calendar): description + `connection` param now say "the uuid of an EXISTING connection, discovered via list_connections or created via create_*_connection; placeholders are rejected at save" — and explicitly that there is **no separate settings page**, so the model has no folklore left to hallucinate. **Editor:** the flow canvas accepts the intuitive reverse commit gesture (`flow.rs::wire_edge`, replacing raw `add_edge` on drop): dragging a write node's OUTPUT back onto the collect trigger normalizes into the canonical trigger-`commit`-port edge (one commit target per trigger — rewiring replaces the old gate; never stored as a write→trigger execution edge, which could only cycle), and a meaningless gesture (any edge into a non-collect trigger, a commit gate onto a trigger) surfaces in a new dismissible canvas banner (`.flow-wire-hint`, token-based colors) instead of silently drawing a graph that fails validation later. Rendering follow-up (user screenshot: data edge + commit gate drew as two identical overlapping solid arrows into one anchor): the `.flow-edge-commit` class flow.rs had referenced since the sync-as-automation slice **never had CSS** — now dashed amber (`--warn-fg` tokens) with its own colour-matched `#flow-arrow-commit` arrowhead (a marker can't inherit path stroke), and `edge_endpoints` lands commit gates on the target's **bottom edge** (`commit_anchor_point`) instead of the input port so gate and data edge never overlay; commit port + label got matching amber styles. **Verified (live stack):** clippy `-D warnings` clean (api/ingest/automation native + web wasm); api lib **409** green on the live DB incl. 2 new DB-gated tests (Fastmail-shaped jmap create → stored blob pinned, secrets absent from listings, per-kind gate denies a calendar-scoped caller email listing, dormant→collecting flip once an enabled collector heads at it; placeholder / ghost-uuid / wrong-kind rejections with actionable messages + `update_automation` symmetry); ingest schedule suite green incl. the new placeholder-skip test; automation **78** green (catalog examples re-validate); web trio green — **309** tests (4 new `wire_edge` cases: reverse gesture normalizes, rewiring replaces the gate, meaningless targets error, plain edges pass through; + the commit-anchor separation), `trunk build` success. **Deferred (disclosed):** no `delete_connection` tool (destructive — stays REST/UI); the Gmail path takes a ready refresh token (the OAuth dance stays on the web's google flow); store-direct automation writers (seeds/tests) bypass the authoring guard; and an already-saved placeholder automation isn't auto-healed — the scanner now skips it quietly, but its `connection` must be fixed by hand (which a chat can now actually do)._

_2026-07-04 — **The chat composer stays live during generation: a Stop button, and messages sent mid-turn are placed at the agent's next step (SOUL §7/§12).** Three layers. **(1) Agent loop (`catalerum-llm`):** `AgentConfig` gains `cancel: CancellationToken` (re-exported; default = dormant token, so every existing `..Default::default()` site is untouched) and `AgentOutcome` gains `stopped`. A cancel interrupts at the tightest safe point: mid-stream (`stream_turn` races the SSE against `cancel.cancelled()`; partial text is kept, **half-assembled tool calls are dropped** before persist so nothing dangles), between/mid tool dispatch (the in-flight call's future is abandoned; it **and every remaining call** get a synthesized `{"error":"cancelled…"}` result — emitted as `ToolResult` events, appended, and persisted like real ones, so the transcript stays replayable), or between rounds (no next paid turn). Mid-turn input rides a new `TurnObserver::poll_user_input` hook (default empty): drained at each round boundary — **right after a round's tool results**, and again at a would-be clean finish, where a non-empty drain keeps the loop going for one more round instead of ending the turn (so a message typed during the final answer still gets answered in the same exchange). **(2) WS route (`catalerum-api/routes/ws.rs`):** the socket is now **read while a turn streams** — `drive_turn_future` gained an inbound select arm feeding a per-turn `TurnIntake` (`Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<ClientFrame>>>` + the cancel token). New `{"stop":true}` client frame (disjoint parse from chat/approval; stale stop = no-op) cancels + discards the uninjected queue; same-conversation non-regenerate chat frames queue and `WsObserver::poll_user_input` persists each as a user row **at its injection boundary** (transcript order = what the model saw) and acks it with a new additive `{"type":"user_message", message_id}` frame (also sent for every turn's anchor the moment it persists — live user lines get their regenerate id immediately instead of at `message_done`); everything else (other-conversation turns, regenerates, approval decisions, post-stop frames) defers and re-drives as its own turn after — `handle_socket` now works a `pending: VecDeque<PendingWork>` before reading the socket again. `message_done` gains `stopped: bool`. Also fixed latent: `patch_dangling_tool_calls` on the replay seed synthesizes an "interrupted" tool result for any persisted assistant tool call whose result row never landed (crash / dropped client mid-dispatch previously wedged the conversation on strict providers). **(3) Web client:** composer no longer disables while streaming — the button flips to **"Queue"** and a mid-turn submit pushes a dimmed dashed user line (`ChatLine.queued` + "queued" tag), registers it in a `queued_sends` FIFO, and relays over a per-turn `MidTurnCmd` channel that `drive_turn`'s read loop now `futures::select!`s against `next_update` (send/stop relayed on the same socket between frames); the `user_message` ack stamps the line's server id + clears the dimming (first unstamped-anchor ack goes to the turn's own user line). A **◼ Stop** button appears beside Queue while streaming (`stopping` gates double-stop and queueing-into-a-dying-turn); on `Done{stopped}` the bubble gets a "_(stopped)_" note and any never-placed queued sends are reclaimed — lines removed, text back into the draft, attachments back onto the staging row — so nothing typed is ever lost (same reclaim on error/socket-drop). A `Done` with acks still outstanding keeps reading: the server answers leftover queued frames as follow-up turns on the same socket (fresh bubble per turn). **Verified:** native workspace clippy + wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean; `catalerum-llm` agent suite **22** green (new: injection extends a clean finish, injection lands after tool results, stop mid-stream keeps partial + drops half-assembled calls, stop mid-dispatch synthesizes cancelled results for in-flight **and** never-started calls, pre-cancelled run opens no model turn); api ws suite **12** green (frame disjointness ×3, `TurnIntake::accept` routing incl. stop-discards-queue + post-stop deferral, `user_message` tag, dangling-call patch + idempotence); web **308** green (new: `stopped` flag decode, `user_message`→`UserPlaced`) + `trunk build` success. **Deferred (disclosed):** a stop abandons the in-flight tool call's future — external side effects already in motion (a running terminal command, a sent webhook) are not rolled back; messages queued behind an `ask_user`/approval-deferred turn end are answered as plain follow-up turns (no special form semantics); injected mid-turn messages don't resolve pending `ask_user` forms server-side (only turn-opening messages do); the queued-send path skips the brief pre-turn gaps (conversation still minting / channel not yet open) by declining and keeping the draft; `delegate` subagent runs don't observe the parent's cancel token beyond their dispatch future being dropped._

_2026-07-04 — **A "thinking" toggle for chat threads and the LLM-Agent automation node (SOUL §7/§11/§12).** The reasoning plumbing already ran end-to-end — `ChatRequest.reasoning_effort` → `client.rs` copies it onto the llmleaf SDK request → provider → `StreamEvent::ReasoningDelta` captured, assembled, and echoed back on tool-call round-trips, with the chat UI already rendering the collapsible "Thinking" trace — but **nothing ever populated it**; this wires the two request-side surfaces. **Chat (per-conversation, persisted, mirroring the model picker):** new `Conversation.reasoning_effort: Option<String>` (core model + store `ConversationRow`/`TryFrom` + all six SELECT/RETURNING column lists), migration **0055** (`ALTER TABLE conversations ADD COLUMN reasoning_effort TEXT`), a `ConversationRepo::set_reasoning` setter, and `POST /conversations/{id}/reasoning` (`SetConversationReasoning` body, `conversation:write`, trims blank → clears). `ws.rs`'s `run_turn` sets `request.reasoning_effort` from the thread (blank/unset → provider default). _2026-07-04 — **Auto-compaction: agent loops fold their own context instead of dying at the model's window (SOUL §7/§12) — two layers, in-run + persistent chat-thread.** **(1) In-run, every loop consumer** (web chat, channel/profile runs, `delegate` subagents, `LlmAgent`/`RunSkill` automation actions): new `catalerum_llm::compact` module + `AgentConfig::compaction` (`CompactionConfig { enabled, context_window, trigger_ratio 0.8, keep_recent 12 }`, **default-on everywhere** — the existing `..AgentConfig::default()` sites inherit it with no changes). Before every model turn the loop projects the next prompt — the **max** of a chars/4 estimate and the previous turn's provider-reported `prompt+completion` tokens — and past the budget it folds `messages[system prefix .. tail]` into a dense summary via one extra **tool-less** turn on the run's own model (`COMPACTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT`; output ≤2048 tokens; the summarize prompt itself is front-truncated to half the budget so it fits the same window), splicing a marked user message (`COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX`) in place of the head. The tail boundary skips forward past tool results so the kept tail never opens on an orphaned tool result; a <2-message head refuses (re-folding a lone prior summary is a no-op). **Fail-open by design**: a failed/empty/cancelled summarize warns and proceeds uncompacted — compaction can never be the thing that kills a run. The summarize turn's usage joins the run's accounting (the §19 `cost_limit` sees the spend); a new synthesized `StreamEvent::Compacted { folded, summary }` rides the observer relay + bus (the web mirror's `#[serde(other)] Unknown` arm ignores it until a UI marker lands); `AgentOutcome` gains `compactions` and `context_tokens` (the *final* turn's prompt+completion — the live context size, unlike the summed `usage`). Unknown window → `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` 128k. **(2) Persistent chat threads** (`catalerum-api/src/chat_compact.rs` + migration **0054**): a chat re-seeds from Postgres every turn, so an in-run fold alone is forgotten by the next turn — now, when a turn ends with `context_tokens` (or the estimate over the run transcript) past 0.8× the window, a spawned background task folds everything but the newest ~16 messages (advanced to a **user-turn boundary**) — together with any prior summary — into a **rolling summary stored on the conversation** (`conversations.summary` + `summary_upto`, one tool-less `client.chat` on the turn's model), and the next turn seeds `[summary bridge] + list_recent_after(summary_upto)` instead of the whole history (`CHAT_HISTORY_LIMIT` stays as the coarse backstop; **messages are never deleted** — the conversation view still shows everything, only what the model re-reads shrinks). Invalidation is structural: `summary_upto` is an FK `ON DELETE SET NULL` onto `messages`, so a **regenerate** whose tail-prune deletes the covered anchor nulls the pointer (a half-set pair is ignored as "no usable summary"), and `run_turn` re-reads the conversation right after the prune so even the pruning turn itself never replays against a stale anchor. Window resolution: new `AppState::model_context_window` — the gateway catalog's `context_length`, fetched once per process and cached (a failed fetch returns `None` uncached so a later turn retries; compactor default meanwhile), wired into the ws chat's `AgentConfig` and the thread-fold trigger. **Verified (live Postgres):** full workspace clippy `-D warnings` clean — which also re-verifies the api trio the concurrent deferred-advertising entry below had to defer; llm **52** green (compact units: estimator, max-of-signals trigger, boundary split incl. tool-result alignment, transcript render/front-cap, tool-less summarize request + prior-summary fold; loop e2e ×3: an oversized seed folds *before* the first turn with the summarize deltas never reaching the caller's observer while `Compacted` does, summarize-error fails open on the full history, disabled stays off); api lib **403** green (chat_compact trigger/boundary units); store `conversations_repo` green (summary round-trip, `list_recent_after` strict-after + bound, FK anchor-delete nulls the pointer, workspace-scoped setter). **Deferred (disclosed):** profile/automation/subagent loops run on the 128k default window — `AppState`'s catalog cache isn't plumbed into those runners (they'd need the resolver threaded through `prepare_run`/`action_runner`); the web UI renders no compaction marker yet (the `Compacted` frame is dropped by the mirror's `Unknown` arm) and a folded thread's transcript view carries no badge; only the ws chat turn calls the post-turn thread fold (channel/MCP-origin conversations get the in-run layer only); `trigger_ratio`/`keep_recent` are code constants, not `[llm]` config; two racing turns can both fold (last-write-wins on the summary row — benign, one summary survives); the chars/4 estimator ignores tool-spec/schema overhead (the 0.2 headroom absorbs it)._

_2026-07-04 — **Deferred tool advertising: agent runs no longer ship every tool spec on every request (SOUL §7; ~15k prompt tokens → a pinned handful + an on-demand load path).** Any agent loop without an explicit tool allow-list now advertises only a **pinned discovery subset** up front — `search_tools` + the new **`list_tools`**, plus the tools that run's standing prompts promise (chat: `delegate`, `remember`/`update_memory`/`forget`, `ask_user`; profile/worker runs: `delegate` where it exists) — and a generated **system note** maps the rest of the catalog as `- domain: tool, tool, …` lines (grouped by `required_capability` domain, ungated → `general`; sorted both ways so the prompt prefix stays byte-stable for provider caching). Loading is the **widening protocol**: `AgentConfig::discovery_tools` names the pinned set, and when a pinned tool's successful result carries a top-level `"tools": [{"name": …}]` array, the loop advertises those tools' full specs from the next round on (`ToolRegistry::specs_for`), filtered to the run's allow-list and deduped — advertising is *visibility only*, dispatch still capability-gates every call. `search_tools` results now **embed each hit's argument schema** (so a discovered tool stays usable on later turns — the schema persists in the transcript even though the advertised set resets to the seed each turn), and `list_tools` (registered beside it over the same post-registration snapshot, same `tool_allowed` capability filter, both excluded from their own results) browses names+descriptions (`filter` substring) or loads exact `names` with full schemas + an `"unknown"` echo for refused/missing ones; it needs **no embedder**, so discovery survives an embedding outage. Registry gains `specs_for` + `domain_groups` (core). Wired at every empty-allow-list `run_agent` site: web chat (`ws.rs`), `run_profile`/prepare, `delegate` named-profile + ephemeral-worker runs, and the `LlmAgent`/`RunSkill` automation actions; a pinned profile/skill/action tool list keeps full advertising of exactly that set, and a seed matching nothing registered (e.g. a minimal registry) falls back to advertising everything — degrade verbose-but-correct. **Verified:** core + llm clippy `-D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-core` tool suite green (+2: `specs_for` order/skip, `domain_groups` grouping+allow-list) and `-p catalerum-llm` agent suite **22** green (+3: pinned-seed→widen-across-rounds with per-round advertised-set assertions, allow-list-respecting widening incl. the catalog note, empty-seed fallback with no note injected); api-side `list_tools` unit tests written (catalog capability/filter/sort + `names` schemas/unknown) — api clippy/test run was **blocked at verification time by a concurrent in-flight change** (an unrelated `StreamEvent::Compacted` addition breaking `catalerum-ingest`), so the api trio needs a re-run once the tree settles. **Deferred (disclosed):** no config kill switch — deferral is simply the new default for unpinned runs (pinning tools on the profile/skill/action is the escape hatch); the catalog note lists registry-wide names (minus the allow-list) without per-caller capability filtering — the model may see domains it can't call into (results/dispatch stay filtered); tools of an MCP server connected **mid-run** don't auto-advertise (`connect_mcp_server`'s result doesn't speak the widening protocol) — they're searchable/listable immediately, one discovery call away; `search_tools`' fatter hits (schemas) raise its per-call result size — the `limit` default stays 10._

_2026-07-04 — **Settings gained an "MCP clients" page: copy-paste config for using the workspace from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor & friends (SOUL §12/§26/§30).** A config *generator*, not a config store (`components/mcp_connect.rs`): pick what to expose — the whole-workspace `POST /mcp` or a scripted `/mcp/e/{name}` endpoint (picker fed by the previously web-unused `GET /mcp-endpoints`; hidden when none exist) — pick a product, and copy ready-substituted commands/config. Nine products, each syntax verified against its current docs: Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http … --header` + `.mcp.json`), Codex CLI (`codex mcp add --url … --bearer-token-env-var` + `[mcp_servers.*]` TOML — Codex takes tokens via env, never inline), Cursor (`mcp.json` `url`+`headers`), VS Code (`code --add-mcp` + `.vscode/mcp.json` `servers`/`type:"http"`), Claude Desktop (stdio-only → `npx mcp-remote` bridge, header split through `env` to dodge the Windows arg-mangling bug), Windsurf (`serverUrl`), Gemini CLI (`httpUrl`), Zed (`context_servers`), and a generic tab (curl `tools/list` probe + `mcp-remote` for any stdio-only client). Auth: paste a token, mint a 90-day full-role one inline (the same self-scoped `POST /tokens` as API keys — the secret is woven into the snippets, shown only there), or — for scripted endpoints — mint a **public share URL** (`POST /mcp-endpoints/{id}/token` → `/mcp/s/{token}`), which flips every snippet to header-less; empty token = `YOUR_CATALERUM_TOKEN` placeholder. JSON snippets are built via `serde_json` (never string-spliced), URLs on `api_base()` (the API origin, not the SPA's). Tab classified **per-user, not admin chrome** (members keep it in `multi_user` — connecting one's own agents is the per-user feature; the mint is self-scoped server-side; rationale in `is_admin_chrome` docs). New web plumbing: `MCP_ENDPOINTS_PATH` + tolerant `McpEndpointInfo`/`MintEndpointToken`/`MintedEndpointToken` contract types, `rest::list_mcp_endpoints`/`mint_mcp_endpoint_token`; copy buttons via `navigator.clipboard` (web-sys `Navigator`+`Clipboard` features added). **Verified:** web trio green — wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean, `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **302** (8 new: every JSON snippet parses back, bearer woven in / share mode drops all auth, per-product field spellings pinned as regression tests, Codex env routing), `trunk build` success. **Deferred (disclosed):** no OAuth story (claude.ai custom connectors are OAuth-only, so they can't connect — noted for a future §26 chunk); the share-URL mint takes the server default TTL (no TTL field in the UI); the endpoint picker lists disabled endpoints (marked) but doesn't manage them — there is still no endpoint-management UI._

_2026-07-04 — **`jit_workspace` now bootstraps the workspace it names — closes the fresh-instance SSO deadlock (SOUL §18).** Diagnosed live on the k3s deployment: new images were rolled out and every hop verified healthy (`/status/login` advertises `sso_login_url`, deployed wasm carries the new login view, CORS ok, `/auth/sso/login` 302s to Keycloak, token endpoint reachable + client secret valid via a bogus-code probe) — yet login still bounced `no_workspace`, because prod has **zero workspaces** (`multi_user`, `dev_login=false` never seeds one) and the just-added `jit_workspace` auto-join was **join-only**: it can't join what nothing ever created, and no admin exists to create it — a bootstrap deadlock. Fix: `provision_workspace_membership` factored into a store-only `join_jit_workspace` core that, when **neither** the configured slug **nor** the default workspace exists, **creates** the configured one (default org, canonical name for the `default` slug else the slug; create-race falls back to re-resolve by slug) and then upserts the membership; an archived target stays fail-closed, and empty-`jit_workspace` behavior is unchanged. Also: `GET /auth/sso/callback` failures were **completely silent** server-side (browsers only see the coarse code, JSON only on `?format=json`) — the callback now `warn!`s the real error + code, so the next prod failure is diagnosable from pod logs. Example-config doc updated. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; api lib **394** green on the live DB incl. the new DB-gated bootstrap test (creates+joins as configured role on an empty instance → second user joins the same workspace → archived target denies and writes no membership). Cluster infra (infra-infrazeug) already sets `jitWorkspace=default`/`jitWorkspaceRole=admin` — publish + rollout is all that's left._

_2026-07-04 — **Config can pin the browser-facing SSO login URL (SOUL §18; follow-up to today's login-href fix).** The SPA's `api.<spa-host>` origin derivation is a heuristic; on deployments where the API lives on an unrelated domain (e.g. a Kubernetes ingress) the SSO button pointed at a host that doesn't exist. New `[sso].public_url` (the API's browser-reachable origin) → `SsoConfig::public_login_url` builds the full `/auth/sso/login` URL from it, falling back to the **explicit** `[server].base_url` (never the `http://<listen>` fallback — meaningless to a browser), else `None`. The anonymous `GET /status/login` now advertises it as optional `sso_login_url` (only when SSO is on; `skip_serializing_if` keeps old-shape responses byte-identical), the web's `LoginStatusInfo` mirrors it with a serde default (older servers keep decoding), and `LoginView` builds the href reactively from the probe: advertised URL wins (appending `?redirect=` with `&` when the pinned URL already carries a query), else the `api_base()`-derived href as before — the probe-failure fail-open path keeps the derived href. Example config documented in `config/catalerum.toml`. Also hardened the carried `?redirect=`: `auth::sanitize_spa_redirect` folds paths under `/auth/` to `/` — the old relative-href bundle parked browsers on `{web}/auth/sso/login` (nginx `try_files → index.html`), and carrying that path forward as the post-login landing (`?redirect=/auth/sso/login`, observed live on the k3s deployment) would bounce users back onto a junk path after SSO. Verified: native workspace clippy + wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **294** green (advertised-URL href cases + wire decode + redirect-sanitizer), api config tests **27** green (new precedence test), `trunk build` success. Deploy note: the k3s chart already sets `[server].base_url = https://api.catalerum.…` (charts/catalerum configmap in infra-infrazeug), so the advertised `sso_login_url` needs **no** new cluster config — the broken cluster login is just the stale pre-fix `catalerum-web` image; publish + rollout picks all of this up._

_2026-07-04 — **Login view: the SSO button no longer flashes on dev, and it actually reaches the API (SOUL §12/§18).** Two `LoginView` bugs. (1) `show_sso_button` treated a pending `/status/login` probe (`None`) as "show", so every dev login rendered the SSO button for a frame and yanked it when the probe answered `sso: false` — the "sometimes SSO, sometimes just the magic-link hint" flake. Semantics flipped: the button shows only on a positive `Some(true)`; the fail-open duty moved to the caller — a *failed* probe resolves to `Some(true)` in `LoginView`, so an SSO-only deployment is still never stranded. (2) `sso_login_href` built a **page-relative** `/auth/sso/login`, which only works where something proxies `/auth` to the API (trunk dev does; the production SPA nginx serves `try_files → index.html`, so clicking the button just reloaded the SPA and the OIDC dance never started). The href is now built on `api_base()` (`api.<host>` in production, `localhost:8787` in dev) — the same origin every REST call already uses; the state cookie and callback both live on that origin, so the Lax cookie round-trip is unaffected. Verified: wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **292** green (href/visibility tests updated to the new contract)._

_2026-07-02 — **The four placeholder automation actions are real: `Summarize`, `WriteObject`, `MoveObject`, `Webhook` (SOUL §11/§9/§27; closes the catalog's "currently unimplemented" quartet).** They existed in `ActionKind`, the node catalog, and the web palette but failed at runtime with "no tool runner yet". Now, house-pattern-first: **three ride new registry tools** (so chat agents, `catalerum.callTool` code nodes, and dry-run simulation get them for free) and one is a direct LLM runner. (1) **`write_object`** (tool + action, `storage:write`): create/overwrite a file from `content`/`content_base64` (16 MiB cap) through the shared `write_object_bytes` core — catalogued, §10-ingested, fires `StorageObject`; keyed-idempotent, so redelivery-safe (already in `is_idempotent`). Closes the §29 "no generic file-write tool" gap the app_data entry recorded. (2) **`move_object`** (tool + action, `storage:write`): `copy_object_between` → `delete_object_at(source)` — content lands before the source dies; a delete-half failure errors with "the copy landed, retry to finish"; gating rationale: a move never destroys content while plain `storage:write` can already overwrite anything, and `delete_object` itself gates `storage:write`. (3) **`send_webhook`** (tool + `Webhook` action, **`web:write`** — the previously-meaningless write half of the `web` domain, comment fixed in `catalerum-iam`): JSON `payload` XOR raw `body`+`content_type`, headers (hop-by-hop/Host/Content-Length/Content-Type refused), post/put/patch, per-delivery timeout ≤300 s. Transport is a new **`WebhookSender` core trait** (mirrors `WebFetcher` — catalerum-api builds catalerum-fetch without reqwest) implemented by `HttpWebhookSender` in catalerum-fetch: same `[fetch]` policy + `GuardedResolver` connect-time SSRF screen, **redirects never followed** (a 3xx returns as its status — no re-POST to an unvetted Location), response echo capped 64 KiB; the binary builds it alongside the fetcher (new `AppState::new` param), and a **non-2xx receiver status fails the step** (deliberate divergence from `fetch_url`'s status-passthrough: an unacknowledged delivery must not advance a run or a collect `commit_on` cursor). (4) **`Summarize`** (direct runner, like the collect writes): a **one-shot** `client.chat` — no tools, no loop — over the template-rendered `input` (unset → the firing event via `firing_event`, so the graph wrapper's `inputs` never leaks in), `instructions`/`max_words` extend the system prompt, 200 KiB input truncation with marker, output `{summary, model, cost_usd?}`; checks `dry_run` itself (direct actions bypass registry simulation) so a dry run spends nothing. Catalog: all four docs rewritten (params, templating examples, redelivery + gating semantics, trigger-vs-action webhook disambiguation) — the "unimplemented" keywords are gone from search. Web: four typed forms replace the raw-JSON fallback in the FlowEditor (`summarize`/`write_object`/`move_object` field forms; `webhook` url+method+validated JSON payload/headers textareas that hold last-good params on a parse error), builders pure + tested. **Verified:** workspace clippy `-D warnings` clean; api lib **391** green on the live DB (+ new: summarize request rules ×2, no-client failure, and a DB-gated write→read-back→move→source-gone round-trip on a real local backend); catalerum-fetch **88** (12 new: SSRF/deny-header/redirect-refusal units + live loopback deliveries against a one-shot TCP receiver asserting method/headers/body on the wire); automation catalog tests re-validate every example parses into typed specs; web trio green (wasm clippy, **292** tests, trunk build). **Deferred (disclosed):** `LlmAgent`/`RunSkill` still run their loop under a `dry_run` grant (only their tool calls simulate — pre-existing; Summarize now does check), a one-shot Summarize can't enforce grant `cost_limit` mid-request (spend is reported as `cost_usd`), the webhook web form covers the JSON-payload path only (raw `body` stays authoring-tool/LLM territory), and the embedded-MCP `AppState` passes no webhook sender (send_webhook absent there, matching its `None` fetcher)._

_2026-07-02 — **Config storage backends can be assigned to specific workspace(s) (SOUL §9/§18).**
`[storage]` / `[storage.backends.<name>]` take a new `workspaces = ["slug-or-uuid", …]` list
(`StorageBackendConfig::workspaces`; the top-level field rides into `default_backend()`): empty =
every workspace (the pre-feature behavior, so existing configs are untouched); set = the store
exists **only** for the listed workspaces — matched by slug (case-insensitive) or UUID via
`config::workspace_assigned`. Enforcement is at the seams, fail-closed: `ConfigStore` carries the
assignment and `StorageRegistry` gained `has_assignments`/`visible`/`infos_for`;
`resolve_store` loads the workspace row **only when some store is assigned**
(`visibility_workspace`) and applies visibility to the named lookup (an invisible config store no
longer shadows — it falls through to the runtime layer, then 404s), the per-user default check, the
config default (an invisible default falls back to the sole-visible-store rule), and the sole-store
count; `GET /storage/stores` lists only visible config stores and flags the default accordingly;
the storage-watch worker skips non-assigned (workspace, store) pairs (no useless scans/inotify).
Entries naming a not-yet-existing workspace are inert until it appears (config = immutable base,
principle 10). Known non-goal: the terminal-flush default handle stays global (writes remain
workspace-namespaced). Verified: workspace clippy clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-api --lib` green
(387, incl. the DB-gated suite) with 3 new tests — the config parse/predicate, registry
visibility/filtered listings, and a DB-gated end-to-end `resolve_store` test (assigned store 404s
from the other workspace; default falls back there). Example config documented in
`config/catalerum.toml`._

_2026-07-02 — **Organisations manager UI rebuilt as a two-pane surface (SOUL §12/§18; supersedes the single-column org modal).** `workspace.rs`: the header "Organisations" button now opens a wider two-pane modal — a left **organisation rail** (one entry per org with name, caller-visible workspace count, and an org-role badge; a "+ New organisation" entry hosts the create flow) and a right **detail pane** for the selected org: header (name + slug chip + role badge), a **workspaces section** with proper rows (status dot, name, mono slug, per-row **Switch** button / **current** badge resolved from the caller's `/workspaces` memberships via pure `ws_switch_state` — org-admin shells the caller can't enter offer no switch, org roles confer no data access), admin archive/restore actions, the create-workspace form, and — `multi_user` + org-admin only — the members panel (avatar-initial rows, email sub-line, role badges) + policy picker, plus the owner-only **danger-zone card** (unchanged `org_delete_affordance` semantics). Non-admin members now get a workspace list too (`MemberWorkspaceList` — previously they saw nothing). **Scale:** the shared dev org holds ~1.8k test shells, so the shell panel gained a name/slug **filter box** (shown above `WS_FILTER_THRESHOLD`=8 shells), a `WS_ROW_CAP`=50 render cap per bucket with an explicit "…N more" note, and `order_live_shells` (current workspace → other memberships → admin-only shells, stable within groups) so the caller's own workspaces never fall past the cap. **Both name→slug forms auto-suggest** (`suggest_slug`, kebab-case, editable — server stays the slug authority). New CSS is all token-based (`org-*` block in `lib.rs`). **Two reactive traps fixed en route:** (1) the create-org form must be mounted behind a boolean `Show`, not inside the org-list-reading closure — the post-create refetch remounted it and wiped its "Created organisation …" notice (same flash-and-vanish class as the lifted workspace notice); (2) the detail-pane selection is `Option` ("auto") resolved at render (`resolved()`) — an eager pin ran before the async org list arrived and stuck on the create view. The header switcher (`select.wb-workspace`, `<optgroup>` grouping) and every server contract are unchanged; e2e specs (`organisations.spec.ts`, `org-admin.spec.ts`) updated to the rail/row structure. **Verified (live stack):** web trio green — `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **292** (+16), wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean, `trunk build` success; **e2e 4/4 green ×3 consecutive runs** against the running dev stack (session minted directly in the dev DB — sha256 token-hash row — and deleted after). **Dev-stack gotchas recorded:** the operator's `cargo watch` (`-i crates/catalerum-web/**`) restarts the API on ANY other repo write — including `e2e/test-results/` from a Playwright run and stray files dropped into `e2e/` — so post-e2e browser probes hit restart windows (fetch failures that look like app bugs); the transient `trunk build` "No such file or directory" race with the operator's `trunk serve` remains. **Deferred:** the default org's ~1.8k test-shell debris itself (needs a DB-side cleanup or a paginated shell listing); member rows lack a "you" marker (no self-id endpoint used); no shell pagination server-side (`GET .../workspaces` returns everything)._

_2026-07-02 — **`just dev` external-DB registration no longer WARNs on every cold build (SOUL §17).** The backgrounded `dev-postgres` registration waited 60×1 s for `/healthz` and then **fell through into the registration attempt regardless** — a cold `cargo run` build takes minutes, so every fresh boot printed the misleading "could not register … (is the API up?)" WARN. Now: up to 15 min (450×2 s) with an explicit `api_up` flag; timeout → an honest NOTE ("skipped … registers on the next `just dev`") and clean exit; the residual WARN (API up, registration still failed) now points at the real remaining causes (API logs / master_key). Everything stays idempotent — a skipped run self-heals on the next boot. Verified: `just --summary` parses; both branches exercised standalone against the live API (up-branch breaks immediately, dead-port branch bails to the NOTE)._

_2026-07-02 — **`just dev` defaults terminals to the scrubbed-env sandbox backend (SOUL §17/§20).** One recipe-scoped env export in the `dev` recipe (`CATALERUM_EXEC__BACKEND="${…:-sandbox}"`, the existing dev-override house pattern — committed config stays empty → `local`): a new terminal session no longer inherits the operator's environment, which in `just dev` includes the dev bearer, S3 creds, and the secrets master key the recipe itself exports. Scope is precise: the knob sets only `TerminalManager.default_backend` (config env override → `backend_kind()` → `terminal.rs`); a per-workdir `backend_override` still wins, and `run_command` keeps the local executor as before. Verified: `just --summary` parses; the env→config→terminal-manager chain confirmed in code (no rebuild needed — justfile-only change)._

_2026-07-02 — **Public download redeem now fails closed on archived workspaces — completes the "fail closed everywhere" invariant (SOUL §9/§18; the one redeem surface the adversarial review flagged as inconsistent).** `GET /download/{token}` was the only public redeem lacking an archived check (trigger + webhook + `/auth/switch` + `issue_session` all had one), so a signed link minted before archival kept streaming the now-inert workspace's file/dir for its TTL. Added the same guard right after resolving `ws` from the verified claims — an archived `archived_at` → the opaque `404` every failure on this route already collapses to (`get` returns archived rows by design, flag tested explicitly), mirroring `triggers.rs::reject_archived_workspace`. Read-only + short-window kept it low-severity (why the review flagged-not-blocked it), but the archive feature's own title is "fail closed *everywhere*" — this closes the last gap. Orchestrator-applied inline (one guard, no agent — right scale). **Verified (live DB):** api `--lib --tests` clippy clean; api lib **383** green._

_2026-07-02 — **Restore now works without superuser — disaster recovery no longer requires a superuser DB role (SOUL §30; closes the caveat the round-trip audit surfaced).** The fast path used `SET session_replication_role = replica` (superuser-only SUSET GUC → SQLSTATE 42501 for a non-superuser role, aborting the whole restore) — a real gap for local-first self-hosters running the app under a non-superuser role. Now restore detects `current_setting('is_superuser')` up front: superuser → the unchanged trigger-disable fast path; else a **dependency-ordered restore** — FK graph from `pg_constraint contype='f'` (no special privilege), Kahn topo-sort (`topo_order`, pure/tested; self-refs drop as no-ordering, composite + duplicate FKs deduped by `(parent,child)`), then a single combined `TRUNCATE … CASCADE` (verified per-table reverse-order truncation is impossible — PG refuses to truncate a referenced table even when the child is empty) + `COPY FROM` in parents-first order with FK triggers left ON, all in one transaction. **Honest privilege floor:** the non-superuser path needs table **ownership** (or `TRUNCATE`+`INSERT` grants) and touches no superuser GUC; the one thing it genuinely can't do without superuser is resolve a true FK **cycle** (can't set the GUC nor disable system FK triggers — `DISABLE TRIGGER USER` doesn't touch FK triggers, `ALL` is rejected as a system trigger) — documented + surfaced as a clear error naming the cyclic tables; today's schema is acyclic so it's never hit. **CI exercise:** since the dev role is superuser, a new test builds the engine `.with_force_ordered_restore(true)` to force the ordered branch and asserts every FK join holds after restore into a fresh DB (org→workspace, the composite `sessions (workspace_id, grant_id) → grants`, mcp_endpoints diamond, no orphans) — a wrong topo order would FK-violate during the trigger-on COPY. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean; `catalerum-backup` **16** (12 unit incl. 5 new topo cases: parents-first, self-ref-ignored, composite/dup-dedupe, deterministic tie-break, cycle-detect+name; 4 integration incl. the superuser regression + the forced-ordered path). **Deferred (all acyclic-today, honest):** a future FK cycle for a non-superuser needs `DEFERRABLE`+`SET CONSTRAINTS DEFERRED` or a superuser; a future self-referential FK still relies on the superuser trigger-off path (ordered path treats self-ref as no-ordering)._

_2026-07-02 — **Backup/restore proven to round-trip today's ~9-migration schema — regression guard added; one production deployment caveat surfaced (SOUL §30).** The concern: 0046–0053 added FK edges the restore path never saw (workspaces→organisations, composite session→grant, app_data/mcp_endpoints→workspace, …) and restore *order* matters under FKs. **Audit result — already safe, and now proven:** `pg::list_tables` is fully dynamic (`information_schema`, alphabetical, no allow/deny list — so no new table is silently un-backed-up; the manifest inventory is asserted), and restore is **order-independent by construction** — `SET session_replication_role = replica` disables FK/user triggers for the whole load, then one `TRUNCATE … CASCADE` + per-table sha256-verified `COPY FROM`, commit, restore the GUC. The proof is real, not incidental: `app_data`/`mcp_endpoints` sort *before* their parent `workspaces`, so they load child-before-parent and succeed **only** because triggers are off. New `tests/roundtrip.rs::backup_restore_round_trips_todays_fk_schema` seeds every 2026-07-02 FK edge (org + active/archived workspaces, org membership, grant + grant-scoped session, app_data, connection→mailbox→email with message_id + attachments JSONB, mcp_endpoint, pod_heartbeat, pod-scoped terminal/sandbox), backs up store A, restores into a **fresh** store B, and asserts every FK resolves via joins — a regression guard so a future migration can't silently break restore. Also ruled out the classic COPY-text killers (no GENERATED columns, no tsvector, zero sequences — all PKs UUID/composite/text; bytea + JSONB round-trip clean). **No production code changed.** **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean; `catalerum-backup` **10** (7 unit + 3 integration incl. the new round-trip). **Deployment caveat recorded (report-only, not a backup-crate bug):** `session_replication_role = replica` is a **superuser-only GUC** — the dev `catalerum` role is superuser so restore works, but a hardened prod deployment whose app DB role is NOT superuser would fail restore at that `SET`. Disaster-recovery depends on it, so the prod DB role must hold the privilege (or the deploy must grant it) — a deploy/privileges follow-up._

_2026-07-02 — **Cross-feature adversarial review found + closed three grant-scope/archive authz holes that isolated per-feature verification missed (SOUL §18/§19/§25).** A read-only reviewer attacked the day's ~35 chunks at their *intersections* (not in isolation) and confirmed three bugs sharing one root cause — **grant-scoped tokens carry the minter's `role`+`user_id` unchanged, so any authz reading those directly instead of via `Auth::require`/`capabilities()` silently ignores the grant** (the same class as the ws-chat fix earlier; the review swept for the rest). **Fix 1 (HIGH):** org routes (`require_org_admin`/`require_org_owner`) resolved the minter's org role and never consulted the grant — a token minted `{notes:read}` could delete orgs / manage members / set policy as owner; both gates now take `is_scoped` and fail closed *before* the DB lookup ("grant-scoped tokens cannot administer organisations"), all 9 call sites pass `auth.grant().is_some()`, mirroring `require_workspace_admin`. **Fix 2 (MEDIUM-HIGH):** the collect-authoring gate checked `role_allows(p.role,…)` — a scoped token could author a `CollectEmail` for a connection its grant omitted (and REST automations store `grant_id: None`, so the run-time gate is inert too); now gates on `auth.capabilities()` via `Capability::covers` (grant caps when scoped, role base otherwise — non-scoped behavior byte-identical, only scoped tightened), stale doc-comment dropped. **Fix 3 (MEDIUM):** the channel→agent-profile dispatch path never got the archive fail-closed guard the automation path did — an archived workspace kept running profile LLM loops + replying to inbound messages; `dispatch_channel_to_profiles` (enqueue) and `run_profile_job` (claim, now takes `store`) now no-op on `archived_at`, matching `dispatch_trigger_event`/`run_automation`'s two-layer guard. **The review also cleared five intersections with depth** (ws-chat authority intersects correctly; Fix: the braces are now produced via just's quoted-literal interpolations, wrapped in a small `hs()` shell helper (one inspect per service, stderr silenced so a missing container reads as not-healthy rather than noise). **Verified:** `just --summary` parses; `just up` against the running stack → "backing services are healthy" in **0.9 s** (was 120 s + WARN, every time)._

_2026-07-02 — **Pod heartbeats: dead pods' terminal/sandbox rows now self-heal (SOUL §20/§16 M7; closes the pod-ownership entry's heartbeat follow-up — which mattered more than disclosed: under the shipped Deployment, replaced pods get random names and NEVER return, so lingering rows were the common production case).** New `pod_heartbeats(pod_id PK, last_seen)` (migration `0053`); every process upserts on a 30 s tick (best-effort, warn-never-crash) and the same tick sweeps rows whose owner is **provably dead** — grace 5 min (10× the interval; a paused-but-alive pod resuming within grace keeps its rows), reclaim = the boot-reconcile semantics (rows only — the dead pod's PTYs/containers died with it). **The two safety rules, reasoned + documented where they live:** (a) *never-heartbeated pods are never swept* — the sweep matches only `pod_id IN (SELECT … WHERE last_seen < cutoff)`, because a pre-heartbeat-code pod in a rolling upgrade never writes a row and its live sessions must survive (those fall to the legacy NULL/boot path); this also shields a just-booted pod; (b) *boot ordering* — main.rs writes the FIRST heartbeat synchronously after `AppState::new`, before boot reconcile and before `serve()`, so any row a pod owns is always backed by a fresh heartbeat and a peer's concurrent sweep can never see it stale. Sweep is **naturally idempotent** (UPDATE matches only non-closed rows of stale-heartbeat pods) so it runs unlocked on every pod; heartbeat rows prune at 7 days. Manifest terminals note updated (self-heals within grace). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean (store `--all-targets`, api `--lib --tests`, binary `--all-targets`); `pod_heartbeats_repo` 4 + terminals 3 + sandboxes 3 (reclaim/never-heartbeated/NULL-exclusion/fresh-survival/grace-boundary/idempotence/prune); store 16, api lib 378; migration 0053 applied. **Disclosed:** a one-time rolling-upgrade transition can strand pre-heartbeat pods' rows (bounded to that upgrade — everything after self-heals); a >5-min-stalled-but-alive pod's swept session stays drivable via its live handle (only `list` omits it) — accepted at grace ≫ interval._

_2026-07-02 — **Terminal/sandbox rows are pod-owned: rolling restarts no longer stomp peers' live sessions (SOUL §20/§16 M7; closes the multi-pod-HA entry's boot-reconcile deferral).** **Identity:** `CATALERUM_POD_ID` env → `HOSTNAME` (k8s-native) → random UUID, resolved **once** at boot into `AppState.pod_id` and handed to both managers (never re-derived — the random fallback must stay stable in-process). **Ownership:** every terminal-session `open` and sandbox `ensure` stamps the creating pod; additive migration `0052_session_pod_id.sql` (nullable `pod_id` on both tables, no index — boot-only reads). **Scoped reconcile:** boot now calls `close_all_active_for_pod`/`mark_all_stopped_for_pod` with the rule `pod_id = $me OR pod_id IS NULL` — a restarting pod reclaims its own + legacy-NULL rows; **peer rows survive** (integration-tested: peers untouched, own+NULL reclaimed, idempotent, peer reclaims on its own restart). **Attach-guard improvement:** a cache-miss on driving a session now consults the durable row and answers precisely — "owned by another pod (X)… enable session affinity" vs "no longer live on this pod" vs the generic unknown/closed — DB lookup only on the already-error path. Manifest terminals note updated (comment-only): stomping fixed; sticky `sessionAffinity` remains the answer for *driving* a session. **Disclosed limitation:** a permanently-dead pod's rows linger until an operator clears them or the hostname returns — no heartbeat exists, so "seen recently" is unknowable; the **pod heartbeat table** is the recorded follow-up. Idle sweep skipped honestly (`terminal_sessions` has no `last_activity`; the reapers work off in-memory, pod-local clocks — schema churn not justified this slice). `session_host_dir` file-ops on a foreign-pod session still fail with a raw I/O error rather than the precise message (noted). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB via `just up`):** clippy clean (store `--all-targets`, api `--lib --tests`, binary); store 16 + `terminals_repo` 3 + `workspace_sandboxes_repo` 3 (incl. both new scoped-reconcile tests; migration 0052 applies); api lib **378** incl. the pod-id resolution-order and foreign-pod attach-error tests._

_2026-07-02 — **Channel dispatch is deduped — the leader-lease fencing window can no longer double-reply (SOUL §25/§6.2; closes the multi-pod-HA entry's exactly-once follow-up).** Per-provider `message_id` reality first: Matrix event ids are globally unique and always present; **Telegram message ids are unique only per chat** — and a blank-`chat_id` channel accepts any chat, so the recorded `{channel}:{message_id}` key would false-dedup two chats' message #7 → the claim key **deliberately folds `source` in**: `channel-msg:{workspace}:{channel}:{source}:{message_id}` (a disclosed correctness deviation; Matrix's constant room-id source is harmless there); Discord/Slack are outbound-only (empty subscribe stream — never reach dispatch). Downstream has no natural idempotence (dispatch enqueues fresh-UUID jobs), so the claim sits at dispatch: `try_acquire` on the bus, **TTL 600 s** (≫ the 45 s lease fencing window), guard dropped **un-released** (expires, never freed); loser skips with a debug log; **no `message_id` → dispatch unconditionally** (never drop mail); **bus error → fail open** (at-least-once floor preserved). Durability honesty in the module doc: a Valkey restart inside the window degrades to the pre-existing at-least-once — deliberately no Postgres ledger (a duplicate is a redundant reply, never corruption). One file touched. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** api `--all-targets` clippy clean; channel tests **17** green (+3: key shape, overlapping-pods-dispatch-once, no-id-passthrough); api lib **378**._

_2026-07-02 — **Gmail push (`users.watch`) resolved documented-impractical; push stays calendar-only (SOUL §8/§16 M7; closes the Gmail-token-store entry's deferred push half — investigation only, nothing built).** Unlike calendar's `events.watch` — which takes a per-channel `address`+`token` and POSTs straight to `/webhooks/google/calendar`, enabling the per-connection HMAC channel-token routing in `google_channel_link.rs`/`google_calendar_push.rs` — Gmail's `users.watch` takes only a Pub/Sub `topicName` and publishes to a **shared** Cloud Pub/Sub topic → one push subscription → one endpoint for all mailboxes. So the per-connection-token escape does not exist: the sole routing key is the notification's `emailAddress`, which the connection doesn't store (`connection_spec_for_kind` stamps `{provider:gmail,label:INBOX}`; sync reads `emailAddress` from `getProfile` only to seed the `historyId` cursor and discards it). Operator burden for push: a Pub/Sub topic, a Publisher grant to `gmail-api-push@system.gserviceaccount.com`, a push subscription at `{base_url}/webhooks/google/gmail`, OIDC-bearer or URL-secret auth (+ possible domain verification), and 7-day `users.watch` renewal — versus calendar's zero-extra-infra "just a public HTTPS base_url." The payload carries only `{emailAddress, historyId}` and no message content, so a notification means "poll now" (the delta still runs `history.list` from the stored cursor) — pure latency, identical benefit to calendar push. Given the `CollectEmail` `every` cadence is clamped to `[60 s, 1 week]` (floorable to `30s`), that latency is already bounded; the Pub/Sub infra + shared-topic routing mismatch is poor ROI for the self-hosted audience, and honest OIDC verification would need `jsonwebtoken` added to api's Cargo. **Supported answer: cadence polling (`every: "30s"` floor).** Deferred (if ever revisited): stamp `config.account_email` from `getProfile` for email-keyed routing; expose a public Google-OIDC-verify helper from `catalerum-iam` (which already holds `jsonwebtoken`+JWKS) rather than adding the dep to api; `[google].gmail_push`/`pubsub_topic` knobs + a `users.watch` kind in `GoogleWatchWorker`._

_2026-07-02 — **MCP push goes cross-pod: the SSE hub rides a new generic bus role (SOUL §6.2/§26; closes the MCP-SSE deferrals in both the streamable-HTTP and multi-pod-HA entries).** The bus grew its **fourth role**: `PushBus` (`bus/src/push.rs`) — generic raw pub/sub (`InProcessPush` broadcast / `RedisPush` PUBLISH-SUBSCRIBE, mirroring `TokenRelay`'s shape, no new deps) — because nothing on the bus previously carried arbitrary bytes. Bridge (`api/src/mcp_push_bridge.rs`, in api because catalerum-mcp has no bus dep and Cargo is frozen): one channel `cat:mcp:push` with `PushEnvelope{origin, workspace, message}` — a single subscriber task per pod filters by workspace and forwards **byte-identical** pre-serialized JSON-RPC into the local hub (new `SessionHub::deliver_serialized`; framing untouched). **Loop prevention** had to differ from the chat relay's role-separation (here every pod both publishes and subscribes): a per-process **origin nonce** — publish delivers locally then relays; the subscriber skips its own origin. Degradation: in-process bus → the nonce skip makes the round-trip a no-op (single-pod behavior unchanged); bus errors warn and never touch local delivery; subscriber resubscribes on stream end (push = latency, not correctness, per §26). `routes/mcp.rs` drops its process-local `SESSIONS` static for the bridge-owned hub; one additive spawn line in `main.rs`. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean (bus+mcp `--all-targets`, api `--lib --tests`); bus **10** (+4 push), mcp 20+14, api lib **375** (+3 bridge: two-pods-exactly-once + no-self-loop, single-pod degradation, relay-sans-subscriber); binary compiles. **Deferred/disclosed:** still **no producer** (deliberate — the seam is now the public `publish_mcp_push` API for the first real one; no fabricated traffic); one global channel + envelope routing chosen over per-workspace channels (avoids pattern-subscribe); cross-pod ordering not guaranteed (fire-and-forget relay — acceptable for best-effort push)._

_2026-07-02 — **Plaintext Google credentials now heal themselves: opportunistic resealing + config scrubbing + in-place re-auth (SOUL §13/§28; closes the Gmail-unification entry's deferred tail).** The blocker fell first: `ConnectionRepo` gains `set_credential_ref(ws, id, Option<&str>)` (touches only that column) and `scrub_config_keys(ws, id, &[&str])` — the **targeted** `config - $keys` delete chosen over a whole-config update so it can't clobber concurrent additive writers like the watch-state `jsonb_set` path. **Reseal sequence (order is the safety argument, documented in code): seal → set_credential_ref → scrub**, gated on `master_key` present + `credential_ref` absent, and only after a **successful refresh-grant proves the plaintext creds work**. Crash-window analysis: die after seal → an orphaned (encrypted, unreferenced) vault entry, connection still plaintext, next sync retries; die after ref → the sealed path takes over next sync and a **residual-scrub** on later syncs removes the lingering plaintext keys (the one window that wouldn't self-heal otherwise — healed explicitly); once sealed the reseal can't re-fire (idempotent).
