api 370 / ingest 72 / store 16._

_2026-07-02 — **Per-App durable state: investigated from the handler's seat, verdict WARRANTED — the `app_data` KV + 4 tools are BUILT (SOUL §12/§19; resolves the §29 "per-App durable state" store half).** **The worked example is the finding** (a habit tracker persisting one JSON doc per user, costed through every primitive an App handler can actually reach via the default `[ui].handler_tools` allow-list): **files are blocked outright** — there is NO generic file-write tool in the registry at all (only copy/mkdir/delete/download-link), `read_object` isn't allow-listed and returns the async-extracted §10 *text*, not the raw bytes (lossy, eventually-consistent read-after-write) — so SOUL §12's "objects + files + sql_query cover it" was aspirational; **notes** work mechanically but are semantically wrong (whole-doc read-modify-write, pollutes the Notes panel + semantic index, keys encoded in titles); **memories/tasks** leak App state into LLM recall / board views; **external Postgres** is admin-heavy (real server + connection + db caps + CREATE TABLE) and per-connection, not per-App; **`initial_state`** is a capped authoring-time seed. A `(workspace_id, app, key) → JSONB` table with thin tools is *less* machinery than making files work. **Built:** migration `0051_app_data.sql` + `AppDataRepo` (get/set/list/count/delete; caps: 64 KiB/value, 1000 keys/app, enforced in `set`); tools `app_data_get/_set/_list/_delete` (get/list `ui:read`, set/delete `ui:write` — both within base-Member, so `tool` AND `script` handlers reach them confirm-free; a Viewer's App can read but never write) added to the default `handler_tools`. **Key design finding:** the runtime couldn't supply the App identity — `ToolContext` gained `ui_id`, set only by the emerged-UI dispatcher, and from an App handler the namespace is **forced** to it (a spoofed `app` arg is ignored); from chat/automation (no `ui_id`) the caller names the app id explicitly — exactly how "automation collects → App presents" writes in, and it answers the §29 binding sub-question for app_data: **resolved per call from context, not pinned in the spec**. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean (core+store `--all-targets`, api `--all-targets`); api lib **370** green (+3: repo CRUD+caps, capability gating, forced-namespace cross-App isolation); store green (0051 applies). **Deferred:** per-user isolation within one App (key convention, e.g. `habits/<user_id>`); name-slug→id resolution for the automation path (id is the safe namespace — names are optional/mutable); no per-key versioning (last-writer-wins); the bucket/external-DB **binding-declaration half** of the §29 question stays open._

_2026-07-02 — **Multi-pod HA: audit-first hardening + a deployable k8s manifest (SOUL §16 M7).** **The audit is the deliverable** — every background loop/shared path classified: **(a) already safe** — job-queue drain (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` + atomic stale-reclaim), schedule scans (bus lock keyed `(automation, deterministic fire-instant)` — per-pod `last_tick` divergence still collides on the key), backup (window-keyed lock held a full interval), google-watch (per-connection lock), chat relay (Valkey pub/sub — cross-pod by design); **(b) double-fires-but-harmless** — storage watch (idempotent upsert/purge scans; caveat: `local` inotify assumes node-local FS), MCP `SessionHub` (documented process-local SSE); **(c) genuinely unsafe, FIXED** — **channel listeners**: every pod subscribed Matrix/Telegram with its own in-process cursor → **every inbound message dispatched N times** (duplicate triggers, duplicate agent replies) — now a per-`(workspace, channel)` leader lease (`leader:channel:{ws}:{name}`, 45 s TTL, 15 s refresh interleaved with the stream via `select!`, losers re-contend after 10 s, definitive loss stops consumption immediately, transient bus errors ride the TTL slack; uncontended in-process bus = single-pod behavior unchanged); and **link-signer divergence**: unset `download_secret`/`trigger_secret` meant per-pod random keys (pod A's links 404 on pod B) — now sourceable from a k8s Secret via new `CATALERUM_SERVER__DOWNLOAD_SECRET`/`__TRIGGER_SECRET` env overrides (dev fallback unchanged). **Fencing honesty (documented in module docs):** the lease is `SET NX PX` coordination, not a fencing oracle — a stalled leader's socket can outlive its lease, so for that window two pods may both dispatch (at-most-once degrades to at-least-once; duplicate = redundant reply, never corruption; exactly-once needs provider-side `message_id` dedup — recorded); the bus `refresh`/`release` ARE guard-token-fenced (existing stale-guard test). **Manifest** (`deploy/catalerum.yaml`, joining the operator's existing `deploy/` kustomize tree): **one combined Deployment at N replicas** (default 3 — the audit proves the whole process scales; **requires Valkey**, else every pod acts alone), RollingUpdate maxUnavailable:0, `/healthz` liveness/readiness/startup probes (the path is `/healthz`, not `/health`), ConfigMap+Secret wiring, PDB, ExternalName stubs; the sandbox operator stays its own `replicas: 1` Deployment (referenced, not duplicated). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run):** api `--lib --tests` + binary clippy clean; channel_listener 2 green (leader-lease single-pod test), bus 6 (incl. the fencing CAS test), api lib 367; manifest parses (6 YAML docs). **Deferred (documented in-manifest):** terminal/sandbox **boot reconcile stomps peer pods' rows** (`close_all_active`/`mark_all_stopped` — the fix needs a `pod_id` ownership column + sticky sessions; PTYs/podman are inherently pod-local — run 1 replica, use affinity, or the operator-owned k8s sandbox backend); MCP SSE cross-pod relay; channel exactly-once dedup._

_2026-07-02 — **Gmail joins the encrypted Google token store — the plaintext-credentials finding is closed (SOUL §13/§28; the calendar OAuth entry's security follow-up).** `GET /auth/google/connect?kind=email` now works: per-kind scope (`gmail.readonly`) + per-kind capability gate (`email:write`), same state cookie/callback, the callback creating/rotating an **Email connection** ("Gmail", `{provider:"gmail",label:"INBOX"}`) with the identical sealed `{client_id, client_secret, access_token, refresh_token, expiry}` blob behind `credential_ref` — which turned out to be a shared column on ALL connection rows, so **no migration**. Provider: `GmailAuth::Sealed` mirrors the calendar seam byte-for-byte (single-flight refresh under a cache lock, rotation persisted, 60 s expiry skew) — mirrored locally as `GmailTokens`/`GmailTokenStore` because email can't depend on calendar (Cargo frozen); ingest's `SecretGoogleTokenStore` implements **both** traits over the same decrypted bytes, so one encrypted entry serves both kinds. **Back-compat: warn-only, no resealing (deliberate):** `credential_ref` present → sealed (master_key absent = clear error, never a plaintext fallback); absent → the legacy plaintext path keeps syncing with a one-per-sync warn naming the connection and pointing at the connect URL. Opportunistic resealing was rejected for this slice — it needs a set-credential repo method (deliberately unadded since the calendar entry) plus plaintext scrubbing; too risky in one slice. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean (email+ingest `--all-targets`, api `--lib --tests`); email **49** (+13 gmail incl. sealed-path, refresh state machine, JSON-shape-matches-calendar, plaintext-still-green); ingest all green; api lib **364** (google_oauth 15); binary builds. **Deferred:** plaintext scrubbing/resealing (needs the set-credential method); Gmail push (`users.watch`)._

_2026-07-02 — **Sole-user caches: investigated honestly, resolved as a profile-only mode-gated cache (SOUL §18; resolves the §29 "sole-user caches" question).** **Findings first:** the per-turn personalization in the chat path is (a) the profile — one indexed single-row Postgres SELECT, message-independent, cacheable; (b) recall — an embedding call over the **current message** + Qdrant search, **inherently per-message, never cacheable**; there is no static memory injection, so memory writes cannot stale anything cacheable (the hypothesized memory-write bumps were deliberately dropped as no-op theater), and the cacheable read is trivial next to an LLM turn — this resolves the question with a correct mode-gated primitive rather than a claimed speedup. **Implementation:** new `personalization_cache.rs` — a workspace-scoped **generation counter** + per-`(workspace,user)` TTL'd (5 min backstop) profile snapshots; `AppState::cached_profile` is the read-through (byte-identical to a direct read; `multi_user` never consults — `DeploymentMode::caches_sole_user()`), `bump_personalization` is called by every editable profile write path (`update_profile`, onboarding `complete`); fills are race-safe (generation captured before the read, stamped on put — a racing write leaves the entry stale-marked, never stale-served; no nested locks). Mode flip = restart; the fresh process never reads the process-local cache — that IS the flip story. Prewarm skipped (no clean sole-user id at boot; first read warms). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** api `--all-targets` clippy clean; api lib **364** green (+8: generation/hit/miss/TTL/race/isolation/mode-gate). **Deferred:** the highest-value consumer — the per-turn profile fetch in reserved `routes/ws.rs` (~L486) — still reads directly; one-line `cached_profile` adoption when the file frees (the cache is meanwhile live on `GET /profile`, not dead code); `llm_settings` equally trivial, deliberately not cached._

_2026-07-02 — **SSO callback failures now explain themselves — coarse error codes, nothing reflected (SOUL §12/§18; closes the login-view entry's error-banner deferral).** The callback's user-facing outcomes map to a closed `SsoErrorCode` enum in a `302 /?sso_error=<code>` redirect: `jit_disabled` ("ask an administrator to invite you"), `email_linked`, `no_email`, `no_workspace`, and `failed` — where **every** security-sensitive fault (CSRF state mismatch, signature/exchange/id_token failures, missing/expired state, IdP-returned errors) funnels through one constructor into the indistinguishable `failed` bucket (test-guarded: `failed_bucket_never_carries_a_specific_code`); provider error text and claims never reach the redirect; `?format=json` keeps the JSON responses; SSO-unconfigured stays a plain 404 (route-doesn't-exist, mirroring `/auth/sso/login`). **Web:** `LoginView` reads-and-scrubs `?sso_error=` exactly like the token param (via generalized `parse_query_param`/`strip_query_param`, old token helpers delegating) and renders a `role="alert"` banner with `--err-*` tokens; unknown codes fold to the generic message (tested with `../../etc/passwd`/`<script>`-shaped inputs — the raw param never reaches the DOM). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** api `--lib --tests` clippy clean, api lib **353** green (sso module 17); web wasm clippy (`--all-targets`) clean, **279** green, trunk build. **Disclosed edge:** a user holding a live session whose background SSO callback fails lands in the Workbench with the param lingering unshown until next navigation (they're logged in; scrubbing is scoped to `LoginView`)._

_2026-07-02 — **Google Calendar push channels: `events.watch` → prompt collects, opt-in and fail-safe (SOUL §8/§11/§16 M7; completes the same-day OAuth entry's deferred push half).** **Lifecycle** (new api-side `GoogleWatchWorker` mirroring `StorageWatchWorker` — an architecture adaptation: the HMAC signer needs api-only deps, so the scan lives beside the signer rather than in the ingest scheduler; the watch HTTP itself is `calendar/src/google.rs` `start_watch`/`stop_watch`, re-exported through ingest): triple-gated opt-in (`[google].push=true` + `[google]` enabled + https `base_url` + `master_key`, warn-and-skip otherwise — poll cadence stays the correctness fallback, push is pure latency); per Google connection a watch is ensured iff ≥1 **enabled** `CollectCalendar` automation names it (dormant model), renewed within a 1-day lead (new channel created before the old stops — no coverage gap), stopped when no collector remains; hourly tick, per-connection bus-lock single-fire. **State** rides the connection's `config.watch` JSONB (additive `ConnectionRepo::set_watch_state`, `jsonb_set`-based — **no migration**). **Webhook:** public `POST /webhooks/google/calendar` (static route wins over the authed `/webhooks/{*path}`) authenticated solely by `X-Goog-Channel-Token` = HMAC-signed `ChannelClaims{workspace, connection, exp}` (new `google_channel_link.rs`, `trigger_link` house style, constant-time verify; token minted to outlive its channel by a day); `sync` handshake → 200-ignore; real states → resolve connection from claims → `enqueue_collect_now` per enabled collect automation; verify-failure/archived → **opaque 404**. **Burst debounce:** a 10 s bus lock (`google-push:{conn}`) lets the first burst-mate through and 200-acks the rest — a lock hiccup favors delivery, and duplicates are harmless anyway (committed ledger). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** calendar **56** (+4 watch fixtures); ingest green; store `connections_repo` 3 (+watch-state round-trip, config not clobbered); api `--lib --tests` clippy clean; api lib **353** (+7) — this re-run also clears the pending gates the attachments and grant-tokens entries noted; binary clippy clean. **Deferred/disclosed:** with `push_secret` unset the per-process random key means channels created before a restart 404 until the scan renews them (set `push_secret` for durability, mirrors `trigger_secret`); Gmail `users.watch`; no push for CalDAV/local; `X-Goog-Channel/Resource-ID` not cross-checked (signed claims are authoritative); one watch per connection (`primary`)._

_2026-07-02 — **JMAP raw blobs: messages now carry raw bytes, so archival works there too (SOUL §28; closes the attachments entry's JMAP deferral).** The session fetch now captures the RFC 8620 §6.2 `downloadUrl` URI template (optional — a server omitting it just disables archival, never fails sync) and the full `Email/get` requests `blobId`; each **emitted** message (never re-listed known ids — cost mirrors IMAP's per-changed fetch) gets its raw blob via minimal `{var}` template expansion (percent-encoded) and a bounded stream read (`read_bytes_capped`, the raw twin of `read_json_capped`, same 64 MiB cap). **Fail-soft:** any failure — transport, non-2xx, cap — warns and yields `raw: None`; the message still upserts and the sync succeeds (archival simply no-ops for it), exactly the pre-existing behavior. One file touched (`jmap.rs`). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run):** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean; email **42** green (+5: template expansion/encoding, blobId round-trip, fake-transport blob-success and blob-404 syncs). **Deferred:** only RFC 6570 simple `{var}` substitution (all JMAP uses); `type`/`name` vars filled with generic hints._

_2026-07-02 — **Grant-scoped API tokens: a minted bearer can carry a §19 grant — external MCP clients hold attenuated authority (SOUL §19/§26; closes the §29 "MCP transport" token-issuance remainder).** **Principal shape (locked):** a grant-bound token is a **member-shaped principal with the grant's capabilities** — `Auth{principal, grant}` where `capabilities()` returns the grant's caps (else role base) as the single source of effective authority; `require()` routes grant-bound checks through the existing `core::capability::allows` (no second matcher); **`require_workspace_admin()` always fails for a scoped token** regardless of the minter's role (admin is role-derived, never inheritable by a scope). Enforcement consults `auth.capabilities()` at: `POST /mcp` (`ToolContext` from effective caps — the point of the feature: `tools/call` is grant-bounded), every REST `auth.require(...)` for free, and `routes/ui.rs` (**closed a latent over-authorization**: a scoped token with `ui:read` previously fired emerged-UI handler tools at full role authority). **Fail-closed:** the extractor re-resolves `grant_id` fresh each request; deleted/foreign grant → 401, never a silent role fallback (the automation recorded-grant precedent) — and the DB backs it: migration `0050_session_grant.sql` adds `sessions.grant_id` with a composite same-workspace FK **`ON DELETE CASCADE`** (nulling would silently escalate; cascade revokes). **Mint gate:** `POST /tokens` takes `grant` (id or name, workspace-scoped); every grant cap must be ⊆ the **caller's own effective authority** (grant caps if the caller is itself scoped — scoped tokens mint only narrower tokens) via the same `attenuate` machinery grants use; 403 on excess, 400 on unknown/cross-workspace. CLI `catalerum token --grant` mirrors it. Panel: grant picker on mint + grant name in the listing. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** iam+store clippy clean, iam **50**; `session_grant_repo` DB test green (round-trip, cross-workspace FK rejection, cascade-revoke; orchestrator fixed its fixed-token-hash collision against the shared dev DB → run-scoped hashes); api `--lib` clippy clean; agent's api lib run **337** green incl. mint-gate + grant-vs-role enforcement tests (orchestrator re-run pending the push-channels agent's transient config churn); web trio green (**276** + trunk). **Deferred/handoffs:** **`routes/ws.rs` chat loop still builds `ToolContext` from role base caps (~line 503)** — a grant-bound token used on `/ws/chat` runs tools at full role authority; one-line fix (`base_capabilities` → effective caps) when that reserved file is next in scope, `Principal.grant_id` already carries the data; revocation fan-out across pods; per-token TTL narrowing UX; grant-capabilities display in the panel; full HTTP mint→`/mcp` integration harness._

_2026-07-02 — **Email attachments + raw `.eml` archival: bucket-and-link, one mechanism (SOUL §9/§10/§28; resolves the §29 attachments question AND closes the 2026-06-26 "raw archival dropped" deferral).** After a `WriteEmail` commits, the raw message archives to `emails/<mailbox_id>/<uid>/raw.eml` and each attachment to `…/attachments/<n>-<sanitized>` in the workspace owner's **default files store** (resolved like a chat upload; keys path-safe via a `safe_segment` mirroring backup's), through the existing `write_object_bytes` — so §10 cataloguing/extraction/embedding, `StorageObject` triggers, and `download_link` all work per-object with zero bespoke indexing. The row keeps references only: `raw_ref` (existing column) + new `attachments` JSONB (additive migration `0049`, the labels-0028 pattern; `set_attachments` kept out of `upsert_by_uid` so a flag-only re-sync never clobbers refs). **Faithful adaptation (disclosed):** archival is an `ActionRunner::archive_email` seam called by the collect pipeline right after a committed write — NOT literally inside `run_write_email` — because `Email.raw` is `#[serde(skip)]` (bytes never reach the trigger JSON, deliberately keeping raw MIME out of the durable run audit) and the api crate has no MIME parser; extraction lives in `catalerum-email::extract_attachments`, mirroring `collect_parts` branch-for-branch (body never mistaken for an attachment, same multipart-bomb bound), and the same `ToolActionRunner` carries a threaded `StorageRegistry` (`with_storage`, wired in `main.rs`) — the deferral's "thread a storage backend onto the action runner" honored. **Per-provider:** Maildir/IMAP/Gmail fully wired (raw already in-hand); JMAP no-ops cleanly (raw-blob download deferred — sync-path risk). **Semantics:** opt-in (no default store → clean no-op), warn-not-fatal with refs left unset so re-collect heals, redelivery-idempotent (already-archived row skipped); **deletion hygiene:** `delete_stored_email` captures archived keys first, then `cleanup_email_archive` runs each through `delete_object_at` (blob + catalogue + de-index + `deleted` trigger). **Verified (agent, live DB + local-FS store; orchestrator spot-run):** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean across core/email/automation/store/ingest + api `--lib --tests`; email **37**; store `mailboxes_emails_repo` **6** (0049 applies); api lib **337** incl. the end-to-end archive test (archives, links refs, redelivery adds nothing, cleanup deletes blobs); reconcile 4/4; automation 12; workspace builds. Orchestrator's api re-run was blocked by the concurrent push-channels agent's mid-edit config literal — re-verify after it lands. **Deferred:** JMAP raw/attachments; archival authority runs under base-Member (doesn't gate on the automation's specific grant — recorded refinement); default-store staleness caveat (refs carry keys, not store names — same disclosure as chat uploads); orphaned-blob possibility on best-effort delete failure._

_2026-07-02 — **Organisation deletion (owner-only, empty-only) + the flash-and-vanish workspace-created notice fixed (SOUL §12/§18; the two bugs the e2e specs surfaced).** **Notice fix:** the "Created workspace…" confirmation state was owned by `OrgPanel`, which remounts on the post-create org-list refetch — lifted to `OrgModal` (which survives the reload, like the org-created notice's home) as an org-tagged `WorkspaceNotice` signal (`notice_for_org` renders it only under its org; switching orgs hides, not discards; cleared on modal close). **`DELETE /organisations/{id}`:** gate = org **Owner** only (new `require_org_owner`; admins 403 — deletion is structural); preconditions via pure `org_delete_precondition` — the default org is never deletable (409), and an org with ANY workspace, **live or archived**, is 409-undeletable (workspaces can only be archived, so the error says exactly that); memberships go via the existing `ON DELETE CASCADE` (migration 0046 already had it — no new migration), the non-cascading `workspaces` FK is the fail-closed backstop; 204 on success. Web: owner-only "Delete organisation" affordance (confirm; 409 surfaced verbatim; presentation-gates on caller-visible live workspaces — the server is authoritative). **Design gap discovered (open):** the 17 accumulated e2e orgs each hold exactly one *archived* workspace, making them **permanently undeletable** under these rules — since workspaces can only ever be archived, an org that has ever contained a workspace can never be disposed of. Wants a decision: hard-delete of archived workspaces (org-owner, data-destroying) or org deletion cascading through archived-only contents. The e2e specs' asserted strings verified unchanged. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean (api `--lib --tests`, store `--all-targets`, web wasm); api lib **334**; store `organisations_repo` **5** (incl. delete/cascade/idempotence); web **276** + trunk build._

_2026-07-02 — **Google Calendar is real: OAuth2 + Calendar v3 `syncToken` incremental sync replaces the placeholder (SOUL §8/§16 M7 first slice; push channels deferred).** **Provider** (`calendar/src/google.rs`, `is_incremental() = true`): initial `events.list?singleEvents=false` paged → `nextSyncToken` cursor (`gsync:<token>`); incremental via `syncToken` with `status=="cancelled"` → `SyncBatch.deletions` (feeding the just-landed reconcile); **410 GONE → clear token + full resync while `is_incremental()` stays true**, so the collect path's snapshot-deletion guard can't fire — a forced full pass never masquerades as delete-everything (trade-off, matching Gmail's `historyId` expiry: deletions inside the token-expiry gap surface only when they re-surface); RRULE carried verbatim (like the iCal backends, exception instances stored by their own Google id), timed/all-day mapping, bounded 64 MiB streamed reads. **OAuth flow:** `[google]` config (client_id/secret/redirect_url/state_secret); authed `GET /auth/google/connect?kind=calendar` (`calendar:write`) → signed HttpOnly state cookie (own signer + key context mirroring `sso_state`, secrets not shared) → Google consent (offline, `calendar.readonly`, `prompt=consent`); callback seals `{client_id, client_secret, access_token, refresh_token, expiry}` **AES-GCM-encrypted** behind the connection's `credential_ref` (fails closed without `[secrets].master_key`), creating/rotating a normal `Calendar` connection — immediately collectable and dormant-annotated like any other. Provider reaches tokens via a `GoogleTokenStore` seam (`ingest/src/google_tokens.rs`) with **single-flight transparent refresh** persisting rotations; api (no reqwest) drives the exchange through ingest re-exports; worker gains `with_secret_store`, and `_with(secrets)` delegating variants keep every existing signature compatible. **Security finding (queued, not fixed here):** the existing **Gmail provider reads `client_id`/`client_secret`/`refresh_token` from PLAINTEXT connection config** — no browser flow, no encryption; unifying Gmail onto the encrypted token store is the follow-up. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy clean (calendar+ingest+binary `--all-targets`, api `--lib --tests`); calendar **52** green (mapping/syncToken/410/refresh fake-clock/seam); api lib **334** green (+12: state-cookie, route helpers, config); ingest all green incl. `collect_reconcile` 4/4. No live-Google tests (impossible in CI) — HTTP kept thin over fixture-tested pure functions. **Deferred:** push/webhook channels; CalendarList multi-calendar discovery (`primary` default); write-back (readonly scope; `create/update/delete_event` stay `Unsupported`); local RRULE expansion; Gmail token-store unification; re-auth of a `credential_ref`-less connection creates a new one (no set-credential repo method — deliberately unadded)._

_2026-07-02 — **Playwright e2e specs for the day's features + the `just e2e` recipe made honest (SOUL §17).** Three new spec files (+ shared `helpers.ts` with login/REST plumbing), all UI-driven against the seeded stack: **`organisations.spec.ts`** — create org → create workspace in it → switcher groups by `optgroup` → switch in/back → archive (confirm dialog) → gone from switcher, listed under Archived → restore → returns (asserts what single_user mode actually shows; REST cleanup in `finally`); **`dormant-connection.spec.ts`** — a local-`.ics` connection created through the calendar panel shows the "nothing collects from this source yet" idle notice; **`automation-actions.spec.ts`** — REST-created collect- and trigger-headed automations (the visual builder is too brittle for e2e — fixtures via `POST /automations`, affordances driven through the UI), asserting Collect-now → "Collect started." and Fire-signal with JSON payload → "Fired — 1 automation matched." **Verified (agent):** 3/3 passed, stable across 3 consecutive full runs (org spec 5/5 under stress) using the dev session bearer; the pre-existing login spec self-skips without `CATALERUM_MAGIC_TOKEN` (one-time token, unmintable against an already-running stack). Orchestrator run confirms the specs self-skip safely with no credentials. **Recipe fix (orchestrator):** `just e2e` was a stub violating §17's non-zero-exit contract — it ran `npx playwright test` from the repo root (fetches a mismatched playwright → "No tests found") and swallowed everything via `|| echo` → **exit 0 with zero tests run**. Now: `cd e2e`, install-if-missing (`--no-package-lock`), local playwright, `set -euo pipefail`, no swallow — failures propagate; token-less specs skip honestly (skipped ≠ green). Automatic token minting/ephemeral-stack wiring stays a TODO in the recipe comment. **Bugs the specs surfaced (real, queued):** the "Created workspace …" notice lives in `OrgPanel`, which remounts on the post-create refetch — the confirmation can flash-and-vanish (made the spec ~2/3-flaky until asserting the durable outcome instead); **no delete-organisation API exists** (workspace delete = archive only), so e2e-created orgs accumulate in a shared DB (16 inert empty orgs left); a concurrently-rebuilding `trunk serve` can transiently flake specs._

_2026-07-02 — **Multi-user settings split + two genuine authz fixes (SOUL §12/§18/§19; resolves the §29 "multi-user settings split" question).** **The inventory IS the answer** — the 9 settings tabs classified: per-user preferences (About/Appearance/General-timezone/Models&voices/Web-search/Files — all `profile:*`-backed or localStorage) **keep full depth for every role in every mode**; operational/diagnostic views (LLM gateway, Status — both read-only `GET /status` views) and API-keys chrome **collapse** for multi-user non-admin members. Audited the non-modal (b)/(c) surfaces for real server gaps: **found two — plain members could register/delete external-DB connections and storage backends** (shared infra carrying AES-GCM secrets); both lifecycle writes now require **workspace admin** via a new `Auth::require_workspace_admin()` (belt-and-suspenders after the capability gate, deny-by-default; new iam `is_admin(role)` helper) — a mode-independent authz fix, exactly the design rule (`mode` never gates, roles do). Deliberately NOT gated: reads + data-plane writes (uploads, labels, `db:write` schema/migrations — members' Apps legitimately manage their own schema on a provisioned connection), token minting (self-scoped, carries only the caller's own role — hidden as chrome, not blocked), grants/agent-profiles (attenuation within the caller's ceiling is a member feature §19). Org policy was already `require_org_admin`; channels have no config CRUD; backup has no route. **Web:** `settings_tabs_for(mode, role)` — single_user → full; admin → full; multi_user + *positively-known* non-admin → curated subset; unknown role → full (fail toward showing more: the collapsible tabs are read-only/self-scoped, over-showing is harmless, wrongly hiding from an admin is not). Role comes from the `/workspaces` active membership (already exposed — no server gap); the tab rail re-pins to About if the active tab collapses. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** api `--lib --tests` clippy clean (still fully green); api lib **320** (+4 gate tests incl. both lifecycle-requires-admin); iam **49**; web trio green — wasm clippy, **274** tests, trunk build. **Deferred:** admin re-exposure of individual knobs (no config surface exists); LLM-gateway/Status hidden rather than shown read-only ("fewer knobs" per §18)._

_2026-07-02 — **Collect pipeline hardened: the collect capability is enforced and upstream deletions reconcile (SOUL §11/§19/§28; closes two deferrals disclosed by the 2026-06-26 sync-as-automations entry).** **(A) Capability.** Chosen shape: `email:read@<connection-id>` / `calendar:read@<connection-id>` — NOT a new `collect` verb, because adding an `Action` variant breaks exhaustive matches in files reserved by other sessions (the explicit-verb migration is a recorded handoff: add `Action::Collect`, its match arms in tool_gate/grants/auth/tool, Member-not-Viewer base caps, then swap the two check sites). Semantically sound: the pull is a provider *read*; local landing stays gated by `email:write`/`calendar:write` on the write actions. **Run/poll-time gate** (`authorize_collect` in `collect.rs`, both collect paths, before any provider I/O): an automation with a recorded grant must cover the connection's read cap or the run **fails closed** (new `IngestError::Forbidden`, a visible job failure — never a silent skip); no grant → the runner's existing default authority (workspace-owner + base-Member caps) applies, which holds domain-wide read — collect is Member-implied, Viewer excluded where Viewer authority binds. **Authoring-time gate** (`require_collect_authority` in `routes/automations.rs`, create+upsert, on *compiled* triggers so graph/legacy gate identically) checks the caller's role base caps — the same authoring-ceiling pattern the mint paths use; today it bites only sub-Member principals (structural hook; run time is the hard gate). **(B) Deletions.** Investigation found every implemented provider already surfaces its signal: IMAP vanished-UID delta, JMAP complete-snapshot diff (truncated → none, fail-safe), Gmail `history.list` deletions, CalDAV report-level 404s — all provider-emitted `deletions`; Maildir/webcal/local-`.ics` are snapshots → **full-snapshot diff**, guarded by the sync path's exact conditions (`!incremental && drained_fully && cursor_changed && !batch_uids.is_empty()` — a no-change poll, partial drain, or emptied read never masquerades as delete-everything). Handled **inline in the collector before the per-item fan-out** (no Delete action node; deletion carries no automation semantics; mirrors sync.rs) — `delete_stored_email/event` + `committed.remove(uid)` so a re-appearing uid re-collects; a failed delete fails the job → cursor doesn't advance → the deletion re-emits next poll (deletions advance the cursor exactly like writes, only once applied); redelivered deletions are no-ops and don't route through the redelivery gate. **Hard-delete** (house pattern; no tombstones) with derived-artifact cleanup through the existing reconcile purges (`ingest_email` → document+vector purge; `project_event` → Neo4j detach-delete), enqueue-failure warn-not-fatal like the write path. `CollectReport.deleted` surfaces counts in job logs. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live stack):** clippy clean (ingest `--all-targets`, api `--lib`); ingest all 13 test binaries green incl. new `collect_reconcile` 4/4 (capability deny/cover/domain/no-grant matrix; Maildir + local-`.ics` end-to-end deletion reconciles with idempotent re-poll); api lib **316** green incl. the pre-existing collect end-to-end now running through the new gate + 2 authoring-gate tests. **Deferred/disclosed:** explicit `collect` verb (handoff above); a snapshot source emptied to zero items keeps its last local rows until any item reappears (matches pre-existing sync reconcile); JMAP truncated-snapshot deletions surface once the mailbox fits a complete snapshot; Google Calendar is an M7 placeholder (nothing to collect)._

_2026-07-02 — **SSO first cut: OIDC login is BUILT — Authorization Code + PKCE, JIT provisioning disabled-by-default, sessions through the guarded `issue_session` chokepoint (SOUL §18/§16 M7; resolves the §29 "SSO first cut" question — OIDC ships, SAML deferred).** **Flow** (`routes/sso.rs`): `GET /auth/sso/login` mints `state`/`nonce`/PKCE-verifier into a signed `HttpOnly SameSite=Lax` cookie (new `sso_state.rs` `SsoStateSigner`, house HMAC style) and 302s to the IdP (optional `?redirect=` allow-listed to same-origin relative paths); `GET /auth/sso/callback` verifies+consumes the cookie (constant-time state compare), exchanges the code (`client_secret_post` default / `_basic` knob), validates the id_token, resolves the user, and issues the session **through the same `IamService::issue_session` magic-link uses** — the archived-workspace guard applies by construction. **Validation** (`iam/src/sso.rs::validate_claims`, pure): RS256 (+ES256), alg pinned to the JWK type (no HS256 downgrade), `iss` (with issuer-match on the discovery doc so a poisoned doc can't repoint endpoints), `aud` string-or-array, `exp`/`nbf` (+`leeway_secs`), `nonce`, `azp==client_id` when present, `iat`-not-future, non-empty `sub`; JWKS cached by `kid` with one refetch on unknown; PKCE helper matches the RFC 7636 test vector. **Identity:** match order = `(issuer,sub)` binding → verified-email first-login link to an **unbound** user (`email_verified` or `trust_email`; an email bound to a different subject is refused) → JIT create; **no migration needed** — `0001_init.sql` already had `users.sso_issuer`/`sso_subject` + unique pair index (better than the planned lone-column design, so the agent used the pair). **JIT lands org-only:** provisioned users join `jit_organisation` (default org) at `jit_org_role` (member) and get NO workspace until invited — the fail-closed option; landing workspace for members = first non-archived membership. **Config:** `[sso]` — issuer/client_id/client_secret/redirect_url (defaults `{base_url}/auth/sso/callback`)/scopes (`openid email profile`)/jit_provisioning (**disabled**)/jit_organisation/jit_org_role/trust_email (false)/token_auth_basic (false)/state_secret (per-process random fallback)/leeway_secs (60); enabled iff issuer+client_id set, else the routes 404; `GET /status` gains `sso: bool` (the web button's seam). **Cargo delta (the one allowed):** `jsonwebtoken 9.3` (+transitive `simple_asn1`); also wired the workspace's existing `reqwest` into iam — a disclosed deviation, since neither iam nor api actually had a usable HTTP client (api builds catalerum-fetch without reqwest features and its fetch seam is GET-only). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** iam **48** green (+12 validation, +8 match-order tests: wrong-nonce/aud/iss/expired/future-iat/azp/tampered-sig/unknown-kid/…); api lib **314** green; `cargo build --workspace` clean (wasm web unaffected — iam is native-only); clippy conditional-green on the two known concurrent-session lints. **Deferred:** SAML; web login button; logout/RP-initiated logout; refresh tokens (12 h opaque bearers unchanged; access token discarded, no refresh stored); fake-provider wiremock integration test (unit fixtures cover the security-critical paths)._

_2026-07-02 — **Graph-entity dedup: a kind-scoped deterministic-id seam — the §29 "Entity/memory dedup" question is now fully resolved (SOUL §5/§6.3/§22/§29).** **Findings first (they shaped the design):** entities have **no Postgres table** (the `0001_init.sql` header lists "entities" aspirationally only) and are **not embedded in Qdrant** (the vector payload's `entity_ids` are mention references, not points) — they are a Neo4j-only derived projection, and the *only* production mint path is note tags / event labels synthesized as `:Topic` nodes in `ingest/src/graph.rs` with a hardcoded non-kind-scoped `topic:` UUIDv5. **Seam** (new `ingest/src/entity_dedup.rs`, mirroring the memories seam): `normalize_entity_name` (trim/collapse/casefold) → **kind-scoped** `entity_id(ws, kind, key) = UUIDv5(ws, "<kind>:<key>")` — duplicates resolve to the same id so the idempotent `MERGE` folds them onto the survivor, while same-name-different-kind stays distinct (Person "Mercury" ≠ Place "Mercury"); the Topic prefix stays `"topic"` so **existing node ids are byte-for-byte unchanged** (test-guarded); `topics_from` now routes through the seam. **Observability for future §10 extraction paths:** `project_entity_deduped(...) → EntityStoreOutcome{entity, status: Created|Deduplicated}` backed by a new `GraphStore::project_entity_reporting` (existence probe + `MERGE` in one transaction; probe reads pre-MERGE state) + a `node_exists` cypher builder; the batch tag/label path deliberately stays structural (per-topic status is meaningless under re-projection). **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live Neo4j):** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean on graph+ingest; graph **29** green incl. the live created-vs-deduplicated test; `entity_dedup` **9** green (8 pure + 1 live); the refactored topic tests still green (ids unchanged). **Deferred (recorded in module docs):** retroactive merge of existing entities (edge re-homing — the destructive escalation), LLM-assisted borderline judging, an embedding-similarity layer (entities aren't embedded; the 0.95 same-kind ANN slot is documented for when they are), Unicode NFC folding (needs a dep addition currently reserved; composed/decomposed accents stay distinct — a safe false-negative; `normalize_entity_name` is the single slot)._

_2026-07-02 — **Per-trigger collect cadence + "collect now" + `WriteEvent` redelivery signal (SOUL §11/§28; resolves the §29 "Collect cadence" question and the redelivery entry's WriteEvent deferral).** **Cadence:** `CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar`'s optional `every` now has a real parser — bare integer = minutes (keeps the codebase's `every` convention so old specs work), `{"minutes":N}`, `{"seconds":N}`, or compact duration strings `"30s"/"5m"/"1h30m"/"2d"` via new `parse_duration_secs` (unit-less strings rejected so `"300"` can never silently disagree with `300` = minutes); clamped to `[60 s floor (= the scheduler's tick, can't poll faster), 1 week cap]` — clamps, never errors; only an uninterpretable shape skips+warns. Unset → `DEFAULT_COLLECT_EVERY_SECS = the shared 60 s tick` (the literal §29 resolution; **flagged behavior change:** unset previously inherited the 5-min graph default). No per-trigger durable state — the established stateless deterministic bucketing pattern (re-list each tick, wall-clock bucket over `(after, now]`, single-fire via the existing lock), with `graph_due` refactored into a shared seconds-resolution `due_bucket`. **Collect now:** discovered there was NO working manual collect (no run-now endpoint; the named-signal path never matches poll-driven collect triggers) — a collect's "run" is a *poll*, so new `enqueue_collect_now(store, ws, &automation)` enqueues the same durable collect job the scheduler would (bypassing the cadence bucket) behind `POST /automations/{name}/collect` (202 / 404 absent / 400 non-collect; `automation:write`). **WriteEvent signal:** `EventRepo::get_by_uid(workspace, calendar, uid)` added (mirroring the email probe) and `run_write_event` now emits `newly_written` like `run_write_email` — the calendar path joins the engine's redelivery gate. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run, live DB):** clippy `-D warnings` clean on automation+ingest+store `--all-targets` + api `--lib`; automation 66; ingest suites green incl. new `collect_every_*`/`duration_secs_*`/`due_bucket_*` units and the DB-gated `collect_now_enqueues_one_immediate_collect_job`; api `action_runner` **23** green incl. `write_event_reports_newly_written_true_then_false_on_redelivery`. **Deferred:** web "Collect now" button (trivial follow-up against the new endpoint); `backfill_window`/`FIRST_POLL_CAP` defaults untouched; authoring-time `every` validation intentionally absent (validated/clamped at scan time, matching GraphQuery)._

_2026-07-02 — **Archived workspaces now fail closed everywhere: by-id trigger dispatch, queued-run claim, and magic-link login (SOUL §11/§18; closes both follow-ups disclosed by the same-day soft-archive entry).** **(Gap 1, dispatch)** the chokepoint turned out to live in `catalerum-ingest`, not the api: `dispatch_trigger_event` (`ingest/src/automation.rs`) now returns `Ok(Vec::new())` for an archived workspace — one check covering every by-id surface that funnels through it (authed + public trigger fire, webhooks, kanban, channels, storage events, channel listener, kanban/trigger-link tools); the authed route's fail-closed response is `202 {matched:0}`. **(Queued-run window — real, guarded)** archiving doesn't drain already-queued `run_automation` jobs, so a pre-archival job would be claimed later: `run_automation` now settles such jobs as `Done` without executing (like a paused/deleted automation), which also backstops the `run_automation` tool path. **(Public opacity)** on top of the chokepoint, the public token `redeem` maps archived → opaque `404` via `reject_archived_workspace`, indistinguishable from a bad token — the one deliberate per-route check, mirroring the existing verify-failure collapse. **(Gap 2, login)** the guard landed in `IamService::issue_session` — the shared chokepoint for magic-link redeem AND `/auth/switch` — returning a new `iam::Error::Forbidden` → HTTP 403 (switch's own pre-check kept as defense-in-depth). Login audit: magic ✓, switch ✓, SSO n/a (not built), dev-seed unaffected (default workspace is never archived); **deliberately not covered:** `issue_session_with_ttl_days` callers (admin service-token mint in `routes/tokens.rs`, dev stable token) — authenticated minting operations, not human login; lifting the guard there is an easy follow-up if wanted. Also disclosed: no session revocation on archive — a pre-archival bearer stays valid but every reachable action surface now fails closed, so the residual authority is inert. **Verified (agent, live scratch-DB tests; orchestrator re-run):** clippy `-D warnings` clean on iam+ingest `--all-targets` + api `--lib`; iam 28 green (incl. archived-session-forbidden), api lib 299 green (incl. opaque-404 redeem test), ingest `automation_run` 5 green (incl. archived-dispatch-matches-nothing + queued-then-archived-skipped)._

_2026-07-02 — **Memory dedup: every memory write now flows through one dedup seam — the chat's proactive `remember` loop stops accumulating repeats (SOUL §22; resolves the memories half of the §29 "Entity/memory dedup" question).** New `catalerum-ingest/src/dedup.rs` — `store_memory_deduped(...) → MemoryStoreOutcome{memory, status: stored|deduplicated|refined}` — lives in ingest because that's the crate already binding Postgres + embedder + vector store. **Layers:** (1) heuristic, always, no embedding — `normalize_memory_text` (trim/collapse-ws/casefold) against the workspace's memories *in the candidate's own scope+owner class*; exact-equal or existing-contains-candidate → **skip + `MemoryRepo::touch`** (bump `updated_at`, return the existing row so the model learns it's already known); candidate a strict whole-word superset and longer → **refine** (update text in place + re-embed, Postgres and Qdrant kept in sync); (2) similarity, only when a vector backend is configured — embed + ANN (`kind=memory`) with `MEMORY_DEDUP_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.95` cosine (doc-justified: near-paraphrase, deliberately high to favor false-negatives — a dropped new fact is worse than a stored near-dup); same skip-vs-refine rule; (3) neither → stored + embed enqueued. **All three producers route through the seam:** the `remember` tool (returns additive `status`), `POST /memories` (which previously never embedded at all — now it does; `201` stored / `200` dedup-or-refined), and the chat auto-store curate job (replacing its ad-hoc seen-set). No other producer exists (automation remember goes through the tool). **Deliberate choices:** cross-scope dedup NOT done (a private re-remember of a shared fact keeps a private copy — never edit shared state from a private write); threshold a named const, not config (no memory-tuning surface exists); async-embed window accepted (a near-dup seconds old may miss ANN; the heuristic still catches identical/extended text). **Verified (agent, live DB+Qdrant; orchestrator re-run):** clippy clean on store/ingest `--all-targets` + api `--lib` (api `--all-targets` conditional-green on the known `tool_gate.rs`/`external_db.rs` concurrent-session lints); ingest 62 lib green (+4 pure dedup) + `curate` 2 + `memory_dedup` 2 (DB+Qdrant, topic-keyed fake embedder); api lib **299** green; store 16. **Deferred:** LLM-assisted borderline judging (recorded as the escalation in the module doc); graph-entity dedup; `updated_at`-aware recall ordering (`list_visible` still orders by `created_at` — the column is now maintained for it)._

_2026-07-02 — **Idempotent redelivery is closed — the §29 "one unresolved correctness hole" is RESOLVED (SOUL §11/§28/§29).** At-least-once collect delivery could re-run non-idempotent nodes (`LlmAgent` double-spending tokens, `LabelEmail` re-labelling) on a redelivered item. Design = the **"newly written" gate**, a general engine-level mechanism (not an email hack): **(signal)** `run_write_email` (`action_runner.rs`) probes the store for `(mailbox_id, uid)` before its upsert and reports `newly_written: false` in its step output on a redelivery — a store probe rather than a ledger lookup because the store row is exactly what survives the crash window between an item's write and its per-item ledger persist (the §11 collect docs' disclosed hole); **(gate)** the DAG executor carries a per-run `redelivery` latch — seeded from `trigger.redelivery`, flipped when any node output reports `newly_written: false`, restored on crash-resume from recorded step outputs — and once latched, non-idempotent action nodes auto-`Skip`, classified by a new `ActionKind::is_idempotent()` (keyed upserts / pure transforms / reads are re-run-safe; `LlmAgent`/`LabelEmail`/`Notify`/`RunSkill`/creates are not; lockstep unit test). Per-node `"rerun_on_redelivery": true` opts back in; the latch is exposed as `input.redelivery` for Condition/Code branching; mirrored in the linear path and inside ForEach bodies. **`commit_on` preserved:** the redelivered `WriteEmail` still runs (idempotent) and `Succeeds`, skips count as intentionally-committed, so the cursor advances without re-spending — asserted by test. Fail-safe by construction: the latch only flips *after* a write runs, so it can never cascade a needed write off. Rejected: whole-run skip at the collect layer (starves `commit_on`, email-specific); "skip classify when a verdict exists" (LabelEmail-only). Catalog docs the gate + new param on the affected nodes; `collect.rs` module doc updated (doc-only). **Verified (agent run on the settled tree, live Postgres):** clippy `-D warnings` clean on automation `--all-targets` + api `--lib` + ingest `--lib`; automation **66 lib + 12 integration** green (incl. the 2 new redelivery tests + `RecordingRunner` fixture); api `action_runner` **22** green incl. the new `newly_written` true-then-false test and the pre-existing end-to-end collect idempotency test; ingest 56+ green. Orchestrator re-run: automation clippy + 66 lib green; the 12 DB-gated integration tests currently fail on the shared dev DB **only** because a concurrent agent's in-flight `0048_workspace_archive.sql` added an `archived_at` column the dev DB hasn't migrated yet (`_sqlx_migrations` at 47) — re-green after the next boot-migrate. **Deferred:** `WriteEvent` doesn't emit `newly_written` yet (needs `EventRepo::get_by_uid`, then ~10 lines mirroring `run_write_email`; calendar's canonical flow has no non-idempotent downstream today); the pre-existing independent-failing-branch → `commit_on` starvation (disclosed 2026-06-26) is unchanged._

_2026-07-02 — **Mermaid `mindmap` + `gitGraph` now render — the last two common diagram types leave the raw-source fallback (SOUL §21).** Both follow the established per-type parse→render, dependency-free-SVG module pattern. **`mindmap`** (`mermaid/mindmap.rs`): indentation-based hierarchy (tabs = 2 cols; a dedent past the root re-attaches to the root so the tree stays single); shape markers `(rounded)`/`((circle))`/`[square]`/`{{hexagon}}`/`)cloud(`/`(-ellipse-)` + optional discarded leading id; unrecognized/unbalanced markers fall back to a rounded box keeping the literal text; `::icon(...)`/`::class` lines skipped. Layout: tidy left-to-right layered tree — x from accumulated per-depth column widths, y via **iterative** post-order (deep nesting can't overflow the stack), cubic-bezier branch curves, top-level subtrees tinted from the shared `PALETTE`. **`gitGraph`** (`mermaid/gitgraph.rs`): `commit` (`id:`/`tag:`/`type: NORMAL|REVERSE|HIGHLIGHT`), `branch` (creates+switches), `checkout`/`switch`, `merge` (ring marker + curved cross-lane edge, `id:`/`tag:`), `cherry-pick` (diamond marker); merge/checkout of a nonexistent branch is skipped, unknown directives (incl. `%%{init}%%`) ignored. Layout: conventional horizontal graph — one colored lane per branch in creation order, commits left→right by global sequence, tags boxed above dots, explicit ids below (mermaid's random-hash default ids omitted as noise). Dispatcher: both keywords registered; the unsupported-fallback fixtures in `mod.rs` and `tests/render_html.rs` (which used `mindmap`/`gitGraph`!) swapped to `sankey-beta`/`C4Context`; `examples/gallery.rs` gained one example of each. Both modules carry `never_panics_on_malformed` fuzz-ish tests (truncated markers, unterminated quotes, garbage indentation) and empty-diagram → `Err` (raw-source fallback), per the engine contract. **Verified (agent + orchestrator re-run):** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean; full suite green — 131 lib + 54 integration/doc tests (19 new across the two modules); gallery example builds and contains both SVGs. **Deferred:** `gitGraph` `TB:`/`BT:` direction tokens parsed-but-ignored (always horizontal, guarded by a test); mindmap `::icon` not rendered (no icon-font dep); circle/cloud shapes approximated; cherry-pick doesn't link back to its source commit._

_2026-07-02 — **Wiki-as-a-service pipeline: terminal git-clone → Files copy with per-file events → conditional (de-)indexer → prefix-scoped semantic search → Boa-scripted, per-subdir MCP endpoints (SOUL §9/§10/§11/§26). BUILT + verified.** Four additive slices turning "clone a GitHub wiki, index a subdir, expose it as a vectorized MCP endpoint" into existing primitives + bounded new code. **(A) Prefix-scoped vector search:** `PointPayload` gains `bucket_name` + `key` (emitted only for object sources) plus a derived `key_prefixes` ancestor-array (Qdrant has no prefix operator, so a subdir search is an exact `match` against the array); `SearchFilter` gains `bucket_name` (exact) + `key_prefix` (normalized to a directory boundary); `VectorStore::delete_by_key` (de-index by storage path when the object row is already gone); threaded through `ingest_object` (bucket name from the bucket row, matching the trigger's `bucket` label) and `search_semantic` (`bucket_name`/`key_prefix` params). Requires a one-shot re-index (index is rebuildable from Postgres, §3.1). **(B) Terminal→Files copy emits per-file events:** `TerminalManager::persist` now `catalogue_and_notify`s each written file (immediate `StorageObject` created/updated triggers + durable ObjectIds, instead of waiting on the 60 s watch scan) and takes an optional `source_subdir` (copy one folder of a cloned repo); `persist_terminal` tool + catalog updated. **(C) Conditional indexer:** `index_document` now addresses a source by `{bucket, key}` (resolved via new `BucketRepo::get_by_name` → `objects().get_by_key`) in addition to `{source, id}`, plus `operation: index|delete` (delete → `delete_by_key`); templating already worked, so a `storage_object` trigger → `condition` on `{{ trigger.event }}` → this action is the whole author-side pattern (catalog documents it). **(D) Boa-scripted scoped MCP endpoints:** new `McpEndpoint` model + `McpEndpointId` + `0047_mcp_endpoints.sql` + `McpEndpointRepo` (CRUD, `get_by_name`); a stored JS program declares MCP tools and, on `tools/call`, reaches a **narrow host bridge** (`EndpointToolHost: UiScriptHost`, reusing the emerged-UI `run_ui_script` seam) that allow-lists **only** `search_semantic` and **force-injects** the endpoint's `bucket_name`/`key_prefix` so a script can never widen its scope (enforced at the bridge + Qdrant filter, **not** via capability constraints — sidestepping the known `attenuate()` gap); each endpoint gets its **own** isolated `McpServer` (script tools never leak into the main `/mcp` registry); served over `POST /mcp/e/{name}` (workspace token) and public `POST /mcp/s/{token}` (HMAC scoped token via new `mcp_endpoint_link.rs`, sharing the download signer's key); management REST `routes/mcp_endpoints.rs` (CRUD + mint-token). The pragmatic "dedicated wiki workspace + Viewer" path needs no code; these slices add the git-in, per-file events, de-index, and custom-endpoint layers. **Verified:** `cargo build --workspace` clean; `catalerum-vector` 16 (payload round-trip, ancestor-prefix, filter clause, `delete_by_key`), `catalerum-api` mcp_endpoint 2 (scope-pinning + tool allow-list refusal) + mcp_endpoint_link 5 (signer mint/verify/expiry/tamper/forge) green; `cargo clippy` clean on core/vector/ingest/store/api for the touched files (2 remaining api-test warnings are in `external_db.rs`/`tool_gate.rs`, not this work). **Incidental unblock:** completed a concurrent in-flight migration's loose end — added the missing `catalerum_core::PendingApprovalId` crate-root re-export (the durable-`PendingApproval` approval refactor had left `routes/ws.rs`'s import unresolved). **Bulk re-index (follow-on, BUILT):** a `reindex_objects` tool + `ReindexObjects` automation action enumerate catalogued objects under an optional `bucket`/`key_prefix` and enqueue the idempotent `ingest_object` for each (bounded `limit`, default 500 / max 5000), gated `vector:write`, registered with `[qdrant]` — the literal "(re)index ALL files" step: after `persist_terminal` copies a wiki subdir, one `reindex_objects key_prefix="wiki/"` (LLM / code-node / scheduled action) indexes the whole folder and rebuilds the index after the Phase-A payload change. Verified: catalog `ACTION_KINDS` + count-comment updated (30 actions), `catalerum-automation` 66 green, `catalerum-api` lib 378 green, clippy clean. **Deferred (disclosed):** create/update auto-ingest on file landing means the conditional indexer's real added value is delete-handling + selective logic (not gating the common case); endpoint management is workspace-scoped like the API-keys panel (no `mcp:expose` capability gate yet); no web authoring panel for endpoints (backend/CLI-first); sub-workspace scoping relies on `key_prefix` (directory-boundary prefixes only) since per-workspace Qdrant collections already isolate tenants._

_2026-07-02 — **Dormant-connection warning: a configured connection that nothing collects from is now flagged, server + web (SOUL §12/§28, closes the §29 "dormant-connection warning" question).** A connection with no enabled Collect automation ingests nothing, and the UI gave no hint — the "I added my email but see no mail" trap. **Server:** new `catalerum-api/src/connection_status.rs` — a pure `is_collecting(automations, kind, id)` (an automation counts iff it is **enabled**, its trigger kind matches the connection kind (`CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar`), and the trigger's `connection` equals the id, trimmed like the ingest scanner's `parse_connection`) plus a `ConnectionView` that `#[serde(flatten)]`s the existing `Connection` and adds a top-level `collecting: bool` — purely additive on the wire. Both `GET` connection listings (`routes/email.rs`, `routes/calendar.rs`) now annotate via one extra `automations().list_by_workspace` scan; only the derived boolean is exposed (same `email:read`/`calendar:read` gate, no automation contents leak). Non-collectable kinds (Storage/Channel/Postgres) always report `true` — dormancy is meaningless there. **Web:** the calendar sidebar "Sources" list renders a warn-token notice under a dormant source ("Idle — nothing collects from this source yet…" + tooltip), styled with the existing `--warn-*` CSS-var tokens (all 5 themes, no raw hex); `Connection.collecting` decodes with `#[serde(default = "default_true")]` so an absent field never false-alarms against an old server. **Discoveries recorded:** email has **no** standalone connections panel in the web UI (email connections are created inline inside a `CollectEmail` flow node, inherently wired to a collector), so the visible warning lives only in the calendar Sources list — the annotation on `/email/connections` is ready for any future email panel; and a calendar source can legitimately show `synced` (the legacy one-shot `/connections/{id}/sync` cursor) *and* `Idle` (no cadence without a Collect automation) — intentional per the sync-as-automation design, flagged for later product reconciliation. **Verified (agent run + orchestrator spot-check):** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --lib -D warnings` clean at agent-run time (a later re-run trips 9 unrelated dead-code lints from a concurrent session's in-flight endpoint-tools work); `connection_status` 9/9; `routes::email` 9 + `routes::calendar` 15; wasm clippy clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-web` 245 green; `trunk build` success._

_2026-07-02 — **Attenuation now checks per-capability constraints — the latent "child grant loosens its parent cap's constraints" escalation is closed (SOUL §19).** `attenuate()` checked a child capability against the parent authority via `Capability::covers`, which by contract ignores per-cap `constraints` — so a child grant could carry a capability whose constraints were *looser* than the covering parent cap's (parent `exec:run` with `{"net":"none"}`, child mints unconstrained `exec:run`), a real escalation once net/lang/cpu enforcement lands. Now a child cap is within bounds iff **some single** parent cap both `covers` its `(action, resource)` **and** subsumes its constraints (`constraints_subsume`): every parent key must be present on the child (a dropped key = dropped restriction → reject, the error names the key); extra child keys are fine (more restriction); for a shared key, equal values subsume, **arrays subsume iff child ⊆ parent** (allow-list convention), and any other unequal shape fails closed (open per-key JSON semantics are undefined, so only provably-narrower shapes pass). Both halves check the **same** parent cap — a looser sibling can't launder a tighter cap's constraints. Scoped to minting via a new `Capability::covers_for_attenuation`; runtime `covers()` (request authorization) is **unchanged**, so constraint-free requests keep working. `AttenuationError` gains a `constraint: Option<String>` field naming the offending key. All four mint call sites (`routes/grants.rs`, `routes/agent_profiles.rs`, `tools.rs`, `profile_agent.rs::subagent_within_parent`) needed **no** changes — parents there are role base sets (constraint-free caps subsume trivially); the delegation path is exactly where the check now bites. Global `Grant.constraints` needed no equivalent fix today: every mint parent has empty global constraints (children can only tighten) and delegation already fails closed via `has_unenforced()` — **deferred:** add `Constraints`-level subsumption at mint sites if a constrained parent authority ever becomes mintable-from. **Verified (independently re-run):** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-core --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `catalerum-core` 60 + `catalerum-iam` 22 tests green (13/13 capability, incl. the new drop/loosen/tighten/array-⊆ cases); `catalerum-api --lib` 276 green incl. the attenuation/delegation tests._

_2026-07-02 — **MCP streamable-HTTP: the SSE-streaming half now shipped — authenticated `GET /mcp` server→client stream + progress-streaming `POST /mcp` (SOUL §26, closes the §29 "MCP transport" remainder).** The HTTP MCP surface was request/response only; this adds the push half of the streamable-HTTP transport (protocol rev 2025-03-26), fully backward-compatible. **`GET /mcp`** (`Accept: text/event-stream`, same `Auth` extractor as the POST; non-SSE clients get `406`) opens a standalone server→client SSE stream: it subscribes to a new per-workspace push hub and interleaves 15 s keep-alive comments until the client disconnects. **Streaming POST:** when the client accepts SSE *and* the request carries a `progressToken` in `params._meta`, the response is `text/event-stream` — a `notifications/progress` `started` event flushes immediately (while the call runs), then on completion a `completed` notification + the final JSON-RPC response, then the stream ends. No token / no SSE → the existing single-event-SSE / plain-JSON paths, unchanged. Progress is an honest coarse `started`→`completed` bracket — `ToolContext` has no per-tool progress channel yet; richer events slot into the same stream when one lands. **Correlation choice:** HTTP `initialize` mints no `Mcp-Session-Id`, so the GET stream is scoped to the **bearer's workspace** via a new `SessionHub` (per-workspace `tokio::broadcast` fan-out in `catalerum-mcp/src/sse.rs`, alongside `sse_frame` JSON-RPC→SSE framing); per-session routing is additive if a session handshake later lands. `protocol.rs` gains `JsonRpcNotification` (+ `progress()` builder) and `JsonRpcRequest::progress_token()`; `routes/mcp.rs` gains `handle_get`, the progress-stream path, shared SSE framing, and `router()` → `post(handle).get(handle_get)`. **Verified (agent run):** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-mcp --all-targets -D warnings` + `-p catalerum-api --lib` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-mcp` 20 unit (8 new) + 14 integration green; `cargo test -p catalerum-api --lib` 276 green (4 new negotiation/ordering tests) **at the time of writing** — a concurrent agent's mid-flight `catalerum-core` edit transiently breaks workspace builds right now; re-verify when it settles. **Deferred:** `Last-Event-ID` resumability (spec-optional); per-session `Mcp-Session-Id` routing; cross-pod fan-out (the hub is process-local); no production producer publishes to the GET hub yet (the `publish` seam is wired + tested, publishing now would be fabricated traffic)._

_2026-07-02 — **Design addition — organisations above workspaces, switching/creation policy, single- vs multi-user deployment mode, and durable data for emerged Apps (SOUL §3/§5/§6.1/§12/§13/§14/§17/§18/§29) — RECORDED, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.** Four user-directed requirements folded into the spec. (1) **Organisations:** a new grouping above workspaces — `Organisation` + `OrgMembership { role: Owner|Admin|Member }` in the §5 sketch, `organisations`/`org_memberships` tables in §6.1, `Workspace` gains `organisation_id`. Org roles govern administration only (create/archive workspaces, org members, policy) and **confer no data access** — the workspace stays the sole data + capability boundary (principle 14 amended); organisations never appear in capability strings. `just dev` seeds a **default organisation** (slug `default`) holding the default workspace. (2) **Switching & creation:** the §12 switcher picks organisation → workspace and re-scopes the session (workspace-scoped tokens — switching mints, never widens); creation is policy-gated deny-by-default — org policy `workspace_creation = admins|members|disabled`, instance policy `organisation_creation` (same values), creator becomes Owner. (3) **Deployment mode:** one `[server] mode = single_user | multi_user` knob — **presentation, defaults, and optimizations only, never schema/API/authz/tenancy** (a single-user instance is a multi-tenant instance with one human; flipping the mode is a config edit, not a migration). `single_user` (what `just dev` runs) surfaces full per-user settings depth, hides member/role/SSO chrome, auto-selects the default org/workspace, and permits sole-user caching (profile/recall prewarm); `multi_user` shows members curated admin-preconfigured defaults and fewer knobs; creation policies default `members` vs `admins` by mode. (4) **Emerged Apps own durable data:** §12 now documents the shipped emerged-UI feature (closed-vocabulary `UiSpec`, three handler kinds + `ai` relay, handlers capped ≤ the viewing user) and requires Apps to persist through the same capability-gated tools everything uses — first-class objects, §9 files, external Postgres via `sql_query` — so "automation collects → data model grows → App presents" works; transient view state stays client-only. New §29 open questions: the multi-user settings split, safe sole-user caches, organisation backfill for existing deployments, and whether a dedicated per-App JSONB store is warranted. **Status: SOUL.md updated; code unchanged.** Backlog: `organisations`/`org_memberships` migration + repos + org routes; `Workspace.organisation_id` threading; the `mode` + creation-policy config knobs; mode-aware settings/nav + org→workspace switcher + create flows in `catalerum-web`; seed's default org; default `[ui].handler_tools` review so storage/`sql_query` are App-reachable._

_2026-07-01 — **External fire surfaces for the `trigger` signal: authed `POST /triggers/{name}`, a public signed-token link, and a `trigger_link` tool (SOUL §11/§12/§18).** Extends the same-day `trigger`/`fire_trigger` work with the HTTP surfaces so a signal is fireable from outside the app. **New `routes/triggers.rs`:** `POST /triggers/{name}` — authenticated (session/token, §18), workspace-scoped, `automation:write`, an optional JSON body carried as the run's `payload` — dispatches via the shared `dispatch_trigger_event` bridge (202 `{matched, jobs}`); `POST /triggers/mint/{name}` — authed mint of a short-lived public link (`automation:write`); and `POST /triggers/fire/{token}` — the **public, unauthenticated** redeem (the one route with no `Auth` extractor: the HMAC-signed token *is* the capability, §19), verifying signature+expiry then firing exactly the one signal in the token's workspace, every verify failure collapsing to an opaque `404`. **New `trigger_link.rs`:** a `TriggerSigner`/`TriggerClaims{workspace,name,exp}` mirroring `download_link.rs` (stateless HMAC-SHA256 token `base64url(payload).base64url(sig)`, constant-time verify, reusing its `VerifyError`→404 mapping), keyed by a new `[server].trigger_secret` (or a random per-process key when unset) — independent of `download_secret` so they rotate separately. **New `trigger_link` tool** (`tools.rs`, `automation:write`, registered unconditionally from `AppState` — no storage dep): mints `{url, expires_at}` for a named signal (default 1 h TTL, clamped `[60 s, 7 d]`), the public twin of `fire_trigger`. Wired the signer into `AppState` (field + `from_config` construction + `trigger_signer()` accessor), merged the router in `lib.rs`, and documented the knob in the sample TOML. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --lib` clean and the new unit tests green (5 `trigger_link` signer tests — mint/verify round-trip, expiry, wrong-key/tampered/malformed + signature-before-payload; 2 `routes::triggers` tests — name normalization, payload parsing of empty/null/JSON/malformed) **at the time of writing**; `catalerum-automation` suite green (65). **Env caveat (not mine):** a concurrent session is mid-refactor on `catalerum-core`'s `ask`/`UserAsker` (a newly-untracked `ask.rs` + an edited `routes/ws.rs` importing a now-absent `UserAsker`), so `catalerum-api` currently fails to build on that **one** unrelated import — confirmed the sole error, none in the trigger files — and will build once that refactor settles. **Deferred:** links are stateless (no pre-expiry revocation — shorten the TTL); one workspace-wide signing key (no per-automation secret); the visual builder still doesn't author `payload` (it's supplied by the firing caller)._

_2026-07-01 — **`web_search` tool now dedups repeated queries so a duplicate isn't paid for twice (SOUL §27)** — the tool assembles its run list from `queries[]` plus an optional lone `query`, then searches each concurrently and returns a `searches` map keyed by query. It didn't dedup that list, so `queries: ["rust", "rust"]` (models re-emit the same query, and `query` can duplicate a `queries` entry) fired **two identical metered/paid engine calls** even though the output map keys by query and collapses them anyway — pure wasted cost + latency. Added a first-seen-order dedup (`retain` over a `HashSet`) right after the list is assembled, before the searches fan out; the batch-vs-single output shape is unchanged (it keys off whether a `queries` array was present, not the deduped length). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-search --all-targets -D warnings` clean; suite green (7 tool tests) incl. new `duplicate_queries_are_searched_once` — a call-counting `WebSearcher` confirms `["rust","rust","go"] + query "go"` fires exactly **2** engine calls and yields a 2-key map. Small in-crate efficiency fix — no schema/output change._

_2026-07-01 — **New `trigger` automation trigger + `fire_trigger` tool: a named on-demand signal an emerged UI (or chat) can fire (SOUL §11/§12).** There was no way to run an automation *on demand* from a UI — every trigger had an external source of its own (a webhook path, a Kanban move, a schedule, a channel message, a storage event). Added a push-driven **named-signal** trigger and the tool that fires it. **catalerum-automation:** `Trigger::Trigger { name }` (kind `"trigger"`, `kind()` arm added) and the matching `TriggerEvent::Trigger { name, payload }` — `matches` keys on `name` alone (exact, case-sensitive); the optional `payload` is carried on the run's trigger event for a downstream `Condition`/`LlmAgent` to read but is **never** part of matching. Added a `trigger.trigger` catalog doc (+ `TRIGGER_KINDS`/count-comment updates) so the node surfaces in the palette and semantic search. **catalerum-api:** a `fire_trigger` registry tool (thin `dispatch_trigger_event` client, gated `automation:write`) that takes `{ name, payload? }`, enqueues a durable `run_automation` job per matching automation — the same bridge the webhook/Kanban sources use — and returns `{ matched, jobs }`. It's ≤ base-Member so it stays script-callable, and it's added to the default `[ui].handler_tools` allow-list so an emerged-UI button/handler (declarative `tool` or Boa `catalerum.callTool`) can fire it out of the box; the caller's role gates *triggering* only — each automation still runs under its own §19 authority. **catalerum-web:** the visual trigger builder gains a "Named signal (on demand)" kind with a single required `name` field (shared by the raw builder + flow canvas). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api` + `-p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean; `cargo check --workspace --exclude catalerum-web` clean; `catalerum-automation` suite green (new `manual_trigger_matches_on_name_and_ignores_payload` + updated catalog count); `catalerum-api` lib tests green (updated the trigger-count assertion 9→10). **Deferred (disclosed):** no unauthenticated/public fire path (it goes through the capability-gated tool, like the webhook route's first cut); `payload` isn't authored in the visual builder (it's set by the firing caller, not the trigger spec); no dedicated `POST /triggers/{name}` REST surface — `fire_trigger` via chat/UI/code-node is the surface._
