_2026-07-01 — **Labels on stored files & directories: user/agent-applied tags keyed by `(store, path)` (SOUL §9).** There was no way to tag a file or folder — the only per-object metadata was the §10 catalogue row, which files can't carry arbitrary categories on and which **directories don't have at all** (they're implicit key prefixes). Added an end-to-end vertical slice. **catalerum-core:** an `ObjectLabel { id, workspace_id, store, path, is_dir, label, author, created_at }` (`ObjectLabelId`) — deliberately keyed by `(store, path)` rather than an object id, so a **directory** path (no `objects` row) or a not-yet-catalogued file can be tagged; `store` is the `?store=` selector ('' → default) since a path is only unambiguous within a backend. **catalerum-store:** migration `0042_object_labels.sql` (a `UNIQUE(ws, store, path, label)` dedup index + store/path and label lookup indexes; `author` split as `(author_kind, author_id)` like `links`/`notes`) + `ObjectLabelRepo` — `add` idempotent via `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE` (rejects blank path/label with `StoreError::Invalid`→400), `list_for` (one path), `list_by_store` (prefix-filtered — the panel's tree badges), `list_by_label` (the filter), `delete` (by id), and `delete_for_path` (the delete-cleanup). **catalerum-api:** label routes on the storage router (`GET /storage/labels?store=&prefix=` or `?label=`, `GET /storage/labels/for`, `POST /storage/labels`, `DELETE /storage/labels/{id}`; all `storage:read`/`storage:write`, workspace-scoped), authored by the caller; the `DELETE /storage/objects/{key}` handler **and** `scan_store`'s vanished-object purge now best-effort `delete_for_path` so a label can't outlive its file. **catalerum-web:** `FileLabel`/`NewFileLabel` DTOs + `rest::{list_labels,add_label,delete_label}`; the Files panel renders label chips (each with an "×" remove) + a "+" add (via prompt) on **both** directory and file tree rows, reloading via an `Effect` on the picked store; chip/add clicks `stop_propagation` so tagging a folder never toggles its expand; CSS uses only `:root` theme tokens (§ theme rule). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-core -p catalerum-store` clean; `catalerum-store` `object_labels_repo` integration test green **run against a throwaway DB** (full 0001→0042 migration chain — add/idempotency/blank-rejection/prefix+label listing/dir-vs-file/`delete_for_path`-keeps-dir-label/isolation), leaving the shared dev DB untouched; `catalerum-web` wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean; `catalerum-api` builds and `routes/storage.rs` is error/lint-free (the crate's remaining clippy findings are all in the in-flight `tool_gate`/`profile_agent` refactor, not this feature). **Environment note:** the working tree already carried a parallel `0040_external_postgres.sql` + `0041_tool_guard.sql`, so this migration is `0042`; a parallel process had also applied a phantom "object labels" v40 to the shared dev DB (hence the isolated verification). **Deferred (disclosed):** no graph projection of labels as `:Topic` nodes (unlike note tags/event labels — Neo4j-optional, left for a follow-up); no agent/automation `label_file` registry tool or `LabelFile` action (the symmetric analogue of `LabelEmail` — the REST + Files-panel surface is the requested one); labels don't follow a file across rename/move (keyed by path); directory labels don't cascade to contained files (a tag on the exact path only)._

_2026-07-01 — **`download_link`: the agent can now hand the user a click-to-download URL for a stored file or directory (SOUL §9/§18/§19)** — there was no way for the agent to give a user a link to a file it created (a report written in a terminal, a synthesized clip, a copied object): the only download surface, `GET /storage/objects/{key}`, is bearer-authenticated, so a plain link click can't fetch it. Added a **signed, single-purpose, unauthenticated** download link. **New `catalerum-api/src/download_link.rs`**: a `DownloadSigner` (HMAC-SHA256 over compact `DownloadClaims {workspace, store, key, dir, exp}`, token = `base64url(payload).base64url(sig)`) with constant-time `verify` (signature-before-payload, opaque on any failure). The key is `[server].download_secret` (SHA-256-derived, so links survive restarts / span pods) or a random per-process key when unset (single-pod dev). **New public route `GET /download/{token}` (`routes/download.rs`)** — the one storage surface with **no `Auth` extractor** (the token *is* the capability, §19; narrower than a bearer — one object/prefix, short TTL): verifies → resolves the store workspace-scoped (§18) → streams the file as an attachment, or, for a directory link, streams every object under the prefix as an on-the-fly `.tar.gz` (GNU headers for long keys; built in `spawn_blocking`; bounded by `DEFAULT_OBJECT_LIMIT` count + a 256 MiB total-size cap). **New `download_link` registry tool** (`tools.rs`, gated `storage:read`, Boa-callable like `copy_object`): takes `{key, store?, ttl_secs?}`, infers file-vs-directory (trailing `/`, or a `stat`-miss that resolves to a non-empty prefix), validates existence + the archive-size cap at mint time, and returns `{url, kind, expires_at, size, object_count}`. TTL defaults to 1 h, clamped `[60 s, 7 d]`. Directory claims carry a trailing-slash key so listing scopes to exactly that folder (no sibling-prefix bleed). Registered from `AppState` beside `copy_object` when storage is configured; a `download_signer` field + accessor threads the signer to the redeem route, and `config.server.download_secret` + the sample TOML document the knob. Also shipped a first-party **`share-file` skill** (`catalerum-skills`) that runbooks the flow (`copy_object` a stray file into a store, then `download_link`). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api -p catalerum-skills --all-targets` clean (no findings in the new files); 11 new unit tests green — signer mint/verify round-trip, expiry, wrong-key/tampered-payload/malformed rejection, signature-before-payload ordering, dir-flag round-trip, `basename`/`Content-Disposition` sanitization, and a real gzip-tar build+read-back — plus the skills suite (incl. the `share-file` fixture). **Incidental, disclosed:** the working tree's in-flight `tool_gate` refactor (added `ToolContext.gate` + `NewAgentProfile.guard`, both `Option`) had left 9 initializer call sites un-updated, so `catalerum-api` didn't build at all; completed them with the mechanically-correct `gate: None` / `guard: None` (the safe "no programmable gate/guard" default for those internal/system contexts) purely so the crate compiles and this feature verifies — revert if the refactor intends real gates there. **Deferred:** links are stateless (no server-side revocation before expiry — shorten the TTL instead); the directory archive buffers in memory under the size cap (no chunked/streaming tar yet); no web-UI "copy link" button (the tool/route are the surface)._

_2026-07-01 — **Web-fetch HTML→Markdown: `<mark>` now preserved as `==highlight==` (SOUL §27)** — the fetch converter (`catalerum-fetch/src/markdown.rs`, the reader the fetch/RAG tool feeds the LLM) maps semantic inline elements to the Markdown a reader sees — `<del>`→`~~…~~`, sup/sub→Pandoc `^…^`/`~…~`, `<q>`→quoted — but `<mark>` (highlighted text: search hits, editorial emphasis) fell through to the plain-text fallback, dropping the highlight signal. Added `"mark" => wrapped("==", …)` (the GitHub/Obsidian/Pandoc highlight convention), consistent with the file's established "preserve what the reader sees" choice — and with the deliberate precedent that this converter targets the LLM/external consumer, so it already emits `^`/`~` that catalerum's own engine doesn't parse. Empty `<mark>` collapses (no stray `====`, via the shared `wrapped` empty-guard). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; suite green (74 tests) incl. new `mark_renders_as_highlight` (highlight round-trips; empty collapses). One-line match arm — no converter-structure change. **Note:** catalerum-markdown has no highlight AST node, so if fetched Markdown is *re-rendered* by the engine (rather than read by the LLM) the `==` shows literally — the same accepted trade-off already made for sup/sub._

_2026-07-01 — **Markdown engine: block-math now carries the `catalerum-math-block` wrapper on the HTML path too (renderer-parity fix, SOUL §21)** — the shared engine has two renderers that must agree: `render/html.rs` (md→HTML string) and `render/leptos.rs` (md→DOM). For a ` ```math ` fence, the Leptos renderer wraps the MathML in `<div class="catalerum-math-block">` — the CSS hook that gives block equations `text-align:center` + `overflow-x:auto` (so a wide equation scrolls instead of overflowing its column; the class is defined in `examples/gallery.rs`) — but the HTML renderer emitted **bare** `<math>`, so block math rendered via the HTML path (e.g. chat-stream HTML) lost the centering and, worse, overflowed on wide formulas. Wrapped the HTML renderer's block-math output in the same `<div class="catalerum-math-block">…</div>`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean; full suite green (101 lib + integration) with the existing `math_renders_to_mathml` extended to assert the fence output carries `class="catalerum-math-block"` (matching Leptos). Pure `push_str` change on the HTML path — no Leptos/wasm impact. **Left as-is (consistent between the two renderers):** `$$…$$` display math is an *inline* AST node in both, so neither wraps it in `catalerum-math-block` — a separate design question (whether `$$` should be block-level) not touched here._

_2026-07-01 — **Quick-start step 4 reworked from a goals/environment skill-drafting form into an assistant-led personalization chat (SOUL §12/§22/§23)** — the old step 4 asked the user to fill two textareas (goals + environment) and one-shot `POST /onboarding/suggest-skills` drafted skills; personalization was a form, not a conversation, and it only produced skills (not memories). Replaced it with a back-and-forth chat where the assistant asks the questions. **Server (`catalerum-api/src/routes/onboarding.rs`):** `POST /onboarding/suggest-skills` → `POST /onboarding/personalize` (`skill:write`); request is now the visible conversation (`PersonalizeRequest { messages: Vec<PersonalizeTurn{role,content}> }`, empty ⇒ opening turn), response is `PersonalizeResponse { reply, memories: Vec<String>, skills: Vec<SkillDraft>, done }`. `build_personalize_messages` seeds a hidden kick-off when history is empty (so the assistant greets + asks first), maps roles, and caps the replay at `MAX_HISTORY_TURNS` (§18); one `state.llm().chat()` under the same prompt-for-JSON contract (now a `{…}` object, parsed tolerantly by `parse_personalize`/`extract_json_object`, degrading to raw-text-as-`reply` when the model drops the envelope). Still persists nothing — the client writes chosen memories via `POST /memories` and skills via `PUT /skills/{name}` (§16). Kept `SkillDraft` + the name/tool normalizers; dropped `suggest-skills`/`build_suggest_prompt`/`extract_json_array`. **Web (`catalerum-web`):** step 4 (`Step::Skills`→`Step::Personalize`, nav pip "Personalize") is now a bubble chat — an `Effect` fires the opening question the first time the step is shown, `run_turn` replays the transcript and folds newly proposed memories (dedup by normalized text) + skills (dedup by name) into two default-selected review lists, Enter-to-send composer (Shift+Enter newline), a typing indicator, and a `done` "Finish" nudge; Finish `POST /memories` (user scope) each chosen fact + `PUT /skills/{name}` each chosen draft, then `complete`. New DTOs (`PersonalizeTurn`/`PersonalizeRequest`/`PersonalizeResponse`), `rest::personalize`, `ONBOARDING_PERSONALIZE_PATH`, and chat/proposal CSS. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets` + full native workspace clippy clean; `cargo clippy -p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean; 12 onboarding unit tests pass (message assembly + history cap, object parsing with fence/prose stripping + raw fallback, memory cap, skill dedup/hollow-skip). **Deferred (unchanged):** drafted `tools` stay advisory (§23 restricted-tool enforcement still deferred); model ids unvalidated against the gateway catalog; the chat still does not connect external data sources (the §11 Collect-automation flow)._

_2026-07-01 — **Wire request: fixed a duplicate-`provider`/`models`-key bug in `WireRequest` serialization (SOUL §7)** — `catalerum-llm`'s `WireRequest::build` lifts `provider`/`models` out of `ChatRequest::extra` into typed fields, but it read them with `.get()` (leaving them in `extra`) and `extra` is `#[serde(flatten)]`-ed — so a caller who stashed routing in `extra` got each key serialized **twice** (typed field + flattened extra), i.e. a malformed body with duplicate JSON keys. The existing test used `serde_json::to_value` (whose `Value` map silently dedups), hiding it. Fixed `build` to `.remove()` the two keys from an owned clone of `extra` before flattening (changed the field from `&'a Map` to an owned `Map`), so each serializes exactly once. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-llm --all-targets -D warnings` clean; suite green (4 wire tests incl. new `lifted_provider_and_models_are_not_serialized_twice`, which checks the serialized **string** — not a dedup-ing `Value` — has exactly one `provider`/`models` key and that other `extra` keys still flatten through). **Noted, not acted on:** the whole `wire` module (`WireRequest`/`WireMessage`/`ChatChunk`/…) appears **superseded** — the client now builds/sends via the external `llmleaf_client` SDK, so only `ProviderRouting` is still used; the rest are unused-but-`pub` (hence no dead-code lint). So this bug never manifested at runtime; the fix keeps the public API correct. Whether to prune the dead wire types is left to you (a public-surface removal I didn't want to make unilaterally)._

_2026-07-01 — **Math renderer: `\pmod{n}` now renders, and `\bmod` shows "mod" not "bmod" (SOUL §21)** — modular-arithmetic notation was broken in `catalerum-markdown`'s LaTeX→MathML: `\bmod`/`\mod` were listed in `is_function`, which uses the command name verbatim as the operator text — so `a \bmod b` rendered the literal **"bmod"** (the `b` is LaTeX's "binary operator" designation, not shown, so it should be "mod"); and `\pmod{n}` wasn't handled at all — it degraded to the literal "pmod" followed by a stray `{n}` group. Added explicit `command_body` arms (ahead of the `is_function` fallback): `\pmod{n}` → an `M::Row` of ` (mod n)` (leading space, parens as `<mo>`, upright "mod", thin space, the argument), and `\bmod` → the upright "mod" `<mi>`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean; suite green (20 lib math tests incl. new `modular_arithmetic_pmod_and_bmod`, which checks `\pmod{n}` emits a parenthesised "mod" with its argument and that `\bmod` never leaks the literal "bmod"). Pure additive parser arms — no `M` variant or renderer change (reused `Row`/`Op`/`Ident`/`Space`). _2026-07-01 — **Uploaded source-code/config files are now §10-indexed instead of silently skipped (SOUL §9/§10)** — the local-fs backend derives an object's content type purely from its key extension (`content_type_for`), and the §10 ingest indexer only extracts text when `is_text_like(content_type)` holds. `content_type_for` mapped the *data/markup* text types (`.json`/`.xml`/`.yaml`/`.toml`/`.ndjson`/`.csv`/…) — the code's own comment even warns those must be typed "otherwise [they'd] be silently skipped despite being extractable" — but mapped **no source-code or plain-text config extensions**, so a locally-stored `.py`/`.rs`/`.sql`/`.sh`/… returned `content_type = None` → `is_text_like(None) = false` → its content never reached the search/graph index. Added a `text/plain` mapping (which `is_text_like` accepts via its `text/` prefix, verified) for a broad set of unambiguously-text code/config/prose extensions: `rs py go java c h cc cpp cxx hpp rb php sh bash zsh sql kt kts swift scala lua pl pm r jl ex exs clj hs ini cfg conf properties rst tex adoc`. **Deliberately excluded** `.ts` (collides with MPEG transport-stream binaries — would garbage-index a video via lossy UTF-8 decode) and `.env` (secret-bearing — avoids embedding API keys into the vector index). Local-backend only; S3/WebDAV return the stored upload content type. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-storage --all-targets -D warnings` clean; suite green (16 tests) with `content_type_covers_text_like_and_web_extensions` extended to assert the new code/config extensions → `text/plain` and that the excluded `.ts`/`.env` stay `None`. Additive extension-table change — no trait/indexer change; `is_text_like` already accepts `text/plain`._

_2026-07-01 — **Math renderer: filled gaps in the LaTeX→MathML symbol table (SOUL §21)** — `catalerum-markdown`'s `math::symbol` lookup was missing a batch of common commands, and (per `command_body`'s fallback) an unknown command **degrades to its literal name** — so `\mid` rendered as the text "mid", `\models` as "models", etc. Added, purely additively (new match arms only, zero change to existing symbols): the missing uppercase Greek `\Upsilon` (Υ); the divides relations `\mid`/`\nmid` (∣ ∤, common in set-builder `{x \mid …}`); logic turnstiles `\models`/`\vdash`/`\dashv` (⊨ ⊢ ⊣) and constants `\top`/`\bot` (⊤ ⊥) — all especially relevant now that the app has a Datalog layer; order relations `\prec`/`\succ`/`\preceq`/`\succeq` (≺ ≻ ≼ ≽); circled operators `\odot`/`\ominus`/`\oslash` (⊙ ⊖ ⊘); and the long double/bi-directional arrows `\longleftrightarrow`/`\Longrightarrow`/`\Longleftarrow`/`\Longleftrightarrow` (⟷ ⟹ ⟸ ⟺). Verified codepoints against Unicode names; `\mid`/`\nmid`/turnstiles/etc. are `op` (→ `<mo>`, proper relation spacing), `\top`/`\bot`/`\Upsilon` are `id` (→ `<mi>`). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean; suite green (19 lib math tests incl. new `extended_symbol_coverage`, which asserts each new symbol resolves to its codepoint and that the command name no longer leaks as literal text). Pure additive lookup change — no parser/renderer restructure._

_2026-07-01 — **Graph querying moved from raw Cypher to a safe in-process Datalog language (SOUL §6.3/§18) — the §18 "structural-scope bypass" hardening TODO is now RESOLVED.** The two operator-authored raw-Cypher surfaces (`POST /graph/query` and the `GraphQuery` automation trigger) no longer accept Cypher; both take a program in a new **Datalog** language and evaluate it in-process. This deletes the heuristic `validate_graph_query_cypher` + `strip_cypher_literals_and_comments` (and their tests) rather than patching them: the documented `… = $workspace_id OR 1=1 …` cross-tenant bypass, the `UNION`/`USE`/`CALL` escapes, and injection generally are now **impossible by construction** — the language has no syntax to name a workspace, no writes, and no query text ever reaches Neo4j (the fact loader is the only boundary and it loads exactly one workspace). **New crate `catalerum-logic`** (pure, deps `serde_json`+`thiserror`): a hand-rolled lexer/recursive-descent parser (desugars label/edge shorthand `note(X)`→`node(X,"Note")`, `references(F,T)`→`edge(F,"REFERENCES",T)`, and `ieq`/`like` builtins), a validator (range-restriction/safety, arity, reserved-head, unknown-predicate, size caps), and a **bottom-up semi-naive** evaluator with hard caps (derived-fact budget, iteration budget, wall-clock deadline). Termination is structural (no function symbols ⇒ finite active domain), so recursion (transitive closure) is supported and safe; v1 ships without negation (an AST `negated` hook remains for stratified negation later). Base relations `node(Id,Label)`/`edge(From,Type,To)`/`prop(Id,Key,Value)`; output columns are the goal's distinct variables, rows set-deduped. **`catalerum-graph`** gained `load_workspace_facts` (two fixed, `{workspace_id:$workspace_id}`-scoped reads → `WorkspaceFacts` triples) + `load_nodes`/`load_edges` builders + a `LABELS`/`EDGE_TYPES` drift-guard test (dev-dep on `catalerum-logic`, no runtime coupling); the raw-Cypher `Statement::query` constructor was **removed** — its one remaining caller (a `RELATES_TO` link-projection verification read) now uses a typed `relates_to_link_ids` builder, so the crate exposes no raw-query escape hatch. **`catalerum-automation`** renamed `GraphQuery{cypher→query}` (no serde alias — hard replace), swapped the authoring validator to `catalerum_logic::validate`, and updated `catalog.json`. **`catalerum-ingest`** poller parses+loads+evaluates (in `spawn_blocking`+timeout), keeps the ≥1-row fire semantics, and **warns+skips** any legacy trigger still using the retired `cypher` field (never crashes the scan; a stored old payload no longer decodes). **`catalerum-web`** explorer + automation-builder form now author Datalog. **Verified:** per-crate `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean (logic/graph/automation/ingest/api); `catalerum-web` wasm `cargo check` + `clippy` clean; unit suites green (logic 22, graph 27, automation 63, ingest, api graph-route 10); live Neo4j/Postgres tests remain env-gated and self-skip (the `scan_graph_queries` live test now seeds a `:Note` first, since an empty graph yields no rows)._

_2026-07-01 — **Terminals are now always ephemeral — the persistent "workdir" (directory) concept is fully removed (SOUL §20)** — a terminal launches in a throwaway temp dir every time; there is no durable named working directory to pick, manage, or bind. the `backend` override on `open_terminal` stays (it's runtime selection, orthogonal to directories). **Verified:** `cargo clippy` clean on `catalerum-core`/`-store`/`-automation`/`-api` `--all-targets` and `catalerum-web` on `wasm32 -D warnings`; the automation catalog tests (39 docs, every kind covered), the api `action_runner` mapping tests, and the rewritten store `terminals_repo`/`agent_profiles_repo` all green. **Note:** a full `--workspace` build can't complete because of **pre-existing, unrelated** WIP breakage in `catalerum-logic` (a borrow error; the crate is brand-new/untracked) and `catalerum-graph`/`catalerum-ingest` (a `Statement::query` API drift) — none of which this change touched. **Deferred/left as-is:** SOUL §20's own prose still describes the persistent-workdir design (a doc revision, not code); _2026-07-01 — **Charts: a dependency-free SVG chart family, wired into the emerged-UI vocabulary so AI-authored Apps (and any panel) can plot data (SOUL §12)** — the workbench had SVG only for the automation `flow` canvas; there was no way to visualise numeric data (usage/cost, run durations, storage) and no chart element an emerged App could author. Added a **`catalerum-web/src/components/charts.rs`** module: pure `data → AnyView` renderers for **pie, donut, bar (vertical + horizontal), line, area, sparkline, gauge, radar, heatmap**, built directly on SVG the way `flow.rs` is — unit-tested geometry helpers (`polar`/`wedge_path`/`ring_path`/`open_arc`/`nice_ceil`) feeding a `view!` tree. Every colour resolves to a new `--chart-1..8` theme token (added to `:root` + light/AAA overrides in `lib.rs::STYLE`), so a theme switch recolours all charts at once (heatmap shades one token by opacity, so it re-themes for free). Each renderer is **total** — empty/degenerate/adversarial input yields a "No data" placeholder, never a panic — and slice/point/cell counts are capped so a large state array can't explode the DOM. Exposed the same nine as **append-only `NodeKind` variants** in `catalerum-core::model_ui` (leaf, non-input, non-interactive — so the existing validator rejects children/bind/events for free) and its `catalerum-web` deserialize mirror; the emerged **`render.rs`** interpreter gains one arm per kind plus a `chart_host` reactive wrapper (reads `st.data` once per render, so a chart redraws only when its bound `data`/`value` prop changes) and prop resolvers that accept a literal array, a `{"$path":"state.path"}` ref, or a `{{path}}`/bare-path string. Documented the new kinds + a worked `donut_chart` example in the `get_ui_schema` tool (`catalerum-api/src/tools.rs`) so the authoring LLM knows the vocabulary. **Verified:** `catalerum-core` clippy clean + 17 `model_ui` tests green incl. the new `chart_kinds_are_read_only_leaves` (every chart kind is a read-only leaf: rejects children/bind/events, a bare chart validates); `charts.rs` linted in isolation on **wasm32 `-D warnings` clean** (a scratch leptos crate sharing the workspace target — which surfaced + fixed a `needless_range_loop` in `radar_chart` the workspace clippy had suppressed) and its **7 tests pass** (geometry cardinal points, `nice_ceil` rounding, `num` NaN-guard, palette fallback/cycling, and a never-panics sweep over empty/degenerate input for all renderers); the emerged `render.rs` wiring type-checks (clippy caught + I fixed its one real error — Leptos requires the reactive closure be `Send`, so `chart_host`'s `build` param gained `+ Send`). **Honest gap:** a full `catalerum-web` wasm clippy + `trunk build` can't currently complete because the working tree has an **unrelated pre-existing WIP** (an in-flight `terminals`/`TerminalSession.kind` refactor leaves `chat.rs`/`terminal.rs` non-compiling, and the `catalerum-api` `terminals` fields likewise) — all remaining errors are in files this change never touched; the same WIP left `catalerum-logic` a member with no `src/`, so a placeholder `lib.rs` was added to let the workspace load at all. **Deferred (disclosed):** multi-series bar/line, scatter/histogram/box-plot, and interactive hover tooltips (the plain form covers the chosen scope); charts are single-series where applicable; no live-data Stats panel was built (the emerged wiring + reusable components are the delivered surface)._

_2026-07-01 — **Backup retention now counts only complete backups — a crashed partial can't evict a good one (SOUL §30)** — `run()` writes a backup's `manifest.json` **last** (after every Postgres table dump + object blob), so a backup that dies mid-dump leaves a directory with data files but no manifest. `list_backup_ids` counted *any* directory containing a nested file as a backup, so such a partial showed up in `list()` as if restorable and — the real hazard — occupied a slot in `prune`'s `keep` window: `prune` deletes `ids[..len-keep]` (the oldest), so a broken newer partial could push a **good, complete** older backup out of the retention window and delete it. Fixed `list_backup_ids` to only surface ids that carry a `manifest.json` (detected in the same single list pass via `rest.split_once('/')` → `tail == "manifest.json"`, no extra reads), so `list()`/`prune`/`restore` all operate solely on complete, restorable backups; a manifest-less crash dir is simply ignored. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-backup --all-targets -D warnings` clean; suite green (7 tests, 0 failed) incl. the new `list_backup_ids_returns_only_complete_backups_sorted` — builds two complete backups + one newer manifest-less partial on a real `LocalFsBackend`/tempdir and asserts the partial is omitted while the rest come back sorted oldest→newest (added `tempfile` as a dev-dep; `catalerum-storage` was already one). Doc comments on `list`/`list_backup_ids` updated to say "complete". **Deferred:** actively *garbage-collecting* orphaned partial dirs (they now leak instead of being pruned — a rare, small leak, and far safer than the previous evict-a-good-backup behaviour); a dedicated `gc_incomplete()` is a separate follow-up._

_2026-07-01 — **Mermaid `journey` (user-journey) diagrams now render, + iCal single-occurrence regression test (SOUL §21, §8)** — two additive refinements. **(1) Mermaid journey:** `journey` diagrams previously hit the dispatcher's `Err("unsupported diagram type")` and fell back to raw source. Added `mermaid/journey.rs` (modelled on the timeline renderer's parse→render shape): parses `title`, `section <name>`, and task lines `name : <score> : Actor, Actor …`; renders the diagram's defining visual — each task's 1–5 satisfaction **score plotted on a shared axis and joined into the journey's satisfaction curve** (`<polyline>`), points tinted red→green by score, consecutive same-section tasks under a coloured band (reusing the timeline band logic + shared `PALETTE`), actors listed under each task label. Scores clamp to 1..=5; a line with no numeric score isn't a task; all text escaped. Wired into `mermaid/mod.rs` (module + dispatch `header.starts_with("journey")` + doc), so it's automatically live in **both** the HTML and Leptos (native + wasm) render paths — the renderers call the one central `mermaid::to_svg`. **(2) iCal test hardening:** `ical.rs`'s `parse_labels`/`parse_attachments` read from `multi_properties()`; the existing SAMPLE only exercised the *multi*-line path, so added `single_categories_and_attach_occurrence_are_captured` to lock in the common lone-`CATEGORIES`/lone-`ATTACH` case (probed empirically first — icalendar does park single occurrences there, so no bug, just a guarded gap). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown -p catalerum-calendar --all-targets -D warnings` clean; markdown suite green (99 lib + integration, incl. 5 new `mermaid::journey` tests covering the curve/scores/actors/sections, score clamping + no-curve-for-one-task, escaping, empty→unsupported, and a never-panics sweep) and the dispatch tests updated (journey moved from the unsupported list to `dispatches_by_diagram_type`, `gitGraph` swapped in as the unsupported example); calendar suite green (38 lib). Pure additive, in-crate — no schema/API/renderer-plumbing change. **Deferred:** mermaid.js's actor-face glyphs + a per-actor colour legend (the actor *names* are rendered, just not faces)._

_2026-07-01 — **Local storage backend now streams `get` in chunks instead of reading the whole object into memory (SOUL §9)** — `LocalFsBackend::get` used `tokio::fs::read` to slurp the entire object into one `Vec<u8>` before handing back a single-item `ByteStream` — flagged in-code as "chunked streaming is a later refinement". For a large blob (an ingested document, a big attachment) that pins the whole file in RAM per concurrent download. Replaced it with a `read_chunks` helper that opens the file eagerly (so a missing object still fails `NotFound` at the call, before the stream is polled — unchanged semantics, and the existing `get("missing")` test still passes) and streams the body in 64 KiB chunks via `futures::stream::try_unfold` over `tokio::fs::File` — no new dependency (futures + tokio `io-util` were already in the crate). Memory is now bounded to one chunk regardless of object size; an I/O error mid-stream surfaces as a stream error through the same `map_io`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-storage --all-targets -D warnings` clean; full crate suite green (16 tests, 0 failed) incl. the new `get_streams_large_objects_in_multiple_chunks` (a 200 KiB object round-trips byte-exact **and** arrives as ≥2 non-empty chunks, proving it isn't buffered whole). Local-backend only — the S3/WebDAV backends already stream; no trait/API change. **Deferred:** a matching chunked-`put` (the write path still drains the incoming stream to disk chunk-by-chunk, which is already bounded, so no change needed there)._

_2026-07-01 — **Automation graph validation now rejects a Condition's dead-branch out-edges (SOUL §11)** — a `Condition` node routes execution solely through its `"true"`/`"false"` out-ports: the DAG executor (`executor.rs`, the `on_taken_branch` check) follows a condition's out-edge **only when the edge's `from_port` equals the branch the condition took**. So an out-edge leaving a condition on any *other* port — most commonly the default `""`, i.e. an edge a user drew on the canvas without picking a branch — is **dead**: it can never fire, and the automation silently does nothing down that path with no error. `Graph::validate` checked node-id uniqueness, edge endpoints, ≥1 trigger, no-edge-into-trigger, the collect-trigger/`commit_on` rules, and acyclicity — but not this — so a mis-wired condition persisted happily and failed silently at run time. Added a check (right before the acyclic pass) that every out-edge from a `Condition` node uses `from_port` `"true"` or `"false"`, erroring `edge from condition node '<id>' uses port '<p>' — a condition routes only through its 'true'/'false' out-ports` otherwise. Non-condition nodes ignore `from_port` (the executor takes all their out-ports), so the rule constrains only conditions. Because `validate` also runs on the executor's load path (`executor.rs:247`), this catches a broken graph both at author time (create/update route + the `manage_automation` tool) and defensively at run time. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-automation --all-targets -D warnings` clean; full suite green (54 lib + 10 integration, 0 failed) incl. the new `condition_out_edge_on_a_non_branch_port_is_rejected` (covers the default `""` port, an arbitrary `"maybe"` port, and — guarding against over-rejection — that the valid true/false form still passes). The one integration fixture with a condition (`tests/executor.rs`) already uses `"true"`/`"false"`, so nothing regressed. Pure in-crate validation change — no schema/executor-semantics/API touch._

_2026-07-01 — **k8s sandbox keepalive: an attached-but-quiet terminal no longer gets idle-suspended out from under the user (SOUL §20)** — the operator idle-suspends a workspace Pod (`replicas:0`) purely on the CR's `status.lastActivity`, and the only thing that advanced that clock was `K8sSandbox::ensure_inner` (which `exec_session`/`run` call at *start*). So an interactive PTY that stayed open but ran no new commands — user reading long output, or just typing (`session_write` never re-stamped the clock) — would, after `idle_ttl_seconds`, have its Pod scaled to 0 and its live `kubectl exec` killed. The api-layer `WorkspaceSandboxManager` already tracked open sessions (that's what protects the podman backend from its own idle reaper) but never pushed that liveness to the operator. Fix: added a **default-no-op `keepalive(workspace_id)` method to the `WorkspaceSandbox` trait** (podman needs nothing — its reaper skips a sandbox with open sessions), overridden by `K8sSandbox` to call the existing `patch_activity` (patches `status.lastActivity = now`); and a `WorkspaceSandboxManager::keepalive_active()` that, on **every 30s reaper tick**, refreshes the idle clock of every workspace with ≥1 live session. Collect-ids-under-a-short-read-lock, drop the lock, then await the backend keepalives (so a slow patch never holds the `live` map). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-exec -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; exec's 22 lib tests pass; two new `catalerum-api` unit tests (`keepalive_targets_only_workspaces_with_open_sessions`, `no_open_sessions_means_no_keepalive`) cover the pure `workspaces_with_sessions` selector without needing a DB. Additive + backward-compatible — the trait default keeps every non-k8s backend unchanged; no schema/migration/config touch. **Deferred:** stamping activity inline on each `session_write`/`session_read` (the 30s heartbeat already covers the window since `idle_ttl` is ≫ 30s; per-byte patching would be far chattier against the API server for no real gain)._

_2026-07-01 — **Mermaid ER diagrams now render entity attribute columns (§21 markdown engine)** — the `erDiagram` renderer (`catalerum-markdown/src/mermaid/er.rs`) previously *declared* an entity from its `ENTITY { … }` attribute block but threw the columns away ("aren't rendered yet"), so an ER diagram showed bare boxes with nothing inside. It now stacks the columns under the entity name inside the box as a `name: type [PK]` row per attribute, reusing flow's existing `<br/>`-split multi-line label path — so **no change to `flow.rs`**; the blast radius is ER-only. Restructured `to_svg` from a single streaming pass (which let a later relationship's `node_def` clobber an entity's rich label back to just its name) into a **collect-then-build** shape: one pass gathers first-seen entity order (drives layout), each entity's attribute rows, and the relationships; then nodes are defined once with the full multi-line label and edges wired by index, so a relationship mentioning an entity can never overwrite its declared columns. `parse_attribute` reads mermaid's `type name [KEY…] ["comment"]` rows → `name: type` plus any `PK`/`FK`/`UK` markers, dropping the quoted comment; each column line is individually escaped by flow's renderer (a `<` in a column name comes out `&lt;`, never raw), and flow's `node_size` already grows the box height/width to the stacked rows. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean; full crate suite green (94 lib + 54 integration tests, 0 failed) incl. two new `mermaid::er` tests — `attribute_block_columns_stack_under_the_entity_name` (name heads the box as line 0, columns render as `<tspan>` rows incl. the `PK` marker, and the relationship doesn't clobber them) and `attribute_comment_is_dropped_and_html_in_columns_is_escaped`. Pure-function, in-crate change — no schema/migration/API touch. **Deferred:** true table-style ER rendering (a header rule + two aligned type/name columns like mermaid.js) and attribute-level FK edges are still out of scope; this is the readable single-column approximation._

_2026-06-30 — **Chat self-improvement: the chat now proactively `remember`s durable facts about the user + their workflows (SOUL §22)** — closed the **write** half of the personalization loop. The *recall* half already ran every turn (`recall_memories` semantically pulls the 5 most relevant memories into the chat system prompt under "Relevant things you remember about the user", via `build_system_prompt`), and the `remember`/`recall`/`update_memory`/`forget` tools were all registered — but **nothing encouraged the model to save what it learns**, so the memory rarely grew and the chat never improved across conversations. Added a standing `CHAT_MEMORY_NUDGE` system message in `routes/ws.rs` (the same ephemeral-prefix mechanism as `DELEGATE_NUDGE`/`CHAT_OUTPUT_GUIDANCE` — inserted into every turn's seed before `seed_len`, so it's never persisted) that tells the chat to proactively `remember` durable, reusable facts: who the user is (role/expertise/projects/tools), how they like answers (format/depth/tone/language), recurring workflows + conventions, and corrections they give — at `user` scope by default (`workspace` for a shared fact); to `update_memory`/`forget` a changed/wrong fact rather than duplicate one already shown under the recall section (the nudge names that section by the **literal title `build_system_prompt` emits**, kept in sync by a test); and to skip one-off chatter/ephemeral task detail/secrets and never let the silent save delay the actual answer. Member+ holds `memory:write` (a Viewer is read-only, so a `remember` call simply fails closed — harmless). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; the 6 `routes::ws` tests pass incl. the new `memory_nudge_points_at_the_real_tools_and_recall_section` (asserts the nudge names `remember`/`update_memory`/`forget` and references the exact recall-section title `build_system_prompt` produces — guards the prompt + the renderer from drifting apart). Prompt-only — no schema, migration, or store change. **Deferred:** the §22 "background extractor that proposes memories from chats" (an out-of-band pass that mines memories independent of the model volunteering a `remember`) is still unbuilt; this nudge is the in-loop, agent-driven path to the same goal._

_2026-06-29 — **CalDAV sync: a `propstat`-level `404` no longer masquerades as a deletion (prevents wrongful event drop) (SOUL §8/§28)** — a real data-loss bug in the WebDAV `multistatus` parser. The `<status>` handler captured **any** status element into `entry.status`, and `is_deleted()` treats a `404` status (with no `calendar-data`) as a deletion — driving `deletions.push(uid)` in the `sync-collection` loop (`caldav.rs`). But RFC 4918 §13 lets a server split one response into a `200` propstat for the found properties **and a separate `404` propstat for requested-but-absent ones** (e.g. a `calendar-data` the server declined to inline). For such an *existing* resource the `404` propstat status overwrote `entry.status`, and since `sync-collection` requests carry only `getetag` (so `calendar_data` is `None`), `is_deleted()` returned **true** — the event would be wrongly deleted from the local store on the next sync. Fix: only capture the **response-level** `<status>` (the RFC 6578 deletion signal) by checking the status element's parent on the element stack is `response`, not `propstat`. `entry.status` is consumed solely by `is_deleted()`, so ignoring propstat statuses is safe and correct. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-calendar --all-targets -D warnings` clean; the full 37-test calendar suite green incl. two new tests — `split_propstat_404_does_not_look_like_a_deletion` (a 200-propstat + a 404-propstat on one existing resource ⇒ `status == None`, `!is_deleted()`; fails under the old any-status capture) and `response_level_status_is_still_captured` (a genuine response-level `404` still flags the deletion) — and the existing `parses_sync_collection_with_token_and_deletion` unchanged (the updated resource's propstat `200` is now simply not captured, which doesn't affect its `!is_deleted()`). Backend-only, self-contained in `multistatus.rs`. Companion to the prior `calendar-data` fragment-accumulation and href-decoding fixes — the CalDAV sync path now reads fragmented bodies in full, matches special-char-UID deletions, and no longer invents deletions from split propstats. **Deferred:** `entry.status` still keeps only the last response-level status if a server (non-conformantly) emits more than one; immaterial since a `response` has exactly one top-level status._

_2026-06-29 — **Bare email autolinks — completes the GFM extended-autolink extension (SOUL §21/§12)** — the deferred half of the earlier bare-URL work: a `local@domain.tld` typed in text now becomes a `mailto:` link (the angle form `<a@b.com>` already worked; bare emails — common in chat/agent output — rendered as plain text). Built on the same post-pass machinery: the scanner now tries `match_email` at each GFM boundary after `match_url`, the cheap signal gate adds `@` (so still zero-alloc on `@`-free spans — alloc budgets unchanged), and a new `Piece::Email` flows through the shared `emit_pieces`/`Inline::Link` path (so it inherits `is_safe_url` + `escape_attr` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). `match_email` uses GFM's conservative extended rule — a `[a-zA-Z0-9._+-]+` local part, `@`, a dotted domain of alphanumerics/`-`/`_`, with trailing `.`/`-`/`_` trimmed — so a bare `@handle` (no local part) and a dotless host (`user@localhost`) are correctly **left as text**, and code spans / link labels / the angle form are untouched as before. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32**; the full crate suite green — 93 lib + render_html (a new `bare_email_autolinks` test: `mailto:` dest with `+`/`.` local part kept, trailing-punct excluded, `@handle`/dotless-host left plain, code-span literal, and an email inside `*emphasis*` still linking) + allocations + security + streaming + fuzz + doctests. **Saw it work:** probed `to_html` — `foo.bar@example.com`, `a@b.co.uk.` (dot trimmed), `bob+tag@mail.example.org!` (bang excluded) all link; `@handle`, `user@localhost`, `` `x@y.com` `` stay plain; `_alice@corp.com_` links inside the emphasis. **Deferred:** the broader RFC local-part set (`!#$%&'*/=?^...`) the angle form accepts isn't honoured for the bare form (GFM's extension is deliberately narrower, to avoid false positives in prose); IDN domains as before._

_2026-06-29 — **Fetched-page table conversion now honours `colspan`/`rowspan` — the agent reads spanning tables without column corruption (SOUL §27)** — the HTML→Markdown converter (what the agent *reads* the web through) collected `<td>`/`<th>` cells 1:1, so a single spanning cell shifted every following column: a `colspan="2"` header or a `rowspan` label (ubiquitous in Wikipedia infoboxes, pricing/spec tables) misaligned the GFM grid and put data under the wrong heading — silent corruption of exactly the structured data tables are *for*. Replaced the row-collection loop with a **grid model** (`Vec<Vec<Option<String>>>`): each cell is placed at the next free column of its row, then its `colspan`×`rowspan` region is reserved — content in the top-left slot, `""` in the spanned remainder, and columns already claimed by a rowspan coming down from above are skipped — so the grid stays rectangular and every datum sits under its column. Per-column alignment is recovered from the first row that has cells (mapped across each cell's colspan); fully-empty rows (e.g. a row that's only rowspan continuations) are dropped; a new `span_attr` clamps the span to `1..=1000` so a malicious `colspan="99999999"` can't inflate the grid. GFM has no native span, but a rectangular grid with the content in the lead slot is the faithful, readable rendering. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean (backend crate, no wasm target); the full fetch suite green — 73 lib + 6 integration — incl. 3 new tests (a `colspan=2` header padding to keep data aligned; a `rowspan=2` cell carrying its column down so the next row's lone cell lands in column 2; a combined colspan+rowspan table staying rectangular + the absurd-span clamp) and every existing table test (`table_to_gfm`, alignment, caption, pipe-encoding) unchanged — the grid refactor is behaviour-preserving for non-spanning tables. Self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** the spanned slots are blank rather than repeating the spanning content (keeps cells unambiguous; a reader still sees the value once, in its starting column); deeply nested tables inside a cell still flatten to inline text (a GFM cell can't hold a block table)._

_2026-06-29 — **Hardened the raw-Cypher graph surface instead of removing it — closed a metadata/admin denylist gap + bounded the explorer's blast radius (SOUL §18/§19/§11/§6.3)** — the operator-facing "read-only Cypher over the derived graph" feature (the web **Graph** panel, `POST /graph/query`, and the §11 `GraphQuery` automation trigger) is flagged dangerous because its guard is a substring heuristic, not a parser. Rather than drop the feature, tightened it. **(1) Denylist gap, the real find:** `validate_graph_query_cypher` (catalerum-automation — the **single** guard all three entry points share, at authoring *and* execution) rejected writes + `CALL`/`LOAD`/`USE`/`UNION` but let **`SHOW`** / **`TERMINATE`** / privilege-admin verbs through — each is technically read-only and can carry a `$workspace_id` token, so it passed both checks while escaping the workspace read: `SHOW DATABASES|CONSTRAINTS|INDEXES … WHERE … $workspace_id` discloses cluster/schema metadata (and a `SHOW … WHERE` even satisfies the scope-presence test), and `TERMINATE TRANSACTIONS` can kill **another** tenant's running query (cross-tenant DoS). Added `SHOW`, `TERMINATE`, `GRANT`, `REVOKE`, `DENY`, `ALTER`, `RENAME` (and regrouped `DROP`) to `FORBIDDEN_CLAUSES`; whole-word tokenising means none false-reject this domain's properties (`updated_at`/`summary`/`starts_at`/`display_name`/`labels`/…), pinned by a no-false-positive test. **(2) Blast-radius bound:** `POST /graph/query` now caps returned rows at `MAX_GRAPH_QUERY_ROWS` (1 000) via a pure `cap_rows` helper and flags a capped result `truncated` — a scoped-but-broad read (`MATCH (n {workspace_id:$workspace_id}) RETURN n`) can no longer stream a whole workspace slice out in one response. Mirrored the `truncated` field into the web `GraphQueryResponse` (serde-`default`, so older payloads still decode) and the Graph panel's meta line ("capped — narrow the query"). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-automation -p catalerum-api --all-targets` clean + `cargo clippy -p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings` clean; tests green — automation `graph_query_*` (incl. the new `graph_query_cypher_rejects_metadata_and_admin_clauses`: 10 metadata/admin rejections + the property-name false-positive guard), api `routes::graph` (incl. the new `cap_rows_truncates_and_flags_only_when_over_the_cap`), and web `graph_query_response_decodes` (now asserts `truncated` defaults/decodes). **Residual (unchanged, honestly documented):** the `… = $workspace_id OR 1=1 …` structural-scope bypass still needs a real Cypher parser or the typed-query-only route (SOUL §18 hardening TODO); the row cap bounds the *returned* set, not Neo4j's server-side work (a Cypher `LIMIT` is still the way to bound that). **Recommended next (not done — config/ops change):** run this surface under a **read-only Neo4j credential** so a guard miss can't write even in principle (the explorer currently shares the read-write projection store)._

_2026-06-29 — **Headings now carry GitHub-style anchor ids — deep-linkable / TOC targets (SOUL §21/§12)** — continuing in the core engine (affects every rendered heading, in chat and the web docs the engine powers). `# Getting Started` now renders `<h2 id="getting-started">…`, so sections are addressable by `#slug` and a TOC can target them. **Shared slug helper** `heading_slug` (in `parser::inline`, next to `inline_text`): plain-text lowercased, punctuation dropped, whitespace runs collapsed to a single `-`, `-`/`_` kept, Unicode letters preserved (lowercased), no dangling trailing dash; empty (symbol-only heading) ⇒ no id emitted. **Stateless on purpose:** no `-1`/`-2` de-duplication, because the `StreamRenderer` renders each committed chunk via a fresh `to_html`, so cross-chunk dedup state is unavailable — a stateless slug makes the **streaming and one-shot renders agree byte-for-byte** (the byte-by-byte streaming-equivalence test confirms it). Wired into **both** renderers: the HTML string renderer (`escape_attr`'d id, so it's attribute-safe even when the heading text isn't) and the feature-gated **Leptos** renderer (`id=Option<String>` — `None` omits the attribute). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32**, plus `--features leptos --target wasm32` clean (validates the Leptos `view!` change); the **full** markdown suite green — 93 lib + render_html (a new `heading_anchor_slugs` test: multi-word, punctuation/underscore/trailing-dash, inline-markup-text-only, Unicode `café`, symbol-only⇒no-id, and an attribute-injection guard) + allocations (budgets unchanged) + security + streaming + fuzz + doctests; and `cargo test -p catalerum-web` green (6/6, the Leptos renderer compiles). **Updated the expectations this changed** (heading output now carries an id): the lib doctest, `headings_atx_and_setext` + the streaming prefix test in the markdown crate, and `catalerum-web`'s `delegates_to_the_engine_safely`. The `catalerum-fetch` `<h1>` references are HTML *input* to the readability extractor (reverse direction) — untouched. **Deferred:** duplicate-heading id de-duplication (omitted for stream/batch parity + rarity); no auto-injected anchor link/¶ marker (the id is enough for `#slug` navigation and a separate TOC component)._

_2026-06-29 — **GFM extended (bare) autolinks — `http(s)://…` / `www.…` typed in text are now clickable links (SOUL §21/§12)** — broadened the focus from niche diagram types to the **core inline grammar**, which affects *all* rendered content (chat, agent output). The engine only did CommonMark angle autolinks (`<https://…>`); bare URLs — which LLMs/chat emit constantly — rendered as plain text. Now they become links. **Architecture-aware approach:** the hot tokenizer finds inline-significant bytes via a SIMD/nibble set scan; adding `h`/`w` triggers would wreck that, and scanning flushed text runs would split URLs containing `_`/`*`/`~` (those are emphasis-delimiter bytes). Instead it's a **post-pass over the flattened inline tree** (`autolink_nodes`): `push_inline` already coalesces adjacent text (so intraword `_` in `…/Foo_bar` survives as one Text node), and a cheap `has_url_signal` gate means **no allocation on URL-free spans** (the alloc-budget test still passes unchanged). The scanner honours GFM boundary rules (start / after whitespace / `*_~(`), requires a dotted authority (so `http://localhost:3000` is left alone), and applies GFM trailing trimming (drop trailing `?!.,:*_~'"`, unbalanced `)`, and a trailing `&entity;`); `www.` gets an `http://` dest while keeping the shown text. Recurses into emphasis/strong/strike but **not** link text or code spans, and link/image labels parse via a new non-autolinking `parse_inlines_plain` (CommonMark forbids a link inside a link — this fixes a nested-`<a><a>` bug found mid-change). Autolinks flow through the existing `Inline::Link` render path, so they inherit `is_safe_url` + `escape_attr` + `rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"` — a mid-URL `"` is escaped, `javascript:` never matches (only http/https/www), and a `<` ends the scan (the rest is escaped, not injected). Also reaches the event-stream + Leptos renderers for free (just more `Link` nodes). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32**; the **full** crate suite green — 93 lib + render_html (2 new tests: the happy paths incl. `Foo_bar`/trailing-punct/paren-balance, and an over-trigger/injection guard) + allocations (budgets unchanged) + security + streaming + fuzz. **Saw it work:** probed `to_html` directly — `see https://example.com here`, `www.rust-lang.org!` (trailing `!` dropped, `http://` prefixed), `…/wiki/Foo_bar` (underscore kept), `(https://a.io/x)` (paren balanced), a URL inside `*emphasis*`, and the injection cases all render correctly; bare email + code-span + existing-link cases are correctly left untouched. **Caught two regressions** the suite surfaced: the nested-link bug (fixed via `parse_inlines_plain`) and a stale `mermaid_fence` integration test that asserted `classDiagram` was *unsupported* (it's supported since this session's class-diagram work) — updated it to use the still-unsupported `mindmap`. **Deferred:** bare email autolinks (`user@host.com` without `<>`) — the angle form still works; uppercase schemes beyond the case-insensitive prefix; IDN/punycode niceties._

_2026-06-29 — **New Mermaid diagram type: timelines (`timeline`) + verified that `\overbrace`/`\underbrace` can't stretch (a font limit, not a bug) (SOUL §21/§12)** — two findings this pass. **(1) Investigated the long-deferred over/underbrace non-stretching.** They already emit the stretchy brace glyphs (`U+23DE`/`U+23DF`, `<mo stretchy="true">`) but render as a tiny brace over the middle character. I rasterised three MathML encodings in the repo's headless Chromium — `accent="true"` (current), `accent="false"`, and no `accent` attr — and **none stretch**: Chromium's fallback math font lacks the horizontal glyph-assembly for the curly-brace characters, so this isn't fixable via MathML attributes (the `\overline` CSS-border trick doesn't transfer — a brace isn't a straight edge). Left the code unchanged and recorded the empirical result so the deferral isn't re-attempted; a real fix would need a bundled math font or an SVG-drawn brace, both out of scope. **(2) Added `timeline` diagrams** instead — a clean, font-independent SVG win that LLMs frequently emit for chronologies. **timeline.rs (new, ~250 lines, bespoke):** parses `TimeLabel : event : event …` period lines (a bare label ⇒ a period with no events) and optional `section`s; renders a title, per-section coloured bands spanning each run of consecutive same-section periods (palette-cycled, reusing `mod::PALETTE`), a shared horizontal axis with a section-coloured dot per period, bold time labels above the axis, and the events as tinted/bordered cards stacked below each period; **all text escape-safe**. `mod.rs` dispatches `timeline`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32**; 93 lib tests pass incl. 6 new timeline tests (periods/multi-event/title + one dot per period; two section bands with distinct palette colours + event tinting; a period with no events still gets a dot; `<script>`/`<t>` escaped; empty⇒unsupported; 7-case no-panic fuzz) and every existing diagram-type test unchanged. **Saw it work:** added a timeline to the gallery (Early/Modern sections; 1991/1994/2008/2015 with the 2015 period carrying two events), rasterised with the repo's headless Chromium — blue/green section bands and dots, bold year labels on the axis, event cards stacked (Rust 1.0 + WebAssembly under 2015), all colour-coded by section. Additive — zero impact on existing types. **Deferred:** long event text isn't wrapped (card width is clamped, text may overflow); no per-period colour overrides; the axis is evenly spaced by column, not proportional to the (free-text) time values._

_2026-06-29 — **New Mermaid diagram type: gantt charts (`gantt`) (SOUL §21/§12)** — one of the top-requested Mermaid types (project timelines), now rendered as a real **date-axis timeline**: sections group task rows, each task a bar positioned by its start/end on a shared time scale, with `done`/`active`/`crit` status colours and `milestone` diamonds. **gantt.rs (new, ~360 lines, bespoke — not a node graph, so no flow reuse):** a parser for the metadata grammar `Label : [tags,] [id,] start, length` where a token is classified by shape — status tag (`done`/`active`/`crit`/`milestone`), a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, `after <id…>` (starts at the latest referenced end), a `<n>d`/`w`/`h`/`m` duration, or the bare id — so the variable-arity field list parses without positional guessing. Start resolves to explicit/`after`/the previous task's end (implicit chaining); end to an end-date / start+duration / zero-length milestone / a default day. Dates use a **built-in civil-day calendar** (Howard Hinnant `days_from_civil`/`civil_from_days`, round-trip tested) because the crate deliberately pulls in **no date library** (stays wasm-light). Renders a title, tinted section bands, left-gutter task labels, status-coloured bars (milestones as diamonds), and a start/end date axis; **all text escape-safe**. `mod.rs` dispatches `gantt`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32** (fixed an `unnecessary_lazy_evaluations` on the end-resolve); 87 lib tests pass incl. 7 new gantt tests (civil-day round-trip incl. a leap day + a 30-day span; sections/tasks/title + one bar per task + correct axis span; the four status colours + a milestone polygon and bar-count excluding it; an `after`-dependency + implicit-start chain landing on the right end date; `<script>`/`<x>` escaped; empty⇒unsupported; 9-case no-panic fuzz incl. a bad date and a lone milestone) and every existing diagram-type test unchanged. **Saw it work:** added a gantt to the gallery (Design/Build/Ship sections, `after`-chained tasks, a `crit` QA bar and a `milestone` launch), rasterised with the repo's headless Chromium — bars step correctly along the `after` chain (Mockups starts where Research ends, Backend/Frontend share the post-Mockups start), grey/blue/red status fills, a purple launch diamond, and the axis reading 2014-01-01 → 2014-02-03. Additive — zero impact on existing types. **Deferred:** the axis shows only the span endpoints (no intermediate gridline dates / `axisFormat`); `excludes`/weekends, `todayMarker`, click/interaction, and bar text labels are skipped; sub-day `h`/`m` units are converted to fractional days (fine for day-scale charts but not separately tick-labelled)._

_2026-06-29 — **New Mermaid diagram type: class diagrams (`classDiagram`) (SOUL §21/§12)** — the single most common Mermaid type still unsupported in software/LLM output, now rendered with real **three-compartment boxes** (name/stereotype · attributes · methods) and the full set of **UML relationship arrowheads**. **flow.rs (reuse seam):** the layered layout is now driven by caller-supplied box sizes — extracted `layout_with_sizes(graph, sizes)` from `layout()` (ranking unchanged; placement reads the passed `(w,h)`), and made `Placed`/`Layout` + `box_exit` `pub(super)` — so a sibling type that draws its own node bodies reuses the battle-tested ranking/centring/cycle-cap without flow's text sizing. **class.rs (new, ~330 lines):** a parser for both the `class X { +T m }` block form and the `X : +member` line form (visibility `+/-/#/~` kept, `(` ⇒ method compartment else attribute, à la Mermaid), `<<interface>>` stereotypes (rendered «guillemet» italic), and `~T~` generics → `<T>`; relationships parse all six operators — inheritance `<|--`, realization `..|>` (dashed), composition `*--` (filled diamond), aggregation `o--` (hollow diamond), association `-->`/`--`, dependency `..>` — plus `"1"`/`"*"` multiplicities and `: label`. Self-contained in `math.rs`. **Resolves** the "doesn't stretch" deferral noted in the accents, overset/braces, and array entries (for over/underline specifically; `\overbrace`/`\underbrace` braces are a different glyph and still don't stretch)._

_2026-06-29 — **New Mermaid diagram type: state diagrams (`stateDiagram` / `stateDiagram-v2`) (SOUL §21/§12)** — a state diagram is a directed graph, so rather than write a bespoke engine I made the flowchart's layered layout + SVG renderer **reusable** and drove them from a small state-syntax parser. **flow.rs (reuse seam):** `Graph`/`Dir`/`Shape`/`Style` + `Graph::{new,add_edge,node_def,is_empty}` + `render_graph` are now `pub(super)`; added a `Shape::Point` (a small filled dot, no label) for the `[*]` pseudo-state. **state.rs (new, ~120 lines):** a two-pass parser — pass 1 collects `state "desc" as id` labels + the `A --> B : label` transitions, pass 2 builds a `flow::Graph` (named states → `Round` nodes with their display label, each `[*]` → the shared start `Point` when a source / shared end `Point` when a target) and calls `flow::render_graph`. `mod.rs` dispatches any `stateDiagram*` header to it. **Cyclic-layout fix (general, benefits flowcharts too):** state diagrams are routinely cyclic (`Running --> Idle`), and the longest-path ranking let a back-edge push ranks up every pass — a 5-state diagram laid out **1196px** tall. Capped each rank at `n-1` (the most a DAG of `n` nodes can need, so a true DAG is unaffected); the same diagram is now **444px**. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32**; 63 lib tests pass incl. 4 new state tests (states/transitions/labels + two pseudo-dots; `state "…" as id` label aliasing; shared start dot reused across two outgoing transitions; contentless ⇒ raw-source fallback) + the dispatch/unsupported tests updated; the engine's no-panic fuzz + security suites green. **Saw it work:** added a state diagram to the gallery (`[*] --> Idle --> Running --> Idle/Failed --> [*]`), rasterised with the repo's headless Chromium — rounded-rect states, filled `[*]` dots (start + end), labelled transitions, compact layout after the cycle cap. Additive — zero impact on existing diagram types (no flowchart syntax maps to `Point`). **Deferred:** composite states (`state X { … }`), notes, choice/fork `<<…>>` and concurrency `--` are skipped (flattened/ignored); isolated declared-but-untransitioned states aren't placed; the reused DAG layout is readable but not hierarchy-optimal for dense cyclic graphs._

_2026-06-29 — **Mermaid flowcharts support the `&` node-group shorthand (`A & B --> C`) (SOUL §21/§12)** — previously a flowchart using `&` (the fan-in/fan-out shorthand) failed to parse — `&` is neither an edge-start nor a node-id char, so `lex_node` errored and the **whole diagram fell back to raw source**. Reworked `parse_statement` to treat each edge endpoint as a *group* of nodes (`node ('&' node)*`): an edge between two groups expands to the **cartesian product** of edges (`A & B --> C & D` ⇒ A→C, A→D, B→C, B→D), the same data flowing into the existing layout/render. A plain `A --> B` is just the one-element-group case, so chains, inline edge labels, and shaped/labelled grouped nodes (`A[Start] & B[Init] --> C`) all keep working. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32**; 59 lib tests pass incl. a new `ampersand_node_groups_fan_in_and_out` (fan-in 2 edges, fan-out 2 edges, 2×2 cartesian = 4 edges + all nodes present, shaped grouped nodes) + 4 added no-panic cases (trailing/doubled/leading `&`, `&`-then-edge) — the existing simple/one-line/direction/shapes flowchart tests are unchanged (the rework preserves single-node behaviour). **Saw it work:** the gallery flowchart now uses `C & D --> E` (Process **and** Reject converge on Done); rasterised with the repo's headless Chromium — both edges land on the Done node, no raw fallback. Self-contained in `flow.rs`. **Deferred:** chained groups across `&` and edges follow the cartesian rule (Mermaid's semantics); subgraphs are still ignored (their clustering needs a layout change, unlike this parse-only addition)._

_2026-06-29 — **LaTeX `aligned`/`align` environments now align their columns at the `&` (SOUL §21/§12)** — multi-line derivations (`\begin{aligned} f(x) &= … \\ &= … \end{aligned}`) rendered as a borderless `<mtable>` with **centered** columns, so the `=` signs didn't line up — the whole point of an alignment environment. _2026-06-29 — **Per-workspace sandbox + a true Kubernetes operator (SOUL §20/§18)** — the container/k8s executor backends spun a **fresh** container/Pod per command or session; there was no compute boundary per workspace. Added an opt-in (`[exec].per_workspace`) posture: **one long-lived, secure sandbox per workspace**, into which every terminal session and `run_command` `exec`s, sharing a persistent `/work` volume. A new `WorkspaceSandbox` trait (`catalerum-exec/src/sandbox.rs`) has two impls: **`PodmanSandbox`** — a deterministically-named `catalerum-ws-<id>` container per workspace via podman/docker (adopt-by-name on restart, per-ws ensure gate, sessions = `exec -it`, idle reaper destroys it keeping the named volume); and **`K8sSandbox`** — declares a `WorkspaceSandbox` **custom resource** (`catalerum.dev/v1alpha1`) and `kubectl exec`s into the Pod the new **`catalerum-operator`** reconciles. The operator (`crates/catalerum-operator`, kube-rs 2.0.1 / k8s-openapi 0.26) is a real CRD controller with a finalizer: per CR it server-side-applies a per-workspace Namespace + hardened Deployment (drop ALL caps, no-priv-escalation, RuntimeDefault seccomp, `fsGroup`, `tail -f /dev/null` keepalive) + `/work` PVC + ResourceQuota/LimitRange + a precise NetworkPolicy (Full = internet egress minus `169.254/16` metadata, same-ns ingress; Isolated = DNS + same-ns) + the API's per-ns `pods/exec` RoleBinding (created **before** Ready so the API never races its grant); idle-suspends via `replicas:0` (the API's `status.lastActivity` patch wakes it) and hard-deletes per the CR TTLs. CRD types live in a small shared `catalerum-k8s` crate (keeps kube out of `catalerum-core`); the API/exec crates stay **kube-free** (kubectl only). Wiring: `WorkspaceSandboxManager` (`catalerum-api`) owns lazy-ensure + DB row + idle/self-exit reaper; `TerminalManager.open()` + `RunCommandTool` route container/k8s through it; new migration `0037_workspace_sandboxes` (one row per workspace, PK = `workspace_id`) + `WorkspaceSandboxRepo`; config `[exec].per_workspace`/`idle_timeout_secs`/`volume_size`/`sandbox_network`; `deploy/` kustomize (CRD + operator RBAC/Deployment + API RBAC) + operator Dockerfile + `just crd`/`operator-image`/`operator-dev`/`operator-install`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy` clean across catalerum-core/store/exec/api/operator/k8s + the binary (workspace clippy green except the pre-existing unrelated `catalerum-markdown` WIP); the podman integration test (real podman 5.8.3) ensures one container, runs a command + two sessions `exec`ing into the **same** container over a shared `/work`, then destroys; operator unit tests (CRD identity, Full/Isolated NetworkPolicy, hardened Deployment) green; `cargo run -p catalerum-operator -- crd` emits the committed CRD yaml; store repo tests (upsert/status/touch/`mark_all_stopped`/tenancy/one-per-workspace) green **against live Postgres**; terminal-manager + `run_command` tests still green. **Deferred:** the k8s end-to-end (apply CR → operator → exec) is unit/structure-verified but not yet run on a live kind+Calico cluster; the API needs its own Dockerfile for in-cluster deploy; ephemeral-subdir cleanup inside the shared container and `run`-time env injection on the k8s path are minor follow-ups; `host_dir=None` for sandboxed sessions disables the workdir file tools (`read_file`/`create_file`/`edit_file`) exactly as the per-session k8s backend already does._

_2026-06-29 — **Mermaid sequence diagrams now render activation bars (`activate`/`deactivate`) (SOUL §21/§12)** — closes the deferral from the autonumber entry: `activate`/`deactivate` were among the silently-skipped directives, so a participant's active period wasn't shown. Added `Ev::Activate(p)`/`Ev::Deactivate(p)` (parsed from `activate <p>`/`deactivate <p>`, replacing the skip), and during the render walk a per-participant **stack** of start-y tracks nesting: a `deactivate` pops and emits a bar `(participant, depth, y0, y1)`; any bar left open at the end is closed to the last event's y. `render_activation` draws a thin (`ACT_W=10`) rounded rectangle on the lifeline, **nested bars shifted right** so the stack is visible, drawn behind the messages so arrows land on the bar edge.
