_2026-06-29 — **Sandboxed one-shot `run` now sets `HOME` (defaulted to the cwd), matching the interactive PTY path (SOUL §20)** — the scrubbed-env (`sandboxed`) executor dropped the inherited environment and, for a one-shot `run`, replaced it with **only `PATH`** — no `HOME` at all, even when a confined `cwd` was given. The interactive PTY path already defaults `HOME` to the cwd (a scrubbed shell needs it); the one-shot path didn't, so a sandboxed automation command (`git …`, `python …`, anything reading `~/.config`/`~/.cache`) ran with `HOME` unset and could fail or misbehave. Fixed `run` to default `HOME` to `cwd` inside the scrub block (set **before** the caller's env, so an explicit `HOME` in `cmd.env` still wins) — bringing it in line with the PTY path. `TERM` is deliberately **not** set on the non-PTY one-shot path (the child isn't a terminal). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-exec --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `sandboxed_run_defaults_home_to_cwd` test (scrubbed `sh -c 'printf %s "$HOME"'` with a cwd → `$HOME` == cwd; a caller `HOME` overrides) plus all 18 exec tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `lib.rs`. **Deferred:** when a scrubbed execution has **no** cwd at all (both paths), `HOME` is still unset — rarer (sandbox sessions are created with a confined workdir), so a synthetic fallback (e.g. a temp dir) is left as a possible follow-up rather than guessed at here._

_2026-06-29 — **Fetched-page `<var>`/`<cite>`/`<dfn>` now render as emphasis (SOUL §27)** — completes the inline-element coverage thread: these three are rendered **italic** by browsers (a variable, a work's title, a defining term) but the converter flattened them to plain text, dropping the emphasis a reader sees. Added them to the existing `"em" | "i"` arm in `inline_element` (→ `*…*`). With this the converter now covers essentially all common inline semantic elements — strong/b, em/i/var/cite/dfn, del/s/strike, sup, sub, q, code/kbd/samp, a, img, br. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `var_cite_dfn_render_as_emphasis` unit test plus all 69 fetch lib tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** `<mark>` (highlight) remains the one common inline element with no faithful portable-Markdown rendering — left flattened to text (its content is preserved, only the highlight styling is lost)._

_2026-06-29 — **Fetched-page `<kbd>`/`<samp>` now render as inline code (SOUL §27)** — both elements are monospace in a browser (keyboard input / sample program output), but the HTML→Markdown converter flattened them to plain text, dropping the monospace distinction a reader sees (`press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>` → `press Ctrl+C`). Routed `kbd`/`samp` through the existing `<code>` arm in `inline_element`, so they become inline code with the same backtick-escaping and empty-skip handling (`press \`Ctrl\`+\`C\``). Inline code is the faithful Markdown equivalent of these monospace elements. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `kbd_and_samp_render_as_inline_code` unit test (keyboard combo, sample output, empty `<kbd>`) plus all 68 fetch lib tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`, closes a deferral noted in the sup/sub entry. **Deferred:** `<var>` (a variable, italic) and `<cite>` (a citation, italic) could map to emphasis, and `<mark>` (highlight) has no portable Markdown form — left as the converter's remaining minor element gaps._

_2026-06-28 — **CalDAV multistatus parser accumulates `calendar-data` across fragments instead of overwriting (SOUL §8/§28)** — the WebDAV multistatus XML handler set `entry.calendar_data = Some(value)` on **each** text/CDATA parser event for a `<calendar-data>` element, so when a server delivers the ICS body as more than one event — plain text interleaved with a `<![CDATA[…]]>` section is the realistic case — only the **last** fragment survived and the rest of the event body was silently lost (a parse-then-store of a truncated VEVENT). Changed it to accumulate (`get_or_insert_with(String::new).push_str(&value)`), which reconstructs the full body; the common single-event case is unchanged (append onto an empty buffer == set). Other fields (`href`/`getetag`/`status`) are single-token and keep their existing semantics. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-calendar --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `calendar_data_spanning_text_and_cdata_is_accumulated` regression test (text + CDATA + text → all three fragments present; it fails under the old overwrite, keeping only the trailing text) plus all 35 calendar tests pass — the existing `parses_sync_collection_with_token_and_deletion` is unchanged. Backend-only, self-contained in `multistatus.rs`. Pairs with the prior href-decoding fix — together the CalDAV sync path now both reads a fragmented body in full and matches a special-character UID's deletion. **Deferred:** `trim_text(true)` trims each *text* fragment's edge whitespace, so whitespace landing exactly at a text↔CDATA boundary could be dropped — immaterial for real ICS bodies (no server fragments mid-line) and CDATA itself is never trimmed._

_2026-06-28 — **CalDAV deletion now percent-decodes the resource href, so an event whose UID needs URL-encoding is correctly reconciled (SOUL §8/§28)** — when a CalDAV `sync-collection` REPORT reports a *deleted* resource (no body to read a real UID from), `uid_from_href` recovers the UID from the conventional `<uid>.ics` resource name — but it used the raw path segment verbatim. A UID containing characters that must be percent-encoded in a URL path (a space, `#`, non-ASCII, …) arrives as e.g. `My%20Event%20%231.ics`, so the derived UID was `My Event %231`-encoded and **didn't match** the raw VEVENT UID stored at ingest → the deletion silently failed to reconcile (a deleted event lingered in the catalogue). Added a small inline `percent_decode` (no new dep, mirroring the in-crate iCal DURATION parser): `%XX` → byte, malformed/truncated `%` kept literal, invalid UTF-8 lossy, plain-ASCII unchanged (the common UID case is a no-op). Applied it in `uid_from_href` and to `collection_name` (so a calendar display name like `My%20Calendar` shows as `My Calendar`). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-calendar --all-targets -D warnings` clean; the extended `uid_from_href_uses_file_stem` (now incl. `My%20Event%20%231.ics`→`My Event #1`, `caf%C3%A9.ics`→`café`), a new `percent_decode_handles_escapes_and_malformed` (no-op/`%20`/UTF-8/`100%`/`%ZZ`/`%2`), and `collection_name_decodes_the_path_segment` plus all 34 calendar tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `caldav.rs`. **Deferred:** a server that names resources by an opaque slug (not `<uid>.ics`) still can't be matched by filename — the documented best-effort limit; this only improves the conformant `<uid>.ics` case for special-character UIDs._

_2026-06-28 — **Emerged-UI `initial_state` size cap now counts object entries, not just array items (SOUL §12/§13)** — `validate_ui_spec` bounds an AI-authored UI's seed `initial_state` via `count_json_elements` against `MAX_INITIAL_STATE_ELEMENTS` (10 000), but that counter only tallied **array** items (and recursed into object *values*) — it never counted an object's own **entries**. So a key-heavy object with no arrays (`{"k0":0,…,"k50000":0}`) summed to **0** and slipped straight past the cap the validator exists to enforce, letting a buggy/adversarial spec seed an unbounded state map (JSONB storage + client serialization + renderer state bloat). Added `map.len()` to the object arm so each object's entry count is included (arrays unchanged), matching the function's name and the cap's "bound the seed state" intent. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-core --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `rejects_oversized_object_initial_state` unit test (a >10k-key object now rejected as `TooLarge`) plus all 42 core lib tests pass — the existing `rejects_oversized_initial_state` (array path) is unchanged, and no legitimate small-object spec is affected (10k is generous). Backend-only, self-contained in `model_ui.rs`; consistent with the DoS-cap hardening elsewhere (SSE decoder, email response, backup segments). **Deferred:** a single enormous **string** value still counts 0 — a separate byte-size metric, likely already bounded by request-body limits; the structural element count is what this cap targets._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page `<q>` inline quotations keep their quote marks (SOUL §27)** — the HTML→Markdown converter flattened the `<q>` element to its bare text, dropping the quotation marks a browser renders around it — so `She said <q>hello</q>` became `She said hello`, losing the quoting the reader/agent would see. Added a `"q"` arm in `inline_element` wrapping the content in `"…"` via the existing `wrapped` helper (so inline formatting inside the quote survives, an empty `<q>` adds nothing, and edge whitespace is preserved). Plain Markdown has no `<q>` syntax, so straight double quotes are the faithful rendering. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `inline_quotation_keeps_quote_marks` unit test (quoted text, emphasis-inside-quote, empty `<q>`) plus all 67 fetch lib tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Re-confirmed deferral — GFM bare-URL autolinking:** traced the markdown engine's inline path and found its `parse_inlines` fast path returns a single borrowed Text node for plain prose (no tokenize/alloc); autolinking bare `http(s)://` would require scanning every Text node for `://`, eroding exactly that hot path the engine is built around — a perf/design tradeoff that's the user's call, not an autonomous one, so it stays deferred (with this concrete reason now recorded)._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page ordered lists now honour `<ol start="N">` (SOUL §27)** — the HTML→Markdown list renderer always numbered ordered-list items from 1, ignoring the `start` attribute — so a continued or offset list (`<ol start="5">`, common in step-by-step docs split across sections) renumbered to `1.` `2.` …, silently changing the meaning the agent reads. `list()` now seeds its counter from the `<ol>`'s `start` (parsed from the element attribute; a missing/non-numeric value falls back to 1; unordered lists ignore it), and the per-item increment is `saturating_add` so a pathological huge `start` can't overflow. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `ordered_list_honours_start_attribute` unit test (`start="5"`→`5.`/`6.`; invalid `start="x"`→`1.`; `start` on a `<ul>` ignored) plus all 66 fetch lib tests pass — the existing `nested_ordered_list`/`unordered_list` tests are unchanged (no `start` ⇒ identical output). Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** the `reversed` attribute (count-down lists) is still not honoured — rarer, and it needs a pre-pass to count items before numbering; left as a noted follow-up._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page table `<caption>` is no longer dropped — it renders as a line above the table (SOUL §27)** — `table()` collected only `<tr>` cells, so a `<caption>` (the table's title/description — common on Wikipedia and data-heavy pages: "Table 3: Quarterly revenue by region") was silently discarded, losing real context the agent reads. Now the direct `<caption>` child is captured first and emitted as a paragraph immediately above the table (blank-line separated, so it reads as the table's heading), with its inline formatting preserved (a link/`code`/emphasis in the caption survives). A skipped or empty caption contributes nothing; a table with no rows still emits nothing. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `table_caption_renders_above_the_table` unit test (caption → line above; an inline link in the caption preserved) plus all 65 fetch lib tests pass — the existing alignment/`table_to_gfm` tests are unchanged (caption-less tables behave exactly as before). Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Considered but deferred:** GFM **bare-URL autolinking** in `catalerum-markdown` (a pasted `https://…` becoming clickable in chat) is higher-value but architecturally risky in that engine's SIMD inline scanner — it would need `h`/`:` as scan triggers (a perf + correctness hit on the most-fuzzed component) or a separate post-pass over Text nodes; left for a focused change rather than forced here._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page tables now preserve column alignment (SOUL §27)** — the HTML→Markdown converter emitted every GFM table's delimiter row as a flat `| --- | --- |`, discarding the source columns' alignment — so a right-aligned numeric column or a centred header read as default-left, losing a real signal on the data tables the agent fetches. `table()` now derives per-column alignment from the **header (first non-empty) row's** cells — each cell's `align` attribute, else a `text-align` in its `style` — via a small `Align` enum (`None`/`Left`/`Center`/`Right`) whose `marker()` emits the GFM form (`:---`, `:---:`, `---:`, `---`); `cell_align` reads the attribute first and falls back to parsing the style (`justify`/unknown → none). Columns past the header (ragged rows) default to none. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `table_preserves_column_alignment` unit test (left/center/right via `align=`, right via `text-align` style, and an unaligned table still producing the plain `---` delimiter) plus all 64 fetch lib tests pass — the existing `table_to_gfm` is unchanged, so no regression for unaligned tables. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** alignment is taken from the header row only (GFM alignment is per-column anyway); `<col>`/`<colgroup>` alignment and per-`<td>`-only alignment (no header cell) aren't consulted — both rare, and the header is the conventional source._

_2026-06-28 — **LaTeX math engine adds `\overset`/`\underset` and `\overbrace`/`\underbrace` (SOUL §21/§12)** — extends the accent/binom work with the common over/under constructs. `\overset{mark}{base}`/`\underset{mark}{base}` stack an **arbitrary** expression (not a fixed accent glyph) over/under the base — a new `M::Stack { base, mark, over }` variant rendering a full-size (non-accent) `<mover>`/`<munder>` (so `\underset{x \to 0}{\lim}` reads as a proper limit, `\overset{!}{=}` as an annotated relation). `\overbrace`/`\underbrace` reuse the existing `Accent` machinery with the stretchy curly-bracket glyphs (U+23DE/U+23DF). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean **native + wasm32**; 53 lib tests pass incl. a new `overset_underset_and_braces` (mover/munder shapes, brace glyphs, accent flag on braces); the engine's no-panic fuzz covers the new arms. **Saw it work:** added a stacks/braces line to the gallery, rasterised it with the repo's headless Chromium at 2× — overset (`!` above `=`) and underset (`x → 0` below `lim`) stack correctly. **Deferred:** as with `\overline`/`\underline`, the over/underbrace glyph doesn't *stretch* across a multi-element group in current browser MathML (it renders a centred brace) — readable and correct, just not spanning; a label on a brace (`\overbrace{…}^{n}`) lands as an msup to the upper-right rather than centred above the brace._

_2026-06-28 — **Chat file uploads now land in a files store as references, not inlined bytes — with a settable default store and agent copy/stage tools (SOUL §9/§12/§13/§20)** — a chat turn was text-only; the only way to give the agent a file was the Files panel out-of-band. Added an upload affordance to the chat composer that pushes each picked file to a **files store** (`PUT /storage/objects/chat/<ts>-<rand>-<name>`, no `?store=` → the user's default) and attaches only a **reference** to the message — the bytes are never embedded. **Three parts, all decided with the user.** **(A) Settable default files store** — a new per-`(workspace,user)` `StorageSettings { default_store }` record mirroring `SearchSettings` end-to-end (core model, migration `0034_storage_settings.sql`, `StorageSettingsRow` + `StorageSettingsRepo` get/set, `Store::storage_settings()`, `GET/PUT /storage-settings` in `routes/settings.rs`, and a "Files" tab in the web Settings dialog). The store resolver `routes/storage.rs::resolve` was refactored into a reusable `resolve_store(registry, store, ws, user_id, name)` whose no-`?store=` fallback order is now **per-user default → `[storage]` config default → sole-store inference** (a stale per-user pick falls through rather than erroring). **(B) Structured chat attachments** — `Message.attachments: Vec<Attachment>` (reusing the calendar `Attachment` shape) + migration `0035_message_attachments.sql` (a `[]` JSONB column), threaded through `NewMessage`/`MessageRow`/the message SQL; the chat WS frame carries them, persists them on the user turn, and `to_chat_messages` renders a compact reference block (filename, type, size, store + key) into the **ephemeral** prompt the model sees — so the stored content stays clean and the model learns the file exists and how to reach it. **(C) Two Boa- and LLM-callable tools** — `copy_object` (store→store, streams `get`→`put` across backends then catalogues + ingests + fires the `StorageObject` trigger exactly like an upload; gated `storage:write`) and `stage_object` (the inverse of `persist_terminal`: streams a stored object into a terminal session's workdir so the shell can work on it, resolving *any* source store via `resolve_store`; gated `exec:run`). Both are normal registry `Tool`s, so they're automatically reachable from §11 Boa code nodes via `catalerum.callTool` with no Boa-side change. **Verified:** full gate `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean **and** `catalerum-web` wasm32 `-D warnings` clean; the native suite passes against live Postgres (91 test groups, 0 failures) including two new DB-gated store tests (`messages_attachments_repo` — a user turn round-trips its references, assistant rows stay empty; `storage_settings_repo` — default-store upsert/overwrite/clear) which also prove migrations 0034/0035 apply; `trunk build` ✅. **Deferred:** an attachment reference records only the key (not the resolved store name), so changing your default store mid-conversation could stale a prior reference — acceptable, matches the calendar attachment pattern; no dedicated `copy_object`/`stage_object` dispatch tests (they'd need a test-only `StorageRegistry` constructor + an executor for staging — the streaming primitives they reuse are already covered, and the round-trip is in the e2e plan); orphaned uploads from an abandoned send are not garbage-collected; `copy_object` is registered only when a config store exists (a runtime-only deployment is an unusual edge)._

_2026-06-28 — **Backup store-segment naming can no longer emit a path-traversing `..` segment (SOUL §30/§13)** — `safe_segment` (which turns a store name into the `<prefix>/<id>/objects/<segment>/` sub-path of a backup) sanitised everything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` to `_` and empty→`store`, but **kept `.` and `..`** since dots are allowed — so a store named `..` (or any all-dots config name) produced a literal `..` segment, making blob keys `…/objects/../<key>` that resolve *out* of the `objects/` root: a local-FS or WebDAV dest rejects `..` outright (the whole backup errors), and S3 stores a confusing literal key that restore mis-routes. Its own doc promised "a safe path segment", which `.`/`..` violate. Fixed by extending the fallback: an empty result **or** an all-dots segment (`.`/`..`/`...`) now becomes `store` (and `segments_for` then dedupes multiple such names → `store`, `store-1`, …). A `/`-containing name with `..` was already neutralised (the `/` → `_`, so `a/../b` → `a_.._b`), and a legitimately dotted name (`my.store`, `.hidden`) is still preserved. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-backup --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 6 backup lib tests pass with new `safe_segment` cases (`.`/`..`/`...`→`store`, `a/../b`→`a_.._b`, `.hidden` kept) and a `segments_for` case proving `[".", "..", ""]`→`store`/`store-1`/`store-2`. Backend-only, self-contained in `lib.rs`; matches the path-traversal guards the local-FS (`resolve`) and WebDAV (`validate_key`) backends already enforce. **Deferred:** store names remain free-form at config time (no authoring-time validation) — `safe_segment` is the single chokepoint, and the manifest records the chosen segment per store so restore round-trips regardless of the original name._

_2026-06-28 — **SSE chat-stream decoder is now memory-bounded against a misbehaving gateway (SOUL §7/§13)** — the streaming chat decoder (`sse.rs`) buffered raw body bytes into `self.buf` until a `\n`, and accumulated `data:` lines into `self.data` until a blank-line terminator — **with no cap on either**. A buggy/compromised LLM gateway (catalerum is self-hostable and the gateway may be a 3rd-party/self-hosted llmleaf/OpenRouter endpoint) could stream an endless line, or endless `data:` lines that never terminate an event, and OOM the worker — the exact threat model `catalerum-email`'s `read_json_capped` already hardens for HTTP bodies, but the SSE path had no equivalent. Added a 16 MiB `MAX_SSE_RETAINED` bound on the retained bytes (unparsed `buf` + the running `data_len` of the current event's accumulated lines). Past it the decoder **poisons**: it drops its buffers and emits nothing further, so the consumer sees a clean end-of-stream instead of an OOM. The cap is vast headroom for a real chat stream (KBs retained — one partial line / one small event), so it never triggers in normal use; the public API stays infallible (`push`/`finish` return empty once poisoned). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-llm --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 12 sse tests pass incl. 2 new (`an_endless_line_is_bounded_then_poisons_the_decoder` — a >16 MiB no-newline blob is dropped and a later well-formed event yields nothing; `many_data_lines_without_a_blank_terminator_are_bounded` — 32 MiB of un-terminated `data:` lines poisons rather than retaining) and the 4 existing decoder tests (normal split-chunk/CRLF/`[DONE]`/multi-event paths unchanged). Backend-only, self-contained in `sse.rs`. **Deferred:** poisoning ends the stream silently (no surfaced error) — sufficient since it only triggers under an abusive upstream where terminating *is* the correct outcome; the cap is per-decoder/per-request, complementing (not replacing) any transport-level read timeout._

_2026-06-28 — **Stored HTML objects are now indexed as readable text, not raw markup (SOUL §10/§27)** — the §10 object indexer's `extract_text` lossy-UTF-8-decoded a text-like object and indexed it **verbatim**, so an `.html` file went into full-text + embeddings as its raw source — `<div>`/`<span>`, every class/`style` attribute, and the contents of `<script>`/`<style>` — polluting search (a query could match a CSS class or inline JS rather than the page's words). Fixed by routing HTML/XHTML through `catalerum_fetch::html_to_markdown` (the same converter the fetch tool uses, now an ingest dependency — `catalerum-fetch` depends only on `catalerum-core`, so no cycle) before indexing, with `main_content_only:false` (a stored file may be a fragment — index all of it, don't risk a heuristic dropping content) and links/images off (clean, low-noise text). A new `is_html` helper gates this on the bare type (`text/html`/`application/xhtml+xml`, charset param tolerated); every other text-like type (JSON/YAML/XML/CSV/NDJSON/…) is still indexed verbatim, since there the structure *is* the content. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-ingest --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `extract_text_renders_html_to_readable_text` unit test (heading/paragraph text kept; tags, CSS, and `<script>` body gone; charset-param HTML → `plain`; XML still verbatim) plus all 54 ingest lib tests pass. **Pairs with the previous entry:** local storage now *types* `.html` files and the indexer now *reads* them well. **Deferred:** SVG (`image/svg+xml`, text-like via the `+xml` suffix) is still indexed as raw XML — its `<text>` content is captured but so is path data; a targeted SVG-text extractor is a possible follow-up. The conversion runs at ingest time, so re-indexing an existing HTML object (a storage-change re-trigger) upgrades it automatically._

_2026-06-28 — **Local-storage content-type detection now covers the text-like types the §10 indexer can extract — XML/YAML/TOML/NDJSON/SVG files are no longer silently unindexed (SOUL §9/§10)** — the local FS backend tags each object's content type from its extension (`content_type_for`), and that type is what the §10 object indexer's `is_text_like` consults to decide whether to extract+search a file's content (`object.content_type`, catalerum-ingest). But the map only knew txt/md/json/html/csv/pdf/png/jpg — so a locally-stored `.xml`, `.yaml`/`.yml`, `.toml`, `.ndjson`/`.jsonl` config/data file got **no** content type and was skipped by the indexer, even though `is_text_like` already recognises `application/xml`/`application/yaml`/`application/toml`/`application/x-ndjson`. Extended `content_type_for` to emit those (plus `xhtml`→`application/xhtml+xml`, `css`→`text/css`, `js`/`mjs`→`text/javascript`, `tsv`, `log`→`text/plain`, `markdown`/`text` aliases) — each string deliberately chosen to satisfy `is_text_like` (the `+xml` suffix covers `xhtml`/`svg`), so those files now extract and become content-searchable. Also added the common image types `svg`→`image/svg+xml`, `gif`, `webp` for correct download content types. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-storage --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `content_type_covers_text_like_and_web_extensions` unit test (xml/yaml/yml/toml/ndjson/svg/css/js/log mappings, gif/webp, case-insensitive ext, unknown/extension-less → None) plus all 12 storage lib + S3/WebDAV roundtrip tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `local.rs`. **Deferred:** the S3/WebDAV backends carry the **server-reported** content type (not derived here), so this gap was local-FS-specific; code-file extensions (`.rs`/`.py`/…) still map to None — mapping every language to `text/plain` would index source dumps but is a broader policy call left for later._

_2026-06-28 — **Automation-graph validation now rejects an edge *into* a trigger node (SOUL §11)** — `Graph::validate` (the authoring-time check a create/update runs before persisting) caught duplicate ids, dangling edge endpoints, missing triggers, multi-trigger collect graphs, bad `commit_on` refs, and cycles — but **not** an edge pointing *to* a trigger. A trigger heads the graph: the DAG executor seeds trigger nodes as entries (in-degree 0, driven by the firing event) and every other node runs only when an upstream edge into it is *taken*. So an `action → trigger` edge is meaningless — the node is simultaneously a seed and an apparent dependency; the executor would run it once as an entry while the edge silently does nothing, and the author gets a confusing graph that looks wired but isn't. Added a check (right after the no-trigger guard, reusing the already-computed `trigger_nodes`): any edge whose `to` is a trigger id is rejected with a clear message. Runs **before** the cycle check, so a back-edge into a trigger reports the precise cause rather than a generic "cycle". **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-automation --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `an_edge_into_a_trigger_is_rejected` unit test plus all 52 lib + 10 executor integration tests pass (the existing valid-graph/diamond/linear cases are unaffected — none wire into a trigger). Backend-only, self-contained in `graph.rs`. **Deferred:** an **orphan** non-trigger node (no incoming edge, so the executor records it `Skipped` and it never runs) is still accepted — flagging it would help authors but risks rejecting a legitimately half-wired graph mid-edit, so it's left as a possible future *warning* (not a hard reject) once the editor can surface non-fatal diagnostics._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page Markdown now renders `<details>`/`<summary>` as a bold disclosure title, not an undistinguished paragraph (SOUL §27)** — `<details>`/`<summary>` are ubiquitous on the GitHub READMEs and docs the agent fetches (collapsible "Build steps", "Show output", FAQ entries). Both were already classified as blocks but had no `emit_block` arm, so `<details>` fell to the transparent-container case (correct — its body should render) while `<summary>` *also* did, emitting the disclosure title as a plain paragraph **indistinguishable from the body** — the reader lost the "this label heads a collapsible section" cue. Added a `"summary"` arm that renders the summary's inline content as a **bold** standalone line (mirroring the `<dt>` term style), with `<details>` left transparent so the body follows as normal blocks beneath it. Inline formatting inside the summary (e.g. `<code>--help</code>`) is preserved; an empty/absent summary contributes nothing and the body still renders. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `details_summary_renders_summary_as_bold_title` unit test (exact output `**Build steps**\n\nRun \`make\`.`, plus no-summary and inline-code-in-summary cases) and all 63 fetch lib tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** the collapsible isn't visually nested/indented under the title (plain Markdown has no portable disclosure syntax; bold-title-then-blocks keeps the association without a non-GFM extension) — same trade-off as the definition-list rendering._

_2026-06-28 — **LaTeX math engine gains accents (`\hat`/`\vec`/`\bar`/…) and binomials (`\binom`) — common notation no longer leaks the command name (SOUL §21/§12)** — with the chat now steered to use math (the `CHAT_OUTPUT_GUIDANCE` entry), the gaps in the TeX subset matter more: `\hat{x}` parsed as an unknown command and rendered the literal text **"hat"** then `x` (→ "hatx"), and `\binom{n}{k}` showed "binomnk" — both common in real math. _2026-06-28 — **Matrix outbound truncation is now byte-accurate, so a long CJK/emoji message can't be rejected wholesale (SOUL §25)** — the same bug class as the earlier Telegram UTF-16 fix, on a different channel: Matrix caps a whole event (PDU) at **65536 bytes**, but the sender capped the `body` with `truncate_message` (Unicode **scalar** count) at 32 768 — fine for ASCII (32 KB) but a digest of CJK (3 bytes/char) or emoji (4 bytes/char) at that char count is ~98–131 KB, **over** the byte limit, so the homeserver rejects the entire event and the notification/reply is dropped. Added `truncate_message_bytes(text, max_bytes)` to `lib.rs` (cuts on a `char` boundary so the result stays valid UTF-8 and within `max_bytes`, same `[…]` marker) and switched the Matrix sender to it with the budget reframed in **bytes** (`MATRIX_MAX_BODY = 48_000` — strictly *more* permissive than before for ASCII while finally safe for multibyte, with ~17 KB headroom for the event envelope + JSON escaping). Telegram keeps UTF-16, Discord/Slack keep code-point counts (their real units). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-channels --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 24 channels tests pass incl. 2 new `lib` unit tests (a 1000×中 message stays ≤ the byte cap with the marker and head preserved; short multibyte passes through borrowed) and the existing `over_limit_body_is_capped_before_sending` retargeted to a CJK payload asserting the **byte** cap (it would now exceed 65536 under the old char cap). Backend-only. **Deferred:** still truncates rather than splitting into multiple events (the deliberate deliver-the-head design across all four channels); a Matrix `formatted_body` HTML render of the reply Markdown (via `catalerum-markdown`) remains a possible future enhancement — left out here to keep this a focused correctness fix, since truncating rendered HTML safely is a separate problem._

_2026-06-28 — **iCalendar events that use `DURATION` instead of `DTEND` no longer collapse to zero length (SOUL §8) — a correctness bug** — RFC 5545 §3.6.1 lets a `VEVENT` define its span with **either** `DTEND` **or** a `DURATION` (e.g. `DTSTART:…T090000Z` + `DURATION:PT1H30M`), and providers/clients do emit the DURATION form. But `parse_event` only consulted `event.get_end()`, and the `icalendar` crate's `get_end` reads the `DTEND` property *only* (verified in the 0.17.11 source — it never derives from DURATION), so a DURATION-only event fell through to the "no DTEND" arm: a timed event became **zero-length** (`end == start`) and an all-day event defaulted to exactly one day regardless of a multi-day `DURATION` — silently wrong end times feeding the calendar/agenda. Fixed in `ical.rs`: when DTEND is absent, parse a `DURATION` and apply `start + dur` (preserving the all-day flag), keeping the prior 1-day/zero-length defaults only when neither is present; **DTEND still wins when both are set** (DURATION is the fallback). Added a self-contained `parse_ical_duration` (no new dep) covering the week form (`P2W`), the date/time form (`P1DT12H30M`, `PT45S`) and an optional sign (`-PT15M`), with checked arithmetic and strict rejection of the month form (`M` before `T`) and other malformed input. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-calendar --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 32 calendar tests pass incl. 4 new (`timed_event_with_duration_instead_of_dtend` → +1h30m end; `all_day_event_with_multi_day_duration` → `P3D` spans 3 days; `dtend_wins_over_duration_when_both_present`; `ical_duration_parsing` — 8 valid forms + 9 malformed → `None`). Backend-only, found by tracing the DTEND/DTSTART resolution path. **Deferred:** a negative DURATION parses faithfully (end before start) rather than being clamped — out-of-spec for an event span but harmless; `TZID`/`VTIMEZONE` resolution for the DURATION's anchor is unchanged (DURATION is timezone-independent — a fixed number of seconds)._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page Markdown now preserves superscript/subscript instead of flattening them (SOUL §27)** — the HTML→Markdown converter (what the agent reads from a fetched page) handled strong/em/del/code/links/images inline but let `<sup>`/`<sub>` fall through to the "flatten text" arm, so `E = mc<sup>2</sup>` became `mc2`, `H<sub>2</sub>O` became `H2O`, and a footnote marker `claim<sup>1</sup>` became `claim1` — real semantic loss on the general web (scientific text, chemistry, ordinals, footnotes) the agent fetches. A superscript wrapping a footnote link keeps the link inside the markers (`claim^[1](…)^`). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `superscript_and_subscript` unit test (`mc^2^`, `H~2~O`, footnote-link case, empty-wrapper case) plus all 62 fetch lib tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** `<mark>` (highlight) still flattens — no portable Markdown for it and it's presentational; `<kbd>`/`<samp>` (monospace semantics) could later map to inline code, left out to keep this change to the clear information-loss case._

_2026-06-28 — **Chat user messages gain a "Regenerate" control — re-run the conversation from any of your turns (SOUL §12)** — a bad answer (or a turn you'd phrase differently in hindsight) could only be retried by typing again; there was no way to re-run an existing turn. _2026-06-28 — **Mermaid flowcharts gain parallelogram + trapezoid shapes — `[/…/]`/`[\…\]`/`[/…\]`/`[\…/]` now render as real polygons, not literal slashes (SOUL §21/§12)** — closes a flagged deferral from the Mermaid-shapes work: the flowchart engine supported rect/round/stadium/rhombus/circle/hexagon, but the four standard I/O-and-manual-operation shapes parsed as a plain `[…]` rect whose label kept the slashes (`A[/io/]` → a box labelled `/io/`). _2026-06-28 — **Automation code/condition Boa nodes can call registry tools — `catalerum.callTool` under the automation's own authority (SOUL §11/§19/§20)** — closes the asymmetry where emerged-UI scripts (§12) could call tools but §11 graph Code/Condition nodes were a deliberately *pure* transform (input-in, value-out, zero host fns). A `"js"` node's body now gets `catalerum.callTool(name, args)` that dispatches one registry tool **through the same deny-by-default capability gate an Action node uses** — so a code node can reach **no tool an action node couldn't**: there is **no separate allow-list or confirm exclusion** (an automation is headless; the capability cap *is* the gate — delete/exec/egress stay unreachable unless the run's §19 grant confers them, and a `dry_run` grant simulates each call). **Design reuses the emerged-UI bridge's native machinery rather than duplicating it:** new pub trait `catalerum_script::CodeToolHost { call_tool(workspace_id, grant, tool, args) }` (grant-aware, vs the UI path's per-event `UiScriptHost`); `ScriptCodeRunner` gained `tool_host: Option<Arc<dyn CodeToolHost>>` + `with_tool_host(..)`; per evaluation `run_js` wraps the host in a private `CodeHostAdapter` that pins *this* run's `workspace_id`+`grant` and re-exposes it through the existing `UiScriptHost` seam, so the `UI_HOST` thread-local + `native_call_tool` + `HostScope` are reused verbatim and only `callTool` crosses back to Rust (`build_code_program` defines a minimal `catalerum.{callTool,log}` only when a host is present; otherwise the pure IIFE wrapper is unchanged and a code node still returns its `return` value, not the UI `{state,actions}` envelope). `CodeRunner::run_code` gained `workspace_id` + `grant` params (mirrors `ActionRunner::run`), threaded through the executor's Code/Condition branches + the linear `eval_condition`; `FailCodeRunner`/test fakes ignore them. The API side is a thin `impl CodeToolHost for ToolActionRunner` (reuses its own `resolve_context` + `registry.dispatch` — so code-node calls and action calls resolve authority identically), and `main.rs` attaches the **same** `ToolActionRunner` instance that runs Action nodes as the code runner's tool host. **Verified:** full gate `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `catalerum-script` 18 tests (+3: callTool round-trip · host-error catchable · no-host ⇒ `catalerum` undefined), `catalerum-automation` 49 lib + 10 DB integration, `catalerum-ingest` 3 (real `ScriptCodeRunner` code/condition via the worker), `catalerum-api` `action_runner` 20 (+1 DB-free `code_tool_host_dispatches_under_authority`: allowed tool dispatches · unknown rejected · capability-exceeding tool denied) — all green against live Postgres. Web untouched. **Note:** this resolves the `CodeRunner::run_code` trait/impl arity transient flagged in the Mermaid entry below (that was this feature mid-flight); the workspace gate is now green. **Deferred:** confirm-required tools are simply unreachable under base-Member rather than specially excluded; no per-automation tool allow-list config (the grant is the policy)._

_2026-06-28 — **Pure-Rust Mermaid→SVG and LaTeX→MathML engines in `catalerum-markdown` — diagrams and math render with NO JavaScript (SOUL §21/§12)** — the Markdown engine emitted `<pre class="mermaid">` and left rendering to a mermaid.js script that was never wired up (and the workbench has no JS build step). Replaced with two in-crate pure-Rust engines so a fenced ```` ```mermaid ```` or `$…$`/`$$…$$`/```` ```math ```` renders to real vector/markup output server- and client-side with zero runtime script. **`mermaid::to_svg`** parses `graph`/`flowchart` (TD/TB/BT/LR/RL; node shapes rect/round/stadium/rhombus/circle/hexagon; edges `-->`/`---`/`-.->`/`==>` with `|pipe|` or inline `-- label -->` text; chains; quoted labels), lays it out with a layered longest-path algorithm (centred ranks, box-clipped edge endpoints, arrowhead marker), and emits a self-contained inlined-style `<svg>`; unparseable input → `Err` so the renderer falls back to the raw source in `<pre>`. **`math::to_mathml`** parses a TeX-math subset (identifiers/numbers/operators, `^`/`_` scripts, `\frac`, `\sqrt`/`\sqrt[n]`, `\left…\right`, `\sum`/`\prod`/`\int`/`\lim` with under/over limits, ~120 Greek/symbol commands, `\text`, `\mathbb/\mathcal/\mathbf/\mathrm`, function names, spacing, and `matrix`/`pmatrix`/`bmatrix`/`vmatrix`/`cases` environments) into browser-native **MathML**; unknown commands degrade to literal text. Both **escape every text atom** (the element/SVG structure is the engine's, never the input's) so the output stays injection-safe; the Leptos renderer embeds the engine-generated SVG/MathML via `inner_html`. Inline `$…$` was added to the Markdown tokenizer with currency guards (open not on whitespace, close not preceded by whitespace nor followed by a digit, so `$5 and $10` stays text). Recursion/iteration caps make both engines DoS-proof. **Verified:** 60+ crate tests incl. parser/symbol/shape/escaping cases and a **16 000-iteration no-panic fuzz** over each engine (random TeX + Mermaid tokens, multi-byte Unicode) — zero panics; `cargo clippy -p catalerum-markdown --all-targets -D warnings` clean and `-p catalerum-web --target wasm32 -D warnings` clean (the `inner_html` SVG/MathML Leptos nodes compile); 222 web native tests pass. **No new runtime dependency** — no mermaid.js, no KaTeX, no `mermaid.run()`. **Deferred:** only Mermaid flowcharts (sequence/class/gantt/pie report unsupported → raw-source fallback); the math subset omits some exotic TeX; layout is readable, not a pixel-match of mermaid.js. (Note: a workspace-wide `cargo clippy` was transiently failing in `catalerum-script` on a concurrently-edited `CodeRunner::run_code` trait/impl arity mismatch — that was the code-node tool-calls feature mid-flight; it is now landed and the workspace gate is green, see the entry above.)_

_Last updated: 2026-06-28 — **Locked the distributed-lock token-safety invariant; bus audit completes the backend subsystem sweep (SOUL §6.2/§11)** — audited the last untraced subsystem, the bus `DistLock` (the scheduler's single-fire-across-pods primitive): both backends are correct — `InProcessLock` is mutex-atomic with token-checked release/refresh, and `RedisLock` uses `SET NX PX` (atomic acquire-if-absent + TTL) with CAS-release/refresh Lua (only the token holder mutates the key). The **test gap**: the existing tests covered acquire-excludes, refresh, release-once, and TTL expiry, but not the **expiry→re-acquire token-safety** race — that a *stale* guard (whose lock expired and was re-acquired by another holder) must NOT release or refresh the new holder's lock. A regression to a plain `DEL`/`PEXPIRE` would pass every existing test yet break this, freeing a lock another pod just took → a double-fired schedule occurrence. Added `stale_guard_cannot_release_or_refresh_a_reacquired_lock` to lock it. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-bus --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 5 bus tests pass. Test-only. **This completes the path-trace audit of every backend subsystem** — storage, exec/script, IAM, email, calendar, automation, ingest, vector, graph, capabilities, and now the bus — all confirmed correct (with real bugs fixed and critical invariants test-locked along the way)._

The one **test gap**: `to_qdrant`'s full-filter shape was covered, but the **empty-filter** path (`is_empty()` true — the "all points in the workspace" query) had no test pinning that it still emits *exactly* the `workspace_id` clause and never an unfiltered cross-tenant query. Added `to_qdrant_empty_filter_is_workspace_scoped_not_unfiltered` to lock it; trimmed an initial draft that duplicated the existing full-filter test. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-vector --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 12 vector tests pass. Test-only, no behavior change — guards a §18 isolation invariant against a future `to_qdrant` refactor dropping the workspace clause._

_2026-06-28 — **WebDAV prefixed list no longer spuriously recurses into sibling directories (SOUL §9)** — `list(prefix)` walks the collection with Depth:1 PROPFINDs, recursing into a directory `k` if `k.starts_with(prefix) || prefix.starts_with(k)`. But dir keys are stored without a trailing slash (`href_to_key` trims it), so the ancestor clause `prefix.starts_with(k)` matched at a non-path-boundary: listing `docs/report` would recurse into a sibling `doc/` (since `"docs/report".starts_with("doc")`) and PROPFIND its **entire** subtree — many wasted network round-trips (results stayed correct via the final prefix `retain`, so it was a perf bug, not a correctness one). Extracted a boundary-aware `should_descend(dir, prefix)` (`dir.starts_with(prefix) || prefix.starts_with("{dir}/")`) — the `"{dir}/"` anchors the ancestor test at a path segment, so `doc/` is pruned while the real ancestor `docs/` and under-prefix subtrees still descend; string-prefix list semantics (e.g. prefix `doc` still matches `docs/x`, like S3/local) are preserved. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-storage --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `should_descend_prunes_siblings_at_path_boundaries` unit test (ancestor/at/under descend; sibling string-prefix + unrelated subtree pruned) + all 11 storage tests pass. Found by tracing the storage backends (S3 list pagination + WebDAV recursion both audited; S3 was already correct). **Audit note:** the JS sandbox (loop/recursion/stack + timeout bounds, no host fns), S3 pagination, and capability attenuation/anti-spoofing tests were all reviewed this pass and found sound._

_2026-06-28 — **Locked the "expired magic-link is rejected" security invariant with a regression test (SOUL §18)** — tracing the IAM auth path: the login-token `consume` SQL gates only on `consumed_at IS NULL` (not expiry), so expiry is enforced one layer up in `redeem_login_token` (`expires_at <= now → Unauthorized`). That layering was correct but **untested** — a future refactor dropping the service-layer check would silently let expired magic links log in (an auth bypass), since `consume` would happily consume an expired-but-unconsumed token. Added `expired_login_token_is_rejected` (mints a token with a negative `login_ttl` via the existing `with_login_ttl`, redeems → asserts `Unauthorized`, then asserts the rejected attempt still consumed it so single-use holds on the expired path). No DB needed (`MemoryIamStore`). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-iam --all-targets -D warnings` clean; the new test + the existing `login_token_is_single_use` pass. Test-only — no behavior change (the path was already correct; this guards it). The rest of this iteration was a continued path-trace audit (cron `due_occurrence`, IMAP/CalDAV deletions, memory-curation dedup, the login `consume`/expiry layering) — all confirmed sound, no new bugs. **Noted:** the `search_emails` over-fetch fix (2 entries below) remains without a dedicated test — judged low-ROI (identical, live-tested `search_semantic` pattern) vs. its heavy email+vector+purge harness._

Earlier this session a full **`--workspace --exclude catalerum-web` run was green: clippy clean + 907 native tests pass against live Postgres + Qdrant, 0 failures.** **Noted (not changed):** per-capability constraints (`exec:run@bao{lang,net,…}`) aren't enforced at tool dispatch — they describe the **unbuilt bao backend** (§29 open question), not a shipped-path gap; shipped exec backends enforce limits via their own `ResourceLimits`. _2026-06-28 — **JMAP email sync no longer false-deletes mail from the catalogue when a mailbox exceeds the 10k snapshot cap (SOUL §28) — a data-loss bug** — the JMAP backend syncs by snapshotting the newest `SNAPSHOT_CAP` (10 000) email ids, diffing keyword signatures against the cursor, and reporting prior-but-absent ids as `deletions` (which the ingest worker applies — JMAP is "authoritative for deletions"). But for a mailbox **larger than 10 000**, a newly-arrived email pushes an older still-existing one past the newest-10k window, so it vanishes from the snapshot and was reported as a deletion — silently removing a real email from the catalogue on every sync where new mail arrived. Fixed: `query_ids` now also returns whether the snapshot was **truncated** (hit the cap), and a new pure `snapshot_deletions(prior, sigs, truncated)` emits deletions **only on a complete snapshot** — a truncated one can't distinguish deleted from fell-past-the-cap, so it returns none (a genuine deletion in a >cap mailbox is left stale-but-present: the safe, no-data-loss direction). Mailboxes ≤ 10k (the common case) are unchanged. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-email --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `snapshot_deletions_only_on_a_complete_snapshot` unit test (complete → real deletions emitted; truncated → none) plus all 36 email tests pass. Backend-only, found by tracing the sync path. **Deferred:** properly reconciling deletions in >10k mailboxes needs real incremental JMAP `Email/changes` (the module deliberately avoids it for a stateless snapshot-diff); a stale-but-present email there self-heals only if it later re-enters the newest-10k window._

_2026-06-28 — **`search_emails` no longer under-fills when a hit's email row was purged out from under its vector (SOUL §6.4/§28)** — the same under-fill class as the `search_semantic` fix below, found by tracing the sibling path: `search_emails` fetched exactly `limit` email-kind vector hits, resolved each to its Postgres row, and **skipped** any whose row was gone (a vector that briefly outlived its async-purged email — a race the code already documented) — so recently-purged emails in the top-`limit` slots silently shrank the result below `limit`. Applied the established guard: over-fetch `limit×4` (bounded 80), resolve in score order, and `break` once `limit` live emails are built (the `break` is load-bearing now — without it the over-fetch could return up to 80). Consistent with `search_semantic` / `recall_memory_texts`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --tests -D warnings` clean; the full 49-test `tools::tests` suite passes **against live Qdrant + Postgres** (no regression; the over-fetched `search_semantic` test included). **Deferred:** `search_emails` has no dedicated test — it had none before, and a real one needs a heavy harness (connection + mailbox + `Email` rows + vectors + a simulated purge) for a behavior identical to the now-live-tested `search_semantic`; the 4× factor is the same heuristic noted there._

_2026-06-28 — **`search_semantic` no longer under-fills results when email/hidden hits crowd the top (SOUL §6.4/§6.5/§18)** — the tool fetched exactly `limit` hits from Qdrant, then dropped email-kind hits (reachable only via `search_emails`, §19) and hidden cross-user memory hits (§22) **after** the fetch — so when those occupied the top-`limit` slots the caller got fewer than `limit`, or nothing, even though eligible note/document hits ranked just below. `recall_memory_texts` already guarded against exactly this by over-fetching; `search_semantic` didn't. Fixed it the same way: fetch `limit×4` (bounded at 80), apply the visibility/email filters, then truncate to `limit`. The `kinds` filter stays pushed into the index (no headroom needed); memory visibility can't be (it's per-user, not in the vector payload), which is why over-fetch is the right tool. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --tests -D warnings` clean; a new `search_semantic_overfetches_past_filtered_email_hits` test (5 email points tying for the top + 1 note below; `limit=2` ⇒ the note is still returned — it would be empty under the old fetch-exactly-`limit`) plus the two existing `search_semantic` tests all pass **against live Qdrant + Postgres**. Backend-only. **Deferred:** the over-fetch factor (4×) is a heuristic — a workspace whose top ~80 vector hits are *all* filtered could still under-fill; a filter-aware index query would be exact but memory visibility isn't expressible in the Qdrant payload._

_2026-06-28 — **Graph topic dedup now folds internal whitespace, not just case/trim (SOUL §6.3/§10)** — note tags and calendar labels each become a `:Topic` node keyed by a normalized name, but normalization was `trim().to_lowercase()` — so `Machine Learning`, `machine  learning` (double space), and `  MACHINE LEARNING  ` minted **three separate** topic nodes, splitting what should be one cluster and diluting graph-based recall. Tightened `topics_from` to collapse internal whitespace runs to a single space (a new `collapse_ws` over `split_whitespace().join(" ")`) before lowercasing for the dedup key and the stable UUIDv5 `topic_id`; the display name keeps first-seen casing in its whitespace-collapsed form. Since the Neo4j graph is a **derived** store (rebuilt from Postgres by re-ingest, §6.3), the id change just re-converges topics on the next projection — no migration. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-ingest --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `topic_normalization_folds_internal_whitespace_and_case` test (three spellings → one node, folded id, clean display) and all 10 graph-ingest tests pass (the existing case-insensitive dedup test still holds). Backend-only, self-contained in `graph.rs`. **Deferred:** this is exact-after-normalization dedup only — fuzzy/alias merging (`ML` ↔ `machine learning`, embedding-similarity) remains the open §29 entity-dedup question._

_2026-06-28 — **Automation text-filter matching is now Unicode-case-insensitive, not ASCII-only (SOUL §11)** — a `ChannelMessage` trigger's `{"text": …}` filter and a `CalendarEvent` trigger's summary/location/description filters both fold case through `contains_ci`, which used `to_ascii_lowercase` — so case-insensitivity only worked for ASCII: a German user's `über` filter wouldn't match `Über`, a `café` filter wouldn't match `CAFÉ`, and non-Latin scripts (Greek, Cyrillic) never folded at all. Since catalerum is self-hostable worldwide and these filters run over message bodies / event titles / locations — exactly where non-English text lives — that silently dropped real matches. Switched `contains_ci` to Unicode-aware `to_lowercase`; channel and calendar filters both gain it (they share the helper), and identifier comparisons (channel/bucket/board/path) stay exact-match as before. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-automation --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `text_filter_case_folding_is_unicode_aware` test (`über`↔`ÜBER`, `café`↔`CAFÉ`, Greek `ΣΊΓΜΑ`↔`σίγμα`, plus a genuine non-match) and all 17 trigger tests pass. Backend-only, one-line behavior change in `trigger.rs`. **Deferred:** folding is locale-independent (`str::to_lowercase`), so locale-specific edge cases (Turkish dotless-ı/İ) follow Unicode default rules rather than a locale tailoring — acceptable for substring filters._

_2026-06-28 — **Telegram outbound truncation is now UTF-16-accurate, so an emoji-heavy long message can't be rejected wholesale (SOUL §25)** — Telegram's `sendMessage` `text` limit (4096) is counted in **UTF-16 code units** (a non-BMP char like an emoji costs 2), but the channel capped by Unicode scalar count (`truncate_message`), so a message of e.g. 3000 emoji = 3000 chars but 6000 UTF-16 units would slip past the cap and Telegram would `400` it — dropping the **entire** notification/reply (the very failure the cap exists to prevent). Added `truncate_message_utf16` (counts `char::len_utf16`, cuts on a char boundary, appends the same `[…]` marker within the real unit budget) and switched the Telegram sender to it; the other channels keep `truncate_message` (Discord/Slack count code points, Matrix has no UTF-16 limit). Respects the existing deliver-the-head design — it only makes the cap measure the unit Telegram actually enforces. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-channels --all-targets -D warnings` clean; two new unit tests (3000-emoji message stays ≤ 4096 UTF-16 units with the marker; short/BMP text passes through borrowed and all-BMP behaves like char-counting) plus all 22 channels tests pass. Backend-only. **Deferred:** still truncates rather than splitting a long reply into multiple messages — that's a deliberate, documented design choice across all four channels (deliver the head, one request), not changed here._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page Markdown now renders definition lists (`<dl>`) with bold terms instead of flat paragraphs (SOUL §27)** — `is_block` already classified `dl`/`dt`/`dd` as blocks, but `emit_block` had no `dl` arm, so a definition list fell through to generic container recursion: each `<dt>` and `<dd>` became an undistinguished plain paragraph — the term wasn't even bolded, and the term→definition pairing was lost (these are common on API-reference/glossary pages the agent fetches). Added a `definition_list` renderer: each `<dt>` becomes a **bold term** line and each `<dd>` its definition rendered as normal block content beneath it (so a definition may itself hold paragraphs/lists/links), with the HTML5 `<div>`-grouped form handled by recursion. Inline formatting inside a term (e.g. `<code>--force</code>`) is preserved. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `definition_list_bolds_terms_and_keeps_definitions` unit test (two-pair list + a term with inline code and a definition with a link) plus all 61 fetch lib tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** definitions aren't visually indented under their term (plain Markdown has no portable definition-list syntax; bold-term-then-paragraph keeps the association without a non-GFM extension)._

_2026-06-28 — **Fetched-page Markdown now detects a code fence's language from `<pre class="language-…">`, not just the inner `<code>` (SOUL §27)** — the HTML→Markdown converter (what the agent actually reads from a fetched page) only inspected the inner `<code>`'s class for a `language-`/`lang-` prefix, so a common highlighter layout that tags the **`<pre>`** instead (`<pre class="language-rust"><code>…`) produced an unlabelled ```` ``` ```` fence — losing the language hint that helps the model read the snippet. `code_block` now falls back to the `<pre>` element's own class when the `<code>` has no recognizable language token; the inner `<code>`'s class still wins when both are present, and an unrecognized highlighter class (e.g. `highlight`) still yields a plain fence (no false language). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new `code_block_language_on_pre_element` unit test (class-on-pre detected, inner-code precedence, no-false-language) plus all 60 fetch lib tests pass. Backend-only, self-contained in `markdown.rs`. **Deferred:** bare highlighter classes without a `language-`/`lang-` prefix (e.g. highlight.js's `<code class="hljs rust">`) stay undetected — too ambiguous to guess a language from a generic class name without false positives._

_2026-06-28 — **SSRF guard now decodes Teredo-embedded IPv4, closing the last embedded-v4 smuggling gap (SOUL §13/§27)** — the fetch egress policy already decodes NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`) and 6to4 (`2002::/16`) IPv6 literals and re-checks the embedded IPv4 against the v4 blocklist, so a public IPv6 name can't smuggle a private/metadata target past the guard — but **Teredo** (`2001:0000::/32`, RFC 4380) was the missing sibling: its last 32 bits are the client IPv4 obfuscated by XOR `0xffffffff`, so on a Teredo-connected host `2001:0:0:0:0:0:5601:5601` routes to `169.254.169.254` (cloud metadata). Added `teredo_embedded_v4` (precise `2001:0000` prefix match, XOR-deobfuscated client v4) to the `to_ipv4 → nat64 → 6to4 → teredo` decode chain in `v6_is_blocked`, so a Teredo literal embedding a private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT v4 is now refused while one embedding a public v4 (or a real `2001:db8::` public address, which isn't Teredo — segment[1]≠0) stays allowed. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; the `blocks_ipv6_local` unit test gained Teredo cases (metadata/loopback/private blocked, public allowed, `2001:db8::` allowed) — all 6 policy tests pass. Backend-only; the IP rules also back the connect-time DNS guard (`first_blocked_addr`) so a rebinding name resolving to a Teredo literal is screened too. **Deferred:** documentation/benchmark/reserved IPv4 ranges (192.0.2/24, 198.18/15, 240/4) are still allowed — not a metadata/SSRF risk, so left out to avoid over-blocking._

_2026-06-27 — **Agent-profile models are now catalog-validated too — shared model/voice validation extracted to one module (SOUL §7/§19)** — extends the `/llm-settings` validation to scoped agents: `POST`/`PUT /agent-profiles` accepted any `model` string, so a typo'd model id silently persisted and then failed when the scoped agent ran. Extracted the four validators (`model_in_catalog`/`validate_model`/`voice_in_list`/`validate_voice`, with their unit tests) out of `routes::settings` into a new shared `crate::model_validation` module; `set_settings` now imports them (unchanged behavior), and `agent_profiles::{create, upsert}` validate the profile's chat model against the gateway catalog before persisting — same graceful degradation (a gateway outage never blocks the save) and a clear 4xx pointing at `/llm-models`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; the two pure-helper unit tests (now under `model_validation`) plus the settings tests pass. Backend-only — the agent-profile form's server-side reject surfaces as the request error; no web change. **Deferred:** the agent-profile **tools** (`create_agent_profile`/`update_agent_profile` in `tools.rs`) hold only a `Store`, not the LLM client, so their model isn't validated yet — covering them needs threading the LLM client into those tools (noted follow-up); the live gateway-call paths remain not integration-tested (no llmleaf in the test env)._

_2026-06-27 — **LLM-settings now also validate the speech voice against the chosen model (SOUL §7/§12)** — completes the previous entry's model-id validation: `PUT /llm-settings` still accepted any `speech_voice` string, so a typo'd voice persisted and broke TTS at call time. `set_settings` now validates a set voice against the speech model's voice list (`state.llm().voices(model)`) — resolving the model from the request's `speech_model`, else the `[llm].speech_model` default it will fall back to (skipped only when no concrete speech model resolves).
