_2026-06-27 — **Content-search hits now download from the store they live on, not always the default (SOUL §9/§10)** — closes a flagged deferral: file content search (`GET /storage/catalogue/search`) spans every store, but a hit carried no store, so the Files panel's "Download" on a result always hit the default backend — a 404 (or the wrong file) when the match lived on a non-default store. Threaded the store through end-to-end: `ObjectTextHit` (catalerum-store) now carries the matched object's `bucket_id` (the search SQL selects `o.bucket_id`); the `search_objects` route resolves each hit's `?store=` selector via a new shared `bucket_labels` helper (`bucket → connection → store name`, factored out of `list_catalogue` so both share one mapping) and returns it on `ObjectTextHitView.store`; the web `ObjectHit` gained a `#[serde(default)]` `store`, and the Files panel builds the hit's download URL with `Some(store)` (empty → default, unchanged). **Verified:** native clippy (`-p catalerum-store -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings`) clean; the `objects_search_repo` DB test passes against live postgres with a new assertion that a hit carries its `bucket_id`; full web trio — wasm clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean, 222 web tests, `trunk build` ✅. **Deferred:** unchanged — runtime-store backup (previous entry) and the §13 secret store remain the open storage items._

_2026-06-27 — **Backup now mirrors every config storage store, not just the default (SOUL §30/§9)** — closes a flagged deferral: a workspace can hold many named stores (the legacy `[storage]` default + each `[storage.backends.<name>]`), but `BackupEngine` took a single `with_source_storage` and copied only the default store's blobs, so files on any other store were silently absent from a backup. Reworked the engine around **named sources**: `with_named_source(name, backend)` (and `with_source_storage` kept as sugar for the `default` name); a backup writes each store's blobs under its own `objects/<segment>/<key>` sub-tree (segments are filesystem-safe, collision-suffixed) and records a per-store inventory in the manifest; restore routes each store's blobs back to the live backend registered under the **same name**, erroring if a backed-up store has no live counterpart (rather than silently dropping it). Bumped artifact **FORMAT_VERSION 1→2** and relaxed the restore guard from `!=` to `>` so the new build still reads a **legacy v1** artifact — its flat `objects/<key>` blobs restore into the default store (`ObjectsManifest.stores` is `#[serde(default)]`, empty ⇒ v1 path). Wired both run paths to attach **all** config stores: the scheduled worker via a new `StorageRegistry::sources()`, and the `catalerum backup`/`restore` CLI via `resolved_backends()` + the now-exported `build_backend` (identical store naming, so a CLI restore reunites the same stores). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-backup -p catalerum-api -p catalerum --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 6 backup lib unit tests (incl. new `safe_segment`, `segments_for` collision-dedup, and a v1-manifest-deserializes-with-empty-stores back-compat test); 2 backup integration tests pass against live postgres — the existing single-store round-trip (now exercising the v2 `default` layout) and a new `backup_restore_mirrors_multiple_stores` (two stores each mirrored + routed back without cross-contamination, plus a partial-source restore correctly errors). **Deferred:** **runtime** (user-added) stores — DB `Connection` rows — are still not mirrored; enumerating them needs an async DB pass at engine-build time (the worker/CLI build the source set synchronously). The common multi-store case (`[storage.backends.*]` in config) is now covered; runtime-store backup is the remaining gap._

_2026-06-27 — **Self-exited terminal sessions are now reaped — no more leaked children, containers/Pods, or phantom `active` rows within a run (SOUL §20)** — closes the last flagged terminal deferral (the boot reconcile below only bounded staleness to a process lifetime). A shell that exits on its own (`exit`, a crash, a finished one-shot) left its PTY child a zombie, the keep-alive container/Pod running, and the `terminal_sessions` row `active` until an explicit `close` or a restart. Added a reaper end-to-end: `SessionStore::reap_exited` (catalerum-exec/pty) non-blockingly `try_wait`s every live child and removes + returns the ids of those already exited (also clearing the OS zombie); a new default-empty `Executor::reap` (catalerum-core) is implemented by Local/Sandbox (just `reap_exited`), Container (`reap_exited` then `rm -f` each dead session's container), and Kubernetes (`reap_exited` then `delete pod`); `TerminalManager::reap` (catalerum-api) folds every backend's reaped ids, drops the live handles, marks each DB row closed, and removes an ephemeral temp dir, returning the count. A 30s periodic task in `main.rs` (spawned only when terminals are configured, `MissedTickBehavior::Skip`) drives it so `list_terminals` and the file tools converge on reality within ~30s of a self-exit. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-core -p catalerum-exec -p catalerum-api -p catalerum --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 16 exec tests pass incl. a new deterministic `reap_exited_collects_finished_sessions_and_keeps_live_ones` (an `exit 0` shell is reaped, an interactive one kept); 5 api terminal tests pass against live postgres incl. a new `reap_closes_a_self_exited_session` (write `exit`, poll reap → DB row closed, live handle gone, ephemeral dir removed, idempotent). The manager-level reap is per-(executor, workspace), not global, so it needs no cross-test serialization (unlike the boot reconcile's `close_all_active`). **Deferred:** the reaper detects a *self-exited PTY* — for container/k8s that is the `exec` process ending; if the keep-alive container/Pod is killed out-of-band while the PTY still blocks on it, detection waits on the PTY seeing EOF; there is no independent per-session liveness probe of the container/Pod itself._

_2026-06-27 — **New `catalerum-markdown` crate — one streaming, SIMD-accelerated Markdown engine for the whole workbench (SOUL §21/§12)** — the web UI's hand-rolled `markdown_preview_html` was a small, non-streaming `String` builder that re-parsed the whole buffer on every chat delta and supported only a thin subset. Replaced by a dedicated crate (native + `wasm32`) that is the single source of truth for Markdown→HTML **and** Markdown→Leptos. **Parser:** two-phase (block tree → inline) covering CommonMark (ATX/setext headings, fenced + indented code, block quotes, tight/loose bullet/ordered lists, thematic breaks, reference defs resolved document-globally) plus GFM (tables with per-column alignment, `~~strike~~`, `- [ ]` task lists, autolinks) with a faithful **delimiter-stack emphasis** resolver (rule-of-three). **Renderers:** `to_html`/`push_html` (injection-safe — every text node escaped, only `http(s)`/`mailto`/`tel`/root-relative/anchor URLs become links, raw inline HTML escaped as text) and a feature-gated `render_markdown` that builds real Leptos `View` nodes (no `inner_html` sink at all). A fenced block tagged `mermaid` → `<pre class="mermaid">` for client-side diagramming. **SIMD:** the hot "find next interesting byte" scan uses a nibble-table (`PSHUFB`-style) membership test with SSSE3/AVX2 (x86-64, runtime-detected), NEON (aarch64) and wasm `simd128` back-ends + a scalar oracle; wasm SIMD is turned on workspace-wide via `.cargo/config.toml` (`+simd128`). **Streaming:** `StreamRenderer`/`stable_boundary` render only the prefix that can no longer change (last blank line outside a fence) and hand back the open tail as plain text — `chat.rs` now holds one `StoredValue<StreamRenderer>` per message row so a streaming reply commits append-only (no reflow/flicker). True delta-reconstruction both ways: each newly-stable block is parsed+rendered exactly once, **and** the boundary scan resumes from the committed mark (a line start outside any fence) so a delta scans only the new tail — O(total) across a stream, not O(n²). **Verified:** 55 crate tests green incl. an exhaustive 65 536 byte-pair SIMD-vs-scalar equivalence check, a 20 000-doc + 5 000-stream **no-panic fuzz harness** (multi-byte Unicode, every char-boundary truncation), security/XSS suite (raw-HTML, `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:` link+autolink+ref rejection incl. whitespace/case/percent-encoding bypass attempts, attribute breakout, mermaid/code escaping), and a **counting-allocator allocation-budget** test. A dedicated allocation-reduction pass (Vec pre-sizing from a SIMD newline count, a no-markup inline fast path returning one borrowed text node, per-item list-buffer reuse, and flattening straight from the emphasis drain) cut allocations — plain paragraph 9→4, bullet list 21→14, inline-markup 14→11, reused-buffer render →3 — which sped `to_html` **~28–48%** (prose 120→193, code 176→301, table 104→142 MiB/s). Criterion benches: after resuming the boundary scan from the committed mark, streaming incremental render is **~125× faster** than naive full-rerender-per-delta (≈80 µs vs ~10 ms — down from 1.1 ms, the prior O(n²) boundary re-scan). `cargo clippy` clean native + wasm `-D warnings`; full native workspace test + 222 web native tests + `trunk build` all pass. An adversarial multi-agent review's one "blocker" (claimed `[b][c]` panic) was disproved empirically and pinned as a regression test; its two real findings (streaming flicker + O(n²) re-render) drove the per-row `StreamRenderer` wiring. **Deferred (documented in-crate):** multi-line reference definitions, some indented-code-inside-list nuances, and a few pathological CommonMark emphasis corner-cases are out of the supported subset; streaming may transiently render a blank-line-separated (loose) list as two lists or miss a forward reference until the final full render — both self-correct when the completed reply is rendered in one shot._

_2026-06-27 — **Boot-reconcile of orphaned terminal sessions — `active` rows can no longer outlive the process that owned them (SOUL §20)** — every interactive PTY / container / Pod handle lives in the `TerminalManager`'s in-memory registry, so after an api restart any `terminal_sessions` row still `active` from the prior process was a phantom: `list_terminals` reported it active while no session existed, and the file tools (`read_file`/`create_file`/`edit_file`) would still succeed off the persisted `host_dir` — a flagged inconsistency from the terminal tool-call review. Added `TerminalSessionRepo::close_all_active`, a single bulk `UPDATE … SET status='closed', closed_at=now() WHERE status='active'` — deliberately the one **non-workspace-scoped** query in the repo (boot maintenance, not a tenant request) — returning the reconciled row count and idempotent (a second pass closes nothing; already-closed rows keep their original `closed_at`). Called once in `main.rs` right after `store.migrate()`, before any new session can open; non-fatal on error (logged), logs the count when > 0. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-store -p catalerum --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 3 terminals_repo DB tests pass against live postgres incl. a new `close_all_active_reconciles_orphaned_sessions_across_workspaces` (closes active rows across two workspaces, leaves a pre-closed row's `closed_at` untouched, idempotent) — the two active-count tests are serialized by a process-wide `OnceLock<tokio::Mutex>` since the global close would otherwise race libtest's concurrent run. **Deferred:** still no per-session child-exit reaper (a shell that self-exits mid-run leaks its zombie child + keep-alive container/Pod + a phantom `active` row until the next restart or explicit close) — boot reconcile bounds the staleness to one process lifetime, it doesn't eliminate it within a run._

_2026-06-27 — **Kubernetes session/run Pods are now hardened to the container backend's level (SOUL §19/§20)** — the k8s executor created Pods via bare `kubectl run` with no securityContext, no resource limits, and a mounted service-account token, so a k8s terminal session was strictly weaker than the container backend (which already does `--cap-drop ALL` / `--security-opt no-new-privileges` / `--network none`) — a flagged gap from the terminal tool-call review. Added `KubernetesExecutor::security_overrides`, a pure function building a `kubectl run --overrides` strategic-merge patch applied to both `open_session` and one-shot `run`: the container drops **ALL** capabilities, blocks privilege escalation (`allowPrivilegeEscalation=false`, `privileged=false`), and gets any configured CPU/memory `limits`==`requests` (Guaranteed QoS); the Pod runs with the **RuntimeDefault** seccomp profile, `automountServiceAccountToken=false`, and `enableServiceLinks=false`. The patch is keyed by the generated container name (== the Pod name for `kubectl run NAME`) and applied with `--override-type=strategic` so it merges onto the real container instead of replacing the image/command (a JSON-merge override would clobber the containers array) — requires kubectl ≥ 1.22. Like the container backend it deliberately does **not** force `runAsNonRoot`, so root-default images (busybox) still start. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-exec --all-targets -D warnings` clean; 15 exec tests pass incl. 2 new override-shape tests (full hardening with limits → QoS requests; empty limits omit `resources` but still drop caps). **Deferred:** the network-isolation equivalent of `--network none` needs a separate per-Pod NetworkPolicy object (CNI-dependent, with its own create/delete lifecycle) and is not yet emitted; `runAsNonRoot`/`readOnlyRootFilesystem` left off for image compatibility (matching the container backend)._

_2026-06-27 — **Terminals settings panel redesigned + a lossless enable/disable toggle (SOUL §20)** — the Settings → Terminals section managed persistent workdirs but was thin and visually off: it referenced several CSS classes that don't exist (`settings-list*`, `settings-button`, `settings-section-help`), so rows/buttons rendered unstyled vs. the rest of Settings; `enabled` was hard-coded `true` with no way to pause a workdir; the host-path field showed even for container/Kubernetes (where it's meaningless); and active sessions weren't surfaced. Rebuilt on the real settings design vocabulary (`settings-conn*` rows, `settings-field`/`settings-label` form, `settings-btn` buttons): each workdir row shows a backend badge, its host path (mono), a Disabled badge + an **Enable/Disable** toggle, and delete; the add-form is **backend-aware** (a per-runtime blurb; the host-path field only for local/sandbox, an explanatory note for container/k8s — and a non-host backend never sends a stray path); a header shows the active-session count and a new read-only **"Active sessions"** list resolves each session to its workdir name (best-effort — a sessions fetch failure never blanks the workdir list). The toggle is **lossless**: new `POST /terminals/workdirs/{name}/enabled` (`exec:write`, mirroring `set_automation_enabled`) backed by `TerminalWorkdirRepo::set_enabled` (UPDATE of `enabled` only) so a backend-specific `config` (image/namespace) set out-of-band survives a pause — unlike the full-replace `upsert_by_name`. Wired `rest::set_terminal_workdir_enabled` (reusing the existing `SetEnabled` DTO) + a few Terminals CSS rules. **Verified:** native clippy (`-p catalerum-store -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings`) clean; wasm clippy (`-p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -D warnings`) clean; `trunk build` ✅. **Deferred:** no inline edit of an existing workdir (rename/path/backend — still delete + recreate); container/k8s `config` (image, namespace, limits) still isn't editable from the UI (config/API only); active sessions are display-only (closing a session is a tool/automation action, not a settings control)._

_2026-06-27 — **Terminal tool-call surface reviewed and hardened — close a `sync_folder` capability/host-path security hole + a Kubernetes host-dir correctness bug (SOUL §19/§20)** — the interactive-terminal feature (4 Executor backends local/sandbox/container/k8s; `TerminalManager`; 10 agent tools `open_terminal`/`terminal_write`/`terminal_read`/`list_terminals`/`close_terminal`/`read_file`/`create_file`/`edit_file`/`persist_terminal`/`sync_folder`; 6 automation action nodes; REST workdir/session CRUD + read-only output WS; web pane) was implemented and fully wired; a multi-agent review (6 lenses → adversarial verify) surfaced defects I then fixed. **Blocker — `sync_folder`/`persist_terminal` gating:** both returned `storage:write` as their `required_capability`, but `ToolRegistry::dispatch` enforces a **single** capability and `storage:write` is held by a base **Member** while `exec` is absent from `catalerum-iam` `DOMAINS` (no base role holds `exec:run`) — so the two storage-backed terminal tools were reachable by a non-exec Member (and base-Member automations), defeating the §19/§20 "exec is unreachable to non-exec roles" invariant. `sync_folder` additionally forwarded an unconstrained absolute `path` straight into the dir→storage sync — an arbitrary host-file read (`/etc`, the secret-bearing config dir, another workspace's `persistent_root/<uuid>/…`) into the caller's own downloadable store. Fixed: both now gate on `exec:run` (single-cap dispatch ⇒ pick the security-critical scope); `sync_folder` **drops the raw `path` mode** and accepts only a named, workspace-scoped `workdir` (admin-configured through the exec-gated REST surface) — tool schema/description + the `catalog.json` node doc updated to match; `persist_terminal` is now registered only when an object store exists (like `sync_folder`) instead of registering and failing at runtime. **High — k8s host-dir backfill:** `TerminalManager::open` did `session.host_dir.clone().or(Some(cwd))`, overwriting the `None` the Kubernetes backend deliberately returns (files live in the Pod, unreachable from the api host) with the empty local scratch dir — so on a live k8s session `persist` reported empty success and `read_file`/`create_file`/`edit_file` silently used the wrong, empty dir. Fixed: trust the backend's reported dir (`session.host_dir.clone()`), so k8s stays `None` and `session_host_dir` hits its intended "session has no host directory" error; local/sandbox/container are unchanged (they return `Some(cwd)` themselves). **Low — `read_wait` data loss:** with both `wait_secs` and `max_bytes` set, each poll drained the **whole** drain buffer then truncated the accumulator to the cap, permanently dropping bytes past it; now drains only up to the remaining budget so the tail stays buffered for a later read. Plus a stale tool-count comment in `state.rs`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api -p catalerum-automation -p catalerum-exec --all-targets` clean; api lib **213**, automation **49** (incl. the `catalog.json` example round-trip), exec **13** tests pass; DB-gated terminal integration tests self-skip (no Postgres). **Deferred (reported, not fixed — real but larger / not testable here):** no child-exit reaper — a self-exited shell leaks a zombie child + (container/k8s) the keep-alive container/Pod + a phantom `active` row until an explicit `close`; no boot reconcile of `active` `terminal_sessions` rows after a restart (write says closed, file tools still succeed off the persisted `host_dir`, list says active); the k8s backend sets no securityContext / resource limits / NetworkPolicy / `automountServiceAccountToken=false` (weaker than the container backend's `--cap-drop ALL` / `no-new-privileges` / `--network none`); one-shot `run()` on container/k8s lacks `kill_on_drop` (latent — only the local executor is wired to `run_command` today); the web pane leaks and can duplicate its output socket on idle session-switch/unmount (no `on_cleanup`/epoch) and force-auto-scrolls past manual scrollback; `read_file` conflates whole-file clipping with window-shortening in its `truncated` flag._

_2026-06-26 — **Quick-start onboarding wizard — first-run setup for connections, models, profile, and AI-drafted skills (SOUL §12/§22/§23)** — a fresh account dropped straight into Chat with no guided setup: the pieces existed as separate endpoints (`/status`, `/llm-settings`, `/profile`, `/memories`, `/skills`) but nothing tied them into an onboarding flow, and there was no path from a user's stated goals to tailored skills. Added a five-step first-run wizard. **Server (`catalerum-api/src/routes/onboarding.rs`, merged flat like `settings`):** `GET /onboarding/state` (`profile:read`) reports `completed`/`chat_model_set`/`profile_empty` from a `quickstart_completed_at` profile sentinel + the user's `llm_settings`, driving the shell's first-run auto-open; `POST /onboarding/suggest-skills` (`skill:write`) resolves the effective chat model (user override else `[llm]` default — the same precedence as `ws.rs`), runs one `state.llm().chat()` completion under a prompt-for-JSON contract (mirroring the §22 memory extractor), and parses the reply into ≤N normalized `SkillDraft`s — tolerant of prose / ```json fences, kebab-casing + de-duping names and dropping runbook-less entries — without persisting (the client reviews then writes via `PUT /skills/{name}`, so every captured artifact stays an editable row per §16); `POST /onboarding/complete` (`profile:write`) merges the sentinel. Reuses the existing `profile`/`skill` capability domains — no new `Action` variant or domain string. **Web (`catalerum-web`, Leptos):** a new `components/onboarding.rs` `OnboardingPanel` — step 1 a live `/status` health read (with a down-services warning), step 2 chat/speech model + voice pickers over the config defaults (datalists modelled on `settings.rs`, a full-replace `PUT /llm-settings` that preserves the hidden transcription field), step 3 a profile form merged via `PUT /profile` plus an optional `user`-scoped memory, step 4 goals + environment → `suggest-skills` → checkbox draft review → idempotent `PUT /skills/{name}` for the chosen drafts, step 5 `complete` + jump to Chat — registered as a `Panel::Onboarding` nav entry ("Quick start") and auto-opened by `Workbench` when `/onboarding/state` reports incomplete; three new rest-client fns + DTOs + wizard CSS. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --lib` clean; 10 new onboarding unit tests (draft parsing, fence/prose stripping, count + name de-dup, kebab-casing, tool hygiene, prompt shape) pass; `cargo clippy -p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean and `trunk build` succeeds. **Deferred (noted):** the `tools` a draft lists are advisory (§23 restricted-tool enforcement is still deferred); persisted/suggested model ids aren't validated against the gateway catalog (same gap as `/llm-settings`); the wizard does not connect external data sources (calendar/email) — that remains the §11 Collect-automation flow._

_2026-06-26 — **Agent profiles are now authorable by the agent itself — `create`/`update`/`list`/`get`/`delete_agent_profile` tools (SOUL §19/§25)** — agent profiles (the durable, named scoped-agent configs that bind a model + tool/skill set + subagents + listening channels + the §19 grant that is their authority) had full REST CRUD (`/agent-profiles`) but **no agent-callable tools**, so an agent could never define or edit a scoped sub-agent. Added five tools in `catalerum-api/src/tools.rs` mirroring `register_automation_tools`: `list_agent_profiles` (name + counts + `has_grant` summary) and `get_agent_profile` gated on `agent_profile:read`; `create_agent_profile` (errors on name conflict), `update_agent_profile` (create-or-replace by name), and `delete_agent_profile` gated on `agent_profile:write`. All five hang off the admin-only `agent_profile` capability domain — no base role implies it (it isn't in `catalerum-iam`'s `DOMAINS`), so only an Owner/Admin `*` reaches them, deny-by-default like grants; `agent_profile` was added to the `PROTECTED` allow-list in the `every_registered_tool_capability_domain_is_role_grantable` guard accordingly. **§19 attenuation is enforced at the tool layer:** a `grant_id` a profile references must be ⊆ the **caller's own** `ctx.capabilities` (not `base_capabilities(role)` as the REST path uses, since `ToolContext` carries the resolved capability set, not a role) — `resolve_profile_grant` rejects an over-broad grant with `Error::Unauthorized`, skipping the check only when `ctx.capabilities` is `None` (a trusted internal caller, matching `ToolRegistry::dispatch`). Registered unconditionally in `build_registry` (harmless for non-admins — dispatch + `search_tools` filter by capability). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets` clean; new unit tests (`agent_profile_body_props`, `agent_profile_spec` normalization) + a DB-gated `agent_profile_tools_crud_and_grant_attenuation` (create→get→list→conflict→update-with-grant→attenuation-deny→unknown-grant→delete) all pass against live postgres; the capability-domain guard still passes._

_2026-06-27 — **Storage scan + ingest + watch — index pre-existing files and keep them in sync (SOUL §9/§10)** — closes the deferral from the browse-store turn below: files already on a backend (a `browse` store's `~/Documents`, a pre-populated S3 bucket) were never catalogued/ingested, so they had no "Indexed ✓" badge and weren't text-searchable; and nothing reacted to on-disk changes. **Scan engine** (`routes::storage::scan_store`, the single reconcile primitive): lists a store's backend (namespaced or raw via the `StorageHandle`), and for each object **new or changed** (by size / etag / last-modified — factored into a unit-tested `object_changed`) upserts its catalogue row + enqueues §10 ingest, leaves **unchanged** ones alone (so a steady-state re-scan does no writes), and **purges** catalogue rows whose key vanished from the backend (row deleted + §10 purge enqueued; the blob is never touched). Idempotent; bounded by `DEFAULT_OBJECT_LIMIT` (1000) with a **no-purge guard** when the listing is truncated (a key past the cap would look "missing"). Returns a `ScanReport {scanned, indexed, unchanged, removed, truncated}`. **On-demand:** `POST /storage/stores/{name}/scan` (`storage:write`) + a "Scan / index" button in the Files panel that reports counts; plus a **background auto-scan on store creation** (spawned, non-blocking) so a new browse/S3 store's existing files appear promptly. **Watch** (opt-in per store via a `watch` flag — `StorageBackendConfig.watch` + `"watch": true` runtime config; surfaced on `StoreView`/`StorageStore` + a "Watch for changes" checkbox + a "· watching" tag): a new **`StorageWatchWorker`** (`catalerum-api`, spawned in `main.rs`, holds `AppState`) runs a periodic reconcile pass (`[storage].watch_interval_secs`, default 60s, floored 5s) over every watch-enabled `(workspace, store)` across config + runtime backends — the sync path for **S3/WebDAV** and a safety net for local — and, for **local** stores, arms a real-time **inotify** watcher (new `notify` dep in `catalerum-api`, recursive, mirroring `catalerum-calendar`'s `watch.rs`) whose create/modify/remove events trigger a **debounced** (750 ms) `scan_store` of that store, so an edit to a watched `~/Documents` is re-indexed in ~1s; the first periodic tick fires immediately, bootstrapping pre-existing files at boot and arming watchers. Watchers are keyed by `(ws, store)` and dropped when a target disappears. **Verified:** native clippy (`catalerum`/`-api`/`-ingest --all-targets -D warnings`) clean; api lib **213** (+`object_changed` change-detection across new/size/etag/mtime, +`runtime_watch`); full web trio — wasm clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean, `trunk build` ✅. **Deferred / honest scope:** watching is per-`(workspace, store)`, so a *config* watch store is scanned once per workspace (intended for the single-tenant browse case — a busy multi-tenant deployment should keep `watch_interval_secs` generous, noted in-code); an inotify change triggers a full store re-scan (debounced) rather than per-file diffing (cheap for the target dir sizes, idempotent); a runtime store's inotify watcher is armed on the next periodic tick (≤ interval) after it's added (its create-time auto-scan covers the gap); overlapping periodic+inotify scans are possible but idempotent._

_2026-06-26 — **Files panel browses a store's real filesystem as a directory tree; local stores can `browse` an existing directory (SOUL §9/§18)** — two coupled gaps: (1) the Files panel listed the **Postgres catalogue** (`GET /storage/catalogue`), so a store only ever showed what catalerum itself uploaded — point a local store at an existing dir (e.g. `~/Documents`) and it looked **empty**; and (2) even the raw backend listing hid those files, because every physical key is **workspace-namespaced** `<workspace_id>/…` (§18, multi-tenant isolation) while files on disk sit at the bare root. The panel was also a **flat table** (directory shown only as a muted breadcrumb), not a navigable filesystem. Fixed both. **Browse flag:** a per-store opt-out of namespacing — `StorageBackendConfig.browse` (config) + `"browse": true` in a runtime store's connection config — surfaced as `StorageHandle.namespaced` (and `ConfigStore.namespaced`). The §18 mapping is now centralized in `StorageHandle::physical_key`/`user_key` (namespaced → `<ws>/key`, browse → raw key, leading slash trimmed), and the storage routes (`list`/`upload`/`download`/`remove`) call those instead of `workspace_object_key`/`strip_workspace_key` — so a browse store lists/reads/writes/deletes its directory **as-is** while every other store keeps full tenant isolation (default stays namespaced; the legacy `"default"` store is **always** namespaced). **Ingest made browse-aware:** `ObjectIngestContext::resolve_backend` now also returns whether the store is namespaced (config browse stores via a new `StorageRegistry::browse_connections()` set threaded in at boot; runtime stores read `browse` from their connection config) and `read_text` reads the raw key for a browse store — so a file **uploaded** to a browse store still gets §10 text extraction instead of a 404'd read. **Frontend rewrite:** the panel now browses the **selected store's backend** (`GET /storage/objects?store=&prefix=`, new `rest::list_objects` + `api::BackendObject`) and **enriches each file from the catalogue by key** (Indexed ✓ badge + extracted-text viewer where a catalogue row exists), rendering an **expandable nested tree** — directories synthesized from the flat key listing (`build_rows`), flattened to visible rows gated by an `expanded` set (`ancestors_expanded`), depth-indented; the store switcher drives both browse + upload and resets expansion on change; truncation at `DEFAULT_OBJECT_LIMIT` (1000) is surfaced. The "Manage storage" form gained a **"Browse existing directory"** checkbox (local kind) with a no-isolation warning. **Verified:** native clippy (`catalerum`/`-api`/`-ingest --all-targets -D warnings`) clean; api lib **211** incl. a new `physical_and_user_key_honor_namespacing` round-trip; full web trio — wasm clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean (+ new `build_rows`/`ancestors_expanded` tree tests), `trunk build` ✅. **Incidental repair:** fixed a pre-existing build-blocking macro-parse error in `skills.rs` (`when=move || tool_count > 0` — the bare `>` made the `view!` macro read the closure as returning `usize`; switched to the file's own `let has = …; move || has` pattern) so the web crate compiles. **Deferred:** pre-existing on-disk files in a browse store aren't auto-ingested (no badge until uploaded/scanned) — a directory **scan-and-ingest** would close that; a browse store has no tenant isolation by design (documented, single-tenant only)._

_2026-06-26 — **Chat now surfaces tool calls — live cards, replay, and bespoke per-tool UIs (SOUL §7/§12)** — the chat UI never showed the tools the assistant ran: the agent loop dispatched them server-side and only the final text streamed back, so a multi-round turn rendered as one merged bubble with no sign a tool ran. Two independent gaps: **live**, the model's `ToolCallDelta` was mapped to `StreamUpdate::Ignore` and **no event for a tool executing or returning existed at all** (tool dispatch runs *after* the model stream and never touched the observer; `StreamEvent` had 5 variants, `ServerFrame` no tool frame); **replay**, `open_session` dropped every non-user/assistant row and any empty assistant turn, so tool rows — and **pure tool-call turns entirely** — vanished despite `tool_calls`/`tool_call_id` being persisted. Fixed in three phases. **P1 (frontend-only):** new `ChatLine.tool_calls: Vec<ToolCallView>`; the replay loop rebuilds each turn's cards from the assistant `tool_calls` paired (by `tool_call_id`) with the `tool` result rows (generalized the `ui_by_call` map into `results_by_call`), and the empty-skip now keeps a row with text **or** UI **or** tools (repairing the vanishing-turn bug); a new `components/tool_render.rs` **renderer registry** gives built-in tools bespoke cards from their args+result (events, notes, `web_search`, `fetch_url`, `recall`, `run_command`, …) and falls back to a generic "smart" render (pretty-JSON / sanitized-Markdown) for unmatched built-ins **and** external MCP tools (server-prefixed, unknown shape); cards are collapsible `<details class="msg-tool">` modelled on the `msg-thinking` block, read through the per-line `row` Memo so a live card updates in place; `present_ui`/`edit_ui` are excluded (they mount inline as `EmergedUi`). **P2 (live status):** two **additive, id-keyed** `StreamEvent`s — `ToolCallStarted` + `ToolResult` (result/is_error/duration_ms/truncated) — synthesized in the agent dispatch loop (timed with `Instant`, 16 KiB wire cap + `truncated` flag), riding the existing `ServerFrame::Token` + bus relay with **no `ws.rs`/bus change**; the web decodes them into `StreamUpdate::ToolStarted`/`ToolResult`, and `send_turn` attaches a `Running` card on start and resolves it by `call_id` (spinner → ✓/✗ + duration). Crucially we do **not** render `ToolCallDelta` — a multi-agent review caught that its per-iteration `index` resets every round (fresh `ToolCallAssembler` per `stream_turn`), so accumulating by index would merge different rounds' calls into garbage; discrete id-keyed events sidestep this and need no client-side reassembly. Exhaustive-match arms added in `agent.rs`/`client.rs`/`curate.rs`. **P3 (replay fidelity):** migration `0031_tool_result_meta` adds `messages.tool_is_error` + `tool_duration_ms`, threaded through `NewMessage`/`MessageRow`/core `Message`/all repo SELECTs+insert; `ws.rs` persistence populates them per tool row from `outcome.tool_invocations` (by `tool_call_id`); replay reads the persisted flag (heuristic `{"error":…}` fallback for legacy rows) + duration. **Verified:** both clippy gates `-D warnings` (native `--workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets`; wasm `catalerum-web`); core/llm/api/ingest unit + integration tests (updated the agent streaming-loop test for the 2 new synthesized events); store DB tests incl. a new `messages_tool_meta_repo` round-trip run against live postgres with `0031` applied; 222 web tests (+ `tool_render` + new frame-decode); `trunk build`. **Deferred (noted):** transcript-shape divergence accepted — live attaches all cards to the single streaming bubble, but persistence writes one assistant row per agent iteration, so reload shows per-round bubbles; replay cross-round **ordering** is nondeterministic for same-microsecond rows (`ORDER BY created_at, id` with a random-v4 id tiebreaker — a latent general issue, a monotonic ordinal / UUIDv7 would fix it); built-in-vs-MCP badge is **done** — tool cards flag external **MCP** tools with an "MCP" badge; the chat panel classifies authoritatively by membership in the global `/tools` built-in catalog (the static registry; MCP tools live only in the per-run overlay) plus the always-on `delegate`, so no per-tool wire/persistence marker was needed._

_2026-06-26 — **Files choose between multiple storage backends — config + runtime (SOUL §9)** — storage was a single backend chosen by precedence (S3 > WebDAV > local in `build_storage_backend`); only one was ever live, so a file couldn't pick where it lived (the data model already modelled connections → buckets → objects, and the Files table already showed a "Bucket" column for >1 bucket — the gap was config + wiring + UI, not the catalogue). Now a workspace holds **many** named "stores", several of the **same kind** allowed, from **two sources** (principle 10: config is the base, runtime layers on): config — a new `[storage.backends.<name>]` map (the legacy top-level `[storage]` stays as the `"default"` backend, so existing configs are untouched) — and **runtime**, user-added and persisted as kind=Storage `Connection` rows whose `config` JSON carries the backend settings (secrets stored **verbatim**, mirroring `mcp_servers.auth`, until the §13 secret store lands; redacted on read). New `catalerum-storage::backend_from_connection` / `backend_from_config` + `StorageSubKind` mirror calendar/email's `provider_from_connection`. `AppState` now holds a `StorageRegistry` of the config backends; `routes/storage.rs::resolve` picks a store per request from `?store=` (else the default, else the sole store across both sources), trying the config registry first then a runtime `Connection` built on the fly. `?store=` rides every blob route (upload / download / list / delete); new `GET/POST/DELETE /storage/stores` list/add/remove backends (secrets never returned, config stores undeletable, all `storage:read`/`storage:write` + workspace-scoped §18). The catalogue view gained a per-object `store` (the `?store=` selector, distinct from the bucket label — they can diverge for the default store), so the Files panel does **store-aware** download/delete plus a destination dropdown (shown for >1 store) and a "Manage storage" add/remove panel. The **object-ingest worker** (`ObjectIngestContext`) now resolves each object's backend by its bucket's connection (config map keyed by connection name → runtime `backend_from_connection` → default-store fallback), so a file on any store still gets §10 text extraction. Boot provisions every config backend's container; backup still mirrors only the default store (named/runtime backends not yet mirrored — tracked). **Adversarial multi-agent review** (correctness / security-tenant-isolation / web / consistency, each finding independently verified) confirmed one real bug — runtime stores catalogued under the *store name*, ignoring their configured `bucket`, so the catalogue label + the `StorageObject` trigger's `bucket` diverged from the physical S3 bucket — fixed with a shared `runtime_bucket_name` (config `bucket`, else the store name) used in both `resolve` and `create_store`, plus a unit test; tenant-isolation + secret-redaction came back clean. **Verified:** native clippy `--workspace -D warnings`; new + existing unit tests (config multi-backend, storage routes incl. `runtime_bucket_name`, storage crate, ingest); wasm clippy; 214 web tests; `trunk build`. **Deferred (noted in-code):** backup mirrors only the default store; content-search-hit downloads target the default store (a hit carries no store); runtime secrets stored verbatim (MCP precedent) pending the §13 secret store._

_2026-06-26 — **Workdir file tools — `read_file` / `create_file` / `edit_file` over a terminal session's working directory (SOUL §20)** — the agent could only touch its sandbox files clumsily over the PTY (`cat`/heredocs/`sed` in `terminal_write`, racing the async output). Added three file-level tools to `catalerum-api/src/terminal.rs`, thin clients of `TerminalManager`, each keyed on a `session_id` from `open_terminal` + a workdir-relative `path`. **`read_file`** returns the file's text with optional 1-based `offset`/`limit` line windowing, plus `total_lines`/`size`/`truncated`; **`create_file`** writes (or overwrites) a whole file, creating parent dirs, reporting bytes-written + `created` vs overwritten; **`edit_file`** does a unique-match string replace (`old_string`/`new_string`, or `replace_all`) with Claude-Code semantics (errors on 0 or >1 matches unless `replace_all`). **Safety:** a shared `resolve_in_dir` enforces the §18 relative-key contract (rejects absolute / `.` / `..` so a tool can never escape the workdir — same rule as storage object keys); reads are bounded (8 MiB hard ceiling → OOM-safe; 256 KiB inline cap with a `truncated` flag); `edit_file` **refuses** a non-UTF-8 or over-ceiling file (a partial read would corrupt it on write-back). the only interpolated token is the node/edge label, sourced from the fixed `NodeLabel`/`EdgeType` enums (`as_cypher()`), never user input — so **no Cypher injection**. The security posture is strong; remaining value is non-security correctness/features, so a fresh value-survey (logic/data-integrity/missing-feature, in stable non-agent-zone areas) drives the next pick. — _Prior iteration:_ **SSRF guard now decodes 6to4 embedded-IPv4 (`2002::/16`) — closes the last embedded-v4 smuggling vector (SOUL §13/§19/§27)** — a targeted security review of `catalerum-fetch`'s SSRF policy (`policy.rs`/`http.rs`). It already re-checks embedded IPv4 for IPv4-mapped/compatible and the **NAT64** prefix (`64:ff9b::/96`) — but **not 6to4** (`2002::/16`, RFC 3056), the same smuggling class: a literal like `2002:a9fe:a9fe::` embeds `169.254.169.254` (cloud metadata) and would pass `validate` (it's not loopback/ULA/link-local/mapped/NAT64), and an **IP literal skips the resolver guard**, so on a 6to4-capable host it routes to the embedded v4. **Fix:** added `sixto4_embedded_v4()` (extracts the v4 from segments `[1]/[2]`, mirroring `nat64_embedded_v4`) into `v6_is_blocked`'s embedded-v4 `or_else` chain — so a 6to4 address embedding a private/loopback/metadata v4 is blocked, while one embedding a *public* v4 stays allowed (only the embedded address counts, matching the NAT64 rule). **Verified:** `cargo test -p catalerum-fetch --lib policy` green (new `2002:` cases in `blocks_ipv6_local`: metadata/127/10 blocked, `2002:0808:0808::`→8.8.8.8 allowed) + `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean. _2026-06-26 — **Email + calendar ingestion is now IMPLEMENTED as user-authored automation nodes — the §8/§10/§11/§28/§29 "Collect trigger / explicit Write action" design (recorded 2026-06-25, see the entry below) is built, and the old always-on email poller is removed.** **Triggers** (`catalerum-automation`): new poll-driven `Trigger::CollectEmail { connection, mailbox?, filter?, commit_on?, backfill_window?, every? }` + `CollectCalendar { …, calendar?, … }` (with `is_collect()`/`collect_connection()`/`commit_on()`/`collect_every()`/`backfill_window()` accessors); **removed** `Trigger::MailReceived` + `TriggerEvent::MailReceived` + its matcher. **Actions:** `ActionKind::WriteEmail` (idempotent upsert by `(mailbox_id,uid)` + enqueue the §10 `chunk→embed→project`), `WriteEvent` (twin, by `(calendar_id,uid)` + event graph projection), `LabelEmail` (records a classifier verdict into a new `emails.labels` column) — special-cased in `ToolActionRunner` **before** `tool_for` (they read the whole collected item off the firing trigger + do a store write, not a templated tool dispatch), each capability-gated (`email:write`/`calendar:write`) by an explicit `cap_allows` check (the special-case path bypasses the registry's own gate) and honoring `dry_run`; both Write actions force `item.workspace_id = action.workspace_id` (defense-in-depth, no cross-tenant write). **The collect job** (`catalerum-ingest/src/collect.rs`, new): `run_collect_email`/`run_collect_calendar` build the provider from the connection row (`provider_from_connection`), drain its pages, and fire **one real `AutomationRun` per genuinely-new item, processed in-order INLINE** via `execute_for_job` — which resolves the §29 out-of-order/contiguous-prefix question cleanly (in-order processing IS the contiguous prefix). `commit_on` is resolved post-run by `list_steps` → `action["node"]` match → `Succeeded`/`Skipped` gates the per-source cursor advance (unset = fire-and-forget). State is a per-source **committed-uid ledger** packed in the connection `sync_token` (alongside the provider cursor), persisted **after each item** (narrows the §29 redelivery window to the single in-flight item). **Cadence:** `ScheduleWorker::scan_collect_triggers` enqueues a lightweight `collect_email`/`collect_calendar` job per due trigger (single-fired via the bus lock, `every` cadence via `graph_due`), and the `SyncWorker` (which holds the automation context) does the heavy provider pull off the 60s clock. `CalendarProvider` gained `is_incremental()` (CalDav=true/Webcal=false) to mirror `EmailProvider`, so the ledger compacts correctly per provider mode. Graph `validate` now checks `commit_on` references a real Action node AND that a collect graph has exactly **one** trigger node (a collect run seeds all trigger nodes, so a second would mis-fire). **Removed:** `EmailSyncWorker`/`scan_email_connections`/`sync_email.rs`, `[email]`/`EmailConfig`, the `main.rs` email-worker block; `routes/email.rs` connection CRUD stays (now "dormant until a CollectEmail trigger pulls it"). Web editor palettes (`flow.rs`/`automations.rs`) gained the 2 triggers + 3 actions; catalog.json gained 5 node docs. **Web UX (per user direction): email/calendar sources are configured IN the collect node, not Settings.** The Settings **Email tab + `EmailSection` were removed** (§28: no dedicated email settings); the `CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar` node config now embeds an **inline "configure source" form** (provider + credentials → `rest::create_email_connection`/`create_connection` → writes the new connection id into the trigger's `connection`). And **`commit_on` is a connectable PORT, not a text field**: a collect node exposes a second dashed `"commit"` out-port you drag to the write node; `graph_to_spec_value` folds every `from_port=="commit"` edge into the trigger's `commit_on` field (and drops it from `edges`), `flow_from_spec` rebuilds the visual edge, and the data-flow helpers (`has_cycle`/`unreachable`/`problem`) skip commit edges — so the backend `Graph` is unchanged (commit stays a trigger field, never a write→trigger DAG edge). **A 5-lens adversarial review (correctness/ledger/commit_on/security/SOUL-divergence) + per-finding verification surfaced 18 confirmed issues; the real correctness bugs were FIXED:** (1) **snapshot double-run** — a no-change snapshot poll returned empty `upserts`, and `advance_source` pruned the committed set to that empty batch → cleared it → re-ran the whole mailbox on the next change; fixed by pruning only when the snapshot was actually re-read (cursor changed); (2) **steady-state backfill flood** — first-poll pre-cutoff items were filtered-and-forgotten, then re-admitted once the cutoff lifted; fixed by marking pre-cutoff items **committed (seen)** on the first poll so they stay bounded; (3) **ledger persisted only at job end** → fixed with per-item + per-source persistence; (4) cross-tenant write hardening; (5) `LabelEmail` order-preserving de-dup; (6) the collect single-trigger graph guard; (7) a stale `MailReceived` rustdoc link. **Honestly NOT done (disclosed, deferred):** raw `.eml` archival to object storage was **dropped** (the removed `EmailStorageContext`) — `Email.raw_ref`/`raw` are now unused on the collect path (a §29-parked follow-up; bodies still persist + embed); **provider deletions are not reconciled to the store** (collect is upsert-only — a source-deleted message/event persists; a future Delete action or reconcile would close it); `email:collect@<connection>` is **not enforced** (the pull runs under workspace-owner authority — the §19 grant engine isn't built); the first-poll backfill default is a fixed **1-day grace** (not literal "newer than the automation's creation" — `Automation` has no `created_at`); no "commit_on unset" / "dormant connection" validation warning yet; the executor's break-on-first-failure means an **independent** failing branch can starve a `commit_on` write (infinite re-collect) — pre-existing executor behavior. **Verified against live Postgres + Neo4j:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean; automation **49** (collect-trigger round-trip, commit_on/single-trigger graph validation), ingest **52** (collect ledger: `advance_source` prefix rule incl. the no-change-poll-keeps-committed regression test, backfill cutoff, email filter, foreign-token tolerance), store `mailboxes_emails_repo` **4** (new `set_labels` round-trip + survives-resync + NotFound), api lib **189** (incl. a live-DB end-to-end `collect_email_fires_per_message_writes_them_and_commits_then_is_idempotent`: Maildir(2 msgs)→CollectEmail→WriteEmail with `commit_on` → 2 runs/2 writes/2 commits, unchanged re-poll → 0, a 3rd message → exactly 1 new run not 3); full **web trio** — wasm clippy clean · web **205** · `trunk build` ✅; catalog **6** (35 docs). **Next:** restore raw `.eml` archival inside `WriteEmail` (thread a storage backend onto the runner); a per-connection collect lock + `sync_token` CAS so overlapping windows can't clobber; _2026-06-26 — **Memory extraction no longer reads the whole conversation — bounded transcript fetch (SOUL §18/§6.1/§22)** — survey pick #4. `extract_memories` (the §22 curation job that distils durable user facts from a chat) fetched **every** message in a conversation via the unbounded `MessageRepo::list_by_conversation` (`fetch_all`, no LIMIT) and then threw away all but the last `RECENT_MESSAGES=8` user/assistant turns — so a long-running conversation (thousands of messages) loaded the entire history into memory just to keep eight turns. **Fix:** fetch only the most-recent `TRANSCRIPT_SCAN=64` messages via the existing `MessageRepo::list_recent` (already used by `read_conversation`), from which `recent_transcript` distils the same last 8 user/assistant turns. **Behaviour-preserving** for every realistic case — 64 is a generous multiple of 8, so interleaved system/tool turns can't starve the 8 user/assistant turns out of the window (an accepted best-effort edge for a >56-trailing-tool-message conversation, on a best-effort curation path). **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-ingest --all-targets -D warnings` clean; the existing `worker_extracts_and_dedups_memories_from_a_conversation` integration test still green (the swap is transparent end-to-end); plus a **new unit test for the previously-untested `recent_transcript`** (`recent_transcript_keeps_last_user_assistant_turns_and_skips_noise`: skips System/Tool/empty turns · keeps the last 8 user/assistant turns chronologically — validating the fetch-window sizing). **No store change** (reuses `list_recent`). **Next:** `SkillRepo::list_by_workspace` §18 cap (2 callers); `MailboxRepo::get_many` to drop the unbounded mailbox-index build in `search_emails` — both clean, both outside the concurrent agent's zones._

for a full snapshot it re-projects the window, idempotent) + lib re-exports. **Honest scope:** this slice projects on **upsert**; a deleted event's node is reconciled on the next full graph rebuild (deletion-purge-on-sync needs the event id at delete time — a documented follow-up). **Verified end-to-end against live Postgres + Neo4j:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-graph -p catalerum-ingest --all-targets -D warnings` clean; graph crate **20**, ingest **lib 48** (+2 pure: event-payload round-trip · `project_event` job-kind token); `note_graph` **4** — a **new** `project_event_round_trips_idempotently_and_purges_on_delete` (project → `:Event`+`:Calendar` = 2 nodes · idempotent → still 2 · delete → purged, calendar survives → 1) and `worker_dispatches_project_event_job_to_the_graph_context` (enqueue → worker drains → `Done` → 2 nodes); A 3-lens adversarial review (each finding confirmed against the code — 2 real of 3 raw, both **low**) **caught two gaps, both fixed:** (1) the tests asserted only `count_nodes`, which is edge/label-agnostic — a wrong `SCHEDULED_IN` type/direction/endpoint or a mislabeled node would still pass; fixed by adding a real edge assertion via a **new `GraphStore::scheduled_in(ws, event_id)`** (the calendar twin of `references_of`), and the tests now assert the event is `SCHEDULED_IN` exactly its own calendar (and that a purged event has no edge). One **intended** behaviour change: a DB error on the batch now **surfaces** as a tool error (mirroring the adjacent `mailboxes()` fetch) instead of the old per-hit warn-and-skip that silently returned empty results — a clearer signal to the agent, no silent failure. **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-store -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; a new store test `get_many_batches_and_is_workspace_scoped` (two in-ws ids + a foreign id + a bogus id in one call → only the two return; foreign never leaks; empty→empty) green; full api **lib 173** in parallel (search_emails wiring compiles + every test green). _2026-06-25 — **Design decision (REVISED) — email + calendar ingestion is a user-built automation headed by a *Collect* trigger; no settings, no background poller, persistence explicit (SOUL §8/§10/§11/§13/§28/§29) — RECORDED, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.** Supersedes the same-day `SyncConnection`-action sketch after a user correction: collection is a **trigger**, writing is **explicit**, nothing is auto-provisioned. Model: new **source triggers `CollectEmail { connection, mailbox?, filter? }` / `CollectCalendar { connection, calendar?, filter? }`** you fill with a §28/§8 connection — each polls its provider on the durable §6.2 `job_queue` (heavy I/O off the 60s clock) and **fires one automation run per new external item** (at-least-once). The trigger carries a **`commit_on`** node reference: set it to a downstream write and the connection `sync_token` advances for an item only after that write `Succeeded` (a **post-run finalization** reads the node's status; the collector advances over the **contiguous committed prefix**, a `Condition`-skipped write counting as intentionally-committed), else fire-and-forget on enqueue. A 3-lens adversarial review against `graph.rs`/`executor.rs` **caught a blocker**: `commit_on` must be a **node reference, NOT a back-edge** — a write→trigger edge fails `topo_order`'s Kahn acyclicity check (rejected as a cycle) and trigger nodes ignore incoming edges at runtime anyway; the reference model keeps the DAG acyclic by construction. Persistence is an **explicit downstream action `WriteEmail`/`WriteEvent`** — idempotent upsert by `(mailbox_id, uid)` / event uid + the §10 `chunk → embed → project` — so **nothing is stored or searchable unless the graph writes it**; classification is an `LlmAgent` node and the verdict is recorded by a second write (`LabelEmail`/`CreateNote`/`CreateTask`). Adding a connection provisions **nothing**: the user authors `CollectEmail(conn) → WriteEmail → LlmAgent → LabelEmail`; an unwired connection is **dormant**. `CollectEmail` **supersedes the `MailReceived` reactor** (no background ingest to react to); `CalendarEvent { lead }` stays a reminder over already-written events. Capabilities: `email:collect@<connection>` (pull from the provider, read-only §14) for the trigger, `email:write`/`calendar:write` (persist to *our* store) for the Write action. **Removed by the plan:** `[email]` config, `EmailConfig`, `EmailSyncWorker` + `scan_email_connections`, and the earlier `SyncConnection` action / managed-automation / `ensure_sync_automation` / `connections:sync` idea. **Kept:** `connections` rows (config + `credential_ref` + `sync_token`), provider traits/backends, the pull + upsert + project primitives (§10) — now invoked by nodes, not a worker. **Status: SOUL.md updated; code UNCHANGED.** Backlog: `Trigger::CollectEmail`/`CollectCalendar` (with a `commit_on` field) as periodic source triggers + a durable collect job that emits one run per item; `ActionKind::WriteEmail`/`WriteEvent`/`LabelEmail` + tools + the collect/write capabilities; the **post-run finalization phase + contiguous-prefix cursor** in the collector layer; offer (don't force) a default Collect automation when a connection is added; delete the poller + `[email]`. Cursor-commit, out-of-order, skipped-write and backfill are now **resolved in shape** (§11/§29); the one unresolved correctness hole is **redelivery re-running `LlmAgent`/`LabelEmail`** (double-spend tokens / re-label), still open in §29 alongside dormant-connection warning + collect cadence._

_2026-06-25 — **Paged provider sync now drains every page — `SyncBatch.has_more` was parsed but never consumed (SOUL §8/§10/§28/§18)** — a real data-loss bug surfaced by the gap survey: `SyncBatch.has_more` ("more data is immediately available") is **set by providers** — IMAP flags it `true` whenever it defers a backlog (`imap.rs`: `has_more: !deferred.is_empty()`) — but **`catalerum-ingest` never read it** (grep found `has_more` only at its definition + provider sites, never in ingest). So `sync_mailbox`/`sync_calendar` called `provider.sync()` **once** and persisted the advanced cursor, silently dropping every page past the first until the *next* scheduled sync (which could re-defer) — a mailbox with a large backlog would trickle in one page per sync interval, or lose mail that aged out. **Fix:** both per-item sync fns now **drain pages in a bounded loop** — fetch, apply (upsert + archive + `MailReceived` + §10 projection for email; upsert + deletions for calendar), then continue from `next_cursor` while `has_more`. A new pure `next_sync_page(has_more, used_cursor, next_cursor, pages, max)` (catalerum-ingest `lib.rs`) gates continuation and **guarantees termination**: stops on `!has_more`, on a **non-advancing cursor** (a provider looping the same page), or at **`MAX_SYNC_PAGES = 1000`** (anti-infinite-loop). Crucially `synced_uids` now **accumulates across all pages** so the full-snapshot deletion reconcile (Maildir / local `.ics`) runs **once after the last page** against the complete set — never mistaking page 1 of a multi-page snapshot for "everything else was deleted"; incremental providers (IMAP/JMAP/Gmail) still skip the diff (`is_incremental()`), and the single-page case is byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving (`upserted > 0` ⟺ old `!upserts.is_empty()`; `any_deletions` ⟺ old `!deletions.is_empty()`). **A 3-lens adversarial review (each finding confirmed against the code — 1 real of 3 raw) caught a low-severity latent defect:** the full-snapshot reconcile is sound only when the drain finished via `!has_more` — if it stopped **early** (the page cap or the cursor-stall guard, with `has_more` still true), `synced_uids` would hold only the *fetched* pages and the reconcile would prune live items on the un-fetched tail. Not reachable with any shipped provider (the only paginator, IMAP, is incremental → skips the reconcile; no calendar provider paginates) but it contradicted the stated invariant on a data-loss path, so **fixed**: a `drained_fully = !has_more` flag now gates the reconcile in both loops (single-page → `drained_fully = true`, byte-for-byte unchanged). **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-ingest --all-targets -D warnings` clean; ingest **lib 46** (+3: a pure `next_sync_page_drains_until_no_more_or_capped_or_stalled` — has-more/no-more · stalled-cursor · page-cap · fresh-None; a live-DB `sync_mailbox_drains_all_pages_of_a_paged_provider` — 3-page incremental mock → **3 sync calls · all 5 persisted · final cursor saved**; and a regression `partial_drain_does_not_reconcile_delete_unfetched_messages` — a non-incremental provider that **stalls** mid-drain must NOT delete a prior message it never re-listed); existing `email_sync` **6** + `local_sync` **1** still green (behaviour-preserving). **Next:** calendar has no paginating provider today (local/CalDAV both `has_more: false`) so its loop is defensive/future-proof; the same drain belongs in storage object sync if that ever pages; the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one user-direction item._

_2026-06-25 — **Calendar grid — Month / Week / Day views (SOUL §8/§12)** — the calendar panel had only the day-grouped **agenda**; added a Month/Week/Day grid switcher beside it so events are seen in a true calendar, not just a list. **All date math is pure, no `chrono` in the wasm bundle** (the agenda's standing constraint): dates are carried as **day-numbers** (days since 1970-01-01) via Howard Hinnant's exact `days_from_civil`/`civil_from_days`, giving clean +/- navigation and a single integer key for bucketing; the week is **Monday-first (ISO 8601)**, the month grid is a fixed **6×7 = 42 cells** (always covers any month), month navigation anchors on the 1st so a 31st never overflows into the next month, and **`event_day_span`** buckets each event across every UTC day it covers with the **exclusive-midnight** convention (an `end = next-day 00:00` event occupies just its start day). Today's anchor + highlight come from **`js_sys::Date` UTC getters**, keeping the grids UTC-consistent with the agenda. **Month** renders event chips (time + title) on every covered day, capped 3/cell with "+N more"; clicking a day/chip drills into **Day**. **Week/Day** share a `render_timegrid`: a sticky day header, an **all-day row** for midnight-to-midnight events (one bar per event, grid-column-spanned + clamped to the visible week), and a **24-hour time grid** of absolutely-positioned blocks **lane-packed per day** (greedy interval-cluster column assignment) so overlaps sit side-by-side; multi-day and **midnight-crossing** timed events clamp to each column's day edges (start-before → 00:00, end-after → 24:00). Navigation and the views themselves work entirely on the **already-loaded in-memory event list** (no refetch on navigate); the From/To filter is scoped to Agenda; a per-calendar **colour stripe** (FNV-hash → HSL hue) distinguishes calendars on chips/blocks. **Adversarially reviewed** (4 lenses — date-math · time-grid placement · Leptos reactivity · CSS/layout — each finding independently **refuted** before counting): the only confirmed defect was a **major** CSS one — the all-day row's sticky offset hard-coded the header height, so when **today** is in view its 1.7rem day-number circle grew the header and the all-day row overlapped it; fixed by giving the day-number a **fixed 1.7rem box** (today only tints it) + deriving both the header height and the all-day offset from a `--tg-head-h` variable. **Verified — the full web trio:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings` clean · `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **197** (was 185; **+12** grid-math units — civil-days roundtrip incl. leap years / pre-1970 / year-boundary, Monday week-start, 42-cell Monday-aligned month coverage, year-wrapping month nav with no day overflow, exclusive-midnight + multi-day spans, lane-packing column reuse, week-title boundary collapsing) · `trunk build` ✅. **The calendar is now a real grid, not just an agenda.** **Next:** an event detail popover + drag-to-create on the time grid; a Sunday-vs-Monday week-start preference; a collapsible all-day row when it grows tall; a client-side range fetch if per-workspace event volume outgrows loading all events._

_2026-06-25 — **`search_tools` — agents semantically search the tools they're allowed to use (SOUL §6.4/§7)** — now that runtime MCP servers can add dozens of tools (a single Playwright adds ~25), advertising every spec each turn is costly and noisy; this lets the agent **discover** the right tool by intent. New in-memory **`ToolIndex` (`catalerum-api/tool_index.rs`)** embeds each tool's `name: description` with the **same llmleaf embedder chat/`search_semantic` use** and ranks an embedded query by cosine. Deliberately **in-memory, not Qdrant**: the corpus is tiny, global, and rarely changes, so there's no collection to manage and it **works whenever the embedder does** (no `[qdrant].enabled` dependency). It is **self-syncing** — `reconcile` embeds tools newly present (reading the §26 dynamic overlay, so a just-connected MCP server's tools become searchable) and prunes tools gone, **incrementally** (only the delta is embedded); it runs on every search and is **pre-warmed at boot** after MCP servers connect. **"(allowed)" = the exact dispatch gate:** results are filtered to tools the caller may actually call — the tool's `required_capability` covered by `ctx.capabilities` (deny-by-default §19), the same check `ToolRegistry::dispatch` applies — and `search_tools` excludes itself. (Chose capability filtering over threading a new `ToolContext.allowed_tools` field through 6+ ctx-construction sites — several in concurrently-edited files — and noted the per-run *advertised* restriction as a softer refinement for later.) The **`search_tools`** wrapper (`tools.rs`) is itself **ungated** — discovering a tool you may use is harmless, and the result set is already scoped to your authority — taking `{query, limit:1-25=10}`, returning `{name, description, score}` per hit. **Wiring:** `AppState` builds the index from `Arc::new(llm.clone())` + `[llm].embedding_model` and registers `search_tools` **last** so its registry snapshot sees every other tool (and shares the runtime MCP overlay); the binary pre-warms it after connecting servers (best-effort — a transient embedder outage just defers to the first search). **No `catalerum-core` change** — reuses the existing `Embedder`/`EmbeddingRequest`. **Verified:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean; **api lib +4** → **163** — `cosine` edge cases (orthogonal · zero-norm · length-mismatch all safe); relevance ranking **and** capability filtering proven with a deterministic offline keyword embedder (a restricted ctx lacking `calendar:read` never sees the calendar tool); `reconcile` adds a hot **overlay** tool then prunes it on removal; `search` lazily reconciles a newly-added tool with no explicit sync. **This is the groundwork for tool-RAG: advertise a small core set + `search_tools` and let the agent pull in the rest on demand, cutting per-turn tool-spec tokens as the registry (and MCP fleet) grows.** **Next:** thread `ctx.allowed_tools` so a profile's *advertised* restriction also narrows results (today: capability-only — correct for chat where all tools are advertised, and ≈ correct for scoped-grant profiles); an opt-in "core + search only" advertise mode to realize the token savings; persist embeddings to Qdrant only if the tool corpus ever grows beyond in-memory comfort._

_2026-06-25 — **Runtime MCP server management — `list/create/edit/delete_mcp_server` tools, hot-(dis)connect with no restart (SOUL §26/§19/§18)** — last turns made catalerum an MCP *client* (stdio + HTTP/SSE + auth); this lets an (admin) agent **manage** those server connections at runtime instead of only via `[mcp.servers]` config. **The crux — a runtime-mutable registry:** `ToolRegistry` gained a second, **dynamic overlay** (`Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, Arc<dyn Tool>>>>`) beside its static map; `get`/`contains`/`specs` consult both (static wins on a name clash) and `register_dynamic`/`unregister_dynamic` mutate it through `&self`. Because **every** per-run/derived registry is built by `.clone()` (chat's `registry_with_delegate`, the `POST /mcp` route, the automation runner) and `Clone` shallow-clones the `Arc`, the overlay is **shared across all of them** — a tool hot-added on one is instantly dispatchable through every clone, no restart; the agent loop only ever *reads* (`specs`/`dispatch`), so adding/removing tools never disrupts a running turn (verified by a 7-agent lifecycle survey before building). **Live `McpManager` (`catalerum-api/mcp_manager.rs`):** connects a stored `McpServerDef` (stdio or HTTP/SSE, reusing the existing `load_*_server_tools` + auth builders) and registers its tools into the overlay, tracking server→tool-names so edit/delete reconnect/tear down cleanly — dropping a tool's `Arc` reaps its stdio child / closes its HTTP client. **Four tools (deny-by-default, §19):** `list_mcp_servers` (`mcp:read` — **redacts secrets**, shows env keys not values + live connection status), `create_mcp_server` (`mcp:write` — persist + connect live, reporting imported-tool count or a connect error **without** un-persisting), `edit_mcp_server` (`mcp:write` — upsert-by-name + reconnect, or disconnect when `enabled:false`), `delete_mcp_server` (`mcp:delete` — disconnect then delete). None held by a base role (owner/admin only, like `agent_profile:*`); *using* the imported tools stays the separate `mcp:use@{server}` gate, so management never widens use. **Persistence (§18):** core `McpServerDef`/`McpAuthSpec` + `McpServerId`; migration `0023_mcp_servers` (JSONB `args`/`env`/`auth`/`tools`, `UNIQUE(workspace_id,name)`, mirrors `agent_profiles`); `McpServerRepo` (create · upsert_by_name · get_by_name · list_by_workspace · **list_enabled** · delete_by_name). **Boot:** the binary reconnects every enabled DB server (`list_enabled`, cross-workspace) into the overlay after `AppState`, beside the static config-file servers — logs-and-skips a failure. **Verified against the running stack:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean; **core +2** overlay tests (a clone sees/dispatches/loses an overlay tool; a static tool shadows a same-named overlay one) → **35**; **api lib +2** (per-transport parse validation · secret-redaction never echoes token/env-values) → **159**; a **live-Postgres `mcp_servers_repo`** test (CRUD · upsert switching stdio→http+bearer · `list_enabled` cross-workspace + enabled-only · tenant isolation) run green against `catalerum-postgres`. **An admin agent can now stand up a Playwright (or any) MCP server mid-conversation and call its tools the same turn, then tear it down — all capability-gated, all persisted.** **Next:** auth secrets are stored verbatim in the `auth` JSONB — move them behind the §13 secret store; the overlay shares one global tool-name namespace, so two workspaces naming a server alike would collide (fine for the single primary workspace today; per-workspace overlays would fix it); no REST/web surface yet (tools only)._

_2026-06-25 — **MCP client gains an HTTP/SSE transport + authentication (bearer · header · OAuth2-SSO) — hosted MCP servers are now reachable (SOUL §26/§19)** — last turn added the stdio MCP client; this adds the MCP **"streamable HTTP"** transport so catalerum reaches **remote/hosted** servers (not just spawned processes), with pluggable auth. **Refactor:** the client is now built around a transport-agnostic **`McpTransport`** trait (`request`/`notify`); the handshake, `tools/list`/`tools/call`, the `mcp:use@{server}` capability gate, and the registry bridge (`RemoteMcpTool` → §7 registry) are **shared** — both `StdioMcpClient` and the new `HttpMcpClient` implement the trait, so a remote tool is indistinguishable from a local one at dispatch. **HTTP transport (`http_client.rs`):** one JSON-RPC `POST` per request carrying `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` + `MCP-Protocol-Version`, content-negotiating the reply — a plain `application/json` body **or** a `text/event-stream` SSE body (the exact shape catalerum's own `POST /mcp` server emits). A `SseAccumulator` parses `data:` events across **arbitrary chunk boundaries** and skips interleaved server notifications; a server `Mcp-Session-Id` is captured and echoed on later requests. **Auth (`auth.rs`):** an `AuthProvider` trait yielding per-request headers, four modes — `none`; `bearer` (`Authorization: Bearer …`); `header` (arbitrary, e.g. `X-Api-Key`); and `oauth2` **machine-to-machine SSO** — `client_credentials` (a service account at an IdP/OIDC token endpoint) or `refresh_token` (an admin completed interactive SSO once; access tokens refresh headlessly). OAuth tokens are fetched on first use and **cached until 30 s before expiry**, then transparently refreshed; the refresh holds a mutex so concurrent callers don't stampede the token endpoint. (Interactive authorization-code + PKCE with a browser redirect is deliberately out of scope for a headless outbound client.) **Config (`[mcp.servers]`):** each entry gains `transport` (`stdio` default | `http`), `url`, and a `[mcp.servers.auth]` block (`kind` + that mode's fields; secrets use the redacting `Secret`, supplied via env e.g. `CATALERUM_MCP__SERVERS__0__AUTH__TOKEN`); `is_http()`/`is_configured()` validate per-transport, and the binary's `build_mcp_auth` maps config→provider at the single point a client is built. **Verified:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean (new `reqwest` + `serde_urlencoded` deps + the trait refactor); **mcp lib 11** unit tests — stdio loopback handshake→list→call against catalerum's own `McpServer`, JSON-RPC error→`Provider` mapping, descriptor/sanitizer, `jsonrpc_result`, **SSE accumulator across split chunks + EOF flush + skipping a foreign-id event**, an **end-to-end HTTP JSON round-trip that asserts the `Bearer` header reached a TCP-mock server**, an **end-to-end SSE round-trip**, static-auth headers, and oauth2 refresh-grant validation — alongside the 14 server/transport tests; **api lib 148**. **catalerum can now consume any MCP server — local stdio or hosted HTTP behind enterprise SSO — through one capability-gated registry.** **Next:** the legacy two-endpoint HTTP+SSE transport (separate `GET` stream) and server→client push (long-running tool-progress events) aren't implemented; OAuth **protected-resource-metadata discovery (RFC 9728) + dynamic client registration** would let a server advertise its IdP instead of hand-configuring `token_url`; per-server stdio calls stay serialized (HTTP is naturally concurrent)._

_2026-06-25 — **MCP read-view resources reach parity: calendar + files added, tasks N+1 removed (SOUL §26/§8/§9/§18)** — chosen by a 7-agent parallel gap survey as the highest-value self-contained chunk. SOUL §26 names notes/tasks/**calendar**/**files** as the workspace read-view resources an external MCP agent attaches as context, but `WorkspaceResourceProvider` exposed only notes + tasks — so a third-party agent over stdio (`catalerum mcp`) or `POST /mcp` could not see the user's upcoming events or indexed files. **Added two resources** (`catalerum://calendar`, `catalerum://files`): the catalogue is now a pure free fn `resource_infos()` (4 entries) that `list()` returns, and `read()` dispatches the two new URIs to `render_calendar()` / `render_files()` — each mirroring `render_notes`' degradation contract exactly (Ok-nonempty markdown · Ok-empty "_No … yet._" · Err → `warn!` + "_Unavailable._", so a provider never breaks the MCP session). Calendar lists **upcoming** events `events().list_by_workspace(ws, None, {from: now}, DEFAULT_EVENT_LIMIT=2000)` (summary · start–end RFC3339 · optional location · id); files lists `objects().list_by_workspace(ws, "", DEFAULT_OBJECT_LIMIT=1000)` (key · optional content_type · id) — both **workspace-scoped + bounded** per §18. **Fixed an N+1 in `render_tasks`** while there: it ran `tasks().list_by_column` once **per column** (1 + boards×columns queries); now one `tasks().list_by_workspace` (already ordered board → column-ordinal → task-ordinal) grouped into a `HashMap<ColumnId, Vec<Task>>` and looked up per column — **2 queries**, behaviour-preserving (per-column order kept; empty columns still render `_(empty)_`). **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean + a pure `lists_all_four_read_view_resources` (order + all 4 URIs + markdown mime) and a live-DB `renders_calendar_files_and_groups_tasks_without_n_plus_one` (seeds a board+task+empty column, an event w/ location, an object; asserts each render's content, the task grouping, the empty-column `_(empty)_`, and unknown-uri → None); full api lib **148 in parallel** (+2). A 3-lens adversarial review (correctness · safety/tenancy · consistency/tests, each finding confirmed against the code — 1 real of 5 raw) **caught a real defect**: `render_calendar` initially passed `from: None`, which with the repo's `ORDER BY starts_at ASC LIMIT` returns the **oldest** 2000 events — hiding the upcoming schedule on a busy calendar (the codebase's own `upcoming_events` passes `from: now` for this reason, and the one-event test couldn't catch it). **Fixed** to `from: Some(Utc::now())` + the test strengthened to seed a past **and** a future event and assert only the future one renders. **MCP read-views are now at §26 parity: notes · tasks · calendar · files.** **Next:** a `graph` read-view slice (§26 also names it) and a `files` excerpt/text variant; the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one user-direction item._

_2026-06-25 — **MCP client — catalerum now *calls* external MCP servers (Playwright MCP, …), the inbound half of principle 15 (SOUL §26/§19/§7)** — catalerum exposed its own tools as an MCP server but could **not call** external MCP servers, so Playwright MCP / filesystem servers / any third-party MCP tool were unreachable (the gap flagged in the feasibility review).
