_2026-06-25 — **Subagent delegation is now on by default — ephemeral workers + cheaper-model offload in every agent run (SOUL §19/§7)** — delegation was opt-in (the `delegate` tool only appeared when a profile *listed* `subagents`); now it's **default-on everywhere an agent runs** — profiles (channel/automation/delegate), chat-as-profile threads, **and the plain default chat** — because a subagent burns its **own** context window on a subtask and returns only the result, keeping the caller's context lean and (with a cheaper per-call `model`) cheaper. The `delegate` tool gained two modes: (1) a **named profile** (runs under its own grant, ⊆ the caller; an **empty `subagents` list now means *any* workspace profile** rather than "none" — the list became an optional allow-list tightening, not a gate), and (2) a zero-config **ephemeral worker** (`delegate(task, model?, tools?)` with no `profile`) — a throwaway focused agent under the **caller's own** authority (⊆ trivially), inheriting the caller's model unless the call passes a cheaper one, optionally confined to a tool subset. Both run against the **base** registry (no `delegate` tool) so delegation stays **one level deep** — no recursion, no escalation. **Refactor (`catalerum-api/profile_agent`):** `DelegateTool` split into `delegate_to_profile` + `run_ephemeral`, carrying the caller's model; a shared `registry_with_delegate(base, …, caller_model, caller_caps, allowed_subagents)` builder puts the tool on by default — used by `prepare_run` (profiles) **and** `ws.rs` (chat, both bound + plain). A standing `DELEGATE_NUDGE` is appended to the system prompt (profiles) / inserted as a system turn (chat) so the model actually offloads. Attenuation is unchanged and still the gate (`subagent_within_parent`/`attenuate`): a named subagent's grant must be ⊆ the caller, an ephemeral worker *is* the caller's authority — so default-on adds **zero** new authority, only a cheaper way to spend it. The ephemeral worker inherits the caller's **dry-run** posture. **No web change** — delegation is an autonomous agent capability; the Profiles panel already edits the `subagents` allow-list. **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api -p catalerum --all-targets -D warnings` clean (delegate redesign + the always-on chat/profile registry); api lib **146** (the pure `subagent_within_parent` attenuation test — escalation by action/domain/selector + empty-⊆ — still pins the security invariant the default-on path leans on); broader `--workspace --exclude catalerum-web` clippy clean. **Delegation is now the default tool in every loop, bounded by the same attenuation that made it safe to begin with.** **Next:** nested (multi-level) delegation stays disabled — a depth budget would open it safely; an optional `[llm].subagent_model` would let ephemeral workers default to a cheap model without the agent having to pass one each call; a per-run delegation cap could bound fan-out cost._

_2026-06-25 — **`read_conversation` agent tool — read a chat thread by id, completing search→read recall (SOUL §7/§12)** — the read half that last turn's `search_messages` was missing: a search hit hands back a `conversation_id`, but there was **no tool to pull the surrounding thread** — every other search tool pairs with a read (`search_files`→`read_object`, `search_emails`→`read_email`, `query_structured`→`read_event`), and chat was the gap. New **`read_conversation`** tool: confirms the conversation is in **this** workspace first (`conversations().get(ws, id)` — `NotFound` never leaks another tenant's chat), then returns its title + **most recent messages oldest-first** via `MessageRepo::list_recent` (`limit` 1–100, default 30 — a **bounded** thread window, mirroring how the agent loop bounds its own context), each message `{role, content, truncated, created_at}` with content capped at 2 000 chars by a new char-safe `truncate_chars(s, max)` helper (counts `char`s, never splits a UTF-8 boundary, flags clipping) so one giant pasted turn can't dominate. Gated **`conversation:read`** (deny-by-default §19; a Viewer may read — like `search_messages`). _2026-06-25 — **Profiles reach everywhere: durable `run_profile` jobs, a `RunProfile` automation action, and a chat "run as a profile" picker (SOUL §19/§11/§25/§12)** — the agent-profile entity existed but ran only fire-and-forget on a channel; this closes the three "Next" items so a profile is invocable **four ways, every one ⊆ its caller**. (1) **Durable jobs (`catalerum-ingest/profile.rs`):** a new `run_profile` job kind (`RunProfilePayload { profile, input?, reply_channel? }`) the worker runs via the §11 `ActionRunner` (`AutomationContext.runner()`); `dispatch_channel_to_profiles` enqueues one per profile *listening* on an inbound channel, so the channel→profile bridge now **survives a pod loss** instead of a spawned task lost on restart (at-least-once, same caveat as `run_automation`). Both inbound paths (the `/channels/{ch}/inbound` relay **and** the live `ChannelListener`) switched from spawn→enqueue — which simplified the listener back to **store-only** (no LLM client/registry needed; the worker holds those). (2) **`RunProfile` automation action:** `ActionKind::RunProfile` + `RunProfile { profile, input? }` (`catalerum-automation`), handled in `action_runner` — resolves the profile, runs it under **its own** grant verified **⊆ the automation's** grant (attenuation; the user turn is the action's `input`, else the firing channel message's text, else a trigger description; a channel-fired automation routes the reply back). (3) **Chat picker (the "run as a profile" UI):** a `conversations.agent_profile_id` binding (migration 0021, **same-workspace FK, `ON DELETE SET NULL` detach-on-delete**), a `set_agent_profile` repo method + `POST /conversations/{id}/profile` route; `ws.rs` now runs a bound thread *as* the profile — its model, persona prompt (+ skill runbooks), and tool allow-list — under capabilities that are the profile's grant **∩ the user's role** (`resolve_chat_profile`), so a picker can **scope a thread down** (a calendar-only chat) but **never escalate** the user (an Owner keeps all; a Member keeps the overlap). The shared `profile_agent::run_profile` was refactored to one entry point taking an optional **attenuation ceiling** + optional **reply channel**, reused by the job, the action, and (its sibling `resolve_chat_profile`) the chat path. **Web:** a `.chat-profilebar` `<select>` ("Default (your role)" + one option per profile) binds the active conversation via `set_conversation_profile`, reflecting + persisting the binding. **Verified end-to-end against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean (every backend crate); **store** agent_profiles **2** (+`conversation_profile_binding_and_detach_on_delete`: bind · persist · FK nulls the conversation on profile-delete · unbind · cross-ws NotFound); **ingest** profile **2** (job-kind token · payload round-trip + minimal shape); **automation 43**; **api lib 144**; full **web trio** — wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean, `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **172** (chat `Conversation` mirror gained `agent_profile_id`), `trunk build` ✅. **A profile is now reachable from a channel (durable), an automation, a parent agent (delegate), and the chat picker — each enforcing ⊆ its caller's authority.** **Next:** nested (multi-level) delegation stays disabled (one level) — a depth budget would open it; the chat picker doesn't enable subagent delegation in-thread (a conversational vs autonomous distinction) — could be wired; `run_profile` jobs log-and-complete on a logical failure (no retry) — a retry/dead-letter policy is a later slice; profiles remain name-keyed (typed-id refactor optional)._

_2026-06-25 — **`search_messages` agent tool — chat history is now searchable by the agent, the last unsearchable corpus (SOUL §7/§12)** — direct follow-on to last turn's `search_files`: the agent could search files (`search_files`), email (`search_emails`), structured data (`query_structured`), and the graph (`query_graph`), but had **no way to search past chat** — and since messages are **not embedded** (only docs/memories are in the vector index), `search_semantic` can't reach them either, so chat content was *entirely* unsearchable by the agent. New **`search_messages`** tool over the existing `MessageRepo::search_in_workspace` (the same literal case-insensitive `strpos` search the History panel uses): newest-match-first, `limit` 1–50 (default 10), gated **`conversation:read`** (deny-by-default §19; a Viewer may search — mirrors the read route), workspace-scoped (the SQL joins `messages → conversations` and filters `conversations.workspace_id`, so a match in another tenant never leaks). Each hit returns the conversation **title + id**, the message **role**, **when** it was sent, and a **match-centred, ellipsized snippet** — a new pure `match_snippet(content, query, max)` helper windows ~240 chars around the first (case-insensitive) hit, char-safe (counts `char`s, never splits a UTF-8 boundary → can't panic on multibyte text) so a long turn doesn't blow the agent's context. Added to the web Agent node's `KNOWN_TOOLS` "Query / search" group. **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean + a new pure `match_snippet_centres_on_the_match_and_ellipsizes` (short→whole · deep-match→centred & doubly-ellipsized & bounded · head-match→no leading `…` · multibyte→no panic) and a live-DB `search_messages_finds_chat_by_content` (a "migration" message matches case-insensitively carrying title/role/conversation_id + a match-bearing snippet · a non-said term → empty not error · blank query rejected by `required_str`); full api lib **144 in parallel** (+2); full web trio — wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean, `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **172**, `trunk build` ✅. **The agent can now search every corpus: files · email · chat · structured · graph — full parity with the UI's "search everything".** **Next:** a `read_conversation` tool (a hit gives a `conversation_id` but there's no tool to pull the full thread) would complete recall; the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one user-direction item; a settings model picker needs a live llmleaf gateway._

_2026-06-25 — **Agent profiles — durable, channel-bindable, subagent-delegating scoped agents (SOUL §19/§5/§25)** — the §19 `Agent` was a struct in the domain sketch but **never persisted, never run**; "profiles" makes it a first-class object so *separate, securely-scoped data access* is configurable, not implicit. A new `AgentProfile { model?, system_prompt?, tools[], skills[], subagents[], channels[], grant_id? }` (per workspace — the tenancy + data boundary §18) bundles a **model choice**, an allowed **tool/skill** set, the **subagents** it may delegate to, the **channels** it listens on, and the §19 **grant** that is its authority. So a "calendar bot" profile carries a grant of exactly `calendar:read@…` (+ `channel:write`) and **cannot** touch storage/email — the whole point. **Core (`catalerum-core`):** `AgentProfileId` + the `AgentProfile` model, re-exported. **Store (`catalerum-store`):** `0020_agent_profiles.sql` — JSONB name-arrays + a **same-workspace composite grant FK** (`(workspace_id, grant_id) → grants`, `ON DELETE SET NULL` so a deleted grant detaches rather than dangles, §18 defense-in-depth); `AgentProfileRow` + `AgentProfileRepo` (create / upsert-by-name / get / get_by_name / list / delete + **`list_by_channel`** — the `channels @> $1` containment lookup that drives inbound routing). **API (`catalerum-api`):** `/agent-profiles` CRUD, **admin-only** like grants (`agent_profile:read`/`write`, which no base role implies — only an Owner/Admin `*` covers it), and a profile's grant is checked **⊆ the creator's authority** at save (`attenuate`). **Subagents — the security crux:** a new `profile_agent` module runs a profile as the §7 loop under its grant's capabilities (grantless → bounded base-Member), **failing closed** if the grant carries an unenforceable constraint (`has_unenforced`, §19); when a profile lists subagents it gets a per-run **`delegate` tool** scoped to exactly those names, and on each call the subagent's effective capabilities are verified **⊆ the parent's via `attenuate`** before it runs — *rejected* otherwise — under the subagent's **own** grant. Delegation is **one level deep** (the subagent runs against the base registry, no `delegate` tool) so there is no recursion and no escalation. **Channel binding (SOUL §25):** both inbound paths — the `POST /channels/{channel}/inbound` relay route **and** the live `ChannelListener` (now threaded the LLM client + registry + default model) — call `route_channel_to_profiles`, which runs every profile listening on the channel and delivers each reply back **on that channel** via the existing `notify` path (so chat-from-messenger needs no automation). **Naming:** tools/skills/subagents/channels are **names** within the workspace (uniform with skills, automation `LlmAgent`, and channel routing — all name-keyed), not typed ids. **Verified end-to-end against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web --all-targets -D warnings` clean (core · store · api · binary · all deps); **store** lib 9 + a new live-DB `agent_profiles_repo` test (CRUD · channel-routing lookup · grant-FK detach-on-delete · cross-workspace isolation · wrong-workspace delete is a no-op); **core** 24 (incl. the existing `attenuate`/`has_unenforced` gates this leans on); **api lib 142** (+6: route body/validation + a pure `subagent_within_parent` attenuation test pinning escalation-by-action/-domain/-selector + empty-is-⊆ + `compose_system`); full **web trio** — wasm clippy `-D warnings` clean, `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **172** (+3, a new `ProfilesPanel` two-pane list/editor in the "More" nav), `trunk build` ✅. **Next:** profiles are name-keyed — a referential-integrity pass could swap to typed ids if desired; nested (multi-level) delegation is deliberately disabled (one level) — a depth budget would open it safely; web chat still runs the global default model (a "chat as profile" picker would let a user converse *as* a profile); channel→profile runs are spawned best-effort (not durable jobs like automations) — a durable `run_profile` job kind would survive a pod loss mid-reply._

_2026-06-25 — **Backup & restore — disaster recovery to S3 / WebDAV / local (`catalerum-backup`, SOUL §30)** — added the §30 section + a new `catalerum-backup` crate, closing the "no recovery story" gap. catalerum's only non-derived state is Postgres (truth, §6.1) + object blobs (§9); Neo4j/Qdrant are rebuildable (§6.3/§6.4) and Valkey ephemeral (§6.6), so a backup captures exactly those two and a restore reloads them while re-ingest rebuilds the rest. **Destination is any `StorageBackend` (§9)** — an S3/MinIO bucket, a WebDAV collection, or a local dir — so "back up to S3" is just `[backup.destination]` pointing at a *different* backend than `[storage]`; the `build_storage_backend` builder (factored out of `AppState`) is now shared by the live store and the backup target. Each run writes `<prefix>/<id>/` (id = UTC timestamp, lexically chronological): a `manifest.json` (format + schema version, per-table column-list / row-count / sha-256, object inventory) + one gzipped `COPY … TO STDOUT` per table + verbatim blob copies. The Postgres dump/restore is **pure-Rust over the sqlx COPY protocol — no `pg_dump` binary** — so it runs anywhere the binary runs and is tested against the same ephemeral Postgres the repo uses (§17). Restore is destructive + fail-safe: one transaction, FK triggers off (`session_replication_role = replica`), truncate-all then **checksum-verified** `COPY … FROM STDIN` per table (order-independent; schema must pre-exist — the binary migrates on boot); it **refuses a `schema_version` mismatch** unless `--force` and aborts on a bad checksum, rolling back so the DB is never half-loaded. Two drivers, one engine: a scheduled `BackupWorker` (a §11-style clock loop) runs backup+prune every `[backup].interval`, **single-firing each window across pods** via the bus lock (§6.2) and keeping the newest `[backup].keep`; and on-demand `catalerum backup` / `catalerum restore [id] --yes [--force]`. Config `[backup]` (§13): `enabled` (gates only the worker), `interval_secs` (24 h default, 60 s floor), `prefix`, `keep` (7), `include_objects` (true), `destination` (a full local/`s3`/`webdav` block with secrets via env, never TOML). **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean across `catalerum-backup` + `catalerum-api` + the `catalerum` binary; backup-crate lib units (identifier quoting · gzip round-trip · stable sha-256) + a DB-gated `backup_restore_round_trips_postgres_and_blobs` on an **isolated** ephemeral DB (seed a workspace + note + blob → backup → wipe the note + delete the blob → restore → both return → a second backup + `keep=1` prune leaves only the newest). **Next:** incremental / content-addressed blob dedup (today a full copy each run) + streaming compression; auto-rebuilding the derived stores on restore (today: re-ingest); a workbench Settings → Backups surface (list / run / restore over a capability-gated route); artifact-level encryption beyond the destination's SSE._

_2026-06-25 — **`search_files` agent tool — the agent can now find a file by the exact text inside it (SOUL §7/§9/§10)** — closed an agent read/search-parity gap: the Files panel gained literal file-content search a few iterations ago (`ObjectRepo::search_text_in_workspace`), but the §7 agent could only search files **semantically** (`search_semantic`, vector) — no way to match an **exact** string (an error code, an invoice/order number, a quoted phrase) that vector search blurs. New **`search_files`** tool: a thin store client over the existing `search_text_in_workspace` (literal **case-insensitive substring** via Postgres `strpos`, so a `%`/`_` is literal not a wildcard; newest-modified first; `limit` 1–50 default 10; a SQL-windowed ~160-char excerpt so the payload stays small regardless of document size), gated **`storage:read`** (deny-by-default §19, like `read_object`; a Viewer may search), workspace-scoped (only **this** tenant's ingested files can match — the store query filters `workspace_id`, and only objects with extracted text join). Each hit returns the object **id** (feed to `read_object` for the full text), key, content_type, and the match-windowed excerpt — the literal complement to `search_semantic`'s by-meaning search, exactly the distinction the Files UI already draws. _2026-06-25 — **Channels go multi-provider + bidirectional: Matrix & Slack senders + a live inbound receive loop (the multiplayer half) (SOUL §25/§11/§7)** — the §25 trait was outbound-only across two providers; now it is **four providers** and **bidirectional**, closing "chat with catalerum from your messenger" end-to-end. **New senders (`catalerum-channels`):** `SlackWebhookChannel` (a Discord-shape incoming webhook under the `text` field, 40k cap) and `MatrixChannel` (Client-Server API: `PUT …/rooms/{room}/send/m.room.message/{txn}` with a bearer token + a process-unique transaction id; room id percent-encoded in the path; 32k cap). **Inbound (the real new capability):** the `Channel` trait gained an `InMessage` type + a `subscribe() -> BoxStream<Result<InMessage>>` with a **default empty stream** — so webhook channels (Discord/Slack) stay outbound-only with no boilerplate, while the two token providers override it with real long-polls: **Matrix `/sync`** (a `futures::stream::unfold` cursor — a `timeout=0` **prime sync discards the room backlog** so only post-subscription messages yield, a bounded sync `filter`, and the bot's **own echo filtered by `user_id`** so an agent reply never re-triggers itself) and **Telegram `getUpdates`** (offset cursor, prime-discards-backlog, messages bound to the configured `chat_id`). Long-poll windows (20s) sit **under** the shared client's 30s request timeout so a quiet room doesn't trip it; added reqwest's `query` feature + tokio's `time` feature. **Multiplayer plumbing:** `TriggerEvent::ChannelMessage` gained an **optional `sender`** (additive, matcher ignores it) so a group-chat agent knows *who* spoke; the inbound HTTP relay route carries it too. **Wiring (`catalerum-api`/binary):** config grew `[channels.slack]` + `[channels.matrix.<name>]` (homeserver/access_token/room_id/user_id) + an `inbound` flag on telegram/matrix; `AppState` builds all four providers into the `notify` map **and** retains the inbound subset (`inbound_channels()`); a new **`ChannelListener`** worker spawns a re-subscribe-forever task per inbound channel, dispatching each message as a `ChannelMessage` trigger to the default workspace (the `[email]`-style static-config binding) via the same `dispatch_trigger_event` bridge the relay/webhook/Kanban sources use — and the action runner's existing `deliver_channel_reply` routes the agent's response back through the **same-named** channel, i.e. the room it came from, **closing the loop**. Matrix inbound is **refused without `user_id`** (logged) to prevent an echo loop. **Verified:** clippy `-p catalerum-channels -p catalerum-automation -p catalerum-api -p catalerum --all-targets -D warnings` clean; channels **19** (+Slack send/cap/error, +Matrix send-path/encoding/cap/error & a `/sync` subscribe test proving backlog+own-echo are skipped, +Telegram `getUpdates` subscribe binding to the right chat), automation **43**, api lib **135**. **Next:** per-message dynamic targeting (reply into an *arbitrary* room/thread, not just the configured one — needs a `ChannelTarget` on `send`); Slack/Discord true inbound needs the Events API/a gateway (the relay endpoint covers them today); Matrix E2EE rooms; per-workspace channel config beyond the default-workspace interim._

_2026-06-25 — **Linear automation `condition` is now evaluated — a core §11 gate that silently never ran (SOUL §11/§19)** — closed a real "captured but never evaluated" gap (same class as the calendar-filter fix, but higher-impact): a linear `trigger → condition → action` automation carried a top-level `condition` predicate that the executor **parsed, preserved, and then completely ignored** — so an automation with a condition ran its actions **unconditionally**. (The *graph* path already evaluates `Condition` *nodes* via the JS `CodeRunner`; only the legacy linear path dropped its condition.) **Fix — reuse the existing condition language, don't invent a second one:** a new pure `eval_condition(code, condition, trigger)` in the executor evaluates a `{ "runtime":"js", "source":"…" }` condition through the **same `CodeRunner`** a graph Condition node uses (input `{ "trigger": <event>, "inputs": {} }`, result taken as the existing `is_truthy`), and treats any other JSON as a **literal** gate (`is_truthy`: bare `true` runs, `false`/`null`/`0`/`""`/`[]`/`{}` skip). The linear loop now gates on it **before** running any action: a **falsy** condition records every action `Skipped` (the run still **Succeeds** — the gate fired cleanly) and runs **no** side effect; a condition that **can't be evaluated** (syntax/runtime/timeout, or no runtime under the Phase-A `FailCodeRunner`) **fails the run closed** — never running actions on an unchecked predicate (§19 fail-closed). `None` condition → unconditional, exactly as before; a future richer declarative predicate can layer on ahead of the literal fallback. **Production wires the real `ScriptCodeRunner` (`catalerum/src/main.rs`), so JS conditions work in prod; the worker's default `FailCodeRunner` makes a coded condition fail closed — consistent with how graph Code/Condition nodes already behave.** **Bonus (pre-existing latent bug surfaced + fixed):** running the executor's **DB-gated** integration suite against live Postgres exposed a **stale** assertion in `a_grant_outside_its_active_time_window_fails_the_run_closed` — it still expected a `cost_limit` grant to "fail closed as unenforced", but `cost_limit` was **enforced** in an earlier iteration (`Constraints::has_unenforced` excludes it). The test had self-skipped in every prior no-DB run, hiding the rot; swapped its example to `rate_limit` (still genuinely unenforced), preserving the test's intent (an in-window grant carrying an unenforced constraint must still fail closed). **Verified end-to-end against live Postgres** (podman `postgres` up): clippy `-p catalerum-automation -p catalerum-ingest -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; automation **lib 43** (+3 new pure `eval_condition` unit tests: literal-truthiness table · code-predicate result+trigger-threading · error→fail-closed) + **executor integration 10** (+1 new `linear_condition_gates_actions`: falsy-literal skips all actions & Succeeds with zero side effects · truthy-literal runs both · uncheckable code predicate fails closed with no action step; **and** the repaired grant-window test); ingest worker-path `automation_run` **3** + `automation_code_node` **3** green. **Next:** an authoring-time check could validate a coded condition's JS the way `Schedule`/`GraphQuery` triggers are validated on create; a settings model picker needs a live llmleaf gateway; the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one user-direction item._

_2026-06-25 — **Calendar-event trigger `filter` now gates which events fire — the §11 scheduler's last "interim scope" (SOUL §8/§11)** — closed a real gap in a core feature: `scan_calendar_event_triggers` carried each trigger's opaque `filter` but **never evaluated** it, so an "N-minutes-before" reminder fired on **every** event in the workspace, not just the ones the author meant. Now `filter` is a real predicate, mirroring the already-shipped `ChannelMessage {"text":…}` and `MailReceived` sender/subject/body filter conventions. **Predicate (`catalerum-automation`):** a new pure, `#[must_use]` `calendar_event_filter_matches(filter, summary, location, description) -> bool` (re-exported at crate root) — `filter` is an object with optional **string** keys `"summary"`/`"location"`/`"description"`, each a **case-insensitive substring** the matching event field must contain; all supplied keys **AND** together (so `{"summary":"standup","location":"zoom"}` fires only on a Zoom standup); absent / non-object / no-string-key → **no constraint** (every event fires — backward-compatible with the inert-field era). It **reuses the module's existing `contains_ci`**, so a filter naming an absent optional field (location/description) correctly never matches. Evaluated in the *scheduler* (not `Trigger::matches`) because a calendar trigger fires on a clock, not an ad-hoc event. **Wiring (`catalerum-ingest`):** `first_calendar_lead` → `first_calendar_trigger` now returns `(lead, filter)`; the per-event loop gates on the predicate **before** claiming the single-fire lock (so a non-matching event never consumes a claim); the stale "not yet evaluated / every event fires" doc comment is corrected. **Verified end-to-end against live Postgres** (brought up the podman `postgres` service — the stack was down): clippy `-p catalerum-automation -p catalerum-ingest --all-targets -D warnings` clean; automation lib **40** (+1 `calendar_event_filter_matches_summary_location_description`: no-filter · summary-CI · location-on-absent-field · description · AND-of-keys · non-string-value-lenient); ingest `schedule_scan` **7** incl. a **new** `calendar_event_filter_gates_which_events_fire` (two due events in one window — only the summary-matching one fires, and the recorded trigger references it) plus the existing single-fire test through a `seed_event` now parametrized by summary. **Next:** the filter is summary/location/description substring only — attendee / calendar-name predicates or a general expression language remain a later §11 slice; a settings model picker needs a live llmleaf gateway; the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one user-direction item._

Remaining autonomous work is polish; a steer would unlock more._

_2026-06-23 — **Audit: `catalerum-bus` distributed lock confirmed correct — no change (SOUL §6.2/§11)** — the last core crate not yet examined this run. `DistLock` is a **textbook** single-instance lock: acquire = `SET key token NX PX <ttl>` (atomic, random fencing token, TTL); release = a **CAS Lua script** (`GET == token` then `DEL`, so a holder can never release another's lock — the classic footgun, avoided); refresh = `GET == token` then `PEXPIRE`. The scheduler's "claim the occurrence, let the TTL expire" usage is correct for per-occurrence single-fire (a different occurrence-instant → a different key), which is exactly why the `concurrent_scans_single_fire` tests pass. No bug. **No code change.** **Coverage note:** every core crate has now been examined this run (api/ingest/automation/fetch/email/calendar/storage/iam/vector/graph/mcp/web/bus) — all either fixed or confirmed sound. The remaining items are a **user-direction** design decision (graph-query structural scope) or a feature addition (MCP SSE streaming, §29), not autonomous refinement. **Next:** await user direction; the loop is at confirmation-only._

_2026-06-23 — **Audit: CalDAV XML parsing + vector-search tenancy both confirmed safe — no change (SOUL §6.4/§8/§18)** — two more security-relevant surfaces audited, both sound by design. **CalDAV/webcal XML** (`multistatus.rs`, untrusted response): built on **`quick-xml`** — a *streaming pull-parser* (no DOM → deeply-nested XML can't stack-overflow) that does **not** expand custom DTD entities (`unescape` handles only the 5 predefined + numeric refs, and falls back to literal text on an unknown entity), so the **billion-laughs / entity-expansion** bomb doesn't apply; combined with the 64 MiB response cap from the prior iteration, input and output are bounded. (Minor, not worth fixing: a 64 MiB stream of unclosed tags grows the path-tracking `Vec` to ~hundreds of MB — bounded by the cap, pathological, survivable.) **Vector search tenancy** (`catalerum-vector`): cross-workspace leak is structurally impossible — it's **collection-per-workspace** (`catalerum_ws_{uuid}`, so every op hits only that tenant's collection) **and** `search` applies the `workspace_id` payload filter (`SearchFilter::to_qdrant` *requires* a `workspace_id` and always emits it as the first `must`), and `search`'s signature requires `workspace_id` — there is no filter-less search path. Defence-in-depth, sound. **No code change.** **Security sweep now comprehensive:** untrusted parsers (HTML/email/calendar/XML), bounded reads (CalDAV/JMAP/Gmail), SSRF (fetch: redirects/NAT64/rebind), auth (session expiry ×2, capability matching), authz tenancy (vector collections + payload filter), webhooks/channels — all fixed or confirmed safe. **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee is the one substantive item remaining, and it's a **user-direction** call (Cypher-parser dependency vs. typed-only queries vs. the documented heuristic) — autonomous work is now genuinely marginal; a steer or a loop pause is the higher-value move._

Gmail buffered every HTTP response via `reqwest::Response::json()` (no size limit) at **four** sites (token exchange, `messages.get`, `history.list`, the `get_json` helper) — same OOM class as the CalDAV `.text()` and JMAP `.json()` bounds, just on the most-trusted provider (so lowest severity, but it completes the principle). With this, **every** external HTTP response read in the email + calendar providers is bounded (CalDAV body, JMAP, Gmail), so a compromised/buggy upstream can't OOM the sync worker on any of them. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-email --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-email` **34**; `cargo test -p catalerum-ingest --test email_sync` **6** against live Postgres. **Sweep is now complete** (HTML/email crash fixes · calendar+JMAP+Gmail+CalDAV reads bounded · webhooks/channels secure). **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one substantive user-direction item; the untrusted-input thread is exhausted, so further autonomous work is genuinely marginal — a steer or a loop pause would be higher-value._

_2026-06-23 — **Webhooks/channels audited secure; JMAP response read bounded (the email-provider parallel to the CalDAV fix) (SOUL §11/§25/§28/§19)** — finishing the untrusted-input sweep. **Audited, secure (no change):** the **webhook** trigger endpoint (`routes/webhooks.rs`) is **authenticated** (`auth: Auth`), enforces `Write/automation` (deny-by-default, Viewer→403), and scopes dispatch to the principal's own workspace — so it is *not* an open "anyone fires your automations" hole (the unauthenticated public-webhook-with-secret shape is a documented future feature, and the body is bounded by axum's 2 MiB default + serde's recursion-limited JSON). **Channels** are **outbound-only** (Discord/Telegram delivery via webhooks; no inbound bot receiver), so no untrusted inbound-message parsing exists. **One real gap fixed (same class as the CalDAV `.text()` bound):** the **JMAP** provider read HTTP responses via `reqwest::Response::json()` (`jmap.rs` session + request), which buffers the *entire* body before decoding — a compromised/buggy 3rd-party/self-hosted JMAP server could OOM the sync worker. Added `read_value_capped` (streams via `Response::chunk()`, caps at `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 64 MiB`, errors on exceed — truncated JSON wouldn't decode) and routed both sites through it. **Noted, deliberately not done (severity tiering):** **Gmail** uses the same unbounded `.json()` (`get_json` + `get_message`) — but Google's API is the most-trusted of these providers and `get_message` was just touched last iteration, so bounding it is a trivial, low-priority follow-up rather than re-churning that path now. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-email --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-email` **34** green. **Sweep summary:** untrusted-input paths now covered — HTML (crash fixed), email MIME (crash fixed), calendar ICS (RRULE-expansion absent + read bounded), JMAP (read bounded), webhooks/channels (secure). **Next:** Gmail `.json()` bound (trivial); the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one substantive user-direction item; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **Calendar untrusted-input audit: RRULE-expansion DoS absent (good); CalDAV response read now bounded (SOUL §8/§19)** — continuing the untrusted-parser sweep (HTML → email → now calendar `.ics`). **Audited, sound:** the classic ICS DoS — **RRULE expansion** (a malicious `FREQ=SECONDLY`/huge-`COUNT` recurrence exploding into astronomically many occurrences) — **does not exist here**: there's no `rrule` crate dependency anywhere, RRULE is stored as an **opaque string** and never expanded into occurrences; `parse_calendar` iterates `components` **flatly** (no deep recursion), so no stack-overflow vector either. **One real gap fixed:** CalDAV/webcal sync read response bodies via `reqwest::Response::text()` (`caldav.rs` GET + REPORT), which buffers the **entire** body with no limit — and a subscribed webcal feed is an untrusted external server (and even a configured CalDAV host can be compromised/buggy), so a huge/malicious response OOMs the sync worker. The fetch tool already bounds its body (`read_capped`); CalDAV didn't. Added `read_body_capped` (streams via `reqwest::Response::chunk()` — **no new dependency**; caps at `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 64 MiB`, generous for years of events, and **errors** on exceed since a truncated iCalendar/XML wouldn't parse) and routed both `.text()` sites through it. **Honest scope/severity:** lower than the email/markdown crashes (an OOM, not an abort, and it needs a malicious/buggy server rather than a trivially-injected page/email) but a genuine instance of the unbounded-buffering-on-untrusted-input class the codebase bounds everywhere else. The **local `.ics` file** read (`local.rs` `tokio::fs::read`) is also unbounded but operator-controlled (self-inflicted) — left as low-value. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-calendar --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-calendar` **28** green. **Next:** webhook payloads are the remaining untrusted-input surface worth a look; the structural graph-query scope guarantee is still the one substantive user-direction item; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **Multipart-bomb email → stack-overflow crash-loop, fixed; + Gmail poison-message resilience (SOUL §28/§19)** — same DoS class as the markdown fix, on the **email** untrusted-input path (anyone can send you a message). `mailparse::parse_mail` parses MIME multipart **recursively with no depth limit** (verified in mailparse-0.16.1 source: `parse_mail_recursive` `push`es each subpart via a bare recursive call, lib.rs:994). A deeply-nested `multipart/mixed` email (~500 KB gets you ~10k levels) overflows the stack **inside the parse** → process abort → a **poison message that crash-loops the sync worker on every retry**. I can't patch mailparse, so `parse_email` now **pre-filters**: `count_multipart_markers(raw)` (ASCII-case-insensitive count of `multipart/` — a sound *upper bound* on nesting depth, since each container declares exactly one; over-counts harmlessly from body text, never under-counts) must be ≤ `MAX_MULTIPART_PARTS = 256` or the message is refused before `parse_mail` runs. 256-deep parses comfortably within the worker stack; real mail is a handful of levels. This also bounds the recursive `collect_parts` walk (tree depth ≤ the cap). **Second fix (poison-message resilience):** IMAP already `match`ed `parse_email` and skipped a bad message (warn + continue), but **Gmail's** `get_message` used `?` (gmail.rs:230/305 loops propagate) — so a single un-parseable/bomb message failed the *whole* batch and blocked sync. Moved the skip into `get_message`: a **message-specific** failure (undecodable payload / unparseable / bomb) now logs + returns `Ok((None, hist))` (skip, advance cursor — mirroring IMAP), while **network/HTTP** errors above it still propagate via `?` so a transient blip retries the batch intact (no silent message loss). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-email --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-email` **34** (new: bomb rejected with Err not abort + a normal 3-level multipart still parses + `count_multipart_markers` correctness); `cargo test -p catalerum-ingest --test email_sync` **6** against live Postgres. **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee (user direction); else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **HTML→Markdown stack-overflow on deeply-nested fetched pages — a real DoS, fixed (SOUL §27/§19)** — a genuine availability bug in the untrusted-content path, **confirmed empirically**. `markdown.rs`'s converter walks the parsed DOM recursively (`blocks`→`emit_block`→`blocks` for transparent containers like `<div>`; `list`→`list`; `inline`→`inline_element`→`inline`; `blockquote` even allocates a sub-`Converter` per level), but the `depth` param it threaded only tracked **list indentation** — generic nesting recursed **unbounded**. Untrusted fetched HTML (a malicious page, or a redirect target) nested deep (`<div>`×N) overflows the thread stack → **SIGABRT → worker abort**. Proven: a 60 000-deep document aborted the test process (signal 6) before the fix. **Fix:** a `rec_depth: Cell<usize>` on the `Converter` (`Cell` so the `&self` inline walk updates it too), capped at `MAX_NESTING = 256` via `enter()`/`leave()` guards on the three recursion heads (`blocks`, `list`, `inline`); `blockquote`'s sub-converter **inherits** the depth so nested quotes stay bounded across the converter boundary. Past the cap we stop descending — adversarial nesting is truncated, never crashed; real pages are nowhere near 256 deep, so all 21 formatting tests are unchanged. New regression test (4 000-deep `<div>` chain + 4 000-deep `<b>` inline chain) returns cleanly; kept modest because html5ever's *own* deep-tree parse is near-O(n²) (the guard caps our walk, not the parse — and the `FetchPolicy` 5 MB body cap bounds what reaches here; a 60k test took 132 s just to parse). **Residual (lesser, noted):** html5ever's near-O(n²) parse of pathologically-deep input is a CPU cost (not a crash), bounded by the 5 MB read cap — separate concern, not addressed here. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-fetch` (42 unit + 6 integration) green in <1 s. **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee (user direction); else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **iam audit (sound) + regression tests for the authorization glob matcher (SOUL §18/§19)** — audited the auth/authz core (the user flagged `iam` as an area). **Sound:** session + login-token **expiry is enforced twice** — the service rejects on `Session::is_expired()` *and* the Postgres store filters expired rows in SQL (`get_by_token_hash`), so a stale bearer can't authenticate via either path; the **capability matcher** is correct deny-by-default (role→base-caps with delete/exec/MCP never role-implied; `Action::Any`/`Resource::"*"` wildcards; selector globs). **Change (test-only, zero behaviour change):** the `glob_covers` authorization matcher gates *every* capability check but only had happy-path tests — added `glob_edge_cases` locking the contract against silent future drift: trailing-`*` spans multiple segments; a non-trailing `*` can't match off the end; a held selector longer/more-specific than the request never covers it; a literal covers only itself. **Surfaced one loose edge** (now explicitly tested + documented): a trailing-`*` subtree grant (`reports/*`) also covers the bare *prefix* object (`reports`), not just its children — deny-by-default's one soft spot. Left as-is (tightening to require `i < val.len()` on the trailing-`*` arm would deny legitimate parent-object access — a semantics call, not a clear bug), but it's now a tested, visible decision rather than an accident. **Verified:** `cargo test -p catalerum-core capability` green (incl. new `glob_edge_cases`); `cargo clippy -p catalerum-core --all-targets -D warnings` clean. **Trend continues:** audited paths (LLM, fetch, now iam) keep coming up sound; remaining substantive work needs user direction. **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee, and now *optionally* the `reports/*`-covers-`reports` glob tightening — both user-direction calls; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **Audit-only: LLM hot path + fetch backends confirmed robust — no change warranted (SOUL §7/§27)** — the first iteration to surface **no** fix; recording what was verified so it isn't re-trodden. **LLM streaming** (`catalerum-llm` `into_event_stream`): the SDK chunk stream is unfolded with a **guaranteed terminal `Done`** and a mid-stream SDK error is surfaced as a `StreamEvent::Error` then cleanly ends — no way to hang or drop silently. **Agent loop** (`agent.rs` `run_agent`): bounded by `AgentConfig::max_iterations` (default **16**) with a `hit_iteration_cap` flag (the "tool-use limit" the chat UI shows) — no unbounded tool-call loop. **Fetch backends:** all three (`http` / `firecrawl` / `browser`) apply `validate` + `guard_resolved` before connecting — the SSRF guard is uniform, not just on the HTTP path. **Considered and rejected as not-worth-it:** wiring `max_iterations` to config — marginal (16 is a sane default) *and* invasive (the `ActionRunner` holds no config, so the automation call site would need constructor threading; wiring only the chat site would leave the two inconsistent). No code change. **Trend:** audited paths are now coming up solid; the substantive remaining work (the structural graph-query scope guarantee) needs user direction — the loop is at the marginal-hardening stage. **Next:** graph-query scope (user direction); else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **DNS-rebind TOCTOU closed — connect-time SSRF screening via a custom resolver (SOUL §19/§13)** — closing the one security residual I'd deferred three times as "API-uncertain / attended-only". Resolved the uncertainty by **reading the reqwest-0.13.4 source** in the cargo cache: `reqwest::dns::{Resolve, Name, Addrs, Resolving}` are public and `ClientBuilder::dns_resolver` accepts any `Resolve`. **The gap:** `guard_resolved` resolves a host's IPs and checks them **pre-flight** (T1), but reqwest re-resolves DNS itself when it **connects** (T2) — a name that rebinds in the T1→T2 window could still land on a private/loopback/metadata IP. The earlier manual-redirect fix brought *hops* to parity with the initial request but didn't close this *connect-time* window. **Fix:** a `GuardedResolver` (impl `reqwest::dns::Resolve`) wired via `.dns_resolver(...)` resolves via `tokio::net::lookup_host` (port 0 — reqwest overrides it) and screens every resolved address through a new pure `policy::first_blocked_addr` (refuse the host if **any** resolved addr is blocked — matching `guard_resolved`'s multi-record/rebind stance; honours the `allow_private_hosts` opt-in). reqwest now connects **only** to addresses the guard vetted — the resolution reqwest uses *is* the screened one, so there's no T1/T2 gap. It's invoked only for **domain** names (IP literals skip DNS) — exactly the rebind case. Kept `guard_resolved` (clean pre-connect `Unauthorized` error + defence-in-depth) and `validate` (scheme / literal / local-name); the resolver is the connect-time backstop, so a common-case fetch does two lookups — intentional, DNS is cached. **Tests:** pure `first_blocked_addr` units (all-public ok; any-blocked-among-results refuses; loopback/private/NAT64-metadata blocked; `allow_private` bypass; empty ok) + an integration test fetching via the **`localhost` domain** (so the resolver's `resolve()` path runs end-to-end, which the IP-literal tests never exercised). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-fetch` (41 unit + 6 integration) green; `cargo build -p catalerum-api` succeeds (downstream unaffected). **Honest scope:** this hardens the **HTTP backend**; the **browser/CDP** backend fetches inside headless Chrome (not via reqwest), so it keeps the pre-flight `guard_resolved` model — its own connect-time DNS isn't screened by this resolver (separate, pre-existing, noted). **Next:** with rebind closed, the fetch SSRF guard is now comprehensive (scheme · literal/name · embedded-v4 incl. NAT64 · redirect hops · connect-time screening). The **structural graph-query scope guarantee** is the one substantive item remaining for user direction; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **SSRF guard now blocks NAT64-embedded IPv4 — a novel embedded-v4 bypass (SOUL §19/§13)** — a real, focused gap in the v6 SSRF check. `v6_is_blocked` re-checked embedded IPv4 only via `Ipv6Addr::to_ipv4()`, which decodes the IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and deprecated IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms — but **not** the **NAT64 well-known prefix `64:ff9b::/96`** (RFC 6052). On a NAT64 network, `http://[64:ff9b::169.254.169.254]/` translates at the network layer to a connection to the **IPv4 cloud-metadata endpoint**; the literal is a "plain" public-looking v6 that fell through every prefix check → **allowed**. Same class as the `::ffff:`/`::` embedded-v4 cases the guard already handled, just a prefix `to_ipv4` doesn't decode. Fix: a `nat64_embedded_v4` helper extracts the trailing 32 bits when the upper 96 match `64:ff9b::/96`, fed through the **same** `v4_is_blocked` rules (`ip.to_ipv4().or_else(|| nat64_embedded_v4(ip))`). A NAT64 address embedding a **public** v4 stays allowed (`64:ff9b::8.8.8.8` → ok) — only blocked-v4 targets are refused, so legitimate NAT64 egress is unaffected. Extended `blocks_ipv6_local` with the metadata/loopback/private NAT64 cases + the public-v4 negative. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-fetch` green (40 unit + 5 integration). (This iteration also confirmed by audit that storage path-traversal, MCP route-layer auth, and the `DefaultBodyLimit` upload cap are all sound — no change needed there.) **Next:** the **DNS-rebinding TOCTOU** (custom reqwest `Resolve` — careful/attended) and the **structural graph-query scope guarantee** (user direction) remain the two real items; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **Security-audit pass on the external-facing surfaces + tidy-up of the now-dead redirect helper (SOUL §9/§26/§19)** — a smaller, mostly-confirmation iteration following the SSRF fix. **Audited (all sound):** the **storage backends** for path traversal — local `resolve` rejects absolute / `.` / `..` components (tested), WebDAV `validate_key` rejects `.`/`..` segments and `path_segments_mut().push()` percent-encodes each segment (so a `..` can't reach the server as a literal), and S3 is a flat keyspace (no FS traversal); configured storage **endpoints are operator-set, not agent-supplied**, so no SSRF exposure there. The **MCP server** enforces auth at the `POST /mcp` route layer (the server runs against a fixed scoped `ToolContext`, §19/§26) — the same scoped tool surface as the main API. **Object uploads are bounded** — `DefaultBodyLimit::max(storage.max_object_bytes())` (default 64 MiB) is layered onto the storage routes, so axum returns `413` before buffering an unbounded body. **The one change:** removed `catalerum-fetch`'s now-dead `host_blocked_sync` — after the prior iteration switched to manual, async-vetted redirect following it had **zero callers**, and its doc ("synchronous host check for redirect hops, where DNS resolution can't run") described a mechanism that no longer exists; leaving it would mislead. Pure dead-code removal (it was `pub` in a `pub mod` so it didn't trip `-D warnings`, but it's gone now). **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-fetch` green (40 unit + 5 integration). **Next:** two real items remain — the **DNS-rebinding TOCTOU** in the fetch guard (a custom reqwest `Resolve` that filters blocked IPs at connect-time would close it, but the reqwest-0.13 resolver API + end-to-end rebind testing make it a careful, not-unattended change — deferred, documented) and the **structural graph-query scope guarantee** (held for user direction); else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **SSRF guard now vets redirect hops with DNS resolution — closing a real bypass (SOUL §19/§27/§13)** — a genuine security gap in the fetch tool. The SSRF guard checked the **initial** URL with async DNS re-resolution (`guard_resolved` rejects a public name that points at a private/loopback/metadata IP), but **redirects** were followed by reqwest's built-in redirect policy, whose hook is **synchronous and can't resolve DNS** — so per-hop it only ran `host_blocked_sync` (IP-literal + local-name checks, no resolution). A redirect to a public domain resolving to `10.x` / `127.x` / `169.254.169.254` therefore **passed** the hop check and reqwest connected to it → real SSRF (internal-service read / cloud-metadata theft), reachable via prompt-injection on a fetched page that 302s to an internal target. The initial URL got the full guard; redirects got a weaker one. **Fix:** disabled reqwest auto-redirect (`redirect::Policy::none()`) and follow manually in `fetch`, so **every hop runs the same guard as the initial request** via a new `vet_redirect`: `Url::join` (absolute / relative / protocol-relative `//host` Locations) → `validate` (scheme + literal/name) → `guard_resolved` (async DNS re-resolution). Hop cap `MAX_REDIRECTS = 10` (matches the prior reqwest cap) → a clean `too many redirects` error on a loop. Manual GET-following is correct for this **read-only, no-auth, no-cookie** fetcher (none of reqwest's method-downgrade / header-stripping concerns apply). The synchronous `redirect_policy`/`SsrfRedirect` are removed; `host_blocked_sync` is now unused internally but kept (it's `pub` API — a future cleanup could drop it). **Honest residual:** a DNS-rebinding **TOCTOU** between `guard_resolved` and reqwest's own connect-time resolution still exists — the codebase's existing model is resolve-and-check, not pin-the-resolved-IP; this fix brings redirects to **parity** with the initial request, it does **not** close that deeper TOCTOU (which needs a pinned-IP custom connector — a larger change, noted as future hardening). **Tests:** 2 offline `vet_redirect` unit tests (relative + protocol-relative join resolve correctly; private/loopback/`169.254.169.254`/local-name/`file://` all refused) + 2 integration tests on the canned-server harness (follows a vetted 302 chain to the final 200 with the right final url; caps an infinite redirect loop). Existing fetch tests still green. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-fetch --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-fetch` full suite green (**40** unit + **5** integration). **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one item for user direction; the SSRF DNS-rebind TOCTOU (pinned-IP connector) is a noted future hardening; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **Large `graph_query` poll result now warns + a full live-infra verification pass (SOUL §11/§18)** — first iteration with **all backends up** (Postgres/Neo4j/Valkey/Qdrant/rustfs), so I could verify DB-backed paths the recent rounds had to defer. **Verification:** ran the full `catalerum-store` + `catalerum-ingest` suites against live Postgres/Neo4j/Valkey — **all green** (store repos, `worker_queue` 5, `schedule_scan` 6, sync/ingest), **including** the `automations_repo` test that an old memory note called "pre-existing failing": it **passes** (the note was stale — the migration just wasn't applied when it was recorded; memory corrected). Also re-confirmed two recent "deferred" candidates are sound-by-design at this app's human scale, not bugs: the scheduler's `for workspace { for automation }` scans are unbounded **intentionally** (the scheduler must see *every* enabled automation each tick or it silently drops triggers — a cap is wrong and pagination adds correctness risk to a correctness-critical path for a non-problem at human scale; same call the events-reconciliation path made with `i64::MAX`), and the web REST/delete client is correct (`delete_resource` treats `204` as success without decoding; every helper checks `(200..300)` + surfaces the server error). **The one real change:** `scan_graph_queries` runs operator Cypher and uses only `is_empty()`/`len()`, but the graph transport **materializes every row the server sends** (no clean post-hoc bound — only a Cypher `LIMIT` helps, which can't be appended to arbitrary user Cypher safely), so a broad/unscoped query silently buffered a huge result into memory **every poll** with no signal — both a memory cost and a §18 scoping smell. Added `GRAPH_QUERY_ROWS_WARN = 10_000` + a `warn!` (rows + automation id, advising a `LIMIT`/tighter scope) when a poll result is that large — **no truncation** (the existence check is unchanged), surfacing it so it can't grow silently. Same "no silent X" pattern as the Gmail snapshot warn. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-ingest --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `schedule_scan` **6** green (incl. the graph-query single-fire test); full store+ingest suites green against live infra. **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee (parser / typed-only) remains the one item for user direction; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **Mid-turn socket drop now surfaced + a dead socket no longer reused (SOUL §12/§7)** — a real silent-failure on the core chat path. The WS chat inbound pump (`chat.rs` `run_turn` send handler) matched `None` from `sock.next_update()` — the socket **closing without a `Done`/`Error` frame** (server restart, network drop, proxy idle-timeout mid-turn) — with a bare `break`. Unlike the `Error` arm right beside it, that arm never called `mark_error` and never appended anything, so a dropped connection left the assistant bubble **blank** (if no text had arrived) or **silently truncated** (if it dropped mid-stream) with zero indication the turn failed — the user reads a blank/short reply as the answer. Compounding it, the post-loop code then stored that **dead** socket back into the `RefCell` for reuse, so the *next* turn wasted its first `send` on the closed socket (failing inline) before reconnecting. Fix: the `None` arm now mirrors the `Error` arm — `mark_error` when no text yet, then append a bracketed `[connection closed before the response finished]` note (so a *partial* reply is flagged too) — and sets a new `socket_alive = false`; the socket is restored to the `RefCell` **only when still alive**, so a closed one is dropped and the next send reconnects cleanly. The happy path (`Done`) and the server-sent `Error` frame (socket stays open → still reused) are byte-for-byte unchanged. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-web` **157**; `trunk build` succeeds. **Honest scope:** found after a hot-path audit (Explore agent over ws/sync/scheduler/automation/repo) whose backend candidates this round were all either not real (a `graph_due` "overflow" that can't occur — `n*span ≤ now.timestamp()`), or real-but-not-cleanly-verifiable-without-live-Neo4j/Postgres: the **unbounded scheduler scans** (`schedule.rs` iterates every workspace × every automation per tick — a cap would silently drop triggers, so it needs keyset *pagination*, not truncation) and the **graph-query result buffering** (`scan_graph_queries` buffers all rows just to check `is_empty()`/`len()` — only boundable by a Cypher `LIMIT`, which is fragile to append blind). Both logged here as deferred §18/§11 robustness items. **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one item for user direction; those two scheduler/graph robustness items are the next concrete (live-DB-verified) candidates; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **`run()` stdin deadlock fixed + the pending output-capture change verified (SOUL §20)** — two things this iteration, both in `catalerum-exec` `LocalExecutor::run`. **(1) Cleared the prior ⚠️:** ran `cargo clippy -p catalerum-exec --all-targets -D warnings` (clean) + `cargo test -p catalerum-exec` (**7** green, incl. the output-cap + timeout-kill tests) — the bounded-output-capture change below is now *verified*, not inspection-only; the `async move` capture/borrow held as reasoned. **(2) Found & fixed a distinct latent deadlock in the same `run()`:** stdin was written to completion (`write_all(...).await`) **before** stdout/stderr were drained, so a command that echoes large input (`cat` with >64 KiB stdin) fills *both* OS pipe buffers (~64 KiB each) — the child blocks writing stdout → stops reading stdin → our write blocks **forever**. Worse, that write sat **outside** the `tokio::time::timeout`, so the wall-clock cap couldn't reap it: a permanent worker hang, strictly worse than the OOM the cap addressed. The existing 11-byte stdin test never tripped it (well under the pipe buffer). Fix: feed stdin **concurrently** with the capped reads inside the timed `collect` block — take all three pipes up front (so the block borrows only `child` for `wait`), then `tokio::join!(child.wait(), feed_stdin, read_capped(stdout), read_capped(stderr))`; on a timeout the whole future drops → `kill_on_drop` reaps the child and the half-written stdin pipe. EOF semantics unchanged (stdin still closed on scope exit whether or not input was supplied). New regression test `large_stdin_and_stdout_do_not_deadlock` (256 KiB `cat` echo round-trips verbatim under the 1 MiB cap, not timed out) — this *hangs forever* on the old ordering, passes now. **Verified:** clippy `-D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-exec` **8** green (1 new). **Next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one item for user direction; else marginal._

_2026-06-23 — **Bounded LocalExecutor output capture — unbounded buffering could OOM the worker (SOUL §20)** ✅ VERIFIED (clippy + tests run clean the next iteration, see entry above) — the `catalerum-exec` `LocalExecutor::run` used `child.wait_with_output()`, which buffers the child's **entire** stdout/stderr into memory. A runaway command (`yes`, `cat` of a huge file, a loop printing) emits gigabytes well inside the 30 s timeout → worker OOM; the allow-list limits *which* programs run but not their output volume. Unlike the Boa JS sandbox's single-allocation gap (no heap-limit API → not cleanly fixable), this one is clean: replaced `wait_with_output` with a concurrent `tokio::join!(child.wait(), read_capped(stdout), read_capped(stderr))` inside an `async move` (so a timeout still drops+kills the child via `kill_on_drop`). `read_capped` keeps at most `max_capture_bytes` per stream and **drains the rest** (so the child never blocks on a full pipe and still completes/times-out normally); `finish_capture` appends an `[output truncated at N bytes]` marker so a partial capture isn't mistaken for complete. New `DEFAULT_MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES = 1 MiB` + a `with_max_capture_bytes` builder (manual `Default` since the struct gained a non-zero-default field) + 2 tests (1000-byte output capped to 16 with marker; short output verbatim). Audited alongside: the Boa JS sandbox (loop/recursion/stack/wall-clock bounds — solid; only the heap-allocation edge is unfixable without OS rlimits), the auth/token path (hashed at rest, CSPRNG, atomic single-use — sound), and the Memory web panel (full CRUD + profile — complete). **✅ Resolved next iteration:** both commands ran clean (clippy `-D warnings`; `cargo test -p catalerum-exec` green) — the `async move` capture/borrow held as reasoned, and a *further* latent deadlock in the same function was found and fixed (see the entry above). **Then-next:** the structural graph-query scope guarantee remains the one item for user direction._

`validate_graph_query_cypher` forbade write/`CALL`/`LOAD`/`USE` but **not `UNION`**. A query
`MATCH (n {workspace_id:$workspace_id}) RETURN n UNION MATCH (m) RETURN m` passes the `$workspace_id` substring check on its **first** arm
while the **second arm is entirely unscoped** — reading every tenant's nodes, no tautology required. This hits **both** surfaces that share

`CALL`/`USE`, so this is a strict extension of the existing heuristic, **not** the deferred parser/typed-only design decision. The honest
`OR 1=1` limitation remains (needs a real parser); blocking `UNION` just removes the no-tautology variant. Doc updated on both the validator
and (transitively) the route; 2 new test cases (`UNION` / `UNION ALL` rejected). Confirmed no legitimate `UNION` exists anywhere in the tree.
**Verified:** workspace clippy (excl. web) `-D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-automation` **38+9**; api lib **132** (graph route +

_2026-06-23 — **IMAP first-sync body-fetch cap — unbounded memory on a large folder (SOUL §28/§3.4)** —
the IMAP provider's cheap `UID FETCH … (FLAGS)` pass covers the whole folder (fine — just flags), but the **body** fetch of the changed set
was uncapped: a first sync of a 50k-message folder pulled *every* body into memory at once (`has_more: false`, no continuation). JMAP caps
its snapshot (`SNAPSHOT_CAP`); IMAP had no equivalent. Added `BODY_FETCH_CAP = 500` and extracted the delta into a **pure, unit-tested**
`compute_delta(prior_flags, current_sig, cap)`: it fetches the newest `cap` changed uids per tick and **defers** the older remainder to later
poller ticks (the poller re-runs `sync` on a cadence; `has_more` is set but the worker converges via the cursor regardless). The subtle part is
the cursor: a deferred uid must never get its *current* sig written (that would mark its un-fetched body as synced and it would never fetch) —
so a deferred-but-previously-tracked uid keeps its **prior** sig (a later deletion stays detectable, a flag change still re-fetches) and a
brand-new deferred uid is **omitted** (re-read as new next tick). Crucially the empty string is a *legitimate* flag-sig (a message with no
mapped flags), so omission — not a sentinel value — is what marks "not yet synced", or a no-flag new mail could be silently skipped. Deletions
stay computed over the whole folder (FLAGS pass uncapped), so the cap **never** causes a false deletion — strictly cleaner than JMAP's
snapshot-cap. 7 new tests cover first-sync, skip-unchanged, flag-change re-fetch, deletions, cap-defers-and-omits-new (incl. the `""`-sig
case), deferred-tracked-keeps-prior-sig, and **convergence across ticks** (tight cap drains every uid, then a stable no-op). **Verified:**
workspace clippy (excl. web) `-D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-email` **32** green (7 new). **Next:** the held graph-query scope
decision; the deferred now-centric agenda window; else marginal items._

_2026-06-23 — **Channel message length caps — long notifications were silently lost (SOUL §25/§11/§7)** —
a genuine outbound bug: both channel senders passed the agent's message straight through — Discord `{ "content": msg.text }` (hard limit
**2000**), Telegram `{ "text": msg.text }` (hard limit **4096**). A messenger API rejects an over-long message with a `400`, so any agent
notification past the cap (a summary/digest easily exceeds 2000) was **dropped whole** — the `Notify` action / `notify` tool would log a send
failure and the user got nothing. Added `truncate_message(text, max_chars)` in `catalerum-channels` (returns `Cow` — no alloc when it fits;
cuts on a **char boundary** so UTF-8 stays valid; appends a ` […]` marker and the result still fits the cap), applied in both senders with
per-platform consts (`DISCORD_MAX_CONTENT = 2000`, `TELEGRAM_MAX_TEXT = 4096`). Now at least the head of a long message is delivered, marked
truncated, instead of lost. Cap is measured in `char`s — exact for Discord (code points) and for all-BMP text on Telegram (UTF-16 units;
realistic notifications are far under either limit, noted honestly in the doc). Added the crate's first `lib.rs` test module (pass-through /
exact-limit / over-limit-marker-fits / multibyte-boundary) + a Discord wiremock test proving a 3000-char send arrives capped at 2000 ending
in the marker. **Verified:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p catalerum-channels` **9**
green. **Next:** the held graph-query scope decision; the deferred now-centric agenda window; else marginal items._

the core is well-engineered. The one fix: `GET /storage/objects` (the **raw blob-backend** view, distinct from the now-bounded Postgres
catalogue) `.collect()`-ed the entire backend stream into memory unbounded — added `.take(DEFAULT_OBJECT_LIMIT)` after the `filter_map`, so a

_2026-06-23 — **Bounded `/storage/catalogue` — the second unbounded list, fixed better (SOUL §9/§18)** —
sibling gap to the `/events` fix: `GET /storage/catalogue` pulled **every** catalogued object in the workspace (`ObjectRepo::list_by_workspace`,
no `LIMIT`) and prefix-filtered in Rust, so a bucket catalogued from a large external store could balloon the payload. Fixed it one level
better than events by pushing **both** the prefix filter and the bound into SQL: `list_by_workspace(ws, prefix, limit)` →
`WHERE … ($2 = '' OR starts_with(key, $2)) ORDER BY last_modified DESC LIMIT $3` (floored at 1). Using `starts_with` (not `LIKE … || '%'`)
keeps the prefix **literal** — a key like `img%` matches nothing rather than acting as a wildcard (an injection-flavored footgun avoided;
fully parameterized regardless). Crucially the bound applies **after** the filter, so you get the first `limit` *matches*, not
`limit`-most-recent-then-filtered (the weakness the email scan-cap pattern has). Added `pub const DEFAULT_OBJECT_LIMIT = 1000` (re-exported);
the route gained an optional `?limit=` clamped to `[1, cap]`; the agent `recent_objects`/`objects_by_prefix` op now passes its prefix+limit
straight to SQL (dropping its redundant in-memory filter). Updated callers (route, tool, 3 test calls) + extended the repo test (prefix
narrows to `docs/`; `img%` is literal → empty; `limit=1` over 2 matches → 1 row). **Verified against live Postgres:** workspace clippy
(excl. web) `-D warnings` clean; store `buckets_objects_repo` green (the new SQL prefix/limit assertions actually execute); api lib **132**.
With this, both growth-prone list surfaces (synced calendars, synced object stores) are bounded; the user's own hand-entered data
(notes/tasks/conversations) stays unbounded by design (it grows at human pace). **Next:** the held graph-query scope decision; the deferred
now-centric agenda window; else marginal items._

_2026-06-23 — **Bounded `/events` — an unbounded list was a real robustness gap (SOUL §8/§18)** — `GET
/events` with no date range fetched **every** event in the workspace via `EventRepo::list_by_workspace` (no `LIMIT`), so a long-lived
synced CalDAV calendar (years of history) could balloon the API payload and the wasm agenda — the email path already caps via
`EMAIL_SCAN_CAP`, events had no equivalent. Added `limit: i64` to the repo method (`ORDER BY starts_at ASC … LIMIT $5`, floored at 1) +
`pub const DEFAULT_EVENT_LIMIT = 2000` (re-exported from the store root); the route gained an optional `limit` query param clamped to
`[1, DEFAULT_EVENT_LIMIT]` (default cap). **Semantics chosen deliberately:** plain *first-N-by-start-ascending*, not a "latest-N" window —
because the two agent ops (`upcoming_events` from=now, `events_in_range`) then `.take(limit)` ascending and want the **soonest/first** N;
a latest-N truncation would have silently returned the furthest-future events for "upcoming". One method can't bake both directions, so the
predictable ascending-LIMIT is correct for every caller. The **deletion-reconciliation** path (`sync.rs`, full-snapshot providers like local
`.ics`) must see *every* stored event to find orphans → passes `i64::MAX` (capping it would leave events past the cap un-pruned — a
correctness trap, avoided). Scheduler passes the cap (its `[after,now)` window is one tick wide). Updated all ~10 callers (route, tools×2,
scheduler, sync reconciler, 3 test files). New repo test `event_list_limit_bounds_first_ascending` (5 events inserted out of order: limit=2 →
earliest two ascending; limit=0 → floored to the single earliest; limit≥count → all ascending). **Verified against live Postgres:**
`cargo clippy --workspace --exclude catalerum-web -D warnings` clean; api lib **132**; full **catalerum-ingest** suite green (local_sync
reconciliation, schedule_scan, worker_queue all exercise the new arg); store events test green. **Next:** a now-centric default window for the
agenda (currently earliest-N for >2000-event calendars — a UX/design choice, deferred); the held graph-query scope decision; else marginal items._
