than first feared):** the agent's `query_graph` **tool is typed** (`related_notes`/`notes_by_topic`, scoped by construction) — so the
cross-tenant Cypher leak is **NOT agent-reachable / not prompt-injectable**. It's only reachable by a human deliberately writing raw
Cypher via the **graph-explorer REST route** or a **GraphQuery automation trigger** (the latter the more concerning: a persistent,
automated cross-tenant poll). Still a real §18 hole for a deliberate authenticated user on a multi-tenant Neo4j, but not an injection
vector. **Robust fix = a design call (still open):** (a) a Cypher parser to verify structural scoping; (b) restrict the raw surfaces to
typed parameterized queries (feature loss for the §12 explorer); or (c) database-per-workspace in Neo4j (migration). No safe
*autonomous* partial fix exists (comment-stripping is theater vs. `OR 1=1`). **Audits this pass (both sound):** `catalerum-bus`
`DistLock` is the canonical single-instance pattern (`SET NX PX` + random fence token + Lua `if GET==token then DEL/PEXPIRE`
CAS release/refresh — so the schedule single-fire is correctly backed, no double-fire); the `Auth` extractor resolves the bearer via
`iam().verify_bearer` (expiry-filtered `get_by_token_hash`) and derives the role from the session-backed principal with deny-by-default
`role_allows` (no client-controlled role/scope). **Every major subsystem is now audited.** **Next:** the user's graph-scope design
decision (recommend: typed-only for the GraphQuery *trigger*, keep raw Cypher in the human explorer) — then only marginal items remain._

_2026-06-22 — **Graph-query Cypher audit: block `USE` + flag a real cross-tenant scope weakness (SOUL §6.3/§18)**
— audited the Neo4j layer. **Projection is injection-safe:** every writer (`merge_node`/`merge_edge`/`delete_node`) parameterizes all
user-derived values (`$workspace_id`/`$id`/`$props`) and only interpolates **enum-derived** labels/edge-types (`as_cypher`) — no Cypher
injection from a malicious note title. **`query_graph` (raw user Cypher, `graph:query`-gated, held by every role) has two issues:**
(1) **fixed** — the read-only blocklist missed **`USE`**, which can switch databases (escaping the per-workspace scope and the single-db
target, potentially reaching `system`); added it to `FORBIDDEN_CLAUSES` + a test. (2) **flagged, not band-aided** — the workspace-scope
check is `cypher.contains("$workspace_id")`, a *substring* test: `… WHERE n.workspace_id = $workspace_id OR 1=1 …` (or the marker in a
comment/string) satisfies it while reading **other tenants' nodes** in the shared graph — a §18 cross-tenant read leak when Neo4j is
enabled multi-tenant. A robust fix needs a real Cypher parser **or** restricting this surface to the typed parameterized queries
(`related_notes`/`notes_by_topic`/… , scoped by construction); a partial heuristic (e.g. stripping comments) is security theater
against the trivial `OR 1=1` bypass, so I deliberately **did not** ship one — documented it in the validator doc + here as a §18
hardening TODO for a maintainer-level design call. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-automation --all-targets -D warnings`
clean; `graph_query_cypher_requires_workspace_scope_and_read_only` extended (now rejects `USE …`) — green. **Next:** decide the
graph-query scope fix (parser vs typed-only); then the `isolated_store` consolidation / canvas edge labels / MCP GET channel (§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **Validate object keys at the storage API boundary — backend-independent contract (SOUL §9/§18)**
— auditing the storage backends found their traversal handling sound (local-fs `resolve` allows only `Component::Normal`; webdav
`validate_key`; S3's flat namespace makes `..` non-exploitable — literal keys stay under the `<ws>/` prefix), **but** the *accepted-key
contract differed by backend*: a `PUT /storage/objects/../weird` is **rejected by local-fs yet accepted by S3** — the same request
behaves differently based on a deploy-time backend choice the client can't see. Fixed at the right layer: a `validate_object_key`
boundary check in the storage routes' `upload`/`download`/`remove` handlers (after the `/`-trim, before `workspace_object_key`
namespacing) rejects empty / absolute / `..` / leading-`.` keys uniformly — matching what local-fs enforces — so the contract is
backend-independent, plus defence-in-depth (no `<ws>/../…` physical key a future canonicalizing layer could mis-resolve). Interior `.`
(`a/./b`) normalizes to `a/b` per `Path::components` and is allowed, same as local. (Other audits this pass — iCalendar parser
panic-safety, ingest re-projection idempotency `delete_by_source`+`replace_for_document` — both **sound**.) **Verified against live
Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; new
`validate_object_key_accepts_normal_paths_and_rejects_traversal` (normal keys ok; empty/`..`/`.`/`/abs`/`a/../../b` rejected) — green;
full api lib **131 in parallel**. **Next:** the `isolated_store` consolidation, canvas edge labels, or the MCP GET push channel (§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **Connect-timeout the external sync clients — close the gap the earlier timeout sweep missed
(SOUL §8/§28)** — auditing the iCalendar parser (sound — `Result`-based, `icalendar`-crate-backed, missing/bad fields degrade to
errors/defaults, never panics) surfaced that the **external-server** sync clients still had **no connect timeout**: caldav (×2),
gmail, jmap all built `reqwest::Client::builder().user_agent(..).build()` with no timeout, and IMAP did a bare
`TcpStream::connect(..)`. The iterations 5-7 timeout sweep fixed the `Client::new()` sites (vector/graph/channels/webdav) but left
these "builder-with-only-user-agent" ones — and these talk to the **least reliable** endpoints (a user's CalDAV/Gmail/JMAP/IMAP), so an
unreachable or stalls-after-accept server would hang the sync worker for minutes (OS TCP timeout) or forever. Added a 10 s
`connect_timeout` to the four reqwest clients and wrapped IMAP's whole **TCP+TLS+LOGIN handshake** in a 30 s `tokio::time::timeout`.
**Connect/handshake-only by design** (no overall request cap) — a large calendar REPORT / mailbox FETCH shouldn't be aborted
mid-transfer (same call as webdav). Did **not** size-cap caldav's `.text()`: truncating an `.ics` would corrupt it; a huge legit
calendar is a capacity matter, not an attack. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-calendar -p catalerum-email --all-targets -D
warnings` + workspace clippy (excl web) clean; calendar 28 + email 25 tests green. With this, **every HTTP/socket client in the tree is
now connect-timeout-bounded** (LLM, fetch, vectors, graph, channels, storage, calendar, email). **Next:** the `isolated_store`
consolidation, canvas edge labels, or the MCP GET push channel (§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **Boa sandbox: pin the VM stack limit explicitly (SOUL §11/§20)** — a small hardening after
two investigations that concluded *no change warranted*: **(a) reasoning passthrough** — catalerum never *requests* reasoning
(`to_sdk_request` sets no `reasoning_effort`; core `ChatRequest` has no reasoning field), so last chunk's empty `reasoning`/`reasoning_details`
send-defaults are correct, not a band-aid; full passthrough is a speculative feature for capability not yet exposed. **(b) Boa memory** —
the JS sandbox bounds CPU (loop/recursion) + wall-clock but not heap; that's the deliberate in-process tradeoff (true isolation = the
container/bao backend, §20), unfixable in Boa. The one concrete change: the runner explicitly set loop + recursion limits but relied on
**Boa's *default*** VM stack-size limit — and the llmleaf drift last chunk just proved dependency-default drift is a live hazard here.
Added `JsLimits::stack_size_limit` (pinned to Boa's current default 10 240 frames, applied via `set_stack_size_limit`) so a future
engine-default change can't silently loosen the sandbox; the limit set (loop · recursion · **stack** · wall-clock) is now fully
explicit. No behavior change. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-script --all-targets -D warnings` + workspace clippy (excl web)
clean; `catalerum-script` 10 tests green (infinite-loop / unbounded-recursion still bounded). **Next:** the `isolated_store`
consolidation, canvas edge labels, or the MCP GET push channel (§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **Fix llmleaf-drift build break + cap `read_object`/`read_email` text (SOUL §7/§9/§28)** — two
items. **(1) Build unblocked (was fully broken):** the sibling `../llmleaf` crate's `ChatMessage` + streaming `Delta` gained
`reasoning` + `reasoning_details` fields (OpenRouter reasoning passthrough), so `catalerum-llm/src/client.rs` no longer compiled —
which blocks the **whole** workspace (llm is a core dep). Added the fields with **send-path defaults** (`reasoning: None`,
`reasoning_details: Vec::new()`) at `to_sdk_message` + the two streaming test stubs; catalerum's core `ChatMessage` carries no
reasoning, so sending none is correct (echoing signed `reasoning_details` back to preserve hidden reasoning across a turn is a separate
future feature, noted). **(2) Robustness:** `read_object`/`read_email` returned a stored object/email's **full** text — but objects can
be tens of MB, so a single read could blow the model's context / cost. Added `cap_read_text` (truncate to **64 KB** on a UTF-8
boundary) + a `truncated` flag on both results; the agent gets the head and can narrow via `search_semantic`. (`read_note` left
uncapped — notes are small.) **Verified against live Postgres:** workspace clippy (excl web) clean; `catalerum-llm` 21 + the new
`cap_read_text_truncates_on_a_char_boundary` pure test; full api lib **130 in parallel** (read_object/read_email tests assert
`truncated:false` for short content). **Next:** the `isolated_store` consolidation, canvas edge labels, or the MCP GET push channel
(§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **SSRF audit of `fetch_url` (sound) + IPv4-compatible-IPv6 defense-in-depth (SOUL §27)** —
audited the agent's web-fetch path for SSRF, the classic risk for a server that fetches arbitrary URLs. **It's well-built:**
`allow_private_hosts:false` default; blocks IPv4 loopback/private/link-local(169.254→metadata)/CGNAT/unspecified and IPv6
loopback/ULA/link-local; **re-resolves DNS and re-checks every resolved IP** (defeats a public name pointing at an internal IP); and
**blocks redirects** to private/non-http targets. One defense-in-depth gap closed: `to_ipv4_mapped()` decoded `::ffff:a.b.c.d` but not
the deprecated IPv4-**compatible** form `::a.b.c.d` (e.g. `::169.254.169.254`) — non-routable on modern OSes but a free completeness
win. Switched to `to_ipv4()` (decodes both; `::`/`::1` are handled above, real public v6 returns `None`), so the embedded-v4 check now
covers every form. **Known residual (not fixed — needs maintainer-reviewed DNS-pinning plumbing, risky in a loop):** a DNS-rebinding
TOCTOU between `guard_resolved`'s lookup and reqwest's connect; the common vectors are all covered. **Verified:** `cargo clippy -p
catalerum-fetch --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `catalerum-fetch` tests green (41), `blocks_ipv6_local` extended with the mapped +
compatible metadata-address forms + a public-v6 negative. **App status:** every high-stakes surface — exec, fetch/SSRF, authz/caps,
email sync, job queue — now audited; the agent + automation + ingest surfaces are comprehensively refined. **Next (marginal):** the
`isolated_store` test consolidation, canvas edge labels, or the MCP GET push channel (§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **`query_structured` enforces per-domain read caps — close a least-privilege leak (SOUL §19/§7)**
— an authz hardening surfaced while auditing the email providers (which are sound — imap/jmap/gmail all correctly override
`is_incremental()→true`, so the ingest never mass-deletes their delta `upserts`). The leak: `query_structured` gated the **whole
tool** on `notes:read`, yet it spans notes / calendar / tasks / storage ops — so a **scoped agent granted only `notes:read` could read
calendars / tasks / objects** through it (a hole I'd just *widened* by adding the `boards` + `calendars` ops under that one gate).
Fix (the `UseSkillTool` pattern): `required_capability()` → `None` (no single-domain dispatch gate) and `invoke` now checks **the op's
own domain read cap** against `ctx.capabilities` — `notes`→`notes:read`, `upcoming_events`/`events_in_range`/`calendars`→`calendar:read`,
task/`boards` ops→`tasks:read`, object ops→`storage:read`; skipped for an unscoped caller (`capabilities==None` = full authority, so
base Viewer/Member — who hold every read — are unchanged). Net: tightens a notes-only grant *and* correctly lets a calendar-only grant
use the calendar ops (previously blocked by the notes gate). **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api
--all-targets -D warnings` clean; new `query_structured_enforces_per_domain_read_capability` (notes-only → calendar/tasks/storage ops
all `Unauthorized`; calendar-only → `calendars` ok but `recent_notes` denied; unscoped → any op) — green; full api lib **129 in
parallel** (no regression to the existing unscoped query tests). **Next:** the `isolated_store` consolidation, canvas edge labels, or
the MCP GET push channel (§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **`notify` surfaces its channel names — finishing the agent-discovery story (SOUL §7/§25)** —

the now-dynamic schema). With this the agent can discover **every handle it needs** — boards, calendars, channels — before calling the
tools that consume them. **Next:** the `isolated_store` consolidation, canvas edge labels, or the MCP GET push channel (§29)._

_2026-06-22 — **Qdrant + Neo4j clients get default HTTP timeouts — no more indefinite worker hangs (SOUL
§6.3/§6.4)** — following the `/status` work, which surfaced that the derived-store clients were built with a bare
`reqwest::Client::new()` (**no timeout on any request**): a Qdrant/Neo4j that accepts the TCP connection but stalls mid-response
would hang an ingest/search/projection worker forever — far worse than the health-probe case. Both `VectorStore::new` and
`GraphStore::new` now build their client via a new `default_http_client()`: a **10 s `connect_timeout`** (fail fast on an unreachable
host) + a **generous 60 s overall `timeout`** (a backstop — normal ops are sub-second and per-document upserts are small, so 60 s is
pure slack). The `with_client` override seam is untouched, so a caller can still supply a custom client. A `.build()` failure maps via
the existing `Transport(#[from] reqwest::Error)` arm (no panic, no silent no-timeout fallback). **Verified:** workspace clippy (excl
web) clean; `catalerum-vector` lib **11 (+1** `new_validates_url_and_builds_the_timed_client`**)** + `catalerum-graph` lib 20
(`rejects_bad_base_url` still green); **live Qdrant roundtrip integration passes through the timed client** (real upsert+search, so the
60 s cap doesn't break real ops). **Remaining untimed clients** (lower-stakes, noted for later): `catalerum-channels` telegram/discord
senders and `catalerum-storage` webdav. **Next:** those, the GET push channel half of streamable-HTTP MCP (§29), or canvas marginalia._

_2026-06-22 — **`/status` health endpoint is now concurrent + timeout-bounded (SOUL §12)** — a resilience
fix. The Settings "Status" panel's `GET /status` probed its five backing services **sequentially**, and the **Qdrant/Neo4j `healthz`
calls use a default `reqwest::Client` with no per-request timeout** — so a store that accepts the TCP connection but never replies
would stall the whole endpoint indefinitely (and even healthy probes paid the *sum* of their latencies). Probes now run
**concurrently** (`tokio::join!` over Postgres / LLM gateway / Qdrant / Neo4j; the bus mode-check is synchronous, kept out of the
join) and each runs under a hard **`PROBE_TIMEOUT` (5 s)** via a new `probe_with_timeout` helper that maps a timeout to `down`
(`"… — timed out after 5s"`). Net: endpoint latency is bounded by the slowest single probe, and a hung service degrades to `down`
instead of hanging `/status`. Display order (truth → gateway → bus → derived stores) and the non-secret payload are unchanged. New
unit tests: `probe_with_timeout_passes_ready_results_through` (ready Ok→up / Err→down) + `probe_with_timeout_marks_a_hung_probe_down`
(a `pending()` future degrades to `down` at a 10 ms limit, proving it can't hang). **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p
catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; **124 api lib tests** (+2). **Next:** the GET push channel / tool-progress streaming
half of streamable-HTTP MCP (§29), or canvas marginalia._

_2026-06-22 — **Email sync no longer floods automations on connect — suppress `MailReceived` during initial
backfill (SOUL §28/§11)** — a real footgun fix + a deliberate **behavior change**. `sync_mailbox` fired the `MailReceived` trigger
for every email whose uid wasn't already stored; on a mailbox's **first-ever sync** nothing is stored yet, so the entire history
counted as "new" — connecting a 10k-message inbox would have enqueued 10k automation runs (triage-inbox, notifications…) replaying the
backlog. Now the first sync is treated as an **initial backfill** (`initial_backfill = cursor.is_none()`) and arrival triggers are
suppressed; they fire only for mail arriving *after* the mailbox is watched. The backlog is **still projected** (chunk+embed) so it's
searchable from sync #1 — only the trigger dispatch is gated. Reliable because every provider returns a concrete `next_cursor` even for
an empty mailbox (`SyncBatch.next_cursor: Cursor`, not `Option`), so any once-synced mailbox has `cursor.is_some()` — no empty-inbox
false-positive. **This flips the previously-tested "first sync fires" behavior**; the integration test
`new_email_fires_matching_mail_received_automation` was rewritten to assert the corrected semantics (backfill → 0 `run_automation`
jobs even for a matching automation; a 2nd email written after backfill → exactly the matching automation fires; no-op re-sync → none)
while keeping its matching-vs-non-matching-filter coverage. **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-ingest
--all-targets -D warnings` clean; **whole ingest suite green — 41 lib + all integration** (email_sync 6/6, incl. the rewritten test).
**Next:** the GET push channel / tool-progress streaming half of streamable-HTTP MCP (§29), or canvas marginalia._

_2026-06-22 — **MCP-over-HTTP content-negotiates SSE — the response half of streamable-HTTP (SOUL §26/§29)**
— `POST /mcp` previously always returned `application/json` and ignored the `Accept` header, so the **standard MCP "streamable HTTP"
client** (which sends `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` and parses the POST body as an **SSE stream**) couldn't talk to it.
Now `handle` reads the `Accept` header and, when the client opts into `text/event-stream`, frames the single JSON-RPC response as a
one-event SSE stream that closes immediately (`axum::response::sse::{Sse,Event}` over a `futures::stream::once`); a plain JSON client
still gets `application/json` (full back-compat). New pure `accepts_event_stream(&HeaderMap)` (matches the `text/event-stream` media
type, tolerant of `;q=`/casing, `*/*` stays on JSON) + `sse_response`; `into_response` gained a `wants_sse` arm (notification → `202`
regardless). This resolves the **response** half of §29's streamable-HTTP open question; server-*initiated* push (a standalone
`GET /mcp` channel + long-running tool-progress events) is the remaining half. **Verified against live Postgres:** `cargo clippy -p
catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean; **122 api lib tests** (+2: `response_is_sse_when_accepted` asserts the
`text/event-stream` content type, `accept_header_opts_into_sse` covers both-accepted / params / casing / json-only / `*/*` / missing;
`notification_is_accepted_with_no_body` extended to both negotiation modes). **Next:** the GET push channel / tool-progress streaming
(§29), or canvas marginalia (keyboard-delete, edge labels)._

_2026-06-21 — **Node-graph automations Phase B — Boa (sandboxed JS) code/condition runtimes (SOUL §11/§20)** — graph
Code/Condition nodes now run **actual code**. New **`catalerum-script`** crate: `ScriptCodeRunner` implements the Phase-A
`CodeRunner` trait — runtime `"js"`/`"javascript"` → **Boa 0.21.1** (pure-Rust JS); the user's `source` is wrapped as an IIFE
function body receiving the merged `{trigger, inputs}` context as `input` (so they `return` a value), the result `JsValue` → JSON
output. **Sandboxed:** no host functions (no fs/net), **bounded** by Boa `runtime_limits` (loop-iteration + recursion limits make an
infinite loop terminate deterministically as an `Err`) plus a wall-clock backstop; Boa's `!Send` `Context` is confined inside
`spawn_blocking`. Non-JS runtimes (`"shell"`/`"python"`…) dispatch to the existing §20 `Executor` via `CommandSpec{code, language}` —
wired and ready for the container/bao backend (the only shipping `LocalExecutor` rejects inline code by design). **Wiring:** the
worker's `AutomationContext` gained a `code: Arc<dyn CodeRunner>` (default `FailCodeRunner`, builder `with_code_runner`); the binary
constructs a `ScriptCodeRunner` (with the configured executor when `[exec]` is on, else JS-only) and installs it, so deployed graph
automations' JS nodes execute. **Built by a dynamic Workflow (script → wire → verify → fix-loop); green on the first verify, 0 fix
rounds.** **Verified against live Postgres:** workspace clippy (excl. web) clean; **`catalerum-script` 10 unit tests** (numeric/object
transform, boolean condition, syntax/runtime error → Err, infinite-loop & unbounded-recursion bounded → Err, no-return → null) +
**DB e2e** (a webhook→JS-code→action graph runs and the code node's `{doubled:42,…}` output flows to the downstream action's
`inputs`; a JS condition routes the true branch, false-branch node `Skipped`); api 117 / ingest 41 lib green, backward-compat
`FailCodeRunner` path intact. **Next — Phase C:** the drag-and-drop SVG canvas editor (frontend)._

_2026-06-21 — **Node-graph automations Phase A — DAG model + executor + `CodeRunner` trait (SOUL §11)** — the
foundation of the no-code node-graph system (a multi-phase feature, built via dynamic multi-agent Workflows). Automations can now be
authored as a **directed acyclic graph** of typed nodes — Trigger / Action / Code{runtime,source} / Condition{runtime,source} —
joined by ported edges, stored in the existing free-form `spec` JSON column (**no migration**); legacy linear automations run
**100% unchanged** (the executor runs the graph only when `spec.graph` is present). **New `catalerum-automation/src/graph.rs`:** the
pure serde model (`Graph`/`Node`/`Edge`/`NodeKind`/`Position`) + total-function helpers — `validate` (unique ids, edge endpoints
exist, ≥1 trigger, acyclic), `topo_order` (Kahn), `trigger_specs` (compile Trigger nodes → the dispatch `triggers`), `from_spec`
(loud-fail on a malformed graph). **`executor.rs`:** a `CodeRunner` trait beside `ActionRunner` (+ a `FailCodeRunner` default — Boa
is Phase B) and `run_graph` — topo-walk seeded by the **fired** trigger node (via `Trigger::matches`), per-node input
`{trigger, inputs:{upstream_id→output}}` (real **data passing**), Action→`ActionRunner`, Code/Condition→`CodeRunner`, condition
truthiness routes the `true`/`false` ports (off-branch nodes `Skipped`), **one durable step per node** via the existing
`add_step`/`finish_step` (node id encoded in the step JSON — no schema change), crash-resume preserved (done nodes not re-run),

and **compile its trigger nodes into the stored `triggers`** so dispatch still fires; non-graph paths untouched. `execute`/
`execute_for_job` gained a `code: &dyn CodeRunner` param (worker + tests pass `&FailCodeRunner`). **Built by a dynamic Workflow
(engine → API → verify → fix-loop); green on the first verify, 0 fix rounds.** **Verified against live Postgres:** workspace clippy
(excl. web) clean; **266 tests pass** (automation 38 lib + 9 integration incl. DB-gated graph data-passing / condition-branch /

_2026-06-21 — **`delete_note` tool — closing the agent-vs-product note-CRUD parity gap (SOUL §21/§7)** — note
deletion was already in the product surface (`DELETE /notes/{id}` route + the web `delete_note` client + the Notes-panel delete
control) but the chat agent had no tool for it, though it could create/edit/read/list notes. New **`delete_note`** registry tool
(mirrors `EditNoteTool`'s `NoteRepo` + `NoteIngest` shape): takes a note `id`, calls `NoteRepo::delete` (NotFound if absent), then
**reconciles the derived projection** via `NoteIngest::enqueue` — the same call the route makes, so the worker finds the note gone
and purges its vectors/chunks/document (best-effort, no-op unless qdrant/graph enabled). Gated on **`notes:write`** (matching the
route — note deletion is a write, not a separate `delete` scope). **Agent-only**, like `delete_event` — no `DeleteNote` automation
`ActionKind`. **Verified against real Postgres (build + run):** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets -D warnings` clean;
`cargo test -p catalerum-api --lib` live → **113 pass (+1** `delete_note_tool_removes_a_note_and_reconciles`: deletes the row, a
second/invalid delete errors, the reconcile enqueue is exercised**)**. **Next:** typed Automations form-builder (web, gated on the
`maildir` web-test fix)._

_2026-06-21 — **`delete_event` tool — completing local-calendar CRUD for the agent (SOUL §8/§7)** — with
`create_event`/`update_event` already shipped, the chat agent could make and edit local events but not **remove** one, even though
`EventRepo::delete` and the `DELETE /events/{id}` route exist. New **`delete_event`** registry tool (thin `EventRepo`/`CalendarRepo`
client) takes an `event_id`, verifies the event exists and sits on a **writable local** calendar (refuses a provider/read-only
calendar, mirroring the REST guard), then `EventRepo::delete`, returning `{ "deleted": <id> }`. Gated on **`calendar:delete`**

it). **Agent-only by design:** there is intentionally no `DeleteEvent` automation `ActionKind` (deletion-via-trigger is a
higher-stakes design call left to the user); the tool just exposes to the §7 agent what the REST API already allows. **Verified

--lib` against the live DB green — **112 pass (+1** `delete_event_tool_removes_a_local_event`: delete makes the event gone, a second
delete / missing-workspace both error**)**. **Next:** typed Automations form-builder (web, gated on the `maildir` web-test fix —

schema/migration (the `filter: Option<Value>` field already exists), no signature change
(`matches`/`automation_matches`/`matching_automations`/`dispatch_trigger_event` keep their shape), so every downstream caller
(ingest dispatch, the `/channels` route) compiles and behaves identically except that a `text`-filtered automation now fires
selectively. **Verified (build + run):** `cargo clippy -p catalerum-automation --all-targets -D warnings` clean; **`cargo test -p

_2026-06-18 — **Local (database-native) calendars — the first writable calendar surface** (SOUL §8/§11/§12) —
calendars/events existed only as a **read-only ingest projection** (a calendar always belonged to a provider `Connection`;
events were written only by the sync worker). This adds a **local** calendar: `calendars.connection_id IS NULL` ⟺ a
read-write, database-native calendar with no external source that is never synced — the writable substrate §11 automations
target. **Migration `0018`:** drop `NOT NULL` on `calendars.connection_id` + a **partial unique index** on
`(workspace_id, external_id) WHERE connection_id IS NULL` (local calendars dedup by `external_id`; the provider
`(connection_id, external_id)` key is moot when there's no connection). **Core:** `Calendar.connection_id` →
`Option<ConnectionId>` (+ `is_local()`). **Store:** `CalendarRepo::upsert_local` (get-or-create a local calendar,
idempotent via the partial-index `ON CONFLICT`); `EventRepo::create` (fresh-`uid` pure insert), `update` (by id; bumps
`SEQUENCE`, preserves the immutable `uid`), `delete` (by id); new `EventPatch`. **API:** `POST`/`DELETE /calendars` +
`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE /events` — `calendar:write`/`calendar:delete`-gated (Viewer `403`); event writes are **restricted to
local calendars** (a provider calendar is managed by sync, never edited in place → `400`); `end ≥ start` + non-empty summary
enforced. **Automations payoff:** a new always-registered **`create_event`** tool (`calendar:write`, thin
`CalendarRepo`/`EventRepo` client) that auto-provisions a default local calendar when none is named, and
`ActionKind::CreateEvent → "create_event"` in the `ToolActionRunner`, so the §11 `CreateEvent` action writes through it; the
§8 `CalendarEvent` trigger already polls **all** workspace events, so local events drive automations with no extra plumbing.
**Web:** "New calendar" + "Add event" forms (writable-calendar picker, `datetime-local`→UTC RFC 3339) + a per-event delete
control on writable calendars; `Calendar.connection_id` → `Option`. **Verified:** native + wasm clippy (`--all-targets -D
warnings`) clean; full native test suite green; a new `calendars_events_repo` integration test + the full store/api DB suites
pass against **real Postgres** (the 0001→0018 migration chain + the partial-index `ON CONFLICT` exercised live). (Pre-existing
unrelated failure left untouched: `automations_repo` uses `GrantId::new()` with no backing `grants` row, violating the
composite `automations_grant_id_fk` from `0016`.)_

(SOUL §18/§12) — multi-workspace tenancy existed end-to-end (memberships, per-workspace sessions, IAM), but the

`routes::auth`): **`GET /workspaces`** — the caller's memberships (`memberships().list_by_user` → `workspaces().get`
for name/slug), each with their **role** + an **active** flag (== the current session's workspace); authenticated
self-data, no capability domain (a user only ever sees their own memberships, §18). **`POST /auth/switch
{workspace_id}`** — mints a **new session bound to the target workspace** and returns its bearer (the existing
`SessionResponse`). **The security gate is `iam().issue_session`'s existing membership check** — it fails
`Unauthorized` if the caller isn't a member and resolves the role from the target membership, so a user can switch
**only to workspaces they belong to** (no new, hand-rolled auth logic — the safe primitive `redeem_login_token`
already uses). **Web:** contract types `WorkspaceMembership`/`SwitchWorkspace`/`SwitchResponse`, two REST client
fns, a new `auth::adopt_token_and_reload` (caches the new bearer, **clears any stale `?token=` from the URL** so
`resolve_token`'s URL-preference doesn't re-apply the old token, then reloads so every panel re-fetches under the new
workspace), and a **`WorkspaceSwitcher`** — a header `<select>` of the user's workspaces (rendered **only when there
is more than one**, since a single-workspace user has nothing to switch), switching on change. Embedded in the shell
header (right-aligned) + a `.wb-workspace` style. **Verified:** API `cargo clippy -p catalerum-api --all-targets
-D warnings` clean + api lib tests **97 pass (2 new** — `SwitchRequest` decode incl. non-UUID rejection,
`WorkspaceMembership` serialize**)**; web `cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -D warnings` clean + web
tests **99 pass (1 new** — membership-list + switch-response decode + body shape**)**. **THE §12 WORKBENCH IS

_2026-06-17 — **§19 `dry_run` constraint ENFORCED — the policy engine's first guardrail** (SOUL §19) —
the first grant **constraint** the runtime actually enforces, refining the prior "any non-default constraint fails the
run closed". A grant carrying **`dry_run`** now **authorizes the action and SIMULATES it**: dispatch checks the
capability, then — `if ctx.dry_run` — short-circuits **before** `invoke`, returning `{"dry_run":true,"tool","args"}`
without committing the side effect. The simulate is at the **single dispatch choke point** (`ToolRegistry::dispatch`),
so it covers every tool-backed action *and* every inner tool call an `LlmAgent` loop makes, uniformly. Plumbing: a
new `ToolContext.dry_run` field (defaults `false` at every construction site via `..Default::default()`);
`apply_grant` sets it from `g.constraints.dry_run` (alongside replacing capabilities — the grant *is* the attenuated
authority); and `Constraints::has_unenforced()` classifies the **still**-unenforced constraints
(env/rate/cost/time-window/approval) so the executor's fail-closed gate fires only for *those* — `dry_run` is no longer
swept up as "unenforceable". **Adversarially reviewed** (security-priority: authorization ordering + fail-open) — the
core confirmed **sound + exploit-free**: the capability gate runs **before** the dry-run short-circuit (an
unauthorized dry-run is still denied — you can't even *simulate* a tool you can't call); all 24 `impl Tool` side
effects live strictly inside `invoke` (nothing commits pre-`invoke`, so the short-circuit is total); the simulated
output echoes only the caller's own args (no cross-tenant leak); the fail-closed gate is unconditional and runs before
the action loop **on resume too** (re-resolved per run, workspace-scoped); `apply_grant` **replaces** (never widens)
capabilities, attenuated at creation. Found + fixed **1 MED + 1 LOW** (fail-closed *robustness* vs future change):
(MED) `has_unenforced()` was an allowlist-by-omission — a *future* `Constraints` field would default to "enforced"
(fail **open**); rewrote it to **destructure `self` with no `..`**, so adding a field is a **compile error** until it's
explicitly classified. (LOW) added **`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`** to `Constraints` so an unknown constraint key
(schema skew / newer-binary write / out-of-band JSONB) **fails the deserialize** → grant-load error → run fails closed,
never silently drops a constraint. **Verified:** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` + wasm + `just check`; a dispatch
unit test (`dispatch_dry_run_simulates_without_invoking_but_still_enforces_caps`: dry-run → simulated marker, a spy
tool's `invoke` **never fires**, yet an unauthorized dry-run is still `Unauthorized`); capability unit tests
(`has_unenforced` classifies all 5 unenforced + the 2 enforced shapes; an unknown key is **rejected not dropped**); the
live-PG enforcement test extended to **4 cases** (no grant → denied; `exec:run` grant → runs; **`dry_run` grant →
Succeeds but the side effect is NOT committed** [no `DRYRUN-MARKER` note]; `cost_limit` grant → **fails closed**);
executor (2) + grants_repo (3) unaffected; core lib + api lib all green. **Next:** the rest of the §19 policy engine
(enforce env_allow/rate_limit/cost_limit/time_window/requires_approval — currently fail-closed) + persist `grant_id`
on `automation_runs` for audit; routing grants through the interactive **chat/MCP** `ToolContext` (they ignore grants
today — safe default, but `dry_run` is automation-only until then); IMAP/JMAP (no IMAP server cached); the Leptos UI
(Playwright unavailable)._

_2026-06-17 — **§19 grant ENFORCEMENT — grants now confer real authority** (SOUL §19) —
the security-critical follow-up to the grants data layer: an automation that references a grant now **runs its
actions under the grant's capabilities** instead of its default base-role authority. `ActionRunner::run` gained a
`grant: Option<&Grant>` param; the `execute` driver loads the automation's grant (`store.grants().get`,
workspace-scoped) once and threads it to every action — a grant that **fails to load fails the run** (deny-safe,
never run under the wrong authority). `ToolActionRunner::apply_grant` **replaces** the `ToolContext` capabilities
with the grant's bundle (the grant *is* the attenuated authority an admin vouched for) and records `grant_id` for
audit, across all `resolve_context` paths. The trait's 3 test mocks updated for the new signature.
**Adversarially reviewed** (security-priority: cross-tenant + deny-by-default) — the core was traced and confirmed
**sound + fails closed**: a cross-workspace grant resolves to `NotFound` → run fails; an **empty** grant is
`Some(vec![])` → deny-all (never the unenforced `None`); the `LlmAgent` loop dispatches inner tool calls under the
grant; a deleted grant fails closed (FK nulls `grant_id`, or `get`→`NotFound`→fail). Found + fixed **2 MED**:
(MED, §18 defense-in-depth) the `grant_id` FK referenced `grants(id)` not the **same-workspace** `(workspace_id,
id)` — made it a **composite FK** (`FOREIGN KEY (workspace_id, grant_id) REFERENCES grants(workspace_id, id) ON
DELETE SET NULL (grant_id)`, with a `UNIQUE (workspace_id, id)` target) so the DB itself rejects a cross-tenant
grant reference; (MED) grant **`constraints`** (env allow-list, rate/cost caps, dry-run, per-action approval) were
silently ignored — a granted `exec:run` ran without its guardrails; the runtime can't yet enforce them (the policy
engine is a later slice), so the driver now **fails the run closed** when a grant carries non-default constraints
rather than running unconstrained. (LOW, noted for the policy-engine slice: persist `grant_id` on the run for
forensic audit.) **Verified:** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` + wasm + `just check`; a live-PG enforcement test
(`grant_elevates_an_automation_above_its_base_authority`: no grant → `run_command` denied [needs `exec:run`, no
base role holds it] → run **Failed**; grant conferring `exec:run` → the same action **runs** → **Succeeded**; a
grant with `dry_run` constraints → **fails closed**); grants_repo store tests (CRUD + §18 + FK-detach + the
composite FK **rejecting a cross-workspace grant**); existing runner/executor/automation tests unaffected
(executor 2, automation_run 3, action_runner 13); api lib 87, all green. **§19 capability grants are now
end-to-end: define (admin REST) → attach (`automations.grant_id`) → enforce (the runner).** **Next:** the §19
policy engine (constraint enforcement: env/rate/cost/dry-run/approval — currently fail-closed; + persist `grant_id`
on runs; + a non-admin grant-create path with the attenuation check already in place); IMAP/JMAP (no IMAP server
cached); the Leptos UI (Playwright unavailable)._

_2026-06-17 — **`Secret` config newtype — credentials never leak into logs** (SOUL §13) —
the consistently-flagged config-hardening item: API keys / passwords / tokens were plain `String`s on
`Debug`-deriving config structs, so a future `tracing::info!(?config)` (or a config-echo endpoint) would dump them
in cleartext (latent — no active sink today, but a real footgun). Introduced **`Secret`** (catalerum-api config):
a newtype that **redacts in `Debug`** (`Secret("***")`) yet (de)serializes **transparently** as a plain string
(so TOML + env round-trip unchanged) and is read explicitly via `expose()` only where a client is built. Wrapped
the six scalar secret fields — `llm.api_key`, `neo4j.password`, `storage.s3.secret_key`, `storage.webdav.password`,
`fetch.firecrawl.api_key`, `channels.telegram.<name>.bot_token` — and updated every read-site (state.rs + main.rs)
with `.expose()`; `enabled()`/`is_configured()` checks now use `Secret::is_empty`, and the env-override + default
paths use `.into()`. The Discord webhook URLs (a `HashMap<String,String>` whose values embed tokens) are the one
remaining secret shape, deferred (wrapping map values is a larger change). **Verified:** clippy `--all-targets
-D warnings` + wasm + `just check`; a unit test — a full `Config` parsed from TOML with canary secrets renders
**no value** in `format!("{:?}", config)` (only `Secret("***")`), while `expose()` returns the values and a bare
`Secret` serializes back to its string (redaction is Debug-only, never data loss); and a **binary leak-smoke** —
boot with canary `llm.api_key`/`neo4j.password`, the running process's full stdout+stderr contains **neither**
canary, yet still logs the non-secret config (listen / "llm client ready") and serves `/healthz`. api lib 86, all
green. **Codebase has no `todo!`/`unimplemented!`/`FIXME` stubs; the big milestones are done** (M1–M6 core, M3
storage local+S3+WebDAV, M5 automations + all §11 triggers, M8 email read-side Maildir). **Next (all
externally-blocked or larger design):** IMAP/JMAP email (no IMAP server cached in-env); the §19 capability-grants
table (grants beyond base roles — a meaty, Postgres-verifiable slice); the Leptos UI (Playwright unavailable);
wrap the Discord-webhook-URL map values as `Secret`._

_2026-06-17 — **Configurable object-upload size cap (`[storage].max_object_bytes`)** (M3,
SOUL §9) — object uploads were silently capped at axum's **2 MiB body default**, so `/storage` could not accept
ordinary files (a real usability bug), and the cap was neither raised nor configurable. Added
**`[storage].max_object_bytes`** (default **64 MiB**, env-overridable via `CATALERUM_STORAGE__MAX_OBJECT_BYTES`)
applied as an `axum::extract::DefaultBodyLimit` on the **storage routes only** (`build_router`) — large enough for
real documents, bounded against an unbounded-upload OOM (the body is rejected with **413** *before* it is fully
read, so no partial blob write / no buffering of an over-limit body). JSON routes (webhooks/mcp/notes) keep the
2 MiB default — they have no reason to accept 64 MiB. **Adversarially reviewed** (focused agent) — the mechanism
confirmed CLEAN: the per-route `.layer()` survives `.merge()` and doesn't leak onto other routes; the `Bytes`
extractor bounds **bytes actually read** (so a chunked / `Content-Length`-lying body can't bypass it or OOM);
`0` maps to the default (never "unlimited"); reads (GET list/download) are unaffected. Found + fixed **1 gap the
e2e couldn't catch**: `max_object_bytes` had **no env override** in `with_env_overrides` (an env-configured
deployment couldn't change the cap) — added `CATALERUM_STORAGE__MAX_OBJECT_BYTES` (mirrors `FETCH__MAX_BYTES`) +
the doc list. **Verified:** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` + wasm + `just check`; config-parse unit test
(default → 64 MiB, explicit honored); a **binary e2e** — with the default cap a **3 MB upload returns 201** (axum's
old 2 MiB default would have 413'd it), and with `max_object_bytes = 1 MiB` a 2 MB upload returns **413** while a

_2026-06-17 — **`GraphQuery` trigger source — every §11 trigger now fires** (M5/M4,
SOUL §11/§6.3) — the last trigger with no live producer. A new **`scan_graph_queries`** runs each tick in
`ScheduleWorker::run` (gated on an attached `GraphStore`, **no new dependency**): for each enabled `GraphQuery`
automation whose `every`-minute poll boundary fell in this tick's window, it runs the operator's Cypher against
Neo4j and enqueues a `run_automation` job **when the query returns ≥1 row** — the periodic "fire while this graph
condition holds" source. `every` = minutes (number, `{ "minutes": N }`, or absent → 5), 1‥10080; the timeline is
bucketed into `N`-minute spans and the automation fires once when `now` crosses a boundary (stateless, a clean
forward partition like the cron/calendar scans; a window spanning several boundaries coalesces to one poll — no
catch-up). Single-fired across pods via the bus lock keyed `(automation, fire-instant)`. The binary clones the
`[neo4j]` `GraphStore` into the scheduler via `ScheduleWorker::with_graph` (inert when `[neo4j]` is off).
**Adversarially reviewed** (focused agent over scoping/write-safety/windowing/resilience) — found + fixed **1 HIGH
+ 1 MED**: (HIGH §18) the raw Cypher bound `$workspace_id` but never **enforced** it — an unscoped `MATCH (n:Note)`
would read **other tenants'** nodes in the shared graph, and the row count leaks into the run's trigger + the
`LlmAgent` prompt; (MED) the commit endpoint runs **writes**, so a Cypher could mutate the read-only derived
projection (and combined with the HIGH, an unscoped `DETACH DELETE` wipes every tenant's graph). Both fixed by a
shared **`validate_graph_query_cypher`** (catalerum-automation): the Cypher **must reference `$workspace_id`** and
**must be read-only** (whole-word keyword scan rejecting `CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/REMOVE/DROP/FOREACH/CALL/LOAD`,
so `createdAt`/`settings` don't false-trip), enforced at **both** authoring (`AutomationSpec::from_json` → REST
`400`) **and** before the poller ever runs the query (`first_graph_query` skips + warns). Review confirmed CLEAN:
bucket/window partition (gap-free, no overflow), single-fire/lock (claim-before-poll is correct for a per-bucket
poll), resilience (a bad Cypher/Neo4j-down is logged + skipped, never aborts the scan; `run_one` never panics),
`every` parsing, and main.rs borrow/move. **Verified:** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` + wasm + `just check`;
unit tests — `graph_due`/`parse_every_minutes` (bucket math, default, out-of-range incl. `i64::MAX`, float) and
`validate_graph_query_cypher` (scope required, writes/`CALL` rejected, `createdAt` not a false positive); a
**live-neo4j integration test** (`scan_graph_queries_fires_on_nonempty_result_single_fire`: a scoped read-only
`RETURN $workspace_id` fires, a scoped empty `MATCH` does not, a disabled automation is excluded, the trigger
records the query + row count, and a re-scan single-fires) — `schedule_scan` 6/6; automation lib 26, api lib 84,
existing scheduler tests unaffected. **§11 trigger sources are now COMPLETE — every trigger
(TaskMoved/Webhook/StorageObject/ChannelMessage/MailReceived/Schedule/CalendarEvent/GraphQuery) has a live
producer.** **Next:** IMAP/JMAP email providers (need a live IMAP server — the cached `maildev` is SMTP-only, no
IMAP, so deferred); S3/WebDAV storage backends (`minio` is cached — verifiable); a real Cypher-parser scope check +

_2026-06-17 — **`CalendarEvent`-lead trigger source — time-driven calendar reminders**
(M5/M8, SOUL §11/§8) — the `Trigger::CalendarEvent { lead, filter }` variant existed but had **no source** (one
of the last two §11 triggers with no live producer). Wired it into the clock scheduler: a new
**`scan_calendar_event_triggers`** runs each tick in `ScheduleWorker::run` alongside `scan_schedules`, enqueuing a
`run_automation` job for each upcoming event whose **lead instant** (`start − lead`) crosses the tick window —
"fire N minutes before the meeting." `lead` = minutes (a bare number, `{ "minutes": N }`, or absent → 0), capped
to ±1 year (`MAX_LEAD_MINUTES`) so garbage can't overflow-panic the scheduler. The window uses the events query's
`[from, to)` over `start` with `from = after + lead`, `to = now + lead` → lead instant `∈ [after, now)`, a
gap-free/overlap-free forward partition (each event covered by exactly one tick); no catch-up across restarts
(mirrors the cron source). Each occurrence is single-fired across pods via the bus lock keyed by `(automation,
event, lead-instant)` — like the cron scanner keys by the fire-instant — so a **rescheduled** event or **changed
lead** re-fires at its new instant rather than being permanently suppressed. **Adversarially reviewed** (focused
agent over windowing/single-fire/overflow/scoping) — found + fixed **2 HIGH + 1 MED**: (HIGH) the lock keyed only
by `(automation, event)` would silently drop the reminder for a moved meeting → re-keyed on the lead-instant;
(HIGH/doc) the docstring claimed the inverse `(after, now]` window → corrected to the real `[after, now)` partition
(behavior was already a clean partition; only the doc was wrong); (MED) a huge integer `lead` panicked
`chrono::Duration::minutes` / `DateTime + Duration`, killing the detached scheduler task → capped in
`parse_lead_minutes` (`unsigned_abs`, so `i64::MIN` itself is safe). Review confirmed CLEAN: §18 workspace-scoping,
no-catch-up, the TTL-not-released lock guard. Documented interim: the opaque `filter` is not yet evaluated (every
workspace event fires, mirroring `Trigger::matches`) and only the first CalendarEvent trigger's lead is used — both
deferred to the predicate-language slice. **Verified:** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` + wasm + `just check`;
`parse_lead_minutes` unit test (number/object/null/garbage/overflow incl. `i64::MIN`/`MAX`); live-PG integration
test (`scan_enqueues_due_calendar_event_reminders_single_fire`: a due event fires once, a +60m event is not-yet-due,
a disabled automation + a non-calendar trigger are excluded, the trigger records the event, and a re-scan
single-fires) — full `schedule_scan` suite 5/5; existing scheduler tests unaffected. **§11 trigger sources: only
`GraphQuery` (periodic Cypher) now lacks a live source — every other trigger
(TaskMoved/Webhook/StorageObject/ChannelMessage/MailReceived/Schedule/CalendarEvent) fires.** **Next:** the
`GraphQuery` poll source (needs Neo4j); IMAP/JMAP email providers (need a live IMAP server); the predicate language
for `filter` / multi-lead; the Leptos UI._

(M8, SOUL §10/§28) — the keystone that makes the whole email vertical live end-to-end: a booted catalerum now
syncs a local **Maildir** into Postgres, so `routes::email` (`GET /mailboxes`/`/emails`), the `get_emails` LLM
tool, and `MailReceived` automations all light up with **actual mail** (previously inert without a sync source).

[0 → 60]) with `enabled()`/`mailbox_name()`/`poll_interval()`. New ingest pieces: **`ensure_maildir_connection`**
(idempotent `ConnectionKind::Email` connection over `{provider:"maildir", root, name}`),
**`scan_email_connections`** (sweeps **every** workspace's email connections → `sync_email_connection` each;
per-connection errors are logged-and-skipped so one bad Maildir never starves the rest), and
**`EmailSyncWorker`** — a periodic poller mirroring `ScheduleWorker` but **scan-first-then-sleep** so a configured
Maildir is ingested **at boot**, not one tick later (local Maildir has no IDLE/push; IMAP/JMAP push land with

up a moved root while the storage catalogue's existence-only ensure (its only other caller, passes `None`) never
wipes a blob. **Known sharp edge (by design, noted not guarded):** a first boot against a pre-existing Maildir
treats all historical mail as new → fires `MailReceived` for every message; a "seed-without-firing" first-sync
flag is a later slice if the backlog fan-out bites. **Verified:** clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` + wasm +

idempotency test, both green on live PG; **two full live-binary e2es** — (1) boot with a temp Maildir of 2

periodic poller** (`upserted=3`), `?sender=&unread=` filter + `/emails/{id}` body all correct, no-op ticks
silent; (2) **repoint** — boot on Maildir A (only A's mail served), then reboot the same DB with the config

_2026-06-16 — **Storage blobs are now workspace-isolated —
closes a HIGH §18 cross-tenant hole** (M3, SOUL §18/§9) — fixes the gap the prior slice's adversarial review
flagged: the blob backend was a single shared root + one global `[storage]` bucket and the routes passed the
**raw** user key, so in a multi-workspace deployment `list`/`download`/`delete` crossed tenants and same-key
uploads clobbered (the Postgres catalogue was already per-workspace; the byte layer was not). The fix is one
convention in `catalerum-core::provider`: **`workspace_object_key(ws, key)` → `"<ws>/<key>"`** (the *physical*
backend key) + `strip_workspace_key`. Every one of the **6 backend call-sites** now namespaces: the storage
routes (`list` scopes the prefix + strips it off each returned `ObjectMeta.key`; `upload`/`download`/`remove`
read/write/delete under `<ws>/…`) **and** the ingest worker's object read (`ObjectIngestContext::read_text`) —
so route-writes and worker-reads agree on where a blob lives. The catalogue (`objects.key`), the API responses,
and the `StorageObject` trigger keep the **user-facing** key; only the bytes move under the namespace. A
crafted `..` key is still rejected by `LocalFsBackend`'s existing path-traversal guard (it validates every
component of the full physical key), so a tenant cannot escape or cross its prefix. **Adversarially reviewed**
(a focused 2-dimension workflow — completeness of namespacing + isolation/edge-cases — **0 confirmed defects**).
Verified: clippy `--all-targets` + wasm + native `just check`; **core unit tests** (`workspace_object_key`
round-trip + *distinct workspaces never collide on the same key*); the object-ingest live integration test
updated to write at the namespaced key and **passing** (proves the worker reads the namespaced path); and a
**full live-binary e2e** — `PUT notes/hello.md` lands the blob on disk at **`<store>/<workspace_id>/notes/hello.md`**
(no raw un-namespaced path), the response + `list` return the user key `notes/hello.md`, `download` returns the
bytes, the worker ingested it into `documents`, and `DELETE` removes the on-disk blob + empties the listing.
**Storage is now §18-correct: per-workspace blob isolation by construction, on top of the per-workspace
catalogue.** **Remaining storage robustness (next):** **(MEDIUM §3.4)** `ensure_bucket`'s storage-`Connection`
find-or-create is still a TOCTOU race (no `UNIQUE(workspace_id, kind, name)` on `connections`) → fix with the

REST + file-browser surface; Matrix channel provider; inbound Telegram; streamable-HTTP SSE; the Leptos UI
(Playwright unavailable in-env)._

_2026-06-16 — **Object text extraction — uploaded files become
searchable documents** (M3/M4, SOUL §9/§10/§6.4) — builds on the object catalogue: a stored file's *bytes*
now become catalogued **text**. On upload the route enqueues a durable **`ingest_object`** job; the
`catalerum-ingest` worker (`ObjectIngestContext`, reusing the backend `AppState` built) claims it, reads the
object's bytes via the `StorageBackend`, **extracts text** (text-like content types only — `text/*`, JSON,
XML, YAML, …; binary is skipped, richer PDF/OCR extraction layers on later), **upserts a `documents` row**
keyed by `SourceRef::Object` (Postgres truth), and **links it from `objects.extracted_text_id`** (§10) — so a
file is now a first-class catalogued *document*. When an `EmbedContext` is present (`[qdrant]`), the same text
is chunked + embedded into Qdrant (derived), reusing the note path's `ingest_source`; without Qdrant the
truth-half (document + link) still runs. Reconciles to the object's current state: a re-upload re-extracts, a
**deleted** object (the route enqueues a purge ingest) and a **text→binary overwrite** both **purge** the
document *and* its vectors (via `EmbedContext::purge` → `vector.delete_by_source`), so no orphan survives
(§3.1/§10). New: `ObjectRepo::get`/`set_extracted_text`; `catalerum-ingest::object` module

_2026-06-15 — **Crash-mid-run resumption — the last
durability gap** (M5, SOUL §5/§11/§6.2) — automations now satisfy principle 5 in full ("a crash mid-run
resumes; it never silently double-fires"). Before: a `run_automation` job re-driven by the §6.2 reconciler
(a worker that crashed mid-run) called `execute` fresh → a brand-new run that re-ran **every** action →
duplicate side effects. Now a run records the `job_id` that spawned it (migration `0012`,
`AutomationRunRepo::start_run` + new `find_active_run_by_job`), and `execute_for_job(store, runner, ws,
automation, trigger, job_id)` **resumes**: if a still-`running` run exists for the job, it loads the prior
steps, **skips** the ones already `Succeeded`/`Skipped` (no re-fire of their side effects), and continues
from the first unfinished action — reusing an in-flight step's row rather than re-`add_step`ing it (the
`(run_id, ordinal)` unique key). The worker passes `job.id`; `execute` stays the fresh-run wrapper
(`job_id = None`). The irreducible residue — a step left `Running` at the crash re-runs once (the engine
can't know whether that one action's effect committed) — is documented; full exactly-once needs idempotent
actions. Verified: clippy `--all-targets` + wasm clean (`just check`); a **DB-gated resume test** (hand-record
a run + finished step 0, re-drive the same `job_id` → **only action 1 re-runs** (`seen == ["Notify"]`), the
**same** run finalizes `Succeeded`, **exactly one** run exists — no duplicate, both steps `Succeeded`,
`find_active_run_by_job` now empty) + the worker→run_automation integration test (now threading `job.id`) +
full store/automation(24)/ingest/api(70) suites green (live PG); binary boots + applies `0012` (`job_id`
column confirmed). **Automation durability is now complete:** durable spec/runs/steps, scheduler single-fire,
job single-claim (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), and crash resumption. **Deferred:** a Leptos automations/runs
view; a skill's `tools` restricting the agent; storage §9 / channel §25 event sources;
`GraphQuery`/`CalendarEvent` poll triggers; per-automation §19 grant resolution._

_2026-06-15 — **Scheduler single-fire lock — multi-pod
HA** (M5, SOUL §11/§6.2/§principle-11) — the clock scheduler is now safe under horizontal scaling: with N
pods each ticking, a `Schedule` occurrence fires **exactly once**, not N times. New
`schedule::due_occurrence(cron, tz, after, now)` returns *which* instant fired (deterministic given the
window, so every pod computes the same value for the same pending occurrence); `due_in_window` delegates to
it. `scan_schedules` now takes a `&dyn DistLock` and, before enqueuing, claims the occurrence with a lock
keyed `automation-fire:{id}:{fire-epoch}` (TTL 5min, left to expire — a losing pod's later scan still sees
it taken). The `ScheduleWorker` holds the `Bus` and passes `bus.lock()`; the binary wires `state.bus()`.
Reuses the existing `catalerum-bus` `DistLock` (`InProcessLock` for single-pod dev, **`RedisLock`** = Valkey
`SET NX PX` for HA) — `catalerum-ingest` gains a `catalerum-bus` dep. Verified: clippy `--all-targets` +
wasm clean (`just check`); **a deterministic single-fire test** (two scans of the same window sharing one
`InProcessLock` → enqueues **once**; the second sees the occurrence claimed; a *fresh* lock re-fires,
proving the lock is the gate) + **a real-Valkey test** (two `Bus::connect` handles = two pods → `a ^ b`,
exactly one fires) + the prior scan/tz tests + full api(70)/automation/ingest suites green (live PG +
Valkey); and the **binary boots with Valkey** ("connected to Valkey bus" → "schedule worker spawned"). The
**run_automation job** is already single-claim (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED); this closes the *scheduler* dup, so
the only remaining at-least-once gap is **crash-mid-run resumption** (a reconciler re-drive starts a fresh
run — `execute` doesn't resume), still deferred. **Deferred:** run resumption; a Leptos automations/runs
view; a skill's `tools` restricting the agent; storage §9 / channel §25 sources;
`GraphQuery`/`CalendarEvent` poll triggers; per-automation §19 grant resolution._

_2026-06-15 — **command execution: a local `Executor` + the
`run_command` tool, protected by capabilities** (M5, SOUL §20) — the agent can now *do real work*
(run shell commands), and it's the cleanest demonstration yet of §19's deny-by-default protected
scopes. `catalerum-exec`'s skeleton becomes `LocalExecutor` — `tokio::process` on the host: runs an
`argv` (inline `code` is the container/bao backends' job → `Unsupported`), pipes stdin, sets env/cwd,
enforces an optional **program allow-list**, and times out with `kill_on_drop` so a slow child is
reaped (no leak). The `run_command` tool (in `catalerum-api`) wraps any `Executor` and requires
**`exec:run`** — a capability **no base role holds** (`exec` isn't in the role domains), so it is
denied by default: a Member/Viewer cannot run commands, and only an explicitly-handed grant can — §19's
"'wipe the local computer' is unreachable unless that exact capability is handed over on purpose".
**Doubly gated:** the tool is registered only when `[exec].enabled` (default off; the binary builds the
`LocalExecutor` with the configured `allow` list + `CATALERUM_EXEC__*` overrides), and even then needs
`exec:run`, and even then the executor's allow-list applies. Verified: clippy `--all-targets` clean;
the full `just test` path (live PG/Qdrant/Neo4j) green (48 result lines, 0 failed) incl. **5
`LocalExecutor` unit tests** (stdout/exit capture, non-zero exit, stdin+env, allow-list rejection,
timeout-kills-child, code-`Unsupported`/empty-`Invalid`) and a **live api `run_command` test**
(Member+Viewer denied; an explicit `exec:run` runs and echoes; empty argv rejected; the tool is absent
without a configured executor); wasm clean; binary boots with `[exec].enabled` logging the allow-list.
**Deferred:** the container (docker/podman, the default sandbox) + bao + Kubernetes executor backends
(§20); **inline `code`** execution (bao/container); interactive `open_session`; per-grant exec
**constraints** (`lang`/`net`/`cpu`, and treating the protected exec scope as *not* covered by a bare

`RunCommand` action (M5)._

_2026-06-15 — **per-action capability enforcement is now live at the
tool dispatch choke point** (M4, SOUL §19) — the security thesis (principle 3/13) moves from *defined*
to *enforced*: a chat tool call is **denied by default** unless the caller's grant covers the
capability it needs. This was the most-repeated deferral ("per-action scoping still pending"). The
pieces existed (the `catalerum-core::capability` model — `Capability::covers`, `allows`, `Action`/
`Resource` — and `catalerum-iam::base_capabilities(role)` mapping roles → caps); the gap was wiring
enforcement. Now: the `Tool` trait gains `required_capability() -> Option<Capability>` (each tool
declares what it needs — `notes:write`, `memory:read`, `vector:search`, `graph:query`,
`profile:write`, …); `ToolContext` gains `capabilities: Option<Vec<Capability>>`; and
`ToolRegistry::dispatch` enforces — when `capabilities` is `Some` and the tool needs a cap, deny
(`Error::Unauthorized`) unless some held cap **covers** it. **Opt-in by design:** a `None` context
skips the check, so internal/legacy callers and the ~40 existing tool tests are untouched — zero
churn. `/ws/chat` populates the context with `base_capabilities(principal.role)`, so the model runs
under the **user's role authority**: a Viewer can read/recall/search but cannot write notes/memories;
a Member can write; an Owner/Admin holds the wildcard. Added `profile` to the iam capability domains.
`fetch_url`'s `web:read` egress is left ungated pending host-glob policy (a §19/§27 protected scope).

result lines, 0 failed) incl. a **core dispatch-enforcement unit test** (read-only denied / writer
allowed / wildcard allowed / no-caps = off) and a **live api role test** (Viewer denied
`create_note`+`remember` but allowed `list_notes`+`recall`; Member writes; Owner wildcard; `None`
context = legacy pass); wasm clean; binary boots. **Deferred:** grant **constraints** (env all-list,

_2026-06-14 — **`catalerum-graph` Neo4j projection client landed &
verified end-to-end** (next M4 vector/graph slice, SOUL §6.3). The skeleton crate is now a thin async
client over Neo4j's **HTTP transactional API** (`POST /db/{database}/tx/commit`) — same shape as
`catalerum-vector`'s Qdrant client, so the projection layer stays dependency-light (no Bolt driver)
with one auth/TLS story. **Injection-safe by construction:** Cypher labels and relationship types
can't be parameterized, so both are **closed enums** (`NodeLabel`/`EdgeType`) with a fixed
`&'static str` table — caller data never reaches a label position; workspace ids, node ids, and
properties all ride as `$parameters`. **Tenancy:** every node is keyed on `(workspace_id, id)` and
**every** query filters on `workspace_id`, so cross-workspace reach is impossible by construction
(§18) — `project_note` even refuses a reference whose entity is in another workspace before any
write. `GraphStore`: `ensure_indexes` (idempotent `(workspace_id, id)` range index per label, the
MERGE-key backing), idempotent `MERGE` writers `project_note` (one tx: upsert the `:Note` node +
each referenced `:Person/:Topic/…` entity node + a `REFERENCES` edge to each) and `project_entity`,
the typed read `references_of`, `count_nodes`, `delete_node` (single-source re-projection basis) and
`delete_workspace` (full per-workspace rebuild, §3.1), plus a low-level `run`/`run_one` over
arbitrary `Statement`s. Neo4j reports Cypher failures in the `errors` array with HTTP 200, so a
non-empty `errors` becomes `GraphError::Cypher` (transport ok, transaction not). Verified: `cargo
build`/`clippy` clean (0 warnings); 17 offline unit tests (statement builders scope on
workspace+id, merge-edge merges both endpoints + relationship, index name/label derive from the
closed enum, tx/commit response parsing incl. Cypher-error surfacing + scalar count, note/entity
prop shaping, bad-url + db-url construction); a **live-Neo4j (5) integration test**
(`NEO4J_URL`-gated, skip-and-pass offline) drove the full contract green against the compose
server — ensure-indexes, project-note, **idempotent re-projection** (count stays 3, no dups),
`references_of` returns both targets, **per-workspace isolation** (a second workspace sees nothing),
cross-workspace-edge refusal, delete-node, delete-workspace; `cargo check --workspace` clean.
**Next M4:** the embed→upsert **ingest worker** (chunk Postgres notes/docs/memories → llmleaf
`Embedder` → `VectorStore::upsert`, consuming `job_queue` §10) — now joined by a **project-to-graph
worker** that consumes the same queue and drives `GraphStore::project_*` — and the
`search_semantic`/`query_graph`/`query_structured` **retrieval tools** wiring both stores into the
chat agent loop (§6.5/§7)._

_2026-06-14 — **`catalerum-vector` Qdrant client landed & verified
end-to-end** (first M4 vector slice, SOUL §6.4/§18). The skeleton crate is now a thin async Qdrant
REST client: `VectorStore` with per-workspace collections (`catalerum_ws_<uuid>`),
`ensure_collection` (idempotent + vector-width-checked — a re-ensure at a different dim **refuses**

(§18). Tenancy: per-workspace collections satisfy §18's partitioning invariant, and the redundant
payload `workspace_id` keeps the §29 "collection-per-workspace vs shared" question a cheap future
migration rather than a rewrite — **provisionally per-workspace**. Verified: `cargo build`/`clippy`
clean (0 warnings); 10 offline unit tests (collection naming, distance mapping, payload JSON

contract — create / idempotent-ensure / dim-mismatch-refusal, upsert, nearest-neighbour +
kind/entity/time-filtered search, per-workspace isolation, delete-by-source, delete-by-id,
drop-collection + lenient empty/zero reads on a missing collection — all green, collections cleaned
